Title: New Year's Eve Greetings Presentation
text: Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose de Lima Massano, at the presentation of kwanza's new family of banknotes and coins Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose de Lima Massano, at the presentation of the new family of banknotes and coins kwanza Your Excellencies, Madam Minister of Culture, Minister of Commerce, Dr. Maria Eugenia Neto, Excellencies Distinguished guests, Ladies and gentlemen, Today we have made official the launch of a new family of banknotes and coins, pursuant to the authorization granted to the National Bank of Angola by Law 20/12 30 July. It is a particular moment for our Kwanza because this January we celebrate the 36th anniversary of its entry into circulation as the currency of all Angolan. Therefore, on this special occasion, it is right to pay tribute to the leaders and technicians who in extraordinarily difficult circumstances, shortly after the proclamation of national independence, engaged in the constitutive acts of a new currency, monetary sovereignty of the Republic of Angola. The Angolan economy has shown a remarkable pace of growth, especially since 2002, the year in which that the country has won peace. This growth intensifies the activity and leads to greater and faster monetary circulation. The money we use passes more rapidly through various economic actors and even with the remarkable advance of electronic means, there are still many cash payments, at least that it is up to us to preserve and increase the comfort of in the handling of the national currency. The current Kwanza family, which has been circulating for more than 14 years, no longer has its characteristics aligned with modern safety standards, so this and other reasons, it has long been required to update it. Therefore, one of the main characteristics of the Kwanza family, whose launch we are today to do, is the incorporation of modern security features, which can be identified through tact and vision, allowing, from the citizen common to the agents of financial institutions, it is easily ensure the genuineness of banknotes and coins. In order to preserve the stability of our economy, we will make a phased introduction of the new banknotes and coins, starting with a campaign of communication so that the new characteristics of the Kwanza are known to all. On February 18, the new coins enter into circulation. The issuance of coins also reveals the BNA's concern with the maintenance of fairer commercial activities. In fact, with the coins a low monetary value, retail traders will be more likely and more alternative the price of goods, avoiding their rounding for ever higher values due to the absence of means of payment of lower denomination. Each of us will contribute to this effect whenever, when making a purchase, we exercise the right to receive the right change. After the coins, on March 22 and throughout the first half of 2013, they enter into circulation, progressively, the new banknotes, including the denomination of 5,000 Kwanzas. The reference to the 5,000 Kwanzas cedula has led to the question of the possibility of contributing to the increase in inflation. The Bank National Authority of Angola would like to take this opportunity to clarify that the introduction of a note of higher face value does not in itself contribute to the increase in prices, i.e. for inflation. From a monetary point of view, the phenomenon of inflation is not due to the face value of banknotes, but yes when the total amount of money to be circulated is greater than the necessary for transactions that take place in an economy. It should be noted that around 70% of the financial value of the paper money currently in circulation, corresponds to the denominations of one thousand and two thousand Kwanzas, and that, from the date of entry into circulation of these denominations to this day, the accumulated inflation reached about 124%, demonstrating, in general terms, to be today double the financial value of these banknotes to maintain the same purchasing power. The non-regularisation of this situation contributes to the transactions, especially those of higher value, other currencies gain space of circulation in our economy, conditioning the action of the monetary authority in the preservation of the value of the national currency, in addition to management of the current environment. The entry into circulation of the 5,000 Kwanzas banknote will not increase the financial value of the paper money in the public's power. It will only be changed your composition, since the introduction of the new banknotes will be made in the fair measure of the value of the banknotes of the current family that are delivered to the National Bank of Angola, or financial value of the banknotes to be injected into the market shall be the same as that collected. There will therefore be no influence on the balance of the monetary base or the means of payment. There will be, yes, an effective saving of resources for the manufacture, storage and circulation of banknotes, as well as a huge gain from the preservation, which will help control inflation. In any case, society must remain vigilant to speculative attempts or acts that may be triggered by some operators under the pretext of new banknotes entering into circulation. The measures to correct structural deficiencies in the economy that the Executive led by His Your Excellency, Eng. Jose Eduardo dos Santos has been adopting, combined with a better link between monetary and fiscal policies, have contributed to inflation is consistently decreasing. In 2012 and for the first time in our recent economic history, it has been possible to keep inflation at single digits. This skin will continue, as is inferfrom the national medium-term development plan. The monetary policy maintains price stability as its and the new members of kwanza's family will contribute to this. In the case of a currency exchange operation, the current banknotes will remain in circulation and should normally be accepted in commercial transactions and until the National Bank of Angola reports the end of its validity period. The new banknotes will be in the possession of citizens through the banking network and Commercial. At the head and regional delegations of the National Bank angola will remain open for the obtaining of coins. The new kwanza family, in addition to honoring the first presidents of an independent and to have hydrographic wealth as a reason, highlight the angolan cultural identity and highlight the strength of our nature. Extensive research work was done so that we could represent our values in each of the notes and coins that make up the new Kwanza's family. Therefore, we would like to express our thanks for the engagement of the Ministry of Culture and, in particular, the specialists of the Anthropology Museum. It was also possible to introduce high safety standards in the note, maintaining its aesthetic beauty, therefore, we also appreciate the work carried out by the Mr. Horacio Da Mesquita who took charge of bringing the elements together and with art to shape the new notes. We also express our thanks to all the technicians and experts of the National Bank angola involved in such a very unrestitable task. With the new family of banknotes and coins, Kwanza is set in a quality standard international law, providing more confidence and credibility in the use of of the national currency. Finally, aware that money costs money, we would like to appeal to all citizens and economic operators in order to make good conservation of notes and coins, thus contributing to the continuous appreciation of our Kwanza. I appreciate everyone's presence. Thank you very much. Security Elements of the new family of banknotes and coins Jan. 29. 2013

Ministra da Cultura, Sra. Ministra do Comrcio, Dra. Maria Eugnia Neto, Excelncias, Distintos convidados, Minhas senhoras e meus Senhores, Oficializamos hoje o lanamento de uma nova famlia de notas e moedas metlicas, nos termos da autorizao concedida ao Banco Nacional de Angola pela Lei 20/12 de 30 de Julho.  um momento particular para o nosso Kwanza porque, neste ms de Janeiro, celebramos o 36 aniversrio da sua entrada em circulao como moeda de todos angolanos. Por isso, nesta ocasio especial,  justo fazermos uma homenagem aos dirigentes e tcnicos que em circunstncias extraordinariamente difceis, logo aps a proclamao da independncia nacional, se empenharam nos actos constitutivos de uma nova moeda, marcando a soberania monetria da Repblica de Angola. A economia angolana tem evidenciado um ritmo notvel de crescimento, sobretudo desde 2002, ano em que o pas conquistou a paz. Esse crescimento intensifica a actividade comercial e leva a uma maior e mais clere circulao monetria. O dinheiro que usamos passa mais rapidamente por diversos agentes econmicos e mesmo com o avano notvel dos meios electrnicos, ainda so muitos os pagamentos em dinheiro, pelo que compete-nos preservar e aumentar o conforto da sociedade no manuseio da moeda nacional. A actual famlia do Kwanza, que circula h mais de 14 anos, deixou de ter as suas caractersticas alinhadas aos modernos padres de segurana, pelo que, por esta e outras razes, h muito se impunha a sua actualizao. Por isso, uma das principais caractersticas da famlia do Kwanza, cujo lanamento estamos hoje a efectuar,  a incorporao de modernos elementos de segurana, os quais podem ser identificados por meio do tacto e da viso, permitindo que, desde o cidado comum aos agentes das instituies financeiras, se possa facilmente certificar a genuinidade das notas e moedas. De forma a preservarmos a estabilidade da nossa economia, faremos uma introduo faseada das novas notas e moedas metlicas, iniciando com uma campanha de comunicao abrangente para que as novas caractersticas do Kwanza sejam conhecidas por todos. A 18 de Fevereiro, entram em circulao as novas moedas metlicas. A emisso de moedas metlicas revela, tambm, a preocupao do BNA com a manuteno de relaes comerciais mais justas. De facto, tendo as moedas um baixo valor monetrio, os comerciantes retalhistas ficaro com maiores possibilidades e mais alternativas na definio do preo dos bens, evitando o seu arredondamento para valores sempre mais elevados por ausncia de meios de pagamento de menor denominao. Cada um de ns contribuir para esse efeito sempre que, ao fazer uma compra, exercer o direito de receber o troco certo. Depois das moedas metlicas, no dia 22 de Maro e ao longo do primeiro semestre de 2013, entram em circulao, progressivamente, as novas notas, incluindo a denominao de 5 mil Kwanzas. A referncia  cedula de 5 mil Kwanzas tem levado a que nos seja colocada a questo da possibilidade de ela contribuir para o aumento da inflao. O Banco Nacional de Angola gostaria de aproveitar esta oportunidade para esclarecer que a introduo de uma nota de maior valor facial no contribui por si s para o aumento dos preos, ou seja, para a inflao. Do ponto de vista monetrio, o fenmeno da inflao no se d devido ao valor facial das notas, mas sim quando a quantidade total de dinheiro a circular  superior  necessria para as transaces que se efectuam numa economia. Importa referir que cerca de 70% do valor financeiro do papel-moeda actualmente em circulao, corresponde s denominaes de mil e 2 mil Kwanzas, e que, da data de entrada em circulao dessas denominaes at aos dias de hoje, a inflao acumulada atingiu cerca de 124%, demonstrando, em termos genricos, ser hoje necessrio o dobro do valor financeiro dessas cdulas para se manter o mesmo poder de compra. A no regularizao dessa situao concorre para que, por efeitos de segurana e fluidez das transaces, sobretudo das de maior valor, outras moedas ganhem espao de circulao na nossa economia, condicionando-se a aco da autoridade monetria na preservao do valor da moeda nacional, alm de se encarecer significativamente a gesto do meio circulante. A entrada em circulao da cdula de 5 mil Kwanzas no ir aumentar o valor financeiro do papel-moeda em poder do pblico. Ser somente alterada a sua composio, pois a introduo das novas notas, ser feita na justa medida do valor das notas da actual famlia que forem entregues ao Banco Nacional de Angola, ou seja, o valor financeiro das notas a injectar no mercado ser igual ao que for recolhido. No haver, por essa via, qualquer influncia sobre o saldo da base monetria ou dos meios de pagamento. Haver, isso sim, uma efectiva economia de recursos pblicos destinados  fabricao, armazenagem e circulao das notas, alm de um enorme ganho com a sua preservao, o que ajudar no controlo da inflao. De qualquer modo, deve a sociedade manter-se vigilante a tentativas ou actos especulativos que eventualmente sejam desencadeados por alguns operadores econmicos, sob o pretexto de entrada em circulao de novas notas. As medidas de correco de deficincias estruturais na economia que o Executivo liderado por Sua Excelncia, o Eng. Jos Eduardo dos Santos, tem vindo a adoptar, conjugadas com uma melhor articulao entre as polticas monetria e fiscal, tm contribudo para que a inflao esteja, de forma consistente, a diminuir. Em 2012 e pela primeira vez, na nossa histria econmica recente, foi possvel manter a inflao a um dgito. Esse esfoo vai continuar, como se infere do plano nacional de desenvolvimento de mdio prazo. A poltica monetria mantm a estabilidade de preos como o seu objectivo central e os novos membros da famlia do Kwanza vo contribuir para que assim acontea. No se tratando de uma operao de troca de moeda, as notas actuais permanecero em circulao e devem ser normalmente aceites nas transaces comerciais e financeiras, at que o Banco Nacional de Angola comunique o fim do seu prazo de validade. As novas notas estaro em posse dos cidados por via da rede bancria e dos estabelecimentos comerciais. Na sede e nas Delegaes Regionais do Banco Nacional de Angola manter-se-o abertos postos para a obteno de moeda metlica. A nova famlia do Kwanza, alm de homenagear os primeiros presidentes de uma Angola independente e de terem a riqueza hidrogrfica como motivo, destacam a identidade cultural angolana e realam a fora da nossa natureza. Foi feito um exaustivo trabalho de investigao para que pudssemos representar os nossos valores culturais em cada uma das notas e moedas que compem a nova famlia do Kwanza. Por isso, gostaramos de expressar os nossos agradecimentos pelo engajamento do Ministrio da Cultura e, particularmente, dos especialistas do Museu de Antropologia. Foi possvel tambm introduzir altos padres de segurana na nota, mantendo a sua beleza esttica, por isso, agradecemos igualmente o trabalho desenvolvido pelo Sr. Horcio D Mesquita que se encarregou de juntar os elementos e com arte dar forma s novas notas. Expressamos ainda os nossos agradecimentos, a todos os tcnicos e especialistas do Banco Nacional de Angola envolvidos em to ingente tarefa. Com a nova famlia de notas e moedas metlicas, o Kwanza insere-se num padro de qualidade internacional, proporcionando mais confiana e credibilidade no uso da moeda nacional. Para terminar, conscientes de que dinheiro custa dinheiro, gostaramos de apelar a todos os cidados e operadores econmicos no sentido da boa conservao das notas e moedas, contribuindo assim para a contnua valorizao do nosso Kwanza. Agradeo a presena de todos. Muito Obrigado. Title: nterveno de abertura do Senhor Governador Manuel Tiago Dias, na Conferncia sobre Incluso Financeira em Angola  Desafios e Oportunidades
text: Opening speech by the Governor Manuel Tiago Dias, at the Conference on Financial Inclusion in Angola - Challenges and Opportunities His Excellency Mr. Mario de Oliveira, Minister of Telecommunications, Information Technologies and Social Communication; Your Excellency Vera Daves de Sousa, Minister of Finance; Your Excellencies Members of the Ministerial Departments; Your Excellency Representatives of FinMark Trust; Your Excellencies Representatives of the National Institute of Statistics; Your Excellencies Representatives of MIRA - LBC; Distinguished representatives of international institutions; Distinguished representatives of Financial and Non-Financial Institutions; Dear representatives of the Universities; Your Excellencies Members of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola; Gentlemen; Ladies and Gentlemen. It is with great joy that I have the honor of welcoming everyone here to be part of this act that adds up to another event in the space of the Cycle I Conferences of the National Bank of Angola. Dear guests, the effectiveness of policies, whether of the financial or socio-political forum, depends on a number of factors, however, the same is not the case statistical information whose instrumental role is, on the one hand, relevant in all phases of the implementation of development programs, from their form, evaluation and/or restructuring and, on the other hand, contributes to the improvement of transparency of information and accountability responsibility. Thus, with your presence and active participation we hope to obtain the essential elements for an efficient and effective management of monetary and financial policy in this way the necessary alignment with socio-economic policies, aware that citizens are the loyal evaluators of public policies. Ladies and Gentlemen, It is our expectation that the conference on the theme "FINANCIAL INCLUSION IN ANGOLA - CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES", will provide a very interactive around the presentation of the central themes, namely: "The Results of the Finscope Angola Survey", "Financial Inclusion: Current Perspectives", "The Developments of Payment Systems", and "The Importance of Insurance for Financial Inclusion". These themes represent a structured set of instruments that aim to raise the level of access and use of financial products and services through their continuous response to the specific needs of the population. Before proceeding, I would like to express my appreciation to FinMark Trust and MIRA - LBC, for their collaboration in carrying out the first Finscope Survey in an extremely important survey to assess the state of Financial Inclusion along with a series of relevant economic and social indicators. From this perspective, we are certain that with the results of the FinScope Survey we have in our possession reliable data comparable to other realities that are considered essential in the assessment of the state of Financial Inclusion at the national level. This will allow us to set more realistic goals and develop policies aimed at increasing access, use and quality of financial products and services with greater assertiveness, in line with international best practices. Dear Guests, This type of survey allows us not only to assess the impact of the implementation of good practices on the state of our current socio-economic condition, but also to achieve a balance between encouraging innovation and preserving the stability of the financial ecosystem. In addition, it is essential to assess the consumer perspective, reflected in the data in this survey on the supply and demand of financial products and services, in order to adopt measures with the aim of having an adverse impact of their expectations on the expected results. This survey also provides an assessment of the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) for 2 ( national goals of poverty reduction, greater social equity and inclusive economic growth. Dear Participants, I wish you all a good debate during this Conference emphasizing the opportunity to share valuable experiences, best practices, and solutions for assertive decisions. With these brief words, I declare open the conference on the theme "FINANCIAL INCLUSION IN ANGOLA - CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES Thank you very much. Published In: Jun 29, 2023

Title: Interveno de Abertura do Governador Manuel Tiago Dias, no Workshop sobre Estatsticas da Central de Balanos e sua Importncia
text: Opening Speech by Governor Manuel Tiago Dias, at the Workshop on Statistics of the Central Balance Sheet Database and its Importance Distinguished Representatives of the Central Banks of the Community of Portuguese Speaking Countries - CPLP and the Bank of Spain, Distinguished Representatives of Ministerial Departments of the Angolan Executive, Dear Heads of the National Bank of Angola, the General Tax Administration and the National Institute of Statistics, Ladies and Gentlemen. It is with great satisfaction that I welcome all the guests who promptly responded to our invitation to participate in the V On the Statistics of the Central Balance Sheet Database and its Importance. The National Bank of Angola, within the scope of its statutory duties, started to produce and publish from the end of 2021 the statistics of non-fin companies, i.e., the Central Balance Sheet Database, to assist in monetary policy decision-making. At present, the production and dissemination of statistics on non-financial corporations contributes to a better understanding of the economic and financial situation of Angolan corporations, reducing uncertainties in decision-making, assessing their ability to absorb the resources of the financial system and their ability to honour their respective commitments. The main purpose of the strategic actions of the National Bank of Angola in this area is to strengthen macroprudential analyses and to assist monetary decision-making. Ladies and Gentlemen, Thus, with a view to improving its instruments to support monetary and exchange rate policy measures and providing society with useful information on economic activity, Banco Nacional Angola has developed, since 2017, the Central Balance Sheet Database, with the support of Banco de Portugal, through a technical assistance mission. In addition, it had the collaboration of three key partners, namely, the General Tax Administration, Institute 1 of Statistics, and Companies in the field of sharing information in the Financial Statements. The Central Balance Sheet Database is the database of economic and financial information of non-financial companies in the country, under the management of the Department of Statistics of the National Angola. This information is mainly based on annual accounting data of a non-consolidated nature, from various sectors of economic activity. The methodology that Banco Nacional Angola uses to produce the "business and sector tables" is based on the United Nations Statistics Division's manual for compiling non-financial statistics from the United Nations Statistics Division. At the end of 2021, the National Bank of Angola published the first statistics on non-financial corporations, based on the central balance sheet. We have published on our Institutional Website the economic and financial indicators, as well as the sectoral analysis reports, of which we highlight the information and communication activities, beverage manufacturing industry, construction and transport and storage. In this context, with the aim of strengthening the availability of information through the Central Balance Sheet Database, the publication of the crude oil and natural gas extraction sector is planned for this year, followed by the trade sector. Dear guests, Although we have achieved remarkable milestones, with the unconditional support of our partners, whom we thank for their collaboration, we understand that challenges persist in order to increase the statistical coverage of the Central Balance Sheet Database, improve methodologies and work processes. We have therefore decided to take the report from the Bank of Spain's experts on the Central Balance Sheet Database. Over several years, the Bank of Spain has accumulated a great mastery of methodologies, developed work processes, published innovative reports and other significant actions, becoming one of the main references at international level. Under the terms of the Constitution of the Republic and its Organic Law, it is the responsibility of the National Bank of Angola to ensure price stability in our economy and to preserve the value of the national currency. According to official INE data, in 2022 there was a reduction in the inflation rate, standing at 13.86/ 27.03% in 2021. The occurrence of domestic and international risks with repercussions on price stability in our economy will lead Banco Nacional Angola to adopt a more pronounced restrictive monetary policy, contrary to the signs of easing it had been giving to the market. For the success of this process, it is essential and imperative that all the actors in our economy collaborate, with a view to bringing together synergies, as well as concerted solutions to overcome the challenges we still face. With these words, I declare open the Workshop on Central Balance Sheet Statistics and Their Importance. Published in: Jun 30, 2023

Title: Interveno do Governador Manuel Tiago Dias, no acto de Lanamento Oficial do KWiK, Instrumento de Transferncias Instantneas
text: Speech by Governor Manuel Tiago Dias, at the Official Launch of KWiK, Instant Transfer Instrument Your Excellency Mr. Pedro Puna, Chairman of the Board of Directors of EMIS Your Excellency Mr. Jose Matos, Chairman of the Executive Committee of EMIS Your Excellency Members of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola Your Excellency Mr. Mario Nascimento, President of ABANC Distinguished Members of the Executive Committee of EMIS Distinguished Members of the Boards of Directors of Financial and Non-Financial Institutions Dear Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, It is with great joy that we have just witnessed the launch of KWiK - Acronym for Instant Kwanza, which is the culmination of a program started by E about two years ago, with the support of the National Bank of Angola. This program resulted from a joint evaluation that was carried out within the scope of the World Bank's technical assistance, with a view to increasing financial levels in Angola. Thus, seeing this project become a reality, we cannot fail to publicly acknowledge the efforts of all those who enthusiastically made it possible to make the first instant transfers using this new payment instrument. Our country currently has a low banking rate, which means that a large part of our adult population is excluded from access to bank employees. If we can say that Angola is doing relatively well when it comes to classic banking services, placing itself at the level of the best practiced in Africa, we cannot say when it comes to solutions aimed at the unbanked population, where the existing offers are still very limited. Access to basic financial services, starting with instant transfers of funds, is very important, not only to promote formal savings, but also to pave the way for access to microcredit, which is truly the main objective of a financial inclusion program. In this context, the BNA, in partnership with EMIS, decided to take an active role in the development of this new payment instrument, which is the modern payment instrument KA, adapted to the reality of the non-banking world, inclusive and user-friendly. The development of a universally accepted payment instrument requires the existence of a financial market infrastructure that allows interoperability between all participating service providers, on equal terms, whether banking or non-banking. Thus, taking into account the importance of interoperability, similar to what is happening in other geographies, where the State assumes responsibility for financial market infrastructures that support inclusive payment instruments, we are evaluating the adoption of an extended moratorium on interoperability costs with the KWiK arrangement, for all participating service providers. For a payment instrument of this nature to be truly inclusive, it is essential that it has a single brand, widely known by the f accepted by most payment service providers, as is the case today with cards, namely those of the Multicaixa brand. We therefore intend that the new payment instrument, KWiK - Kwanza Instantaneous, is developed in our market, in an ecosystem that provides for startups to find space that allows them to make their contribution to the Angolan Payment System The KWiK instant transfers and the Multicaixa card thus correspond to two payment instruments, which should coexist in an integrated way in the payment services market. Before concluding, allow me, ladies and gentlemen, to highlight the indispensable contribution of mobile communications operators to this financial effort. The participation of these operators will be decisive for the inclusion of the population that does not have access to financial services, taking advantage of their cap and their experience in managing agent networks. I conclude by reiterating our commitment to the promotion and expansion of instant payments and, above all, financial inclusion in our country. Thank you very much for your attention. Title: Interveno de Encerramento do Vice-Governador Pedro Castro e Silva, no Acto Alusivo s Comemoraes do Dia do Trabalhador Bancrio
text: Closing Speech by Vice-Governor Pedro Castro e Silva, at the Ceremony Alluding to the Commemorations of the Bank Worker's Day Mr. President of the National Union of Bank Employees of Angola, Distinguished Members of the Boards of Directors of Commercial Banks, Distinguished representatives of the workers associated with the National Union of Bank Employees of Angola, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen. On behalf of the National Bank of Angola, I thank you for the invitation to participate in this already traditional event, promoted annually by SNEBA. This year's motto - "48 Years, Banking at the Service of the Development of Angola", takes us a little through the history of the Banking Sector, since our independence and the main stages of its development, which allows us to reflect on the present and project the future. After the act of 14 August 1975, marked by the takeover of the destinies of the banking sector by Angolan nationalists, it is necessary to highlight a set of aspects, namely the promulgation of Laws Nos. 69 and 70, both of 5 November 1976, which established the National Bank of Angola and the People's Bank of Angola, the former holding the assets and liabilities of the Bank of Angola and the latter, those of the Commercial Bank of Angola. I would like to recognize the courage, dedication, and merit of generations of Angolan bank employees who, since independence, have been committed to this whole process of framing, maturing and evolving the national banking system. Since August 14, 1975, the Banking Sector has been among those that has undergone the most structural changes, with particular emphasis on the number and type of institution Currently, we have 23 banking financial institutions operating in our market, as well as 108 non-banking financial institutions, from pre-presidency payment service companies, exchange houses, remittance companies, microcredit companies, etc. The evolution we are witnessing in the typology of financial institutions operating in our market is a response not only to the demand for financial services by economic agents, but also result of the impact that technological innovation has on the financial system. Hence, we observe that, although the bulk of financial transactions occur in the banking system, the level of penetration of non-banking financial solutions is increasing, with fintechs and other types of payment service providers as intermediaries. The evolution in the supply of financial services, as well as in the channels through which they are made available to economic agents, is accompanied by other types of risks, as banking activity is a risk management activity, par excellence. Therefore, the regulator and the regulated parties have been engaged in a process of convergence with internationally agreed regulations, especially those regarding market, credit, liquidity, operational and money laundering and terrorist financing risks. We will now enter a phase of adapting our regulatory framework in order to prepare the banking system in general and governance models in particular, to manage climate risk. Such a process of adapting our regulation is unavoidable and demanding. The training and capacity building of banking professionals, from the cashier, through the clerk, to the governing bodies are a critical success factor. The National Bank of Angola and the Association of Banks work together to develop standardized training programs on topics such as corporate governance, internal control, etc. Other areas will deserve due attention in the short term. We believe that the robustness of corporate governance systems and the training of bank employees are a condition for us to play the role of financial intermediary, providing financing for economic activity. To conclude, to all of us, workers of today and of our banking of the future, I want to stress the importance of continuing to work with professionalism and rigor, so that together we can continue to build a healthy, modern and inclusive financial system. Congratulations bank employees and thank you very much for your attention! Published in: Aug 31, 2023

text: Speech by The Deputy Governor, Dr. Andre Lopes, at the opening of the Workshop on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Speech by The Deputy Governor, Dr. Andre Lopes, at the opening of the Workshop on Combating Money Laundering and Financing terrorism Mr President of ABANC - Mr Amilcar Silva, Exmos. Presidents and other members of the Boards of Directors and Committees Executives of Financial Institutions, Ladies and gentlemen of the Board of Directors and the Board of Directors of the BNA, Distinguished Guests, Different prelectors, Ladies and gentlemen, On behalf of the Former Governor of the BNA, Dr. Jose de Lima Massano, who by impediment of agenda can't be here with us and in my own name, i would like to greet and thank the presence of all the distinguished guests to the "Workshop on the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing" primarily directed at workers in banking and non-bank financial institutions, supervised by the Central Bank. As you know, in 2010 the Republic of Angola was admitted, as an observer member of the Country Group South and East Africa against Money Laundering (ESAAMLG) and two years later, more precisely in August 2012, became a member of the full right of that regional organisation - a fact that demonstrates the international recognition of the Republic of Angola as a country committed to the prevention of and Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist financing. To this end, a number of actions carried out by the Angolan authorities will have contributed, including the adoption of Law No. 34/11 of 12 December  Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Act, which repealed Law No. 12/10 of 9 July, with the same name, that among other aspects, sets out the general obligations to which the entities subject, the financial and non-financial sectors. In addition, Presidential Decree No. 35/11 of 15 February was approved and published, which institutionalized the Financial Information Unit (FIU), body with the purpose of collecting, analysing, including, where necessary, the request for additional information from external institutions, as well as the dissemination to police and judicial bodies of suspected money laundering operations and Financing for Terrorism. In the same vein, the National Bank of Angola, as a guarantor of the stability of the financial, and in line with the Law to which I have been referring, adopted a set of regulatory regulations, with the aim of providing greater soundness and efficiency to the activity of financial institutions under their supervision prevention and combating crimes in BC and FT. With these measures, particularly those of a preventive nature, we have adto bring for the financial system in particular and for the country in general, which among others, in reducing the crime of money laundering, ensuring the stability of financial institutions and a significant contribution to for economic development with the consequent strengthening of the image of the institutions both internally and externally. Therefore, we have no doubt in mentioning that our country is committed and the engaged, in compliance with anti-money laundering standards Capital Finance and Terrorist Financing, which are essentially the result of the Policies and Recommendations made by the Financial Action Group (FATF) in this matter. Such desideratum does not depend solely on the existence of applicable legislation or on the BNA, as supervisory authority which shall ensure effective compliance with the the legal and regulatory provisions applicable to the financial system under its supervision. Here play a fundamental role the players of the system, the workers of financial institutions, to the extent that they are the ones who, in the first instance ensure compliance with the rules. For this reason, it is essential to invest heavily in the development and implementation of policies, processes and control systems in the field of assessment and management of risk and training of workers, so that everything combined can result in efficient monitoring of customers and transactions, to mitigate the risks of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing in each financial institution. This need for investment is of particular importance in the case of non-bank financial institutions, such as exchange offices and providers of remittance services, due to the nature of their business involving a high volume of transactions in cash and the occasional nature of the institutions, particularly vulnerable to the use by persons or entities involved in criminal activities. In fact only through the adoption of policies, processes and control mechanisms appropriate to the nature and specificity of foreign exchange and remittance trade values, it will be possible to mitigate this potential risk to which these activities are exposed. This is where this WorkShop is included, during which we will have the opportunity to listen renowned national and foreign experts who will share with us their knowledge in this area, in a process that we hope will be eminently but also to exchange experiences between the Institutions. Indeed, for a few hours we will hear about topics such as the legislative framework and regulatory authorities, the role of financial institutions and the regulator, typologies of suspicious transactions, their bank secrecy and duty of communication, as well as the perspective of bankers and external auditors on the matter, whose interest and timeliness, we are sure, will arouse the interest of all and encourage strong participation and interaction. Therefore, hoping with this initiative to contribute to the need for workers in financial institutions present here, can gather the lessons that contribute to the for the consolidation of the ongoing adequacy process, I declare open the work of this worshop on combating money laundering and financing terrorism. Thank you very much 23 Apr. 2013

Senhores Presidentes e demais membros dos Conselhos de Administrao e das Comisses Executivas das Instituies Financeiras, Caros Colegas da Administrao e do Conselho de Direco do BNA, Ilustres Convidados, Distintos Prelectores, Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores, Em nome do Exmo Senhor Governador do BNA, Dr. Jose de Lima Massano, que por impedimento de agenda no pode estar aqui connosco e em meu nome pessoal, gostaria de saudar e agradecer a presena de todos os distintos convidados ao Workshop sobre o Branqueamento de Capitais e Financiamento do Terrorismo dirigido essencialmente aos trabalhadores das instituies financeiras bancrias e no bancrias, supervisionadas pelo Banco Central. Como sabem, em 2010 a Republica de Angola foi admitida, como membro observador do Grupo de Pases do Sul e Leste de Africa contra o Branqueamento de Capitais (ESAAMLG) e volvidos dois anos, mais precisamente em Agosto de 2012, tornou-se membro de pleno direito da referida organizao regional  facto que demonstra o reconhecimento internacional da Repblica de Angola como um Pas empenhado na preveno e Combate ao Branqueamento de Capitais e do Financiamento ao Terrorismo. Para o efeito, tero contribudo um conjunto de aces desenvolvidas pelas autoridades angolanas, nomeadamente a aprovao da Lei n. 34/11 de 12 de Dezembro  Lei do Combate ao Branqueamento de Capitais e do Financiamento ao Terrorismo, que revogou a Lei n. 12/10 de 9 de Julho, com o mesmo nome, que dentre outros aspectos, estabelece as obrigaes gerais a que se encontram vinculadas as Entidades sujeitas, dos sectores financeiro e no financeiro. Adicionalmente, foi aprovado e publicado o Decreto Presidencial n. 35/11 de 15 de Fevereiro, que institucionalizou a Unidade de Informao Financeira (UIF), organismo que tem como objectivo a recolha, anlise, incluindo, sempre que necessrio, a solicitao de informaes adicionais a instituies externas, bem como a disseminao aos rgos policiais e judiciais de operaes suspeitas de Branqueamento de Capitais e de Financiamento ao Terrorismo. Na mesma esteira, o Banco Nacional de Angola, na qualidade de garante da estabilidade do sistema financeiro, e em linha com a Lei a que me venho referindo, aprovou um conjunto de normativos regulamentares, com o objectivo de conferir maior solidez e eficincia  actividade das instituies financeiras sob sua superviso nas tarefas de Preveno e combate aos crimes de BC e FT. Com as referidas medidas, particularmente as de carcter preventivo, auguramos trazer benefcios para o sistema financeiro em particular e para o Pas em geral, que se traduzam, entre outros, na reduo do crime de branqueamento de capitais, na garantia da estabilidade das instituies financeiras e num contributo significativo para o desenvolvimento econmico com o consequente fortalecimento da imagem das instituies nacionais, quer no plano interno como externo. Portanto, no temos dvidas em referir que o nosso Pas est comprometido e as autoridades engajadas, na observncia dos padres de Combate ao Branqueamento de Capitais e do Financiamento ao Terrorismo, que resultam essencialmente das Politicas e Recomendaes emanadas pelo Grupo de Aco Financeira (GAFI) nesta matria. Tal desiderato, no depende apenas, nem da existncia de legislao aplicvel, nem do BNA, enquanto autoridade de superviso que vela pelo efectivo cumprimento das disposies legais e regulamentares aplicveis ao sistema financeiro sob sua superviso. Jogam aqui um papel fundamental os players do sistema, os trabalhadores das instituies financeiras, na medida em que so eles que, em primeira instncia tm que garantir o cumprimento das normas. Por esse facto, revela-se fundamental investir fortemente no desenvolvimento e implementao de polticas, processos e sistemas de controlo em matria de avaliao e gesto do risco e na formao dos trabalhadores, para que tudo conjugado possa redundar numa monitorizao eficiente dos clientes e das transaces, visando mitigar os riscos de Branqueamento de Capitais e Financiamento do Terrorismo em cada instituio financeira. Esta necessidade de investimento adquire particular importncia no caso das instituies financeiras no bancrias, como  o caso de casas de cmbio e dos prestadores de servios de remessas, devido a natureza do seu negcio envolver um elevado volume de transaces em numerrio e o carcter ocasional das mesmas, tornar tais instituies, particularmente vulnerveis  utilizao por pessoas ou entidades envolvidas em actividades criminosas. De facto apenas atravs da adopo de polticas, processos e mecanismos de controlo adequados  natureza e especificidade do comrcio de cmbios e de remessa de valores, ser possvel mitigar este risco potencial a que esto expostas estas actividades.  neste mbito que se insere este WorkShop, durante o qual teremos a oportunidade de ouvir renomados especialistas nacionais e estrangeiros que iro partilhar connosco os seus conhecimentos neste domnio, num processo que esperamos seja eminentemente formativo, mas tambm de troca de experincias entre as instituies. Com efeito, durante algumas horas iremos ouvir falar de temas como o quadro legislativo e regulamentar, o papel das instituies financeiras e do regulador, as tipologias de operaes suspeitas, respectivo sigilo bancrio e dever de comunicao, bem como a perspectiva dos banqueiros e dos auditores externos sobre a matria, cujo interesse e actualidade, estamos certos, ir despertar o interesse de todos e estimular uma forte participao e interaco. Esperando pois com esta iniciativa contribuir para que os trabalhadores das instituies financeiras aqui presentes, possam recolher os ensinamentos que contribuam para a consolidao do processo de adequao em curso, declaro aberto os trabalhos deste worshop sobre o combate ao branqueamento de capitais e financiamento do terrorismo. Title: nterveno de Abertura do Governador Manuel Antnio Tiago Dias, no I Frum de Garantia e Crdito, promovido pelo Fundo de Garantia de Crdito
text: Opening Speech by Governor Manuel Antonio Tiago Dias, at the Io Guarantee and Credit Forum, promoted by the Credit Guarantee Fund Ladies and Gentlemen. Every protocol observed. Welcome to the Coin Museum. It is a great honor for us to host the Io Guarantee and Credit Forum. I would also like to take this opportunity to thank the Board of Directors of the Credit Guarantee Fund for the invitation made, as well as to congratulate those who directly or indirectly participated in the organization of this important event, which adds a lot to the creation of synergies, aiming to strengthen the national financial system and, consequently, to relaunch the participation of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in the productive sector. Thus, I note with satisfaction that the Forum is being witnessed by several individuals representing Banking and Non-Banking Financial Institutions (IFB and IFNB), as well as the productive business segment, academics and other entities with an interest in the subject, which, naturally, allows me to have good debates in the scheduled panels and excellent moments of sharing experience focused on the dissemination of good practices. Ladies and Gentlemen, Due to its relevance, we believe that the holding of this Forum should be institutionalized so that it can be a true platform for consultation and balance of the FGC's interventions and actions in the national financial system. In fact, there has long been a need for a space of this kind that would be able to bring together the IFNB, promoters and specialists to reflect together on the mechanisms for guaranteeing the granting of credit in force in our country. In addition, we understand that the realization of this initiative is an opportunity to disseminate the lines of financing aimed at promoting the national process, as well as the ongoing anchor programs, with emphasis on Notice No. 10/22, PRODESI, the Commercial Agriculture Development Program (PDAC), the National Production Promotion Plans (Grains, Fisheries and Livestock), among other initiatives designed by the Angolan State and which have the partnership. international agencies. It is important to underline that, in economies like ours, which seek to strengthen the business sector and the diversification of production, Financial Institutions, such as the Credit Guarantee Fund, have the mission of facilitating access to bank credit through public guarantee mechanisms. In this way, the action of the FGC constitutes a legal and constitutional imperative, because it represents the interests of the Angolan State in the promotion and protection of a business body made up essentially of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, whose performance is indispensable for the economic growth and sustainable development of our country. For this reason, the National Bank of Angola will continue to provide full support to Financial Institutions that, at the different levels of intervention, contribute to the creation of a good business environment and the maintenance of trust between the banking and the business sector. In fact, the BNA, as the regulatory body of the Financial System, reaffirms its commitment to continue to adopt legal instruments that meet the expectations of economic agents, such as Notice No. 10/22. The central idea is to make Notice No. 10/22, while it is in force, an instrument in and in dialogue with the new dynamics and trends of entrepreneurship, where all strata of the economically active population are represented. Dear guests, In this way, we warmly welcome the holding of this First Forum as a great contribution that the FGC makes to the economy and the development of the Angolan financial system, so that businessmen, entrepreneurs and other citizens know the structuring programs designed by the Angolan State in the context of promotion and dynamization of national production. Such initiatives contribute to our country achieving ambitious goals committed to improving the quality of life of populations, based on the innovation of jobs and the guarantee of food security that we so desire. These objectives are within the reach of our country's economic potential, provided that the beneficiaries of the financing and public guarantees apply the funds for the purposes for which they were granted. Also reporting on the measures to stimulate the economy and the productive sector in particular, it is worth emphasizing that, under Notice No. 10/22, a total of 752 projects were financed in August this year, whose financing corresponds to 1.06 billion Kwanzas, representing 16.49% of the overall bank credit portfolio and 71.18% of the credit portfolio specifically allocated to the real sector of the economy. Overall, these investments generated relevant social benefits such as the creation of 43,882 jobs, with emphasis on the agricultural, livestock and manufacturing sectors. These results allow us to envision a promising future, because, with a greater combination of synergies between the various actors that intervene in the financing of the business sector, we will be able to achieve successes in this campaign in the medium term aimed at achieving a sustained growth of our economy With these words, I declare open the Io GUARANTEE AND CREDIT FORUM. Thank you very much for your attention. Published In: Oct. 5, 2023

Title: Interveno de Boas-vindas do Senhor Governador Manuel Tiago Dias, no Frum Sobre Sustentabilidade no Sistema Financeiro Angolano
text: Welcome Speech by Governor Manuel Tiago Dias, at the Forum on Sustainability in the Angolan Financial System His Excellency Jose de Lima Massano, Minister of State for Economic Coordination. Ladies and Gentlemen Members of the Angolan Executive, Madam President-in-Office of CMC and President of ARSEG, our partners in the Board of Supervisors of the Angoli Financial System Organization of this great event, Members of the Management Bodies of BNA, ARSEG and CMC; Ladies and Gentlemen Presidents of the Management Bodies of Financial Institutions supervised by BNA, ARSEG and CMC, Ladies and Gentlemen Representatives of the Institutions invited to this Forum, Ladies and Gentlemen. In our country, this year, the time of cacimbo was extended until the month of September, not having ceased in the month of August, as would be expected. Today, in plenc November, we experienced rainfall similar to that of April. These are just two examples of the climate changes we have been experiencing. Facts that ask us, about what else is to come and what does this mean or could mean for our financial system? The adoption of sustainable criteria regarding Environmental, Social and Governance - ESG or ESG issues thus becomes a necessary condition to mitigate the risks associated with climate change, as well as to strengthen social responsibility and corporate governance. ESG practices, whose primary objective is to prevent environmental damage, have been expanding in the face of the need to reconcile the development of sustainability, a concern that is not recent and that is beginning to gain more and more strength with the holding of the "Stockholm Conference". Thus, in recent years, several international bodies, governments and supervisors have devoted greater and special attention to environmental policies, in the field of governance, thus developing a set of rules, principles and guidelines that define and guide their performance in the field of risk management policy design in the most varied climate scenarios. In this regard, the concept of Sustainability in the Angolan Financial System emerged in January 2022, when the Board of Supervisors of the Angolan Financial System (CSSF), defined Sustainability as one of the pillars of its Strategic Plan 2022-2023. The CSSF initiative was driven by the commitments made by Angola with the signing of the Paris Agreements and the United Nations Agenda for 2 impose greater intervention by regulators of the financial system, in order to accelerate the transition to a low-carbon economy, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, as well as limit the increase in the earth's temperature to 1.5. C by 2030, through targeted financing. Thus, in December 2022, the CSSF carried out a diagnosis to assess the level of maturity on adherence to environmental principles and criteria, on governance by financial institutions operating in the Angolan market, in a context where there is no specific legislation on the matter. The diagnosis carried out showed that the Angolan financial system is at an embryonic stage in relation to these matters. As a critical factor for the successful implementation of the ESG agenda in the Angolan financial system, the need to ensure a consensual action by the 3 regulators, at the level of the CSSF, with the aim of deepening knowledge about the impact of socio-environmental risks in the different sectors, promoting their mitigation and ensuring the resilience and sustainability of the Angolan Financial System, in line with the initiatives developed by the State and the best international ones. In this sense, in September of this year, the Council of Supervisors of the Financial System recommended to financial institutions the gradual adoption of the Prim Sustainability of the Angolan Financial System, an instrument that represents the initial approach of the regulators of the national financial system, for the development of environmental, social and governance policies, complying with sustainability criteria. Ladies and Gentlemen, Let me share some of the actions that the National Bank of Angola is implementing in particular to prepare the banking system for sustainable finance best practices. As priorities of the BNA's strategy, as a macroprudential authority, is the need to ensure that the entities under its supervision provide knowledge about the risks resulting from environmental, social and governance factors, as well as the transmission mechanisms and how to impact business. In this sense, the BNA has privileged cooperation with international organizations, and its process of joining NetWork for Greening the / System - NGFS is underway. This multilateral institution comprises 114 central banks and aims to help strengthen the global response needed to achieve the objectives of the Paris agreement and strengthen the role of the financial system in risk management and capital mobilization for green and low-income investments. In addition, the National Bank of Angola is now part of the Basel Consultation Group, a body of the Bank for International Settlements, where central banks aim to outline, among others, how the global banking system should manage climate risk. The interaction with multilateral institutions will also allow the National Bank of Angola to prepare itself, as a monetary and exchange authority, to understand how climate change has an impact on the economy, from the perspective of demand and supply. In this way, we will be able to adapt our econometric and policy models to better support our policy decisions. We are also aware that, as an institution, we must adopt sustainability practices. To this end, we have adopted an internal approach to sustainability that includes, among others, measures to reduce the BNA's carbon footprint by including sustainability criteria in our projects and supplier relationships, adopting the best corporate governance practices, supporting social causes and ensuring gender equality. Excellencies Ladies and Gentlemen, The financial system faces increasingly complex challenges, making it necessary to move from intention to action, accelerating the transition and implementing ESG criteria. It is with great pleasure that I have the honour to welcome everyone here, hoping that the approaches and experiences that will be presented to us will be able to find ways and solutions for the implementation of the best sustainability practices in the Angolan financial system. Thank you all very much and, with your permission, I invite His Excellency Jose de Lima Massano, Minister of State for Economic Coordination, to the opening speech of the Forum on Sustainability in the Angolan Financial System - Challenges and Opportunities. Published In: Nov. 30, 2023

Title: Interveno de Abertura do Governador Manuel Tiago Dias, no XII Frum Economia e Finanas, alusivo ao 25. Aniversrio da ABANC
text: Opening Speech by Governor Manuel Tiago Dias, at the XII Economy and Finance Forum, alluding to the 25th Anniversary of ABANC Ex.mo Mr. Mario Ferreira do Nascimento, President of the Board of the Angolan Association of Banks (ABANC), Secretaries of State for Finance and Treasury and Economy, Ms. Nadia Pinto, Executive Director of the Capital Markets Commission (CMC), Ladies and Gentlemen Presidents of the Administration and Management Bodies of Commercial Banks, Ladies and Gentlemen Representatives of the Distinguished Non-Banking Financial Institutions, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, I would like to begin by thanking you for inviting me to deliver the opening speech of this Economy and Finance Forum, organized by the Ang Banks Association (ABANC). I would like to take this opportunity to congratulate the organization on the celebration of its 25th anniversary and also on the holding of this great event, which has already become a tradition in our financial system. The theme of economic diversification and financial markets is not a new approach, but it remains current and presents challenges. Despite the above, there is still a long way to go. The debates we will have will allow us to understand the importance of public policies and the Indian market to achieve the diversification of the economy, and to assess the challenges and prospects. It is clear that dependence on the oil sector makes our economy vulnerable to fluctuations in the price of oil on the international market and to shocks The latest crises in this sector have clearly shown that economic diversification is the way forward to build a balanced economy and economic diversification involves leveraging other sectors of activity, that lack financing from the financial system. It is indisputable that a robust financial system, with sound banks, adequate financial regulation and access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises are allies in the implementation of the diversification process. The BNA is no stranger to this objective, since, without a doubt, this paradigm shift will have a positive impact on monetary policy and, consequently, on the prices of goods and services. It is in this sense that we have sought to support the different programs that aim to boost the diversification of our economy, through guidelines and financial policies that affect the availability of credit and investments in various sectors of the economy. In this area, allow me to highlight some figures, in the framework of Notice No. 10/2023, of April 6, which signal that it has had a significant impact on the economy. Since its implementation, until October of this year, more than billions of Kwanzas have been made available in credit projects contracted by commercial banks, which corresponds to 16.36% of the overall bank credit portfolio and 77.95% of the credit portfolio allocated to the real sector of the economy, with the sectors of manufacturing, agriculture, animal production, hunting, foresting and fishing. The data available to date indicate that, still within the scope of this Call, more than 46,061 jobs have been created, and in terms of scope, the financed LCAs have already been allocated in about 17 provinces. At the same time, it is appropriate to contribute directly to the realization of the "dream of owning a home and boost the real estate sector", the National Bank of Angola published Notice No. 09/2022, of 6 April, on the special regime for housing and construction credit, having subsequently revised the aforementioned regulation and published it No. 09/2023, of 3 August, in view of the constraints identified, as well as the different social and administrative changes. Likewise, the National Bank of Angola has made efforts to create a payment ecosystem conducive to innovation, competition and diversification. In context, the publication of Law No. 40/20, of 16 December - Angolan Payment System Law, which aimed to amend and modernize the legal framework of Angola's Payments, with the aim of promoting more modern payment systems and services, efficient, safe and inclusive. Alongside the publication of the Ombudsman, the introduction of in-depth regulatory reforms at the level of the payment system, making the rules of operation of payment services more consistent. It is also important to highlight the role of the Innovation Laboratory of the Payment System of Angola, LISPA, in promoting innovation, enhancing the supply of financial services and boosting financial and social inclusion. I also highlight the implementation of the Instant Payment System and Payment Arrangement I\ will allow immediate transfers, with the use of digital wallets to make mobile payments and remittances of values. However, the representativeness of the informal sector, low levels of literacy and financial inclusion are major challenges for the diversification and development of the financial system. Despite the programs already carried out, we recognize that there is a long way to go to achieve the depth of the financial system, economic diversification and sustained growth. For this reason, the Coordination Committee of the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion was set up, through Presidential Order No. 201/23, of 25 August brings together the main actors in society in the same mission and vision, with the purpose of increasing the levels of access of the population and financial products and services, financing the economy, expansion of economic activity, reduction of social inequalities and improvement of the well-being of the population The National Bank of Angola will continue to provide full support to financial institutions that, at different levels of intervention, contribute to the creation of a business environment and the maintenance of confidence between the banks and the business sector for investment in the non-oil productive sector. With these words, I declare open the XII Economy and Finance Forum, under the theme of "Economic Diversification and Financial Markets". Thank you very much for your attention. Published In: Dec 5, 2023

Title: Interveno do Governador Manuel Tiago Dias, na 3. edio do Frum Banca e Seguros, promovido pela AJECO
text: Speech by Governor Manuel Tiago Dias, at the 3rd edition of the Banking and Insurance Forum, promoted by AJECO Ex.mo Mr. Joao Jose Joaquim, President of the Board of the Association of Economic Journalists of Angola - AJECO, Ex.mo Mr. Jesus Manuel Teixeira, Executive Director of the Angolan Insurance Regulation and Supervision Agency (ARSEG), Ladies and Gentlemen Representatives of the Distinguished Financial Institutions and the Media, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and gentlemen. It was with great appreciation that I received the invitation from AJECO to deliver the opening speech of the 3.the edition of the Banking and Insurance Forum, which, this year, is held under the motto: "The importance of Agricultural Credit and Insurance for the Growth of the National Productive Sector". I begin, in the first place, by underlining the unequivocal relevance of the role of the journalistic class in the construction of well-informed and formed societies, through d; dissemination of information in an accurate and truthful way, for the construction of positive values that promote cultural and socio-economic development. Allow me to praise the organization of this event, which deigned to bring to reflection this theme of capital importance, since agriculture continues to play a crucial role in society and the economy, as it is the source of most of the food that man consumes and of raw materials essential to the functioning of various industries. In our society, despite the significant advances made to date, the promotion of the agriculture sector is still marked by numerous challenges, and there is therefore room for the formulation of strategies that stimulate sustainable growth, aiming to become the main source to meet national demand ensure the long-awaited food security of our country, as enshrined in the National Development Plan 2023 - 2027. It should be noted that, for the National Bank of Angola, it is important to sustain the productive sector in its entirety, but especially in the agricultural sector, which guarantees a greater domestic supply of food, which by the nature of our economy, according to data from the National Institute of Statistics (INE), account for 54.42% of the representative basket of consumption of Angolan families and in recent times has contributed, on average, with about 65% in the National Consumer Price Index. Ladies and Gentlemen, The growth of the agricultural sector may contribute to facilitating the operationalization of the main mission of the National Bank of Angola, which is to ensure price stability in the economy, with a view to preserving the value of the national currency. Thus, it is essential to recognize that the impetus of the agricultural sector involves the enhancement of credit to the economy, which should facilitate farmers' access to surplus funds deposited in commercial banks, in order to start, develop, modernize their activity and increase their productivity and competitiveness. In this area, let me highlight some success stories, resulting from the implementation of Notice No. 10/2022, which allowed the agriculture sector to benefit from growing credit, within the framework of promoting the diversification of the Angolan real economy and, in this way, reducing excessive dependence on the import of goods and s contribute to the sustainability of the country's external accounts. The number of credit concessions to the agricultural sector went from 216 credits disbursed in 2020, valued at 154.56 billion Kwanzas to 377 credits in October 2023, corresponding to around 550.06 billion Kwanzas, which signals that this has had a significant impact on credit for the sector of the economy. The weight of the agricultural sector in the total stock of credit to the economy went from 6.26% in 2020 to 8.61% in 2022, and as for its weight in the structure of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP), it went from 7.8% in 2020 to 9.1% in 2022. Thus, in view of the resources destined to leverage the agricultural sector, 24 419 jobs were created (direct work in this sector. Ladies and Gentlemen, National production is still insufficient to cover the food needs of our country's population, estimated at 33,086,278 in 2022 and which has an average annual growth rate of around 3%. The deficit in domestic food supply has been covered using food imports, which in 2022 accounted for US2,889.64 million, a situation that has been unsustainable, especially in periods of falling foreign exchange availability. In this regard, it is recommended that the national economy be continuously strived to achieve effective diversification, with a special focus on the primary sector. The need for financing to diversify the economy, particularly in the agricultural sector, is immense, but it should not be overlooked that it is a sector subject to risks, especially linked to climatic conditions, which currently constitute serious obstacles to greater credit concession. In this context, I cannot fail to point out the importance of agricultural insurance in order to dilute the risks associated with the activity of the sector itself, as well as for commercial banks, which must always grant credit responsibly, appearing as a shield against climatic uncertainties, natural adversities and any shock that threatens farmers' incomes. In order to achieve this purpose in our economy, we have to highlight some initiatives, such as the signing of the Angolan Executive Cooperation Agreement and International Financial Cooperation (IFC), with the aim of preparing the conditions for the effective implementation of agricultural credit. On the other hand, it is important to mention that the existence of other instruments such as the granting of public guarantees to national producers, which may be complemented with partial guarantees, made available by other institutions that want to participate, represents a great window for the dynamization of agricultural credit. It should be noted that, in this direction, an insurance company in the market recently signed a memorandum of understanding with the Credit Guarantee Fund. It is important to note that a good agricultural credit system, aligned with insurance and guarantees, will make it possible to put the farmer more focused on productive activity and the very precise Angolan economy, thus benefiting not only the producer and the insurance companies, but, above all, society and the economy in general. However, let me say that the beneficiaries of agricultural credit are faced with an imperative challenge, which consists of the ability to repay the contracted credit, through the profitability of the project, which suggests that the producer should structure viable and sustainable projects, and get into debt to the limit of his ability to repay. Ladies and Gentlemen, The National Bank of Angola, as regulator and supervisor of the banking sector, will continue to provide full support to the main players in this process, which the field of building the regulatory architecture favorable to the granting of credit in a fast and responsible manner, as well as in the flexibility of solutions that contribute to strengthening the national productive fabric, in a more robust and sustainable way. I conclude by expressing my hope that at the end of this edition we can come out better informed and enriched about the challenges and paths to be followed in the field of agricultural financing, and I take this opportunity to urge media professionals to continue to exercise their role of intermediation between actors in the financial system and society in a wise and firm way, with a view to raising the levels of literacy and financial inclusion in our country. With these words I declare open to 3.the edition of the Banking and Insurance Forum, under the theme "The importance of Agricultural Credit and Insurance for the Growth of the National Productive Sect." Thank you very much for your attention. Published In: Dec 8, 2023

text: Public Interventions Address of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the opening of the third forum on The Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the opening of the third forum on Bank Mr. alvaro Augusto Paixao Junior, Secretary of State for Commerce, Mr. Ricardo Viegas D Abreu, Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Your Excellesee, Mr. Carlos Rosado de Carvalho, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and gentlemen, I would like to begin by thanking the invitation made to the National Bank of Angola to forum on the new exchange rate regulation applicable to the Oil. It is well known that until the entry into force of Law 2/12 of 13 January, the operating companies benefited from a special exchange rate regime, enshrined in each decree granting rights for research, evaluation, development and production of oil and natural gas. With the new law, the practices exchange rates in the sector and harmonizes the exchange rate regime in the country, competing for a more effective central bank's share as a foreign exchange authority of the Republic of Angola. The impact of the operationalisation of the new scheme will be at first at the level of the flow and of the monetary stock. In fact, despite oil production have grown significantly in the last ten years, successive commercial discoveries position the industry in a development phase. Over the next five years, investment budgets make up more than half of the total budget oil concessions and given the still low rate of incorporation, payments will take place primarily abroad. But it is expected, also an impact on the stock of the monetary mass in national currency, given the obligation to settle in kwanzas all expenses incurred in the internal market. This increase in the flow and monetary stock will have an impact on a greater availability of internal resources for financing the diversification of the economy, without worsening the levels of exposure to external vulnerabilities, and it is therefore justified to prudent measures to control financial accounts and financial accounts. balance of payments capital. In any case, a greater capacity for financing the economy, possible by the perforating funds from oil business, it cannot delude authorities, nor commercial banks, and many less economic operators, of a increased access to credit. We also have to overcome some of the relevant limitations of the guarantee system, so we welcome the ongoing initiatives in the field of streamlining the registration of horizontal ownership, as well as the efforts of economic operators to ensure that updating their corporate management and provision models information to society, allowing a better assessment of its potential and valences, but your risk profile. The foreign exchange market will change significantly, becoming more sophisticated and complete. Is the market of interbanking, the emergence of foreign exchange risk protection products, including exchange rate trading future developments, giving greater security to economic actors, those involved in foreign trade operations or in the investment phase with the use of acquisition and installation of equipment using the outside. From an operational point of view, we will have corrected forms of central bank intervention in the exchange rates, no longer the main foreign exchange provider, exercise a strengthened role of monitoring and intervention in the foreign exchange market, with the objective of ensuring price stability and ensuring the good state of external accounts. With the new exchange rate framework, it has already been possible to take another step in simplifying payment on the foreigner. The National Bank of Angola will publish in July new regulations on invisible currents. In essence, and as far as the business sector is concerned, some current transactions will be fully liberalised for all sectors of the economy, i.e. will no longer be subject to prior licensing by the National Bank of Angola. In the guise of for example, we mentioned the payment of insurance and transportation of goods, and equipment rental. As for services contracted abroad, the limit of execution without prior intervention of the BNA from Kz 30 million to Kz 100 million, while for the services arising from contracts whose payers are service providers to the oil sector, duly registered and with a programme contract concluded with the Ministry of Petroleum, the limit becomes Kz 300 million. Still with the sense of simplification of processes, in accordance with the new Notice on invisible the National Bank of Angola ceases to approve or validate the Invoices. That competence falls on commercial banks in the context of the customers and their transactions With increased opening of the current account, bureaucracy is reduced in the execution of payments on the external policy, with a reduction in intermediation costs, although, to this end, complementary rules on consumer protection and protection have to be Taken. Ladies and gentlemen, To ensure the implementation of the law, in its fullty, we will continue the meetings that we have maintained with ACEPA, ACIPA and ABANC, associations that operating companies, service providers and commercial banks. These are meetings that have served to clarify the cloistered law, as well as the aspects inherent in its operationalization. The participation and collaboration of these entities has been instrumental in the successful implementation of the new regime, that we will maintain the same sense of dialogue and concertation for the phases and challenges that follow. In any case, and because the question has been raised with a sense of concern, we reiterate that with the new exchange rate regime is not intended to end with the accounts in foreign currency, nor, nor, convert, coercively, deposits into foreign currency foreign currency, it is sought to ensure that internal transactions the use of Kwanza, currency with mandatory legal course and liberating power unlimited on national territory. This is an absolutely necessary step in consolidating the gains of stability macroeconomic crisis, external vulnerabilities are reduced and maintain a continuously favourable framework for investment and socio-economic development of the country. I end by thanking the Expansion for the invitation and the opportunity to bring to the debate a theme of common interest. Publliicado Em:: 4 Jul. 2012
