Title: Speech at the opening of the 2nd National Treasury Meeting
text: Speech by the Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Antonio Andre Lopes, at the opening of the 2nd National Treasury Meeting Speech by the Deputy Governor of Banco Naciona Angola, Antonio Andre Lopes, at the opening of the 2nd National Treasury Meeting Different authorities, Dear bna officials and technicians, Exmos. Guest Gentlemen, Ladies and gentlemen; We would like to first thank you for your presence at this Second National Meeting Treasury, an event that we intend to reissue every 2 whose first edition we held in the Province of Benguela in 2010 and which aims to bring together only frameworks of our financial system, but also national and foreign entities that are in any way related to the theme, coinciding with the release date of the first currency after the national independence. With this cycle of meetings, we intend to create a privileged space for the exchange of experiences and knowledge about the development of the processes of production of banknotes, including here as it could not fail to be its security elements, but also address other aspects related to the management of current environment in its various aspects, with a view to permanently improving the efficiency of with which this activity is carried out in our Country. Coincidentally, the meeting we started today takes place exactly 1 year after the launch of the new family of kwanza notes and coins, which as we know, took place in February 2013, a process that has been going on with complete reassurance, reason for the which we took the opportunity to thank all the entities public and private authorities, members of civil society and all those who have somehow given their contribution to the success that we can rejoice today. This recognition extends to the Angolan population in general, in the responsible, interested and motivated as he faced, assumed and has participated in all this process. Banknotes and coins, commonly referred to as cash, are in our country, the most widely used means of payment in daily transactions, particularly at the level of small trade, although there is already a growing use of electronic means of payment. Because it is a traditional, popular and very secure means of payment, practical use and confidential and immediate liquidity, cash will continue to play an important role in the functioning of economies. In our country, the BNA also has a strong intervention in all phases of the life cycle of banknotes and currencies comprising the activities of production, emission, distribution, circulation, recirculation, sanitation and destruction. With regard to the activity of sanitation circulation and cash recirculation and not despite some ongoing initiatives, there are still great challenges, as in the countries with greater efficiency in this area, those functions have been transferred to financial institutions, or even to other agents, who on behalf of the central bank, through the process called custody of values, carry out such activities. Therefore, the trend has been for central banks to focus only on production tasks, emission and destruction, which means that, in many countries, after the entry into circulation of the banknotes, only return to the central bank, those whose quality is considered insufficient to recirculate. Operations of physical destruction of genuine banknotes, which are in the conditions are exclusively carried out by central banks. It is therefore appropriate that we deepen the debate on this subject, that you can lead us to involvement of other entities in the activities of distribution, sanitation circulation and recirculation of cash. The first step will be to get the cash sanitation process to start rapidly to be carried out mostly by the institutions financial statements and that deposits at the central bank are massively composed of financial unfit for destruction and that surplus banknotes deposits or intended for recirculation, are duly selected. We must ensure that banknotes returning to the market have adequate conditions from the point of view of view of the integrity of their physical characteristics and so that they can fulfill their function without any reservations. We know that the road is long, so we have to focus, in a first phase, on improving current cash reorganisation processes, at the level of financial institutions, which should be detained with appropriate equipment and mechanisms to this end, in addition to the effort to empower their human resources, with a view to improving knowledge of the safety characteristics of banknotes and ability to lose counterfeit banknotes. Another point that we should mention here and for which we would like to see also attention of all professionals related to the management of the in our country, has to do with the re-introduction into circulation of coins, carried out february 2013, at the time of the introduction of the current family of Kwanza notes and coins. This is another challenge that we have embraced in the sense of standardising the process of training prices in our economy and the allocation of the right change, to in addition to the cost savings resulting from it. The coin must be part of any coherent cash structure circulating in a economy, as it fulfils a specific function in the the means of payment and therefore their circulation is a national imperative, without which we will not achieve the required efficiency conditions, in the the field of monetary circulation. If we do not overcome this challenge, we will continue to bear significant costs with the production and circulation of low-face value banknotes, which could be replaced by coins. Therefore, we must continue the efforts of financial education and identification and introduction of on the market, transactional devices and equipment which goods and services which can be paid to be made exclusively in currencies at the same time to enhance the current levels of circulation and recirculation of this means of payment. Cash, as well as the other available means of payment - cheques and electronic means of payment - must continue to fulfil its specific role, according to the type of transaction for which it is most dedicated, so it becomes necessary to continue the dialogue to identify the mechanisms best suited to their efficient and rational use in Angola. Bearing this in mind, during the event, we will also address the theme of the use of certain cash production, such as polymer, advantages and disadvantages, as well as the conditions that must be met for the adoption of a another type of substrate. Ladies and gentlemen, In the context of our country's socio-economic development, the approach to quality issues the paper and safety characteristics of the banknotes, it is critical and current, given the high level of circulation of banknotes, the inadequate stage of education of the majority of our populations, the least how banknotes are still handled, factors that can facilitate the introduction and circulation of counterfeit banknotes even in urban centers. That is why we are sure that all these themes, inscribed in the programme of this II meeting, will be subject to heated and in-depth discussions during the two days in which we will be gathered here and that the lessons required for the improvement of the processes management of the circulating environment in our country. Finally and as the programme is designed, we will take this opportunity to provide to the leaders and technicians of our Regional Delegations, the opportunity to interact with the various central departments, including those taking part in the management of human resources-related issues, statistical information collection, behavioural supervision and financial education. With these words, I declare the II National Treasury Meeting open. THANK YOU VERY MUCH. Feb. 20. 2014

Senhores Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores; Gostaramos de, em primeiro lugar, agradecer a honra da vossa presena neste II Encontro Nacional de Tesouraria, um evento que pretendemos reeditar de 2 em 2 anos, cuja primeira edio realizamos na Provncia de Benguela no ano de 2010 e que visa reunir no apenas quadros do nosso sistema financeiro, mas tambm entidades nacionais e estrangeiras que de alguma forma estejam relacionados com o tema, fazendo coincidir com a data de lanamento da primeira moeda aps a independncia nacional. Com este ciclo de encontros, pretendemos criar um espao privilegiado para a troca de experincias e conhecimentos sobre o desenvolvimento dos processos de produo de notas, incluindo aqui como no poderia deixar de ser os seus elementos de segurana, mas tambm abordar outros aspectos relacionados com a gesto do meio circulante nas suas diversas vertentes, visando melhorar permanentemente a eficincia com que esta actividade  realizada no nosso Pais. Coincidentemente, o encontro que iniciamos hoje, ocorre exactamente 1 ano aps o lanamento da nova famlia de notas e moedas do Kwanza, que como sabemos, teve lugar em Fevereiro de 2013, um processo que tem decorrido com total tranquilidade, razo pela qual aproveitamos o ensejo para agradecer todas as entidades pblicas e privadas, membros da sociedade civil e todos aqueles que de alguma forma deram a sua contribuio para o sucesso de que nos podemos hoje regozijar. Este reconhecimento  extensivo a populao angolana em geral, pela forma responsvel, interessada e motivada como encarou, assumiu e tem participado em todo este processo. As notas e as moedas metlicas, vulgarmente designadas por numerrio, so no nosso Pas, o meio de pagamento mais utilizado nas transaes dirias, especialmente ao nvel do pequeno comrcio, embora se assista j, a uma crescente utilizao de meios de pagamento eletrnicos. Pelo facto de ser um meio de pagamento tradicional, popular e muito seguro, de utilizao prtica e confidencial e de liquidez imediata, o numerrio continuar a desempenhar um papel relevante no funcionamento das economias. No nosso Pais, o BNA tem ainda uma forte interveno em todas as fases do ciclo de vida das notas e moedas que compreende as actividades de produo, emisso, distribuio, circulao, recirculao, saneamento e destruio. No que se refere a actividade de saneamento circulao e de recirculao do numerrio e no obstante algumas iniciativas em curso, subsistem ainda grandes desafios, uma vez que nos pases com maior eficincia neste domnio, aquelas funes tem sido transferidas para as instituies financeiras bancarias, ou mesmo para outros agentes, que em nome do banco central, atravs do processo denominado de custdia de valores, realizam tais actividades. Portanto, a tendncia, tem sido os bancos centrais concentarem-se apenas nas tarefas de produo, emisso e destruio, o que faz com que, em muitos pases, aps a entrada em circulao das notas, apenas retornem ao banco central, aquelas cuja qualidade seja considerada insuficiente para voltar a circular. As operaes de destruio fsica das notas genunas, que se encontrem nas condies que enunciamos, so exclusivamente desempenhadas pelos bancos centrais. Por isso,  pertinente aprofundarmos o debate em torno deste tema, que possas conduzir-nos proximamente ao envolvimento de outras entidades nas actividades de distribuio, saneamento circulao e recirculao do numerrio. O primeiro passo ser conseguirmos que o processo de saneamento de numerrio comece rapidamente a ser efectuado maioritariamente pelas instituies financeiras bancarias e que os depsitos no banco central sejam massivamente constitudos por notas inaptas destinadas a destruio e que os excedentes de notas aptas para tais depsitos ou ainda destinadas a recirculao, sejam devidamente seleccionados. Temos que garantir que as notas que retornam ao mercado, possuam condies adequadas do ponto de vista da integridade das suas caractersticas fsicas e de segurana, para que possam cumprir a sua funo sem quaisquer reservas. Sabemos que o caminho  longo, por isso temos que nos concentrar, numa primeira fase, na melhoria dos actuais processos de saneamento do numerrio, ao nvel das instituies financeiras bancarias, que se devem doptar de equipamentos e mecanismos adequados ao efeito, para alm do esforo de capacitao dos seus recursos humanos, visando melhorar o conhecimento das caractersticas de segurana das notas e da capacidade de despiste de notas contrafeitas. Um outro aspecto que nos compete referir aqui e para o qual gostaramos de ver igualmente viradas as atenes de todos os profissionais ligados a gesto do numerrio no nosso Pais, tem a ver com a reintroduo em circulao das moedas metlicas, efectuada em Fevereiro de 2013, por altura da introduo da actual famlia de notas e moedas do Kwanza. Trata-se de mais um desafio que abraamos, no sentido da normalizao do processo de formao de preos na nossa economia e de atribuio do troco certo, para alm da economia de custos que resulta do mesmo. A moeda metlica deve fazer parte de qualquer estrutura coerente de numerrio que circule numa economia, na medida em que cumpre uma funo especfica no conjunto dos meios de pagamento e por isso, a sua circulao  um imperativo nacional, sem o qual no alcanaremos as condies de eficincia requeridas, no domnio da circulao monetria. Se no vencermos esse desafio, continuaremos a suportar custos significativos com a produo e circulao de notas de baixo valor facial, que poderiam perfeitamente ser substitudas por moedas metlicas. Por isso, temos que prosseguir os esforos de educao financeira e de identificao e introduo no mercado, de dispositivos e equipamentos transaccionais que ao disponibilizarem bens e servios cujo pagamento possa ser efectuado exclusivamente com moedas metlicas, permitam ao mesmo tempo potenciar os actuais nveis de circulao e recirculacao desse meio de pagamento. O numerrio, tal como os restantes meios de pagamento disponveis - cheques e meios eletrnicos de pagamento  deve continuar a cumprir o seu papel especifico, de acordo com o tipo de transao para o qual se encontra mais vocacionado, pelo que se torna necessrio prosseguir o dialogo que permita identificar os mecanismos mais adequados a sua utilizao eficiente e racional em Angola. Tendo isso presente, durante o evento, abordaremos tambm a temtica do uso de determinados substractos na produo do numerrio, como  o caso do polmero, suas vantagens e desvantagens, bem como as condies que devem estar reunidas para a adopo dum ou outro tipo de substrato. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, No contexto de desenvolvimento scio-econmico do nosso pas, a abordagem das questes da qualidade do papel e das caractersticas de segurana das notas,  criticas e actual, dado o elevado nvel de circulao de notas, o inadequado estgio de educao financeira da maioria das nossas populaes, a forma menos correcta como as cdulas ainda so manuseadas, factores que podem facilitar a introduo e circulao de notas contrafeitas at mesmo nos centros urbanos. Por isso estamos certos que todos estes temas, inscritos no programa deste II encontro, sero objecto de acesos e profundos debates durante os dois dias em que estaremos aqui reunidos e que se retiraro os ensinamentos requeridos para a melhoria dos processos de gesto do meio circulante no nosso Pais. Finalmente e como o programa des taca, aproveitaremos esta ocasio para proporcionar aos responsveis e tcnicos das nossas Delegaes Regionais, a oportunidade de interagirem com os vrios Departamentos centrais, nomeadamente os que intervm na gesto dos temas relacionados com os Recursos Humanos, recolha de informao estatstica, superviso comportamental e educao financeira. Com estas palavras, declaro aberto o II Encontro Nacional de Tesouraria. MUITO OBRIGADO. Title: Speech at the Abanc Forum
text: Public Interventions Governor's Speech at the Abanc Forum Speech by the Governor at the Abanc Forum Mr. President of ABANC Mr. E.G. members of the Boards of Directors, Directors and Technicians of the BNA and Banking Financial Institutions Distinguished representatives of the Ministries of Economy and Trade and the National Alfandegas Ladies and gentlemen We meet here for a few hours, to talk in detail about the rules regulations that guide, in our country, the operations exchange rates carried out between residents and non-resident foreign exchange companies, with a focus on foreign exchange operations import and export of market-goes, with a view to contributing to their disclosure among all actors involved, in particular financial institutions importers and exporters. In the current context of global economic integration, propitiated by the phenomenon of globalisation, there is an increasing interconnection between countries and resulting in the need for exchange operations on a global scale. These operations, should be carried out responsibly, taking into account the taking into account the high interests of each country, taking into account the impact they have on their respective economies, in particular in the balance of external accounts and in the macroeconomic stability. The Angolan economy, of course, is not outside the rule, as its increasing integration into the global economic and financial context is visible to all and, from 2008, coinciding with the onset of the international financial crisis, we have seen a strong pressure for capital outflows, which has made the problem of export of foreign exchange, would become one of the main concerns of the Executive and the Central bank. If, on the one hand, it is necessary to ensure an adequate flow of foreign exchange in order to cope with the external commitments of the Country, both in terms of the import of goods, such as capital expenditure and the provision of services and transfers of unilateral, on the other hand, the challenge of the accumulation of reserves, in order to preserve the exchange rate stability and sustainability of the the country's external solvency. Until the complete recovery and diversification of the internal economy and the reactivation of a vigorous export sector - outside the the oil sector, enabling the private financial sector to become dominant in the supply of foreign exchange brought by domestic exporters, the State will continue to be the main foreign exchange provider for the economy and the Central Bank the main responsible for recycling it. Bearing in mind this reality, the Executive and the National Bank of Angola, in their robes of currency authority, have been implementing a set of reforms legislative, regulatory and regulatory framework, with the adoption of more for the licensing, registration, monitoring and control of foreign exchange operations, with a view to maintaining exchange rate stability and ensuring the exchange rate sustainable accumulation of reserves. In this context, we would like to highlight: Notice No. 3/2011 of 2 June, which regulates the remittance services of amounts to and from the exterior of the Country; Notice No 9/2011 of 13 October establishing a new regime for issuing activities, acceptance and use of bank cards; Notice No. 01/2012 of 16 January, which regulates the conditions and terms that must comply with entry and exit of foreign currency in the possession of persons residents and non-resident exchange rates; Notice No. 19/2012 of April 19, which defines the modalities of foreign exchange settlement of foreign exchange transactions import and export of goods, thus giving body Presidential Decree No. 265/10 of 26 November, which introduced the procedures administrative procedures to be observed in the licensing of imports, exports and re-export of goods, as well as Law No. 34/11 of 12 December, which was legal system, preventive and repressive measures of combating money laundering and terrorist financing; Specifically on Notice No 19/12, which entered into force on 25 June, defined a set of rules and procedures, on the settlement of foreign exchange transactions of goods, in particular the principles to be taken into account in the act of assessment, documentary requirements and deadlines for regularisation of exchange operations, control measures and the role and responsibilities of the importer or exporterand banking financial institutions. This standard, while maintaining the principle of liberalisation of the execution of foreign exchange operations in goods at the level of banking financial institutions, however, it imposes greater responsibility on all actors in the proceedings, institutions to adopt mechanisms for registering, monitoring and more effective controls, to prevent the undue outflow of resources and to ensure the entry of resources required, arising from the import and export of goods, respectively. In addition to the diplomas to which we refer, we would also like to highlight the Decree Presidential No. 273/11 of 27 October, which introduces greater rigour in the contracting of foreign technical assistance and management services, while safeguarding, among other other, the principles of economic and social policy relating to the protection of the national interest, the promotion of the development of the labour market and the rationalization of the country's foreign exchange resources. Ladies and gentlemen, The challenges ahead, in terms of foreign exchange operations, are immense and require everyone to us, combined efforts, increased efforts and a high sense of responsibility. Banking financial institutions, it imposes the role of intermediaries that is intended, reliable and credible in this process, and should ensure a rigorous monitoring and monitoring of the execution of contracts for foreign exchange transactions. Economic operators are required to be more responsible for complying with the rules, essentially with regard to the assumptions relating to payments imports, which now have new limits. At the institutional level, two IT systems have been developed, the Integrated Foreign Trade, aka SICOEX and the Integrated Operations System Foreign Exchange Rate - SINOC, which will allow better monitoring of import and export operations goods and their exchange settlement, at the exchange and sharing of information between the Ministry of Commerce, the European National Republic of Angola, the National Customs Service, the Commercial Banks and the Official Dispatchers. To discuss these issues, they have joined this initiative of the BNA, in charge of the Ministries of Economy and Trade, as well as the National customs, with whom we hope to share ideas that lead to the clarification of the content of the Diplomas we mentioned. To all those involved in the international trade process in Angola, we have adared in compliance with the strict and scrupulous of the rules emanating by the exchange rate, certain that if we do so, we will jointly work together to consolidate the macroeconomic stability and strengthen the process of insertion in the global economic and financial context. With these words, I declare open the seminar on exchange rules for the import and export of wares. Thank you very much. 24 Oct. 2010
text_original: Home Publicaes e Media Intervenes Pblicas Discurso do Governador no Frum Abanc Discurso do Governador no Frum Abanc Exmo. senhor Presidente da ABANC Exmo.s senhores membros dos Conselhos de Administrao, Directores e Tcnicos do BNA e das Instituies Financeiras bancarias Distintos representantes dos Ministrios da Economia e do Comercio e do Servio Nacional das Alfandegas Minhas senhoras e meus senhores Encontramo-nos aqui reunidos para durante algumas horas, falarmos, detalhadamente, sobre as normas e regulamentos que orientam, no nosso Pas, as operaes cambiais realizadas entre residentes e no residentes cambiais, com foco nas operaes de importao e exportao de mercadoras, visando contribuir para a sua maior divulgao entre todos os agentes envolvidos, particularmente as instituies financeiras bancrias e os importadores e exportadores. No actual contexto de integrao econmica mundial, propiciado pelo fenmeno da globalizao, assiste-se a uma interligao cada vez maior entre pases e mercados, resultando da a necessidade da realizao de operaes cambiais  escala mundial. Estas operaes, devem ser realizadas de forma responsvel, tendo em conta os altos interesses de cada Pas, atendendo ao impacto que tm nas respectivas economias, nomeadamente no equilbrio das contas externas e na estabilidade macro econmica. A economia angolana, como  bvio, no foge  regra, dado que a sua integrao crescente no contexto econmico-financeiro mundial  visvel para todos e, desde 2008, coincidindo com o incio da crise financeira internacional, temos assistido a uma forte presso para a sada de capitais, o que fez com que a problemtica da exportao de divisas, passasse a constituir uma das principais preocupaes do Executivo e do Banco Central. Se por um lado,  necessrio assegurar um fluxo adequado de divisas para fazer face aos compromissos externos do Pais, quer ao nvel da importao de mercadorias, como das despesas de capital e da prestao de servios e ainda das transferncias unilaterais, por outro lado, h que ter presente o desafio da acumulao de reservas, visando preservar a estabilidade cambial e a sustentabilidade da solvabilidade externa do Pais. Enquanto no se verificar o completo relanamento e diversificao da economia interna e a consequente reactivao de um sector exportador vigoroso  fora do mbito petrolfero, que permita ao sector financeiro privado tornar-se dominante na oferta de divisas trazidas pelos exportadores domsticos, o Estado continuar a ser o principal provedor de divisas para a economia e o Banco Central o principal responsvel pela sua reciclagem. Tendo presente tal realidade, o Executivo e o Banco Nacional de Angola, nas suas vestes de autoridade cambial, tm vindo a implementar um conjunto de reformas ao quadro legislativo, normativo e regulamentar, objectivando a adopo de procedimentos mais eficazes para o licenciamento, registo, monitoramento e controlo das operaes cambiais, tendo em vista a manuteno da estabilidade cambial e a garantia do processo de acumulao sustentvel de reservas. Neste mbito, gostaramos de destacar: O Aviso n. 3/2011 de 2 de Junho, que regula os servios de remessas de valores de e para o exterior do Pais; O Aviso n. 9/2011 de 13 de Outubro, que estabelece um novo regime para as actividades de emisso, aceitao e utilizao de cartes bancrios; O Aviso n. 01/2012 de 16 de Janeiro, que regula as condies e os termos que devem obedecer a entrada e sada de moeda estrangeira na posse das pessoas singulares residentes e no residentes cambiais; O Aviso n.19/2012 de 19 de Abril, que define as modalidades de liquidao cambial das operaes de importao e exportao de mercadorias, dando assim corpo ao Decreto Presidencial n. 265/10 de 26 de Novembro, que introduziu os procedimentos administrativos a observar no licenciamento da importao, exportao e reexportao de mercadorias, bem com  Lei n. 34/11 de 12 de Dezembro, que estatuiu no nosso ordenamento jurdico, as medidas preventivas e repressivas de combate ao branqueamento de capitais e do financiamento ao terrorismo; Especificamente sobre o Aviso n. 19/12, que entrou em vigor no passado dia 25 de Junho, foram definidos um conjunto de regras e procedimentos, sobre a liquidao de operaes cambiais de mercadorias, nomeadamente os princpios a ter em conta no acto de liquidao, os requisitos documentais e prazos para regularizao das operaes cambiais, as medidas de controlo e o papel e responsabilidades do importador ou exportador e das instituies financeiras bancrias. Esta norma, no obstante manter o princpio da liberalizao da execuo das operaes cambiais de mercadorias ao nvel das instituies financeiras bancrias, impe, contudo, maior responsabilidade a todos os intervenientes no processo, obrigando as instituies a adoptarem mecanismos de registo, monitoramento e controlo mais eficazes, para prevenir a sada indevida de recursos e garantir a entrada dos recursos requeridos, decorrentes dos processos de importao e exportao de mercadorias, respectivamente. Para alm dos diplomas a que nos referimos, gostaramos de destacar igualmente o Decreto Presidencial N 273/11 de 27 de Outubro, que introduz maior rigor na contratao de servios de assistncia tcnica estrangeira e de gesto, salvaguardando, dentre outros, os princpios da poltica econmica e social relativos  proteco do interesse nacional,  promoo do desenvolvimento do mercado de trabalho e  racionalizao dos recursos cambiais do Pas. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Os desafios que temos pela frente, ao nvel das operaes cambiais, so imensos e exigem de todos ns, esforos conjugados, redobrados e um alto sentido de responsabilidade. s instituies financeiras bancrias, impende o papel de intermedirios que se pretende, fivel e credvel neste processo, devendo assegurar um rigoroso acompanhamento e controlo da execuo dos contratos das operaes cambiais. Aos agentes econmicos,  exigida maior responsabilidade no cumprimento das normas, essencialmente no que refere aos pressupostos relativos aos pagamentos antecipados de importaes, que tm agora novos limites. A nvel institucional, foram desenvolvidos dois sistemas informticos, o Sistema Integrado de Comrcio Externo, vulgo SICOEX e o Sistema Integrado de Operaes Cambiais - SINOC, que permitiro um melhor acompanhamento das operaes de importao e exportao de mercadorias e respectiva liquidao cambial, ao permitirem a troca e partilha de informaes entre o Ministrio do Comrcio, o Banco Nacional de Angola, o Servio Nacional das Alfndegas, os Bancos Comerciais e os Despachantes Oficiais. Para falarmos destes temas, associaram-se a esta iniciativa do BNA, responsveis dos Ministrios da Economia e do Comrcio, bem como do Servio Nacional das Alfandegas, com quem esperamos partilhar ideias que conduzam ao esclarecimento do contedo dos diplomas que mencionamos. A todos intervenientes no processo do comrcio internacional em Angola, auguramos o cumprimento estrito e escrupuloso das normas emanadas pela autoridade cambial, certos de que se assim procedermos, estaremos em conjunto, a colaborar para consolidar a estabilidade macroeconmica e reforar o processo de insero do Pas no contexto econmico-financeiro mundial. Com estas palavras, declaro aberto o seminrio sobre regras cambiais de importao e exportao de mercadorias. Muito obrigado. Title: Speech at the opening of the XVI Forum of Information Systems and Technologies of the Central Banks of the Community of Portuguese Speaking Countries  CPLP
text: Speech by the Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Ricardo Viegas de Abreu, at the opening of the XVI Forum on Information Systems and Technologies of the Central Banks of the Community of Portuguese-speaking Countries - CPLP Speech by the Deputy Governor of Banco Naciona Angola, Ricardo Viegas de Abreu, at the opening of of the XVI Forum on Systems and Technologies of Information from the Central Banks of the Community Portuguese-speaking Countries - CPLP Mr. Deputy Governor of the Bank of Sao Tome and Principe, Exmos. Mr. S Central Bank Administrators present, Mr. President and General Manager of INACOM, Former Regional Delegate of the BNA in Benguela, Exmos. Directors and Deputy Directors of the participating Central Banks, Ladies and gentlemen, My Lords and My Lords, The 16th Forum on Information Systems and Technologies of the Central Banks of the Community Portuguese-speaking Countries - CPLP, in Angola, benguela, is another step towards the search for standards of excellence based on good internationally accepted practices and standards, such as the main challenge that our institutions have taken on for more than a decade and a half. It is well known that assertiveness in the actions of central banks in their respective markets financial resources can be increasingly facilitated with a significant participation in efficient and effective information technology areas, providing resources to enable the provided the necessary information in a timely manner. We hold this Forum every year, being fully aware that resources are always scarce, imposing on us the permanent reflection on the effectiveness of decision-making processes in terms of investments in technologies and the focus on models that objectively allow the assessment of the level of increase in performance of the business according to each "Byte" invested in infrastructure, thus easing the stigma that has connoted the Departments of Technology, more of a cost than a benefit. How can we see the concerns about the mission performance of each of our institutions have led the Forum to address issues of IT governance, security and information management, which a close look at the agenda for this event can confirm. Others such as terrorism, money laundering and and the computer crimes that are increasingly being felt in our societies, make it possible to the need to strengthen the levels of security of information from central banks. Of course, the impact of information technologies on the regulatory process of the financial development, being one of the pillars of economic development societies, imposes a certain urgency in the adoption of a more pragmatic stance on the materialization of the intentions that have been the subject of discussion in this Forum. In this direction we consider it important to include in the agenda a moment of reflection among representatives at the highest level of delegations following a proposal from the Central Bank of Brazil. Our mission could also be facilitated by the development of sectors such as telecommunications, for which institutions have been invited to responsible in Angola for these issues, as well as the one that most directly participates in the operationalization of the SPA - Angola Payment System, interventions for which we ask in advance for your attention. We must point out that in the BNA, we have adopted a comprehensive modernisation programme - PMO, which with sap's solutions as a reference, we assume the challenge of reviewing the application map depending on the evolution of the short- and medium-term objectives. Of about half a hundred projects planned, four are in course, observing criteria of precedence and criticality capable of ensuring the continued development of the programme. We hope that the approximation between the participants, from a linguistic point of view, cultural and technical, is an asset to be exploited by sharing lessons learned, the application of which may be more likely to be successful in relation to pre-designed solutions and not uncommonly unadjusted to our Realities. Finally, I reiterate on behalf of the BNA Board of Directors a good stay in Angola, a happy return to their respective countries. Thank you very much! Publliicado Em:: 12 de may. 2014

Directores e Subdirectores dos Bancos Centrais participantes, Caros colegas, Meus Senhores e minhas Senhores, A realizao do XVI Frum de Sistemas e Tecnologias de Informao dos Bancos Centrais da Comunidade de Pases de Lngua Portuguesa  CPLP, em Angola, Cidade de Benguela, constitui mais um passo com vista na busca de padres de excelncia baseados em boas prticas e standards internacionalmente aceites, como principal desafio que as nossas instituies assumiram h mais de dcada e meia.  consabido que a assertividade na actuao dos Bancos Centrais nos respectivos mercados financeiros pode ser, cada vez mais, facilitada com uma participao eficiente e eficaz das reas de tecnologias de informao, providenciando recursos que permitam a disponibilizao da informao necessria e de modo oportuno. Realizamos anualmente este Frum, tendo plena conscincia de que os recursos so sempre escassos, impondo-nos a reflexo permanente sobre a eficcia dos processos de deciso em termos de investimentos em tecnologias e na aposta em modelos que de forma objectiva permitam a avaliao do nvel de incremento da performance do negcio em funo de cada Byte investido em infra-estruturas, esbatendo-se assim o estigma que tem conotado os Departamentos de Tecnologias, de serem mais um custo do que um benefcio. Como podemos constatar as preocupaes com o desempenho da misso de cada uma das nossas instituies tm levado o Frum a debruar-se sobre questes da Governao de TI, segurana e gesto da informao, o que um olhar atento  agenda para este evento pode confirmar. Outras como o terrorismo, branqueamento de capitais e os crimes informticos que cada vez mais se fazem sentir nas nossas sociedades, tornam imperativo o reforo dos nveis de segurana dos sistemas de informao dos Bancos Centrais. Obviamente que o impacto das tecnologias de Informao sobre o processo de regulao do sistema financeiro, sendo um dos pilares do desenvolvimento econmico das sociedades, impe uma certa urgncia na adopo de uma postura mais pragmtica relativamente  materializao dos intentos que tm sido alvo de discusso neste Frum. Nessa senda consideramos importante incluir na agenda um momento de reflexo entre os representantes ao mais alto nvel das delegaes participantes na sequncia de uma proposta do Banco Central do Brasil. A nossa misso poder ainda ser facilitada com o desenvolvimento de sectores como o das telecomunicaes, facto pelo qual foram convidadas instituies responsveis em Angola por essas temticas, bem como daquela que mais directamente participa na operacionalizao do SPA  Sistema de Pagamentos de Angola, intervenes para as quais solicitamos antecipadamente a vossa ateno. No podemos deixar de assinalar que no BNA, adoptamos um amplo programa de modernizao - PMO, que tendo como referncia as solues da SAP, assumimos o desafio de rever o mapa aplicacional em funo da evoluo dos objectivos a curto e mdio prazos. De cerca de meia centena de projectos previstos, quatro esto em curso, observando critrios de precedncia e criticidade capazes de assegurar o contnuo desenvolvimento do programa. Enaltecemos que a aproximao existente entre os participantes, sob ponto de vista lingustico, cultural e tcnico, constitui uma valia a ser explorada com a partilha das lies aprendidas, cuja aplicao poder ter maior probabilidade de sucesso em relao a solues pr-concebidas e no raras vezes desajustadas s nossas realidades. Reitero, finalmente, em nome do Conselho de Administrao do BNA votos de boa estadia em Angola, augurando um feliz regresso aos respectivos pases. Muito Obrigado! Title: Speech at the closing of the fifth forum on Banking
text: Speech by the Deputy Governor, Dr. Antonio Andre Lopes, at the close of the Conference on Payment Systems Speech by the Deputy Governor, Dr. Antonio Andre Lopes, at the close of the Conference on Payment Systems Dear members of the BNA and IF CA Ladies and gentlemen of the IF Distinguished Directors of the BNA Expensive pre-readers Because payment systems are a reality with increasingly characteristic characteristics of the global ly, setting the same basic needs and objectives, whatever the national reality in question, the BNA organized this conference, focusing on the principles, with which we intend to make available to the relevant information, from other experiences and realities, which allow us to anticipate situations that will be put with the ongoing development in the ANGOLA'S PAYMENT SYSTEM resulting from the growing and unavoidable opening abroad and internationalization of our economy. During this morning we had the opportunity to make direct contact with swift's experience related to the principles of the CPSS-IOSCO (committee for payment and clearing systems) for financial market infrastructures, their respective services related to compliance with these principles and notes on the operational risk and efficiency of the securities market, which very honours us, to the extent that SWIFT belongs to a group of international institutions with a transnational scope and with intervention in the extremely relevant in standardising procedures in the financial sector in general and in the payment sector in particular. The principles for financial market institutions are essential in any payment system, as well as a structural element to ensure compliance with the public interest objectives that the Law of the System of Angola payments defines. In this way, it will be essential that this conference is seen, not as an isolated act, but as a step in the implementation of these principles by national banking financial institutions and payment service providers and payment subsystem operators. At the afternoon session, we received information on two very current issues, although with impacts and distinct practical relevance: Payment services and the virtual currency scheme. The African continent has been the scene of numerous experiences of providing payment services with successful cases that have demonstrated the entire potential of this offer in the path of financial inclusion and bankisation. Between us, after we first addressed the theme in November 2009, when the BNA defined the fundamental premises that should guide the development of this payment service, we have seen some initiatives which, regrettably, have not materialised in the sense of the emergence of mobile payments in Angola. We will probably have been very ambitious in defining those assumptions or we will not have dedicated the efforts required, so that, as for the most part, african countries, we could already have, even if embryonic, a mobile payment service. To address this difficulty, the BNA recently approved a new regulation on payments aimed, among others, at the creation of the regulatory framework conducive to the emergence of supply, within the scope of the payment service when defining the minimum requirements that must be present in the provision of payment services. With this, we hope that the market can rapidly develop solutions in this area, in order to benefits of all. Finally, the information provided on the subject of virtual currency, introduced here by Dr. Rita Bairros do BdP, respects a reality that despite recent, since it appears in 2009, already has a certain impact on payments, and may have significant considerable role it can play in the future, in view of the its advantages over the paradigms it has acted on, that I would like to play out the role it can play in financial inclusion. To this extent, it is necessary that at spa level we are properly informed and attentive to the developments in other geographies, so that they can properly adjusted to our reality, we can, in due course, incorporate them into the national reality. Dear participants of this seminar: The rapid development of information and communication technologies has provided a systematic developments in payment systems, putting us development and updating opportunities, but also threats and the risk of not being make available to our people, the means and instruments latest, modern and robust payment sprees. From the most traditional payment channels to the emerging forms of transactions by mobile terminals and the recent emergence of virtual currency, the need to regulate, prevent and ensure that all these transformations take place in our economy in a smooth and timely manner, are challenges for which we must be able to face and win in order to modernise the SPA. That is why we hope that the information provided in this seminar will contribute to this desired. With these words I end by thanking the prelectores for their valuable contribution, wishing that they have enjoyed a few moments to get to know our beautiful and have a peaceful return to your countries. Thank you very much. Aug. 26. 2014
text_original: Home Publicaes e Media Intervenes Pblicas Discurso do Senhor Vice Governador, Dr. Antnio Andr Lopes, no encerramento da Conferncia sobre Sistemas de Pagamentos Discurso do Senhor Vice Governador, Dr. Antnio Andr Lopes, no encerramento da Conferncia sobre Sistemas de Pagamentos Prezados membros do CA do BNA e das IF Exmos senhores representantes das IF Distintos Directores do BNA Caros prelectores Pelo facto dos sistemas de pagamentos serem uma realidade com caractersticas crescentemente globais, colocando as mesmas necessidades e objectivos de base, seja qual for a realidade nacional em causa, o BNA organizou esta conferncia, com enfoque nos princpios CPSS-IOSCO, com a qual pretendemos disponibilizar informao relevante, proveniente de outras experincias e realidades, que permitam antecipar situaes que se colocaro com o desenvolvimento em curso no SISTEMA DE PAGAMENTOS DE ANGOLA decorrentes da crescente e incontornvel abertura ao exterior e internacionalizao da nossa economia. Durante esta manh, tivemos a oportunidade de tomar contacto directo com a experincia da swift relacionada com os princpios do CPSS-IOSCO ( comit para os sistemas de pagamentos e compensao) para as infra-estruturas do mercado financeiro, respectivos servios relacionados com o cumprimento desses princpios e algumas notas sobre o risco operacional e eficincia do mercado de valores mobilirios, o que muito nos honra, na medida em que a SWIFT pertence a um grupo muito restrito de instituies internacionais com uma abrangncia transnacional e com interveno extremamente relevante na standardizao de procedimentos no sector financeiro em geral e no de pagamentos em particular. Os princpios para as instituies do mercado financeiro so de cumprimento imprescindvel em qualquer sistema de pagamentos, bem como um elemento estrutural para se assegurar o cumprimento dos objectivos de interesse pblico que a Lei do Sistema de Pagamentos de Angola define. Desta forma, ser imprescindvel que esta conferncia seja vista, no como um acto isolado, mas como uma etapa na implementao desses princpios pelasinstituies financeiras bancrias nacionais e pelos prestadores servios de pagamento e operadores de subsistemas de pagamento. Na sesso da tarde, recebemos informao sobre duas questes muito actuais, embora com impactos e relevncia prtica distinta: Os servios de pagamentos mveis e o esquema da moeda virtual. O continente africano tem sido palco de inmeras experincias de prestao de servios de pagamento mveis, com casos de sucesso que tm demonstrado todo o potencial desta oferta no percurso da incluso financeira e da bancarizao. Entre ns, depois de termos abordado pela primeira vez o tema em Novembro de 2009, altura em que o BNA definiu as premissas fundamentais que deveriam orientar o desenvolvimento deste servio de pagamentos, assistimos algumas iniciativas que, lamentavelmente, no se concretizaram no sentido do surgimento dos servios de pagamentos mveis em Angola. Provavelmente, teremos sido muito ambiciosos, na definio daquelas premissas ou no teremos dedicado os esforos requeridos, para que, tal como na maior parte dos pases africanos, pudssemos ter j, ainda que embrionrio, um servio de pagamentos mveis. Para colmatar aquela dificuldade, o BNA aprovou recentemente uma nova regulamentao sobre servios de pagamentos que visou, entre outras, a criao do enquadramento regulatrio propicio ao surgimento de oferta, no mbito do servio de pagamentos mveis, ao termos definido os requisitos mnimos que devem estar presentes na prestao de servios de pagamentos. Com isto, esperamos que o mercado possa rapidamente desenvolver solues neste domnio, para benefcios de todos. Finalmente, a informao proporcionada sobre o tema da moeda virtual, aqui introduzida pela Dra Rita Bairros do BdP, respeita a uma realidade que apesar de recente, j que surge em 2009, tem j um certo impacto nos pagamentos, podendo ter relevncia considervel pelo papel que pode desempenhar no futuro, face as suas vantagens relativamente aos paradigmas actuai, de que destaco o papel que pode desempenhar na incluso financeira. Nesta medida,  necessrio que ao nvel do SPA estejamos devidamente informados e atentos  evoluo em curso noutras geografias, para que devidamente ajustadas  nossa realidade, possamos, em tempo oportuno, incorporlas na realidade nacional. Caros participantes deste seminrio: O rpido desenvolvimento das tecnologias de informao e comunicao, tm proporcionado uma evoluo sistemtica nos sistemas de pagamentos, colocando-nos perante oportunidades de desenvolvimento e actualizao, mas tambm de ameaas e risco de no disponibilizarmos as nossas populaes, os meios e instrumentos de pagamento mais recentes, modernos e robustos. Desde os canais de pagamentos mais tradicionais, s emergentes formas de transaco por terminais mveis e ao surgimento recente da moeda virtual,  necessidade de regular, prevenir e assegurar que todas estas transformaes se processem na nossa economia de forma suave e oportuna, so desafios para os quais temos de ter condio de enfrentar e vencer, em prol da modernizao do SPA. Por isso fazemos votos que a informao disponibilizada neste seminrio passa contribuir para esse desiderato. Com estas palavras termino agradecendo os prelectores pelo contributo valioso, desejando que tenham desfrutado de alguns momentos para conhecer a nossa bela capital e que tenham um regresso tranquilo aos vossos pases. Muito obrigado. text: Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola at the signing ceremony of the bilateral agreement monetary conversion between the National Bank of Angola and the Bank of Namibia Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the signing ceremony of the agreement bilateral monetary conversion between the Bank National Authority of Angola and the Bank of Namibia Excellency Mr. Acting Governor of cunene province, Excellency, Mr. Governor of the Central Bank of Namibia, Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, Brotherhood among our countries is rooted in the history of mankind. From the beginnings of occupation of African lands south of the Sahara by the Bantu peoples, invasion and colonial presence in our territories, the struggle for an end to oppression and achievements by the self-determination and affirmation of our countries as free and independent nations. Therefore, when we establish terms of direct parity between our currencies, not only we facilitate the integration of our communities or the promotion of trade relations between the two countries, but we have fulfilled another stage of the remarkable common path which we have seen tread, deepening now the paths of the economic and social development. The Bilateral Monetary Agreement that we are celebrating today will allow direct exchange between the Kwanza and the Namibian dollar, no longer needed, in transactions the use of currencies not issued by our Central Banks, eliminating one of the constraints that most afflict trade and integration of our fellow citizens residing in border areas. Despite the advanced stage of preparation and willingness of our institutions, there is work to operational organization that needs to be developed in so that these transactions can be carried out with absolute security. Our central banks, banks operating in our countries, as well as the authorized exchange offices, will have to make adjustments to their equipment and train their staff so that they can easily identify the characteristics of the kwanza and namibian dollar banknotes. This work should be completed by 1 January 2015, so that transactions can be occur. Consolidated this important step, we will have debit cards issued by institutions financial statements operating in Namibia and Angola, to be accepted by the automatic payment terminals available in commercial establishments in both countries, thereby causing greater integration between our financial systems. These advances, in addition to facilitating commercial transactions, will contribute to the appreciation of our currencies and boost the emergence of new opportunities for the micro and small-scale businesses, and are also an instrument for support for self-employment and encouraging social inclusion. But it is also necessary that our business community with medium and large initiatives recognize the opportunities for growth that this moment comes to provide, and it is our expectation that with its dynamism are created capital gains for society, with the generation of provision of goods and services with quality and greater accessibility. We are certain that this is just another step in this long common journey, but we are convinced that that we also celebrate the power of unity between peoples of Angola and Namibia. Well, be there! Thank you very much. 22 Sep. 2014

Estes avanos alm de facilitarem as transaces comerciais, vo concorrer para a valorizao das nossas moedas e impulsionar o surgimento de novas oportunidades para os negcios de micro e pequena dimenso, sendo, tambm por isso, um instrumento de apoio ao auto-emprego e de estmulo a incluso social. text: Public Interventions Address of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the launch of the 2014 edition of the study "Banca em Analise" Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the launch of the 2014 edition of study "Banking in Analysis Mr. President of Deloitte Angola, Dr. Rui Santos, Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, On behalf of the National Bank of Angola I would like to thank the invitation addressed to us to participate in this traditional annual meeting and deliver some words related to the banking sector. The Angolan financial system currently has 23 banks and 61 non-financial institutions Bank. At the end of June of the current year, the total assets of the was Kz 7.2 trillion, an increase of 16% compared to the same period last year. In general, the system remains and the average solvency ratio is around 22%, 12 percentage points above the regulation, and the stability of the financial system above of 60%. The growth of the Angolan banking sector has been extended to all the most varied extracts of the population. The banking rate in June 2014 was around 55% of the adult population. On this occasion, I could not fail to welcome and acknowledge the fact that Deloitte has, in fact, put our hands on the challenge launched in the previous edition, in which we would assessment of the quality of banking services in Angola, and we are sure that the observations and recommendations will be the subject of reflection by each of the financial operators. While recognising the effort to improve the quality of services in banking and to be continuous processes, there are signs that should merit our attention as a regulatory body. For example, of the approximately 2000 complaints registered in the first half of 2014, 30% were associated with the issuance and use of electronic payment cards. This resulted in the instruction to commercial banks in order to create areas specific services for permanent customer service users of Cards. Therefore, by January 2015, financial institutions wishing to maintain the issue of electronic payment cards, they must have a call center in Portuguese, available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, which allows treat with greater opportunity any limitations with the use of so important payment instrument. Banks play a decisive role in allocating resources in the economy through financial intermediation. This should take place on the basis of dynamic processes of innovation and differentiation of products and services, depending on the segments of the market and target customers. This will encourage competition in the sector and expanded the offer of competitive financial solutions. The last 10 years have been one of significant transformations for the Angolan economy, in particular for the banking sector. It highlights the stability of the currency, opening of national and foreign banks, accompanied by the adequacy of the internationally accepted standards. In this particular, it is important to consider that the regulatory initiatives that the National Bank of Angola has been adopt, also aim to stimulate the dissemination of products and innovative services under criteria of efficiency, inclusion, safety and balance in relations with the market. On this path, we take the opportunity to confirm that we have recently regulated the issuance of electronics in Angola, allowing payment services to be can also be provided by mobile phone. It's more of a challenge to the system, but clearly another instrument that will put innovation to the financial inclusion in our society. Embracing innovation as a source of competitive differentiation is therefore a strategic decision that should be seen as an opportunity to materialize concepts such as modernity and simplification, faced with new challenges in our market, solutions practical and secure practices that facilitate the lives of businesses and families. Finally, and before an audience of illustrious personalities of the financial industry, could not fail to mention the importance of the support that should continue to be efforts to diversify the economy. We follow with interest the evolution of the credit and we have a notion of the constraints that will still taking place in its concession, but it is also necessary to continue to reveal and even to intensify the capacity to overcome and the commitment to economic development of the country. Despite the growth trajectory of the Angolan banking sector, it still has a level of low financial deepening. The weight of credit to the economy corresponds to about 25.8% of GDP, therefore below the levels that are observed in emerging economies. On the other hand, the credit granted to the economy remains concentrated in non-productive activities or with a reduced impact on economic growth sustainable. The country continues with high rates of import of essential goods that can be produced internally, so the opportunities that the climate macroeconomic stability provides should be better used by all stakeholders in production processes. The development model of banking financial institutions around the business exchange rate has been rapidly depleting and those who want to give sustainability to its financial operation will have to be more capable in the fields of knowledge, risk management and lending to the real sector of economy. I take this opportunity to congratulate Deloitte on the persistence in holding this event which has been asserting itself as a useful and timely forum for debate in banking paths in Angola. I hereby declare closed the 'Banca em Analise'. Thank you very much. 26 Sep. 2014

text: Public Interventions Address of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the close of the III International Forum on Financial Inclusion Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the close of the III forum nternacional on Financial Inclusion Mr. Vice- Governor of Benguela Province, Dr. Gika Manuel, Excellencies Mr. Deputy Governor of the BNA, Dear guests, Ladies and gentlemen, The National Bank of Angola has been holding a cycle of conferences, framed in the festivities of its 38th anniversary, with a view to discussing with society issues of national interest, related to the inclusive development of the financial system Angolan. Today is increasingly recognised, the importance of the role and the contribution that access and the widespread use of financial services have in stimulating financial savings, financing to the economy and, consequently, to reducing inequalities improvement of the well-being of the general population. We are pleased to recognise that economic growth in recent years has had a positive impact on the growth of the Angolan Banking Sector. Total assets of banking today accounts for about 60% of gross domestic product. However, this growth must be continuously an influence on the in the lives of Angolan families. An adequate expansion of the financial inclusion allows for greater mobilisation of savings to support investment and extends the access to financial capital, which is so necessary for the economic and social development. The National Bank of Angola has taken a number of initiatives aimed at the inclusion of financial crisis, associating with the Government's efforts to reduce the poverty in our country. Thus, a proper regulatory framework has been established for microcredit companies and credit unions. In addition, the provision of service by correspondent banking and more recently payment services mobile phones, allowing mobile phones to be carried out banking. These initiatives aim at creating the conditions for increasing financial service offerings to population in a safe and efficient manner. But, I would like to highlight the launch in 2011, in partnership with 10 commercial banks of financial education campaign, which aimed at access to the of the low-income population. This campaign included the launch of two Main: The Bankita Deposit, which allows the opening of an account with the minimum amount of kz 100 and maximum of Kz 100,000 and Bankita A Crescer Savings Account, a long-term account which can be constituted with the minimum amount of Kz 1,000. Also within the scope of this campaign and for those products, the mandatory presentation of the Identity Card for account opening, being the use of any other identification document recognised as valid by the financial institutions themselves. Bankita accounts have been moving upwards. There are many citizens who have stop a bank account and many are the ones who have already 'Bankitas' accounts for regular bank customers. As of 31 August 2014, these access to basic banking services totaled about 288,000. Today, international savings day, the Forum we held sought to address the current situation of the financial inclusion in the country and particularly women, given the women play in the economic security of Angolan families. The information available shows that access to financial services by women is still limited in our country. Although it is estimated that about 50% of angolan adult population has a bank account and that 52% of the population are women, they are holders of only 28.6% of bank accounts active in banking and hold 22.71% of the payment cards issued. As for credit, women represent only 21.26% of the total granted. We want to find ways that can intensify the financial inclusion of citizens and angolan women in particular. As we can see throughout the of this forum, despite the gains already made, efforts to increase access to the population to financial services, should continue for the sake of sustainable and socially inclusive development. We thank for this very part the hospitality of the Government of this beautiful Province, to our speakers for accepted the invitation, as well as the presence and contributions those present that will greatly contribute to the development of our activity and the reach of objectives of financial inclusion. I declare this conference closed. Thank you very much. 3 Nov. 2014

Uma adequada expanso da incluso financeira permite maior mobilizao de poupanas para suporte ao investimento e alarga a base de acesso ao capital financeiro, to necessrio para o desenvolvimento econmico e social. O Banco Nacional de Angola tem tomado um conjunto de iniciativas voltadas para a incluso financeira, associando-se aos esforos do Governo para a reduo da pobreza no nosso Pas. Assim, foi estabelecido um quadro regulamentar prprio para as sociedades de microcrdito e para as cooperativas de crdito. Adicionalmente, foi regulamentada a prestao de servio por correspondentes bancrios e mais recentemente os servios de pagamento mveis, permitindo que por telemvel possam ser realizadas operaes bancrias. Essas iniciativas visam a criao de condies para o aumento de ofertas de servios financeiros  populao de modo seguro e eficiente. Esta campanha incluiu o lanamento de dois produtos principais: O Depsito Bankita, que permite a abertura de conta com o montante mnimo de kz 100 e mximo de Kz 100.000 e a Poupana Bankita  Crescer, uma conta  prazo que pode ser constituda com o montante mnimo de Kz 1.000. Ainda no mbito desta campanha e para os referidos produtos, foi excluda a obrigatoriedade da apresentao do Bilhete de Identidade para abertura de conta, sendo permitida a utilizao de qualquer outro documento de identificao reconhecido como vlido pelas prprias instituies financeiras bancarias. As contas Bankita tm registado um movimento ascendente. Muitos so os cidados que passaram a deter uma conta bancria e muitos so os que transitaram j das contas Bankitas para clientes regulares da banca. Em 31 de Agosto de 2014, estas contas de acesso a servios bancrios bsicos totalizavam cerca de 288 mil. Hoje, dia internacional da Poupana, o Frum que realizamos procurou abordar a situao actual da incluso financeira no Pas e particularmente da Mulher, dado o papel preponderante que as mulheres exercem na segurana econmica das famlias angolanas. A informao disponvel revela que o acesso a servios financeiros pelas mulheres  ainda limitado no nosso Pas. Apesar de se estimar que cerca de 50% da populao adulta angolana tenha conta bancria e que 52% da populao sejam mulheres, elas so titulares de apenas 28,6% das contas bancrias activas na banca e detm 22,71% dos cartes de pagamento emitidos. Quanto ao crdito, as mulheres representam apenas 21,26% do total concedido. Queremos encontrar caminhos que possam intensificar a incluso financeira dos cidados e das mulheres angolanas, em particular. Como podemos constatar ao longo deste frum, pese embora os ganhos j realizados, os esforos no sentido de incrementar o acesso da populao  servios financeiros, devem prosseguir  bem de um desenvolvimento economicamente sustentvel e socialmente inclusivo. Agradecemos, por isso, a hospitalidade do Governo desta bela Provncia, aos nossos palestrantes por terem aceite o convite, bem como a presena e as contribuies dos presentes que em muito contribuiro para o desenvolvimento da nossa actividade e alcance dos objectivos de incluso financeira. text: Public Interventions Address of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the launch of the first banking correspondent service Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the launch of the first banking correspondent Excellency Mr. Vice-President of the Republic, Excellency Mr. Minister of Telecommunications and Information Technology, Worthy Presidents of the Boards of Directors of the National Post and Telegraph Company of Angola and the Angolan Bank of Investments Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen, It is with great satisfaction that we witness today, the launch of the first service of correspondent banking in the country, after the publication in 2012 of specific rules for this segment of financial activity. text: Public Interventions Address of the Governor of the BNA, Jose Pedro de Morais Junior, at the National Public Debt Investment Forum Speech by the Governor of the BNA, Jose Pedro de Morais Junior, at the National Forum of public debt nvestition Mr President of the Capital Markets Commission Mr President of the Board of Directors of BODIVA, Gentlemen Administrators of CMC and BODIVA, Distinguished Guests Ladies and gentlemen, It is with great satisfaction that I participate in this closing act of the 1st National Forum of Investment in Public Debt of Angola, which dealt with issues of the greatest relevance, related to the importance of the Capital Market in the economic development of the country, in particular the functioning of the secondary level of government debt securities. This initiative fills a historical gap in the our macroeconomic coordination process and, therefore, should be applauded by both investors from all financial quarters and by the European National Authority of Angola, in its magna role of liquidity manager. On the one hand, we have the benefits already widely known to investors who access the realization daily use of transactions in the purchase and sale of public securities, with price transparency and deadlines appropriate to your needs to monetize your assets. On the other hand, we reap benefits from a macro- because the secondary market, by allowing the transfer of securities between investors, is without resorting to transactions committed in institutions financial statements, becomes an important ally of the policies allocated to the Central Bank to ensure monetary stability and stimulate growth national savings, and thereby maintain the solvency of financial intermediation in the country. It is not too much to recall the decisive moment that the organisation of national financial systems is to live since the outbreak of the 2008 crisis, in anticipation of the position that the Group of the 20 Most Industrialised Countries should take in view of the approval, in the United States of America, the Law called Dodd-Frank. This law separation of money and capital markets, rehabilitating the principles of the Glass-Steagall, replacing the principles of self-regulation that from the 1990s led to the merger, by means of derivative products, of short-term assets with long-term liabilities of both markets, planting the prudential imbalance, which led to the current international financial and economic crisis. In this context, the financial systems of the most developed countries are called upon to adopt gradually the mechanisms of volcker rule, i.e. the set of rules proposed to President Obama by the Study Group chaired by Paul Volcker, former President on the organisational separation between the financial policy (consisting of secondary currency-recreator banks, i.e. allowed to capture demand deposits) and the non-monetary financial system (consisting of investment banks and other financial intermediaries that are not the creators of secondary currency, i.e. not allowed to collect deposits at the order). We in Angola have had the virtuous patience to observe this international transition scenario of regulatory model, deduring the implementation of the securities and starting prudently by the secondary securities market. government debt securities, in a clear demonstration of our option for a regulatory model capable of preventing risks to investors and the national financial system. I have no doubt that the careful way cmc has developed and structured the capital market, will contribute decisively to the de-entering investments into the hands of few economic agents, making it possible, through of a rapid redevelopment of capital, the realization of a wider range of productive projects, which will therefore contribute to the diversification of and growth of our economy. Expensive participants, In its role as guarantor of price stability and the financial system, the National Angola pays particular attention to the regulation and monitoring of financial markets, in particular the regulation of liquidity levels. To this end, the Central Bank has liquidity regulation instruments in order to maintain this financial indicator at levels compatible with the objectives of economic growth and price stability. On a weekly basis, the BNA makes known its interventions in the financial market through financial regulation of liquidity supported by government bonds, the National Treasury Securities. The BNA's action, in this context, aims, on the one hand, to remove the surpluses that may put into the objectives of price stability and the stability of the financial system, and, on the other hand, provide liquidity to the banking sector, allowing it to operational fluidity and profitability of its asset structures and Swings. Through the public debt market, the BNA ensures the credibility of policy instruments and respective transmission mechanisms, creating an environment conducive to the formation of the interest rate, with transparency and coherence. This is the role that BNA has been playing in the primary public debt market, as an operator of the state, ensuring the placement of the securities issued by the National Treasure. In the operational plan, public debt issues are in the form of instruments dematerialised, as recommended by international good practice, through an institutionalised electronic mechanism, which allows online access, in a non- in-person, to the participating banking financial institutions this market segment. This mechanism ensures the transparency required for the debt issuance process, promotes the the formation of interest rates on public bond issues, and preserves the safeguarding of ownership of securities. In addition, the National Bank of Angola, guarantees the custody of values, through its Central Custody of securities, both for primary government bond issues, as well as subsequent changes in ownership and custody, arising from market transactions carried out through commercial banks. This function guarantees the investor the registration of the respective investments in that market segment, thus allowing the use of them in conditions of adequate operational reliability. All these transactions would not have been possible if the Central Bank had not created technology and regulatory frameworks for the liquidation of transactions in strict compliance with international rules on payment systems, in particular those recommendations of the International Settlement Bank (BIS) and the IOSCO clauses, ensuring the materialization of the "ECP- delivery against payment" principle, as mitigation of liquidity risk. This is the operational costume that The BNA has to offer in this embryonic phase of the launch by Angolan Stock Exchange and Derivatives (BODIVA) of the transactions on the secondary market for Government Debt Securities. I would just like to reaffirm here to the Managers of the Capital Markets Commission and the BODIVA, our commitment to work with you in the development of the internal market for public debt, to ensure the reliability of transactions with government bonds; ensure the formation of a rate curve reflecting market conditions; provide liquidity to securities on the market, and for that to increase the volume of transactions both in the primary market and as well as on the secondary market; and finally, to ensure the functioning of a technological infrastructure and regulatory, liquidity management in line with the internationally recommended standards. Our institutions have the responsibility to work together to create financial instruments that promote financial stability, encourage investment and encourage national savings. We have challenges ahead of us. I declare the National Public Debt Investment Forum closed. Thank you very much. 7 Oct. 2014
text_original: Home Publicaes e Media Intervenes Pblicas Discurso do Senhor Governador do BNA, Jos Pedro de Morais Jnior, no Frum Nacional de Investimento de Dvida Pblica Discurso do Senhor Governador do BNA, Jos Pedro de Morais Jnior, no Frum Nacional de nvestimento de Dvida Pblica Excelentssimo Senhor Presidente da Comisso de Mercado de Capitais Excelentssimo Senhor Presidente do Conselho de Administrao da BODIVA, Senhores Administradores da CMC e da BODIVA, Distintos Convidados Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores,  com grande satisfao que participo deste acto de encerramento do 1 Frum Nacional de Investimento em Dvida Pblica de Angola, que tratou de temas da maior relevncia, relacionados com a importncia do Mercado de Capitais no desenvolvimento econmico do nosso Pas, em particular o funcionamento do mercado secundrio de ttulos de Dvida Pblica. No  demais recordar o momento decisivo que a organizao dos sistemas financeiros nacionais est a viver desde a ecloso da crise de 2008, na expectativa da posio que o Grupo dos 20 Pases mais Industrializados dever assumir face  aprovao, nos Estados Unidos da Amrica, da Lei chamada de Dodd-Frank. Neste contexto, os sistemas financeiros dos pases mais desenvolvidos so chamados a adoptar gradualmente os mecanismos da Volcker Rule, ou seja, o conjunto de regras proposto ao Presidente Obama pelo Grupo de Estudos presidido por Paul Volcker, ex-Presidente do FED, sobre a separao organizativa entre o sistema financeiro monetrio (constitudo pelos bancos criadores de moeda secundria, ou seja autorizados a captar depsitos  ordem) e o sistema financeiro no-monetrio (constitudo pelos bancos de investimentos e outros intermediadores financeiros no criadores de moeda secundria, ou seja, no autorizados a captar depsitos  ordem). Ns em Angola tivemos a pacincia virtuosa de observar esse cenrio internacional de transio do modelo regulatrio, adiando a implementao do mercado secundrio de ttulos e valores mobilirios e iniciando, prudentemente, pelo mercado secundrio de ttulos da dvida pblica, numa demonstrao clara da nossa opo por um modelo regulatrio capaz de prevenir riscos aos investidores e ao prprio sistema financeiro nacional. Caros Participantes, No seu papel de garante da estabilidade de preos e do sistema financeiro, o Banco Nacional de Angola presta uma especial ateno  regulao e monitorizao dos mercados financeiros, em particular a regulao dos nveis de liquidez. text: Speech of the Governor of the BNA, at the inaugural ceremony for the implementation of the Bilateral Monetary conversion between the National Bank of Angola and the Bank of Namibia Speech by the Governor of the BNA at the ceremony implementation of the Bilateral Agreement Monetary Conversion Between the National Bank Angola and the Bank of Namibia Excellency, Governor of the Ohanguena Region Excellency Governor of Cunene Province Excellency, Governor of the Central Bank of Namibia Distinguished Guests Ladies and gentlemen, The excellent economic and trade relations between Angola and Namibia, driven by leaders of Presidents Jose Eduardo dos Santos and Hage Geingob, the start of the implementation of the Bilateral Monetary Conversion Agreement between the European Central Angola and Namibia, which represents a new step in relations, not only between central banks, but above all between the our communities, which see the conditions for the deepening of its trade relations. The Monetary Conversion Agreement will allow direct exchange between the Kwanza and the Namibian Dollar in the bank branches and exchange offices located in the regions of Santa Clara and Oshikango, in a first phase. As mentioned by Governor Ipumbo Shiimi, the result of a high spirit of cooperation between the National Bank of Angola and the Central Bank of Namibia, were operational and regulatory conditions have been created, so that authorised entities can securely to trade the Kwanzas and the Namibian Dollars. We now need to consolidate this step and carry out a permanent monitoring of operations, so that we do not depart from the purposes of the Agreement and we can make it evolve even more. It is also essential that our corporate community with medium and large-scale initiatives to profile the development occasions that this moment comes to offer, and it is our expectation that with its dynamism gains will be conceived for the community, with the generation of jobs and availability of goods and services with quality and greater accessibility. We are aware that this is just another step in this extensive common itinerary, but we are sure that we also celebrate the strength of unity between the peoples of Angola and Namibia. Thank you very much. 19 Jun 2015
