text: Lecture given by the Governor of the BNA under the theme "FINANCIAL LIQUIDITY IN THE BANKING MARKET" Comrades Leaders of the Speciality Committee of the MPLA's Bankers, Lecture given by the Governor of the BNA under the theme "LIQUIDITY FINANCIAL MARKET" Comrades Leaders of the Speciality Committee of the MPLA's Bankers, Expensive participants, I would like to express my gratitude for the honorable invitation to share with you reflections on the relevant theme of Financial Liquidity in the Banking System. I would like to address this Theme, recalling the problems facing economies when allows for excessive liquidity creation in the system banking (as was the case in the 2008 international crisis); to then bring to our reality the lessons of what has happened in the financial markets International. It will be demonstrated that the Operational Framework for the implementation of the monetary policy defined by the Executive conducted by President Jose Eduardo dos Santos, primarily aims at price stability and the promotion of sustained economic growth. As we know, central banks play a key role in implementing monetary policies conditioned to the political and legal system in which they Operate. Central Banks are basically concerned about two aspects of monetary policy: the management and liquidity management. The first involves promoting sustained economic growth in the long term while maintaining the expansion of credit and currency in line with potential product growth. In this chapter, central banks must operate within the limits imposed by international reserves and external debt. In turn, liquidity management, has a shorter horizon, involving the banking system of the currency and the necessary payments from society. In their day-to-day life, banks central authorities, are concerned about developing liquidity management techniques with a view to influencing the growth of currency and credit through interest rates. The problem arises when the system allows Commercial Banks to create a high volume of liquidity - the so-called secondary or book-entry liquidity, created in the banks' books - without central banks having issued ex-ante primary currency which justified such uncontrollable growth of the secondary currency. This secondary liquidity issuing process was at the root of the financial bubble that caused the international crisis in 2008. Its adverse effects are still felt, although attenuated by the increase in the emission of dollars and euros by the central banks of the United States of America and the European Monetary Union, based on the issuance of new securities issued by the their national treasures. The increase in the fiscal deficit forced a severe adjustment of public accounts, with deep cuts in spending and the consequent increase in unemployment. Excess secondary liquidity actually originated from excessively significant credit transactions leveraged by multiple banks (commercial and investment) of the most developed countries, after the repeal, at the end of the last century, of the Glass-Steagall, 1933, provided self-regulation and free flow of capital in the United States, a practice that has spread in the international financial system with the support of international bodies in the defence of the financial neoliberalism (the so-called Washington Consensus). As a result of excessive leverage, a growing bubble has created in the pricing of underlying real estate in credit operations, giving rise to portfolios much higher than the payment capacity of the debtor bank clientele. The most recent effect of leverage, as we know, is that the central banks of the United States and european monetary union had to buy from banks non-unpaid loans, in addition to reducing their basic interest rates to a level of never seen, between zero and a half percent, making room for for the practice of speculative arbitrage transactions, account for the currencies of emerging countries and in development. It is clear that the governments of developed countries have had to submit to their respective applications for authorisation to increase the budgetary ceiling public debt, generating intense political debate among the opposition parliamentary benches situation, as was the case in the United States of America. In summary, the financial aid provided by the central banks of the United States and monetary union European Union to American commercial and investment banks and Europeans, to save them from the financial collapse, turned into public debt, the cost of which will be paid by the taxpayers of those countries, of the current and of the next generation, either by raising taxes or by resuping part of their social benefits. Another damaging effect of the liquidity artificially created on the books of commercial banks was the proliferation of so-called "derivatives"  i.e. "wind roles", without underlying assets, supposedly representative of trading in the futures market of commodities but in fact mere bets on futures indices of various indicators of the speculative financial market. The effect of the inflated prices of these "paper commodities" was transmitted, in the case of futures on oil, for the spot market, the purchase and sale of crude oil, artificially increasing the price of a barrel to up to 156 million dollars in September 2008, but making it then fall to 38 in early 2009, negatively impacting the balance of public finances and that of balance of payments of exporting countries, including Angola. Over the past 7 years, the Group of the 20 most industrialised countries has been testing measures to put an end to this never-ending crisis by taking the U.S. with the Volcker Plan and the Dodd-Frank Act to at least prevent investment banks and continue to practice promiscuous leverage of long-term credits backed by short-term deposits. In the field of oil prices, however, the clouds of uncertainty, aggravated by by the winds of global geopolitics, coming from both the unexpected change in U.S. strategy in exploiting its domestic shale oil reserves, possible agreement between the US and Iran on issues related to the through which a future lifting of sanctions that still relate to the iranian oil exports. As a result, at the end of 2014 oil prices fell again to a sharp drop in about 45 -- after they have remained on average 107 in 2013 - forcing Angola to quickly adjust the 2015 OGE to a more exchange and tax revenues. In this new scenario of limitations on the performance of the national economy, one of the consequences is the preference of national banks for the increase in resources in their treasuries, leading them to keep their assets fully available or in investments risk-free short-term (such as Treasury Bills), preventing them from adjusting quickly to a possible new scenario in terms of higher rates interest and exchange rate increases. However, the experience of the management of macroeconomic policy accumulated by the Executive in the periods of oil price volatility in recent years. 10 years has taught us the good way of prudence and fiscal austerity. For this reason, we no longer favour market-focused policy instruments short-term financial growth, which are not committed to the growth of of the real product, and we started to use the coordinated management of fiscal, monetary and foreign exchange policies to achieve macroeconomic objectives consistent with the maintaining a level of economic activity that does not secondary the principles of Transparency and Fiscal Responsibility. In this context, the Executive proposes to ensure that inflation is controld at a low and sustainable (the revised objective of macroeconomic programming is to 10.4% in December 2015), as well as maintaining the level of Net International Reserves equivalent to 6 months of imports and continue the efforts to diversify the economy, with a view to gradually reducing dependence on the economy to the oil sector. In practical terms, in compliance with the macroeconomic programming approved by the Economic Commission of the Council of Ministers, the Ministry of Finance and the management of the liquidity of the national currency flows resulting from the payments of the public expenditure, ensuring that the implementation of the OGE does not take place with the issuance of currency in the void, which would make the primary liquidity in the economy and consequently the means of payment. To this end, the National Bank of Angola has established, since the beginning of the year, a restrictive monetary policy, with the main objective of promoting price stability. The monetary policy instruments you are using to control the liquidity of the banking system are: (i) interest rates, (ii) the level of deposits that banks are required to make with the BNA, (iii) the sale of public debt titles from its own portfolio in exchange for liquidity and (iv) the sale of foreign currency currencies. For example, earlier this year, commercial banks had to set up reserves in national level, with the National Bank of Angola, equivalent to 15% of its customers' deposits. From 1 July, they will have to constitute 25%. This increase in amount of deposits that commercial banks have to set up together with the BNA, is designed to reduce its capacity to increase the amount of currency to be circulated in the economy. The current course of monetary policy is consistent inflation dynamics in the first half of the year on 31 May 2015 recorded a level of 8.86% (in the 12-month period) against 7.48% in December 2014 (for the same period). In addition to price stability, the National Bank of Angola is also responsible for managing external availability of the country. I am referring, in particular, to management of international reserves denominated in foreign currency. The change in the balance of international foreign exchange reserves is determined by the effect of of the monetary operations that our economy maintains with its trading partners in the outside the country. Such transactions shall be recorded in a account, called balance of payments. If the value of monetary flows in currency from Angola abroad is greater than the value of its exports, the balance of payments will show a negative balance and the balance of the reserves international currency exchange rate decreases. Given that our economy is in the global and regional economic-financial context, certain rules prudence must be respected. For example, the targets of macroeconomic convergence of SADC indicate that the countries of the region should maintain a minimum number of international foreign exchange reserves which, in a scenario allows the import of essential goods and services to the population for 6 months. The variation in the balance of payments balance is highly correlated with the behaviour of the exchange rate. That is, as the flows increase angola's foreign currency, increases demand for foreign exchange and vice versa. When you increase the demand for foreign exchange, without a capacity to offer there is a need to balance the foreign exchange market. That is, there is a need for the seeks to coincide with supply, and the equiulybrio mechanism that we use is the exchange rate which is a price mechanism, represented by the units in currency national we need for every unit of currency Foreign. With the fall in the price of a barrel of oil in the international market, the value of exports angolans has dropped considerably. Consequently, liquidity in foreign currency, available for supply in the foreign exchange market followed in the same direction. While exchange authority, it is up to the BNA to use the prices to restore balance in this market. That is why, since the third quarter of the the previous year, the national currency has been depreciating in a way that compared to previous periods. The exchange rate that was in the Kz99/USD1, is now at the level of Kz118/USD1. When liquidity in the banking system is in surplus, i.e. when the money supply is greater than that is necessary for the level of economic activity, its price - that is, the interest rate - also decreases. When the interest rate of the national currency reduces, in an environment of rising inflation, demand for currency increases. Economic operators concerned with preserving the value of their savings, prefer to migrate their banking positions denominated in national currency to foreign currency, increasing the demand for foreign reserves international currencies. When so, we have, again, a between demand and supply of foreign currency and pressure on the exchange rate. Is that's what it's about when we talk about speculative attack against our net international reserves. The response to this type of situation is again and largely through the price mechanism. Is what has been done. In recent weeks, the BNA has wiped out liquidity of the banking system, causing the price of the national currency to increase. Indeed, the interbank money market interest rate has increased by 6% at the beginning of the year to 11% in June. If the policy transmission mechanism monetary policy is sufficiently effective, the increase in the interest rates of the interbank money market should influence the interest rate curve in the money market, such as interest rates on government bonds. A secondly, the interest rates on term deposits in commercial banks will be adjusted, encouraging demand for national currency. If the demand for currency increase, will reduce demand for foreign currency, and also reduce the pressure on on the exchange rate. It is perceived that, in order to ensure price stability, in particular, of the prices of goods and services, exchange rates and interest rates, markets should be in balance. To do so, the monetary and exchange rate authority uses various instruments of monetary and exchange rate policy. These instruments will always be used to make the National Bank of Angola comply with its role in promoting macro-macroeconomic stability. With the macroeconomic stability, the conditions for investment and, consequently, the conditions for economic growth and job creation. Dear Comrades Political-party action must be aimed at ensuring at the same time the Democratic State of Sovereign Policy Law and Sovereign Management, treating them as a harmonic duality, capable of achieving the national objective to create an ever more just society for all, fundamental rights inherent in the dignity of the human person. From this perspective, I have no doubt that the militancy of the Banking Specialty Committee the MPLA is now and always a substantial reinforcement for the achieving these important objectives. After these brief words, I make myself available to answer the questions i deem appropriate form. THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR YOUR ATTENTION! 1 Jul. 2015
text_original: Home Publicaes e Media Intervenes Pblicas Palestra proferida pelo Senhor Governador do BNA subordinada ao tema A LIQUIDEZ FINANCEIRA NO MERCADO BANCRIO Camaradas Dirigentes do Comit de Especialidade dos Bancrios do MPLA, Palestra proferida pelo Senhor Governador do BNA subordinada ao tema A LIQUIDEZ FINANCEIRA NO MERCADO BANCRIO Camaradas Dirigentes do Comit de Especialidade dos Bancrios do MPLA, Caros participantes, Quero exprimir a minha gratido pelo honroso convite para partilhar convosco, reflexes sobre o tema relevante da Liquidez Financeira no Sistema Bancrio. Gostaria de abordar este Tema, recordando os problemas que se colocam para as economias quando se permite uma criao excessiva de liquidez no sistema bancrio (como foi o caso na crise internacional de 2008); para seguidamente trazer para a nossa realidade as lies do que se passou nos mercados financeiros internacionais. Ser demonstrado que o Quadro Operacional para a implementao da poltica monetria definida pelo Executivo conduzido pelo Presidente Jos Eduardo dos Santos, visa primordialmente a estabilidade dos preos e a promoo do crescimento econmico sustentado. Como se sabe os Bancos Centrais tm como papel fundamental a implementao de polticas monetrias condicionados ao sistema poltico e legal em que eles operam. Os Bancos Centrais esto bsicamente preocupados com dois aspectos da poltica monetria: a gesto econmica e a gesto da liquidez. A primeira envolve a promoo do crescimento econmico sustentado no longo prazo, mantendo a expanso do crdito e da moeda em linha com o crescimento potencial do produto. Nesse captulo os Bancos Centrais devem operar nos limites impostos pelas reservas internacionais lquidas e pela dvida externa. Por sua vez, a gesto da liquidez, tem um horizonte mais curto, envolvendo o asseguramento pelo sistema bancrio da moeda e dos pagamentos necessrios da sociedade. No seu dia-a-dia, os Bancos Centrais, preocupam-se em desenvolver tcnicas de gesto da liquidez com vista a influenciar o crescimento da moeda e do crdito atravs das taxas de juro. O problema surge quando o sistema permite que os Bancos Comerciais criem um elevado volume de liquidez  a chamada liquidez secundria ou escritural, criada nos livros dos bancos  sem que os bancos centrais tenham emitido ex-ante moeda primria que justificasse tal crescimento incontrolvel da moeda secundria. Este processo de emisso de liquidez secundria esteve na raiz da bolha financeira que causou a crise internacional de 2008. Os seus efeitos adversos ainda se fazem sentir, apesar de atenuados pelo aumento da emisso de dlares e euros pelos bancos centrais dos Estados Unidos da Amrica e da Unio Monetria Europeia, lastreados na emisso de novos ttulos emitidos pelos respectivos tesouros nacionais. O aumento do dfice fiscal da resultante, obrigou a um ajuste severo das contas pblicas, com cortes profundos nos gastos sociais, e o consequente aumento do desemprego. O excesso de liquidez secundria teve origem, de facto, em operaes de crdito excessivamente alavancadas pelos bancos mltiplos (comerciais e de investimento) dos pases mais desenvolvidos, depois que a revogao, no final do sculo passado, da Lei Glass-Steagall, de 1933, facultou a auto-regulao e o livre fluxo de capitais nos Estados Unidos, prtica que se disseminou no sistema financeiro internacional com o apoio dos organismos internacionais irmanados na defesa do neoliberalismo financeiro (o chamado Consenso de Washington). Por consequncia da alavancagem desmedida, criou-se uma bolha crescente na precificao dos activos reais subjacentes nas operaes de crdito, dando origem nos bancos a portflios muito superiores  capacidade de pagamento da clientela bancria devedora. O efeito mais recente da alavancagem, como sabemos,  que os bancos centrais dos Estados Unidos e da Unio Monetria Europeia tiveram de comprar aos bancos os seus crditos malparados, para alm de reduzirem as suas taxas bsicas de juros para um nvel histrico nunca visto, entre zero e meio por cento, abrindo espao para a prtica de operaes especulativas de arbitragem conta as moedas dos pases emergentes e em desenvolvimento.  evidente que os governos dos pases desenvolvidos tiveram de submeter aos respectivos parlamentos pedidos de autorizao para aumentar o limite oramental para a dvida pblica, gerando intenso debate poltico entre as bancadas parlamentares de oposio e situao, tal como se verificou nos Estados Unidos da Amrica. Em sntese, o socorro financeiro dado pelos bancos centrais dos Estados Unidos e da Unio Monetria Europeia aos bancos comerciais e de investimento americanos e europeus, para salv-los da derrocada financeira, virou dvida pblica, cujo custo ser pago pelos contribuintes daqueles pases, da actual e da prxima gerao, quer atravs do aumento de impostos, quer pela supresso de parte dos seus benefcios sociais. Outro efeito danoso da liquidez artificialmente criada nos livros dos bancos comerciais, foi a proliferao dos chamados "derivativos"  ou seja, "papis de vento", sem activos subjacentes, supostamente representativos da negociao no mercado futuro de commodities mas de facto meras apostas sobre ndices futuros de vrios indicadores do mercado financeiro especulativo. O efeito dos preos inflacionados dessas "commodities de papel" transmitiu-se, no caso de contratos futuros sobre o petrleo, para o mercado "spot", o das operaes reais de compra e venda do crude, aumentando artificialmente o preo do barril para at 156 dlares em Setembro de 2008, mas fazendo-o seguidamente cair para 38 dlares no incio de 2009, impactando negativamente o equilbrio das finanas pblicas e o da balana de pagamentos dos pases exportadores, entre os quais Angola. Nos ltimos 7 anos, o Grupo dos 20 Pases mais industrializados tem vindo a ensaiar medidas para colocar um ponto final nessa crise interminvel, tendo os EUA avanado com o Plano Volcker e a Lei Dodd-Frank para pelo menos evitar que bancos de investimento e comerciais continuem a praticar a promscua alavancagem de crditos de longo prazo lastreados em depsitos de curto prazo. No domnio dos preos do petrleo, entretanto, predominam ainda as nuvens da incerteza, agravadas pelos ventos da geopoltica mundial, oriundos quer da inesperada mudana da estratgia dos EUA na explorao de suas reservas internas de leo de xisto, quer de um possvel acordo entre os EUA e o Iro sobre temas nucleares, atravs do qual se supe um futuro levantamento das sanes que ainda incidem sobre as exportaes do petrleo iraniano. Por consequncia, no final de 2014 os preos do petrleo voltaram a sofrer uma queda acentuada para cerca de 45 dlares - depois de se terem mantido na mdia dos 107 dlares em 2013 - obrigando Angola a ajustar rapidamente o OGE 2015 para um horizonte mais mdico de receitas cambiais e fiscais. Neste novo cenrio de limitaes sobre o desempenho da economia nacional, uma das consequncias  a preferncia dos bancos nacionais pelo aumento de recursos nas suas tesourarias, levando-os a manter os seus activos inteiramente disponveis ou em aplicaes de curto prazo sem risco (como os Bilhetes do Tesouro), prevenindo-se para se ajustarem rapidamente a um possvel novo cenrio em termos de taxas mais altas de juro e de cmbio. Contudo, a experincia da gesto da poltica macroeconmica acumulada pelo Executivo nos recorrentes perodos de volatilidade dos preos do petrleo nos ltimos 10 anos ensinou-nos o bom caminho da prudncia e da austeridade fiscal. Por essa razo, deixamos de privilegiar os instrumentos de poltica voltados para o mercado financeiro de curto prazo, que no tm compromisso com o crescimento do produto real, e passamos a usar a gesto coordenada das polticas fiscal, monetria e cambial para alcanar objectivos macroeconmicos consistentes com a manuteno de um nvel de atividade econmica que no coloque em plano secundrio os princpios da Transparncia e da Responsabilidade Fiscal. Neste contexto, o Executivo prope-se assegurar o controlo da inflao a um nvel baixo e sustentvel (o objectivo revisto da programao macroeconmica  de 10,4% em Dezembro de 2015), bem como manter o patamar das Reservas Internacionais Lquidas equivalente a 6 meses de importaes e dar continuidade aos esforos para a diversificao da economia, visando reduzir gradualmente a dependncia da economia nacional ao sector petrolfero. Em termos prticos, cumprindo a Programao macroeconmica aprovada pela Comisso Econmica do Conselho de Ministros, o Ministrio das Finanas e o Banco Central zelam pela gesto da liquidez dos fluxos de moeda nacional resultante dos pagamentos da despesa pblica, garantindo que a execuo do OGE no se faa com emisso de moeda no vazio, o que faria crescer de forma incontrolvel a liquidez primria na economia e consequentemente os meios de pagamento. Com este propsito, o Banco Nacional de Angola estabeleceu, desde o incio do ano, um curso de poltica monetria restritiva, com o objectivo principal de promover a estabilidade de preos. Os instrumentos de poltica monetria que est a usar para controlar a liquidez do sistema bancrio so: (i) as taxas de juro, (ii) o nvel de depsitos que os bancos esto obrigados a constituir junto do BNA, (iii) a venda de titulos de divida pblica da sua prpria carteira, em troca de liquidez e (iv) a venda de divisas em moeda estrangeira. Por exemplo, no incio deste ano, os bancos comerciais tinham que constituir reservas em moeda nacional, junto do Banco Nacional de Angola, equivalentes a 15% dos depsitos dos seus clientes. A partir de 1 Julho, tero que constituir 25%. Este aumento da quantidade de depsitos que os bancos comerciais tm que constituir junto do BNA,  feito para reduzir a sua capacidade para aumentar a quantidade de moeda a circular na economia. O curso actual da poltica monetria  consistente com a dinmica da inflao no primeiro semestre do ano que registou em 31 de Maio de 2015 um nvel de 8,86% (no periodo de 12 meses) contra 7,48% em Dezembro de 2014 (para o mesmo periodo). Para alm da estabilidade de preos, o Banco Nacional de Angola  igualmente responsvel por gerir as disponibilidades externas do pas. Refiro-me, concretamente,  gesto das reservas internacionais denominadas em moeda estrangeira. A variao do saldo das reservas internacionais de divisas  determinada pelo efeito lquido das operaes monetrias que a nossa economia mantm com os parceiros comerciais no exterior do pas. Essas operaes ficam registadas num instrumento contabilstico, denominado Balana de Pagamentos. Se o valor dos fluxos monetrios em moeda estrangeira de Angola para o exterior for superior ao valor das suas exportaes, a balana de pagamentos apresentar um saldo negativo e o saldo das reservas internacionais de divisas diminui. Dado que a nossa economia est inserida no contexto economico-financeiro mundial e regional, determinadas regras de prudncia devem ser respeitadas. A ttulo de exemplo, as metas de convergncia macroeconmica da SADC indicam que os pases da regio devem manter um mnimo de reservas internacionais de divisas que, num cenrio catastrfico, permite a importao de bens e servios essenciais para a populao, durante 6 meses. A variao do saldo da balana de pagamentos est altamente correlacionado com o comportamento da taxa de cmbio. Ou seja,  medida que aumentam os fluxos monetrios de Angola com o exterior, aumenta a procura por divisas e vice-versa. Quando aumenta a procura por divisas, sem que haja uma capacidade de oferta correspondente, h necessidade de se equilibrar o mercado cambial. Isto , h necessidade de a procura coincidir com a oferta, e o mecanismo de equiulbrio que utilizamos  a taxa de cmbio que  um mecanismo de preo, representado pelas unidades em moeda nacional que precisamos por cada unidade de moeda estrangeira. Com a queda do preo do barril de petrleo no mercado internacional, o valor das exportaes angolanas baixou consideravelmente. Consequentemente, a liquidez em moeda estrangeira, disponvel para oferta no mercado cambial seguiu no mesmo sentido. Enquanto autoridade cambial, cabe ao BNA recorrer ao mecanismo de preos para restabelecer o equilbrio neste mercado.  por isso, que desde o terceiro trimestre do ano anterior, a moeda nacional tem vindo a depreciar-se de forma mais acentuada comparativamente a perodos anteriores. A taxa de cmbio que se situava nos Kz99/USD1, encontra-se agora no patamar de Kz118/USD1. Quando a liquidez no sistema bancrio  excedentria, isto , quando a oferta de moeda  maior do que a necessria para o nvel de actividade econmica, o seu preo  ou seja, a taxa de juro - tambm diminui. Quando a taxa de juro da moeda nacional reduz, num ambiente de crescente inflao, a procura por moeda estrangeira aumenta. Os agentes econmicos, preocupados com a preservao do valor das suas poupanas, preferem migrar as suas posies bancrias denominadas em moeda nacional para moeda estrangeira, aumentando a procura por reservas internacionais de divisas. Quando assim , temos, novamente, um desiquilibrio entre a procura e oferta de moeda estrangeira e presso sobre a taxa de cmbio.  disso que se trata quando falamos em ataque especulativo contra as nossas reservas internacionais lquidas. A resposta a este tipo de situaes passa novamente e em grande medida pelo mecanismo de preos.  o que tem sido feito. Nas ltimas semanas, o BNA enxugou liquidez do sistema bancrio, fazendo com que o preo da moeda nacional aumentasse. Com efeito, a taxa de juro do mercado monetrio interbancrio aumentou de 6%, no incio do ano, para 11% no ms de Junho. Se o mecanismo de transmisso da poltica monetria for suficientemente eficaz, o aumento das taxas de juro do mercado monetrio interbancrio dever influenciar a curva das taxas de juro no mercdo monetrio, como por exemplo as taxas de juro dos ttulos pblicos. Num segundo momento, ajustar-se-o as taxas de juro dos depsitos a prazo nos bancos comerciais, incentivando a procura por moeda nacional. Se a procura por moeda nacional aumentar, reduzir a procura por moeda estrangeira, reduzindo-se, igualmente, a presso sobre a taxa de cmbio. Percebe-se, que para haver estabilidade de preos, nomeadamente, dos preos dos bens e servios, das taxa de cmbio e das taxas de juro, os mercados devem estar em equilbrio. Para faz-lo, a autoridade monetria e cambial recorre a diversos instrumentos de poltica monetria e cambial. Esses instrumentos sero sempre usados no sentido de o Banco Nacional de Angola cumprir com o seu papel na promoo da estabilidade macroeconmca. Com a estabilidade macroeconmica, ficam criadas as condies para o investimento e, consequentemente, para o crescimento econmico e criao de emprego. Caros Camaradas A ao poltico-partidria deve estar voltada para garantir simultaneamente o Estado Democrtico de Direito e a Gesto Soberana da Poltica Macroeconmica, tratando-os como uma dualidade harmnica, capaz de conduzir ao alcance do objetivo nacional permanente de se criar uma sociedade cada vez mais justa para todos, com respeito aos direitos fundamentais inerentes  dignidade da pessoa humana. Nesta perspectiva, no tenho dvidas de que a militncia do Comit da Especialidade dos Bancrios do MPLA constitui, hoje e sempre, um reforo substancial para o alcance desses importantes objetivos. Aps estas breves palavras, coloco-me disponvel para responder s perguntas que julguem oportuno formular. MUITO OBRIGADO PELA VOSSA ATENO! text: Public Interventions Address of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the close of the fifth forum on Banking Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the close of the fifth forum on Bank My Greetings to Dr. Carlos Rosado de Carvalho, Director of the Journal Expansao, Organizer of the V Forum Banca; the authorities present, Minister of Finance, President of the CMC; To the Distinguished Speakers who have brightened this Meeting with their teachings on the Corporate Governance in Africa and Angola; To the Presidents of the main Angolan banks that discussed at the Round Table the relevant theme of Corporate Governance Challenges in Angola; To the other Participants, representatives of banking and non-bank financial institutions, insurance companies, telecommunications, energy and water companies and other public and private companies, as well as law firms, consultants and other financial and capital market service providers, Ladies and gentlemen, I thank the organisers for the honorable invitation to deliver the closing address of this important Colloquium, in which the challenges that our country must overcome to align itself with the best corporate governance practices in all areas in which banks, economic agents and regulatory authorities, under the aegis of the Democratic Rule of Law. The quality of the Participants reveals the organisers' commencant concern to ensure that the Annual Banking Forum remains a comprehensive and strategic approach, to deepen our reflections on the interdependence between Banking, the Public and Private Business Sector and public, with a view to achieving the most relevant objectives of the National Development. I am fully aware that, as regards the National Bank of Angola, such interdependence stresses the central bank's responsibility to adopt best practices in The Financial System's Supervision and Monetary Account Management and exchange rates in coordination with tax management, as requirements fundamental to a business environment in which the Banking And its business clientele can also fulfill its responsibilities as a stakeholders in pursuing the best Corporate Governance Practices. The political commitment to the best practices of Country Governance, assumed in the Constitution of the Republic of 05 February 2010, is the main pillar, of the broad legislative package that the Organs of Sovereignty have been building in recent years Years. The most recent advance in this legislative building was the publication of Law No. 12/15 of 17 June - Basic Law of Financial Institutions, which updates and replaces the legal regime established by Law No. 13/05 of 30 September, the previous Financial Institutions Act. The new Law establishes, as of Article 70, the principles of Behavioral Supervision and respective Rules of Conduct to which the financial institutions, in order to ensure their liquidity and solvency, through the universal pillars of Good Corporate Governance, which are as follows: Legal Compliance; Responsible and Timely Accountability; Promoting Transparency (Disclosure); and The Sense of Justice (Fairness). In addition to introducing institutional resolution mechanisms to protect deposits and other assets of clients, the new Law provides that institutions financial statements that present significant losses or are at risk of insolvency may result in be partially or totally disposed of or transferred to another entity. Of course, these measures will only apply when the supervisory body considers that it is not the financial institution at risk will be able to achieve, in a appropriate period, to take the necessary actions to return to the conditions of soundness and prudential ratios. The law extends the governance requirements of financial institutions in the external audit risk control, as well as the control mechanisms and remuneration policies, requiring them to present sound provisions for the governance of society, organise effective processes of identification, management, control and communication of risks and have mechanisms for monitoring "including administrative and accounting procedures and to have remuneration policies and practices that promote and are consistent with sound and prudent risk management." The Executive intends, with the new law, to correspond to the increasing sophistication of the financial system angolan law and align it with international principles and standards, in emanating from the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision 2012 and those that may be consensual for the reform of the financial system group of the 20 Most Industrialised Countries, in the light of the initiatives adopted in the USA which re-established the principle of separation of assets and liabilities financial institutions and capital market institutions. I believe that ideal conditions are created in Angola to move forward with the implementation of Good Corporate Governance Practices not only in Banking but also in in the corporate and corporate sector, in order to allow the capital market to comply with the role that is intended for it in the process of growth and development of the national economy. Ladies and gentlemen, Despite these advances, I must tell you that the central bank's responsibilities in the field of Corporate Governance are not limited only to the provisions of the new Law and in the policies and processes set out in the BNA Regulatory Notices under the corporate governance. Before, on the contrary, I must warn an even greater challenge to our creative and operational capacity. We have before us the ongoing challenge of improving working methods and instruments, in the organization and supervision of the financial system, but also the duty to share our responsibilities in the complex supervisory process, with the two other financial market regulators - i.e. CMC (Capital Markets Commission) and ARSEG (Insurance Regulatory Agency). Much of this complexity stems from the growing trend of financial intermediaries in currency, foreign exchange and capital markets to increase their profits predominantly through treasury operations, structured on products virtual financial resources, shorter-term (and therefore supposedly compared to credit operations in the real sector of the economy. The debate on these matters has made it possible to deepen our reflections on the best practices to build a banking system and a market for modern capitals - each taking care of their specific mission - capable of attracting more investments external to the productive sector of our economy. At the same time, in so that the application of savings in long-term investments can be sustainable development, national macroeconomic planning takes due place on consideration the hard lessons drawn from the international financial crises that have imposed on us fiscal, monetary and exchange rate shocks since independence National. We continue to expect the Group of 20 most industrialised countries to make progress in order to adopt consensually, rules that recognise that resources invested in the capital market should not be anchored in assets of the short-term period raised by the Bank and that prudential ratios should prevent financial institutions from creating means of payment outside the control of central banks. Expensive participants, In this complex scenario of great uncertainties that still overlap over the optimal regulation financial markets, Angola has adopted prudence and commitment to the legal and patrimonial security of our nascent financial system, avoiding expose, to unnecessary risks, the financial savings of the nation, accumulated in The Banking and Sovereign International Reserves. In this sense, it is worth carefully interpreting the fact that the new Basic Law of in article 6(1) (e), to admit, among the activities provided to banking financial institutions, that of "carrying out services and activities investment in securities and derivatives, permitted by securities distribution companies." Apparently, the text can set up a reversal of legislative hierarchy by admitting that standards established by the regulatory body of the securities market securities, specific to value distributors, would make transactions subject to securities financial institutions regulated by the Central Bank. This paradox hypothesis is fortunately immediately removed when reading paragraph 2 of the same article: "2. It is incumbent upon the National Bank of Angola to define the terms and conditions for carrying out the referred to in the preceding paragraph, without prejudice to the competences of the Securities Market Supervision Body and the Angolan Securities and Exchange Agency Insurance Supervision with regard, respectively, to the (e) and (j) both of the preceding paragraph." In other words, the Central Bank preserves its regulatory and supervisory attribution of commercial banks, prohibit the performance of operations with securities and their derivatives involving risks incompatible with good corporate governance banks. In this concept of risk, operations with ndf derivatives (Non Deliverable Forwards) are and CDS (Credit Default Swaps) devoid of assets and/or consistent in mere bets on index developments - so-called "index wind" or "casino betting". In view of the purely speculative nature of these financial products, commercial banks and their customers of depositors to the order and short-term that their cash availability in those types of securities would run the risk of considerable losses in the event of a default in solvency, liquidity and/or the profitability of these derivatives, as has been reported in the 2008/2009 crisis. The caveat to which I have just referred is important, to make it clear, that the institutions financial statements may only carry out transactions with securities and derivative instruments within the strict limits of the rules that may be established by the European central, even though different standards will be established securities distributors by their respective regulatory and supervisory body. However, it seems inevitable that the entities responsible for and regulating the securities market securities will not fail to establish rules of good governance corporate governance also for the entities of the securities distribution system, aiming at protect them from the risks of disseminated toxic derivatives international markets by self-regulation, the harmful effects of which have been brought to light the 2008/2009 international financial crisis. While the Group of the 21 most industrialised countries does not agree with its position, our of the newly published Financial Institutions, incorporates the instruments of action necessary to ensure financial stability and prevent financial crises in the Angolan Financial System. Dear Participants, Ladies and Gentlemen, I apologize for the long approach to this subject, but it is due to the relevance of the theme and the concerns about the future developments of these financial intermediation markets. I conclude by thanking them for their attention and reaffirming my confidence that, united in the common effort to build a dynamic economy, we can make a valuable contribution to the country's path to continuous progress, even in the face of periodic adversities of the external scenario. THANK YOU VERY MUCH! July 9. 2014
text_original: Home Publicaes e Media Intervenes Pblicas Discurso do Governador do Banco Nacional de Angola, no encerramento do quinto forum sobre a Banca Discurso do Governador do Banco Nacional de Angola, no encerramento do quinto forum sobre a Banca Minhas Saudaes ao Doutor Carlos Rosado de Carvalho, Director do Jornal Expanso, Organizador do V Frum Banca; s Autoridades presentes, Ministro das Finanas, Presidente da CMC; Aos Distintos Conferencistas que abrilhantaram este Encontro com os seus ensinamentos sobre a Governao Corporativa em frica e em Angola; Aos Presidentes dos principais bancos angolanos que discutiram na Mesa Redonda o relevante tema dos Desafios da Governao Corporativa em Angola; Aos demais Participantes, representantes de instituies financeiras bancrias e no bancrias, seguradoras, empresas de telecomunicaes, de energia e guas e outras empresas pblicas e privadas, bem como de escritrios de advogados, consultoras e outros prestadores de servios do mercado financeiro e de capitais, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Agradeo aos organizadores o honroso convite para proferir o discurso de encerramento deste importante Colquio, em que se discutiram os desafios que o nosso Pas deve ultrapassar para alinhar-se s melhores prticas de Governao Corporativa em todos os domnios em que interagem os Bancos, os Agentes Econmicos e as Entidades Reguladoras, sob a gide do Estado Democrtico de Direito. A qualidade dos Participantes revela a elogivel preocupao dos Organizadores no sentido de assegurar que o Frum Anual da Banca continue a ser um Encontro abrangente e estratgico, para aprofundar as nossas reflexes a respeito da interdependncia entre a Banca, o Sector Empresarial Pblico e Privado e as Polticas Publicas, visando  consecuo dos mais relevantes objectivos do Plano Nacional de Desenvolvimento. Tenho plena conscincia de que, no que toca ao Banco Nacional de Angola, tal interdependncia reala a responsabilidade que incumbe ao Banco Central de adoptar as melhores prticas de Superviso do Sistema Financeiro e de Gesto das Contas Monetrias e Cambiais em coordenao com a Gesto Fiscal, como requisitos fundamentais para um ambiente de negcios em que a Banca e a sua clientela empresarial possam igualmente cumprir com as suas responsabilidades como stakeholders na prossecuo das melhores Prticas de Governao Corporativa. O compromisso poltico com as melhores prticas de Governao do Pas, assumido na Constituio da Repblica de 05 de Fevereiro de 2010, constitui-se no principal pilar, do amplo pacote legislativo que os rgos de Soberania tm vindo a edificar, nos ltimos anos. O mais recente avano nessa edificao legislativa deu-se com a publicao da Lei n. 12/15, de 17 de Junho  Lei de Bases das Instituies Financeiras, que actualiza e substitui o regime jurdico institudo pela Lei n. 13/05, de 30 de Setembro, a anterior Lei das Instituies Financeiras. A nova Lei estabelece, a partir do artigo 70, os princpios da Superviso Comportamental e as respectivas Regras de Conduta a que devem submeter-se as Instituies Financeiras, no sentido de garantirem a sua liquidez e solvabilidade, atravs dos pilares universais da Boa Governao Corporativa, que so os seguintes: A Conformidade Legal (Compliance); A Prestao de Contas Responsvel e Atempada (Accountability); A Promoo da Transparncia (Disclosure); e O Sentido de Justia (Fairness). Para alm de introduzir mecanismos institucionais de resoluo para proteger os depsitos e outros activos dos clientes, a nova Lei prev que as instituies financeiras que apresentem significativos prejuzos ou se encontrem em risco de insolvncia possam ser parcial ou totalmente alienadas ou transferidas para outra entidade. Naturalmente estas medidas s sero aplicveis quando o organismo de superviso considerar no ser previsvel que a instituio financeira em risco consiga, num prazo apropriado, executar as aces necessrias para regressar s condies de solidez e de cumprimento dos rcios prudenciais. A lei alarga as exigncias da governao das instituies financeiras no plano da auditoria externa e no controlo de risco, bem como os mecanismos de controlo interno e as polticas de remunerao, exigindo que apresentem dispositivos slidos em matria de governao da sociedade, organizem processos eficazes de identificao, gesto, controlo e comunicao dos riscos e disponham de mecanismos de controlo interno, incluindo procedimentos administrativos e contabilsticos slidos e de dispor de polticas e prticas de remunerao que promovam e sejam coerentes com uma gesto s e prudente dos riscos. O Executivo pretende, com a nova lei, corresponder  crescente sofisticao do sistema financeiro angolano e alinh-lo aos princpios e padres internacionais, em especial os emanados pelo Comit de Basileia de Superviso Bancria de 2012 e os que vierem a ser consensualizados para a reforma do sistema financeiro internacional no Grupo dos 20 Pases Mais Industrializados,  luz das iniciativas adoptadas nos EUA que reestabeleceu o princpio da separao de activos e passivos das instituies financeiras e das instituies do mercado de capitais. Considero que esto criadas em Angola, condies ideais para se avanar com a implementao de Boas Prticas de Governao Corporativa no s na Banca como no sector empresarial e societrio, de modo a permitir que o mercado de capitais cumpra com segurana o papel que lhe  destinado no processo de crescimento e desenvolvimento da economia nacional. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Apesar desses avanos, devo dizer-lhes que as responsabilidades do Banco Central no domnio da Governao Corporativa no se esgotam s nas disposies da nova Lei e nas polticas e processos estabelecidos nos Avisos regulamentares do BNA no mbito da governao corporativa. Antes, pelo contrrio, devo alertar para um desafio ainda maior  nossa capacidade criadora e operativa. Temos diante de ns o desafio permanente de melhoria dos mtodos e instrumentos de trabalho, no mbito da Organizao e Superviso do Sistema Financeiro, mas tambm o dever de partilhar as nossas responsabilidades no complexo processo de superviso, com as outras duas entidades reguladoras de mercados financeiros  ou seja, a CMC (Comisso de Mercados de capitais ) e a ARSEG (Agncia de Regulao de Seguros). Boa parte dessa complexidade advm da tendncia crescente dos intermediadores financeiros dos mercados monetrio, cambial e de capitais de aumentar os seus lucros predominantemente atravs de operaes de tesouraria, estruturadas sobre produtos financeiros virtuais, de mais curto prazo (e, portanto, supostamente de menor risco) comparativamente s operaes de crdito ao sector real da economia. O debate sobre estas matrias tem permitido aprofundarmos as nossas reflexes sobre as melhores prticas para edificarmos um sistema bancrio e um mercado de capitais modernos - cada um cuidando da sua misso especfica  capazes de atrair mais investimentos externos ao sector produtivo da nossa economia. Paralelamente, para que a aplicao da poupana em investimentos de longo prazo possa ser sustentvel, o planeamento macroeconmico nacional toma na devida considerao as duras lies extradas das crises financeiras internacionais que nos impuseram choques fiscais, monetrios e cambiais desde a Independncia Nacional. Continuamos na expectativa do Grupo dos 20 Pases mais Industrializados conseguir realizar avanos no sentido de se adoptar consensualmente, regras que reconheam que recursos investidos no mercado de capitais, no devem estar fundeados em activos de curto prazo captados pela Banca e que rcios prudenciais rgidos devem impedir as instituies financeiras de criar meios de pagamento escriturais fora do controlo dos bancos centrais. Caros Participantes, Neste complexo cenrio de grandes incertezas que ainda pairam sobre a regulao ideal dos mercados financeiros, Angola tem adoptado a prudncia e o compromisso com a segurana jurdica e patrimonial do nosso nascente sistema financeiro, evitando expor, a riscos desnecessrios, a poupana financeira da nao, acumulada na Banca e nas Reservas Internacionais Soberanas. Neste sentido, merece cuidadosa interpretao o facto da nova Lei de Bases das Instituies financeiras, na alnea e) do n. 1 do artigo 6, admitir, dentre as actividades facultadas s instituies financeiras bancrias, a de realizar servios e actividades de investimento em valores mobilirios e instrumentos derivados, nos termos permitidos s sociedades distribuidoras de valores mobilirios. Aparentemente, o texto pode configurar uma inverso de hierarquia legislativa, ao admitir que normas estabelecidas pela entidade reguladora do mercado de valores mobilirios, especificas para distribuidoras de valores, passariam a subordinar operaes de instituies financeiras bancrias reguladas pelo Banco Central. Tal hiptese de paradoxo fica, felizmente, logo afastada ao ler-se seguidamente o n. 2 do mesmo artigo: 2. Compete ao Banco Nacional de Angola definir os termos e condies de realizao das operaes referidas no nmero anterior, sem prejuzo das competncias do Organismo de Superviso do Mercado de Valores Mobilirios e da Agncia Angolana de Regulao e Superviso de Seguros no que respeita, respectivamente, s alneas e) e j), ambas do nmero anterior. Ou seja, o Banco Central preserva a sua atribuio reguladora e supervisora dos bancos comerciais, podendo proibir a realizao de operaes com valores mobilirios e seus derivativos que envolvam riscos incompatveis com a boa governao corporativa dos bancos. Enquadro nesse conceito de risco as operaes com derivados do tipo NDF (Non Deliverable Forwards) e os CDS (Credit Default Swaps) desprovidos de activos subjacentes e/ou consistentes em meras apostas sobre evoluo de ndices - os chamados "papis de vento" ou apostas de casino. Face  natureza meramente especulativa desses produtos financeiros, os bancos comerciais e a sua clientela de depositantes  ordem e de curto prazo que aplicassem as suas disponibilidades de tesouraria nesses tipos de papis correriam o risco de sofrer prejuzos considerveis no caso de default na solvabilidade, na liquidez e/ou na rentabilidade desses derivativos, como se verificou disseminadamente no desenrolar da crise de 2008/2009. A ressalva a que acabo de me referir  importante, para tornar claro, que as instituies financeiras bancrias s podero realizar operaes com valores mobilirios e instrumentos derivados nos estritos limites das normas que vierem a ser estabelecidas pelo Banco Central, ainda que normas diferentes venham a ser estabelecidas para as distribuidoras de valores mobilirios pelo seu respectivo rgo regulador e supervisor. Entretanto, parece inevitvel que as entidades de tutela e regulao do mercado de valores mobilirios no deixaro de estabelecer regras de boa governao corporativa tambm para as entidades do sistema de distribuio de valores mobilirios, visando proteg-las contra os riscos dos derivativos txicos disseminados nos mercados internacionais pela autorregulao, cujos efeitos nefastos foram trazidos  luz do dia pela crise financeira internacional de 2008/2009. Enquanto o Grupo dos 21 Pases mais industrializados no consensualiza a sua posio, a nossa Lei das Instituies Financeiras recentemente publicada, incorpora os instrumentos de aco necessrios para garantir a estabilidade financeira e prevenir crises sistmicas no Sistema Financeiro Angolano. Caros Participantes, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Peo desculpas pela abordagem longa deste assunto, mas deve-se  relevncia do tema e s fundadas preocupaes com os desenvolvimentos futuros desses importantes mercados de intermediao financeira. Finalizo, agradecendo-lhes a ateno dispensada e reafirmando-lhes a minha confiana de que, unidos no esforo comum de edificao de uma economia dinmica, poderemos dar uma contribuio valiosa para que o Pas trilhe a senda de um progresso contnuo, mesmo face s adversidades peridicas do cenrio externo. Title: Speech at the opening of the 10th edition of the Banking in Analysis Forum
text: Public Interventions Address of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the opening of the 10th edition of the Banking Forum in Analysis Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the opening of the 10th edition of the Banking in Analysis Dr. Rui Santos Silva, Country Managing Partner of Deloitte Angola, organizer of this 10th Edition banking forum; Dr. Amilcar Azevedo da Silva, President of ABANC; Worthy Presidents and representatives of Angolan banks; Ladies and gentlemen; Participating in the opening session of the Tenth Edition of the Banking Forum is a very special meaning, for the following reasons: First, because it gives me the opportunity to learn about the valuable material information collected by the organizers to support the discussions, analyses and proposals that will emerge from this meeting, on the regulation of of the financial system. This is value documentation invaluable, in these crucial times of new challenges, which need to be scrutinised in the face of pillars of the macroeconomic strategy of transition to a new balance level of the national economy. It is therefore worthy of praise the effort made by DELOITTE to promote, in the agenda of this event, the research and analysis material consisting of important working documents. Secondly, the special significance of this event stifudes from the fact that it is statements of the presidents of the banks, as in the opinions of deloitte's managing managers, the valuable testimony that, in the 10 years of implementation of the forum, remarkable progress has been made in the areas, sustainable and regulated growth of the banking sector, and within the framework of its seamless integration into the fundamentals of fiscal, monetary and exchange rate policies conducted by the Executive in the last 1990s. This important evolution, particularly significant to me, which I had the privilege of exercising minister of finance between 2002 and 2008 is synthesized, in some testimonies published in the study. In addition to the testimonies, Banks as strong drivers of major transformations in our country in these 10 years, indicators of the evolution of the activity are highlighted: 4,300 Employees, employed in the banking in 2005, 19,000 at the end of 2014; 230 Bank Agencies in 2005, more than 1,600 Branches at the end of 2014. Bank Presidents share this vision of explosive growth in the national banking sector and express expectation swell in relation to the current situation. We realize that they have confidence in the prudential measures of the Financial System regulator to improve the solvency standard of the portfolio customers, temporarily hit by the negative effects of a slower pace of growth economic. In this respect, it should be noted that the softer pace of economic growth negatively impacts the growth not only of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), but also gross national product (GNP), with the aggravation that the fall in GNP is greater than that of the gdp due to the following factors: Only the income of foreign exchange residents (covering, in the case of oil, only the profit oil of the State and the taxes collected from the oil); In turn, the incomes of both foreign exchange residents and non-residents are calculated in GDP, in this case covering the share of income in the sector used to reimburse cost oil expenses; The cost oil corresponds, therefore, to a rigid portion of GDP, as it does not contract in the same proportion of the fall in oil export income; In this way, the negative impact of the fall in oil prices is almost entirely on the profit oil of the State and on the taxes paid by Operating companies, causing a stronger contraction in GNP than in GDP, with repercussions revenues from the OGE. However, there are encouraging signs of a reduction in the volatility of the main macroeconomic variables, with clear effects on the most conducive to growth in economic activity in the non-oil sector. As a result of efforts to coordinate the executive's fiscal, monetary and exchange rate policies, BNA will resume its open market operations by liquidity to public securities held by banking institutions, stimulating the intermediation of financial and in this process generating lower inflationary pressure and impact on the Balance of Payments and Exchange Rate. The BNA will continue to offer Commercial Banks, through the Mandatory Reserves mechanism, the possibility of directing your applications into operations to the productive sector and in Treasury Bonds issued at interest rates with percentages above the exchange rate correction. These investments allow the Treasury to expand the raising of funds for the realization of investments in infrastructure, which are key to accelerating the economic diversification. The national productive sector benefiting from new infrastructure will have its production and their increased incomes, increasing their capacity financial institutions, and thus is enabled for new bank credits under more solvency conditions safe and transparent. The BNA continues to seek additional sources of external liquidity, in particular through exchange of currencies, on the basis of which balances of transactions financial transactions with our partners may be paid in our own currency. But the most important thing is to recognize that our country, despite the fall in the price of oil, still benefits from the fact that its future production continues to provide a sound guarantee for access to international credit lines for imports strategic goods and services for the relaunch of the economic activity across the country. I am particularly pleased that the Banca study under consideration addresses the theme of inclusion financial crisis, as a means of increasing the banking of incomes in the economy. It is important that banks not only expand electronic platforms necessary, but also and above all reflect on the following: The financial planning of each aspiring customer obtaining bank credit should continue to be, in the very first place, a responsibility of one's own granting bank of the credit, rather than the bank simply surrounding itself with all sorts of guarantees and leave it up to the customer the responsibility to educate themselves financially, to understand the risks that high interest rates, and the time limits relatively short repayment rates may be a threat factor to the solvency of bank credit. In some countries, there are reports that the growth in non-home credit is attributed to the fact that the client, driven by ignorance in financial matters, assumes commitments in banking with very high interest rates, as if the granting bank of the credit does not the responsibility of verifying, already in the act of preparation of the client's registration form, the absolute incompatibility between its wage income and the level of debt it was taking on with a interest rate totally out of date from your ability to pay. I therefore recommend that efforts be made for the Financial Education of Angolans, starting from the outcentre with the financial planning of its ability to pay. Different participants, Ladies and gentlemen, The Banking In Analysis Study addresses issues of the greatest importance in the development process national level, so that we can create an environment and sustainability, both the continued growth of the product, and of the public debt, for which the real fundamentals will always be the maintenance of the stability of the real rate interest rates or simply in ensuring their fair fluctuation. The commitment we have to the future of our country, still institutionally young, because we will celebrate 40 years of our independence, does not allow us to to give up an increasing effort to diversify the economy and accelerate the economic growth. Only in this way can we ensure the continued increase in employment for a generation of young people who have been increasing access to the benefits of education and basic social services. I reaffirm the commitment of the National Bank of Angola to continue to collaborate with the Banking Forum, through a transparent dialogue on the regulation of the banking system, in order to provide customers with the benefits of financial intermediation effective and efficient, guided by principles of Responsibility to support sustainable growth of the economy. Thanking everyone for their attention, I repay the organizers of this event and wish success to the tenth Banking Forum. Thank you very much! 22 Sep. 2015

Trata-se de documentao de valor inestimvel, nestes tempos cruciais de novos desafios, que precisam de ser escrutinados perante os pilares da estratgia macroeconmica de transio para um novo patamar de equilbrio da economia nacional. , portanto, merecedor de elogios o esforo desenvolvido pela DELOITTE, no sentido e propiciar, na agenda deste evento, o material de pesquisas e anlises constitudo por importantes documentos de trabalho. Em segundo lugar, o significado especial deste evento vem do facto de se constatar, quer nos depoimentos dos presidentes dos bancos, como nas opinies respeitveis dos gestores titulares da DELOITTE, o testemunho valioso de que, nos 10 anos de realizao do frum, foram alcanados avanos notveis nos domnios, quer do crescimento sustentvel e regulado do sector bancrio, quer no mbito da sua perfeita integrao aos fundamentos das polticas fiscal, monetria e cambial conduzidas pelo Executivo no ltimo decnio. Essa importante evoluo, particularmente significativa para mim, que tive o privilgio de exercer a funo de Ministro das Finanas entre 2002 e 2008 est sintetizada, em alguns testemunhos publicados no estudo. Para alm dos testemunhos referirem os Bancos como fortes impulsionadores das grandes transformaes econmicas no nosso Pas nestes 10 anos, so destacados indicadores da evoluo da actividade: 4.300 Colaboradores, empregados na banca em 2005, 19.000 no final de 2014; 230 Agencias Bancrias em 2005, mais de 1.600 Balces no final de 2014. Os Presidentes dos Bancos partilham esta viso de crescimento explosivo do Sector Bancrio nacional e manifestam expectativa em relao a conjuntura actual. Percebemos que eles tm confiana nas medidas prudenciais do regulador do Sistema Financeiro Nacional tendentes a melhorar o padro de solvabilidade da carteira de clientes, temporariamente atingida pelos efeitos negativos de um menor ritmo de crescimento econmico. Neste aspecto,  de notar que o ritmo mais brando de crescimento econmico impacta negativamente o crescimento no s do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB), mas tambm do Produto Nacional Bruto (PNB), com a agravante de que a queda do PNB  maior do que a do PIB, devido aos seguintes factores: No PNB calculam-se apenas os rendimentos dos residentes cambiais (abrangendo, no caso do petrleo, s o profit oil do Estado e os impostos arrecadados ao sector petrolfero); Por sua vez, no PIB calculam-se os rendimentos tanto de residentes cambiais como de no residentes, neste caso abrangendo a parcela dos rendimentos do sector petrolfero usada para ressarcir as despesas do cost oil; O cost oil corresponde, portanto, a uma parcela rgida do PIB, pois no se contrai na mesma proporo da queda dos rendimentos da exportao do petrleo; Deste modo, o impacto negativo da queda dos preos do petrleo recai na sua quase totalidade sobre o profit oil do Estado e sobre os impostos pagos pelas Companhias operadoras, provocando uma contraco mais forte no PNB do que no PIB, com reflexos directos nas receitas do OGE. Entretanto, h no horizonte sinais animadores de uma reduo da volatilidade das principais variveis macroeconmicas, com reflexos claros nas condies mais propcias conducentes ao crescimento da actividade econmica no sector no petrolfero. Como resultado dos esforos de coordenao das polticas fiscal, monetria e cambial do executivo, o BNA retomar as suas operaes de mercado aberto dando liquidez aos ttulos pblico em posse das Instituies Bancrias, estimulando a intermediao financeira e neste processo gerando menor presso inflacionista e menor impacto sobre a Balana de Pagamentos e Taxa de Cmbio. O BNA continuar a oferecer aos Bancos Comerciais, atravs do mecanismo das Reservas Obrigatrias, a possibilidade de direccionar as suas aplicaes em operaes de crdito ao sector produtivo e em Obrigaes do Tesouro emitidas com taxas de juros com percentuais acima da correco cambial. Estas aplicaes permitem ao Tesouro ampliar a captao de recursos destinados  realizao de investimentos na infra-estrutura, fundamentais para acelerar a diversificao econmica. O sector produtivo nacional beneficiado com novas infra-estruturas ter a sua produo e os seus rendimentos aumentados, elevando-se a sua capacidade financeiras, e assim habilita-se a novos crditos bancrios em condies de solvabilidade mais seguras e transparentes. O BNA continua a buscar fontes adicionais de liquidez externa, nomeadamente atravs de acordos de intercmbio de moedas, na base dos quais saldos de operaes comerciais, mas tambm de operaes financeiras com os nossos parceiros podero ser pagos na nossa prpria moeda. Mas, o mais importante,  reconhecermos que o nosso Pas, apesar da queda do preo do petrleo, ainda beneficia do facto, de que a sua produo futura, continua a constituir uma garantia slida para acedermos s linhas de crdito internacionais para a importao de bens e servios estratgicas para o relanamento da actividade econmica em todo o pas. Estou particularmente satisfeito que o estudo Banca em anlise aborda o tema da incluso financeira, como meio de aumentar a bancarizao dos fluxos de rendimentos na economia.  importante que os Bancos no s ampliem as plataformas electrnicas necessrias, mas tambm e sobretudo reflictam no seguinte: O planeamento financeiro de cada cliente aspirante  obteno de crdito bancrio deve continuar a ser, em primeirssimo lugar, uma responsabilidade do prprio banco concedente do crdito, ao invs de o banco simplesmente rodear-se de todo o tipo de garantias e deixar por conta do cliente a responsabilidade de se educar financeiramente, para compreender os riscos que as taxas de juro elevadas, e os prazos relativamente curtos de reembolso podem constituir-se em factor de ameaa  solvabilidade do crdito bancrio. Em alguns pases, h notcias de que o crescimento do crdito malparado  atribudo ao facto de que o cliente, levado por ignorncia em assuntos financeiros, assume compromissos na banca com juros elevadssimos, como se o ao banco concedente do crdito no recasse em primeiro lugar a responsabilidade de verificar, j no acto inicial de elaborao da ficha cadastral do cliente, a absoluta incompatibilidade entre os seus rendimentos salariais e o nvel da dvida que estava a assumir com uma taxa de juros totalmente desfasada da sua capacidade de pagamento. Recomendo pois, que sejam realizados esforos em prol da Educao Financeira dos Angolanos, comeando desde logo com o planeamento financeiro da sua capacidade de pagamento. Distintos Participantes, Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores, O Estudo Banca em Anlise aborda temas da maior importncia no processo de desenvolvimento nacional, para que possamos criar um ambiente e sustentabilidade, quer do crescimento contnuo do produto, quer da dvida pblica, para os quais os verdadeiros fundamentos sero sempre a manuteno da estabilidade da taxa real de cmbio e das taxas de juro ou simplesmente no asseguramento da sua justa flutuao. O compromisso que temos com o futuro do nosso Pas, ainda institucionalmente jovem, pois vamos comemorar 40 anos da nossa independncia, no nos permite abdicar de um esforo cada vez maior para a diversificao da economia e a acelerao do crescimento econmico. S assim podemos assegurar o aumento contnuo do emprego a uma gerao de jovens que tem vindo a aceder de maneira crescente, aos benefcios da educao e dos servios sociais bsicos. Reafirmo o compromisso do Banco Nacional de Angola de continuar a colaborar com o Frum da Banca, atravs de um dilogo transparente sobre a regulao do sistema bancrio, visando proporcionar  clientela os benefcios de uma intermediao financeira eficaz e eficiente, orientada por princpios de Responsabilidade Social, visando apoiar crescimento sustentvel da economia. Agradecendo a ateno de todos, renovo meus cumprimentos aos organizadores deste evento e desejo pleno xito ao dcimo Frum da Banca. Muito obrigado! Title: Speech at the opening of the meeting of the Committee of Governors of the Central Banks of SADC in Angola
text: Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the opening of the meeting of the Governors of the Central Banks of SADC in Angola Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the opening of the meeting of the Committee of Governors of the Central Banks of SADC in Angola Excellencies, Governors Dear Directors Dear Members of the CCBG and SADC Secretariat Ladies and gentlemen, First of all, let me welcome the Most Honorable Governors and all members of the delegations present here and to express our deep satisfaction and honor in hosting this forty-first Meeting of the Committee of Governors of SADC Central Banks. 2015 is undoubtedly a memorable year for our Committee. We welcome because we have achieved twenty years of existence, the year in which coincidentally, Angola celebrates forty years of national independence and thirteen years of peace and National Bank of Angola celebrates thirty-nine years of existence. However, this year has been very challenging for all of us. Our countries continue to face numerous and persistent challenges, related, on the one hand, to the current international situation, marked by uncertainties associated with the fall in food, energy and commodity prices and, on the other hand, higher levels of depreciation and inflation. The current global economic situation therefore raises concerns. But regional integration makes possible to respond to a variety of phenomena that are transversal to member countries, providing a convergence between domestic interests regional regions. It is never too much to remember the importance and role that each of our countries has in the coordinated economic development of the region, as well as for political stabilization and economic macro of our entire community. Only then can we achieve the key objectives outlined for the region, in particular economic growth and development, macroeconomic stability, increased relations with trade agreements between our countries, the eradication of poverty and improving the living standards of our peoples. As in previous years, and under the conduct of The Honorable Governor Lesetja Kganyogo we we're going to be gathered here today for together address issues relevant to our central banks and our economies and in general for all our community. I am fully convinced that our discussions will be fruitful for the definition of sound stability strategies macroeconomic and financial development of our countries. Let us once again observe the the convergence of our economies and consider the reports submitted by each subcommittee and we believe that important recommendations for our countries and our community should leave this meeting. I would like to point out, that in compliance with the guidelines of the CCBG, Angola has prepared a study of Assessment of Financial Stability in the SADC region, whose results we will have the opportunity to share with all of you at this meeting. Today, more than ever and in as a result of the financial crises, we are fully certain that the macroeconomic stability does not necessarily guarantee financial stability. For this reason, we will investigate the extent to which other variables, common to countries, can influence the financial stability of the states of our region. Excellencies, Governors, Ladies and gentlemen, Despite the current unfavourable international situation and the negative impact on many of the our countries need to continue to combine our efforts to achieve the macroeconomic and financial stability of the region and that we move forward firmly towards the integration and harmonisation of our Economies. Thank you very much! 5 Nov. 2015

Title: Speech at the launch of the 50 and 100 Kz coins
text: Public Interventions Address of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the time of launching the coins of 50 and 100 Kz Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the time of the launch of the 50-year coins e 100 Kz Excellencies Mr. Secretary of State for Culture, Mr. Secretary of State for Territory Administration; Ms. Deputy Governor of the BNA Ladies and gentlemen of the BNA Board of Directors Dear Directors, Representatives of the Media Ladies and gentlemen Complying with the competent legislative provision of the National Assembly, the National angola joins the celebrations of the 40th anniversary of the National Independence, putting into circulation two commemorative coins with liberating power 50 and 100 Kz, with the following characteristics: The 50 Kz coin is unicolor, semi-serrated, with metallized color. On the obverse figures the designation " Republic of Angola" and the flag-waving in the National Act to 11 November 1975, an adult element representing a survivor of the Liberation Struggle National Government, a child representing the Angolan Pioneer and a flagof the National Flag with the inscription " 40th Anniversary of National Independence, 1975 - 2015 In reverse, the facial value to the center and the inscription "Kwanzas", the basket would be a symbol of the culture and the year of issue "2015", on the basis. The 100 Kz coin is unicolor, coated in bronze. On the obverse the designation " Republic of Angola", the flag-waving in the act of proclaiming the National Independence on 11 November 1975, an adult element representing a survivor of the of the National Liberation struggle, a child representing the Angolan Pioneer and a flagpole of the National Flag, with the inscription " 40th Anniversary of the National Independence, 1975 - 2015". In reverse, the facial value to the center and the inscription "Kwanzas", the basket would be a symbol of the culture and the year of issue "2015", on the basis. Thus, we have made official today the launch of 50 and 100 Kz coins from the 2012 Series, in the terms of authorization granted to the National Bank of Angola law no. 15/15 of August 21; Despite the slowdown in the pace of economic growth in 2015, due to the sharp and sharp of our main export product, we have an increase in the monetary circulation in the country, particularly in the use of coins and of lower face value notes. The money we use passes more rapidly by various economic actors and even with the remarkable advance of the there are still many cash payments, so there are it is up to us to maintain the conditions of monetary circulation in the appropriate quantity and quality of the needs of the national economy and thereby ensure the comfort of society in the handling of the national currency. The issuance of coins also reveals the BNA's concern with the maintenance of fairer commercial activities. With low-value coins retail traders are more likely and more alternative in terms of setting the price of goods, avoiding their rounding to values, by the absence of means of payment of a lesser denomination. On this special occasion, the National Bank of Angola joins the National Institutions and the People to honor all Angolans who in circumstances extraordinarily difficult, have made it possible to proclaim national independence and committed to the constitutive acts of a new currency, marking the monetary sovereignty of the Republic of Angola Thank you very much Nov. 9 2015
