Title: Speech at the presentation at the National Assembly
text: Public Interventions Address of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose Pedro de Morais Junior, at the presentation at the National Assembly Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose Pedro de Morais Junior, at presentation at the National Assembly GOVERNOR OF THE NATIONAL BANK OF ANGOLA DR. JOSe PEDRO DE MORAIS JuNIOR Luanda, 03 March 2016 Mr President of the Committee on Economics and Finance of the National Assembly; Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen; The National Bank of Angola and the Commercial Banks would like to thank you for the opportunity to be present to this hearing and take the opportunity, to express all the availability and commitment to clarify the issues on the agenda of this session. In recent times the BNA and the national banking system, rightly or without it have been with criticism questioning the goodness of the criteria of its management exchange rate and the accuracy of banking procedures in general. We would like to declare that whenever the criticism seems fair to us, the BNA and the Banks they adjust their procedures and adapt their policies. We are prepared to go the as far as possible in the effort to meet expectations customers. We are penitentiary in relation to all situations in which we fall short of these Expectations. But what the banking system cannot do is promise to distribute advantages and winnings to everyone at no cost to anyone! Mr President, Gentlemen Ladies and gentlemen, The economic climate in 2015, enhanced by the reduction in the price of oil, the main product of export (about 95%) led to a decrease in the number of foreign currency in the country and consequently, lower availability of foreign currency for settlement transactions with the outside world, both at state level and at the companies and individuals. These facts have contributed significantly to the existence of of an imbalance in the foreign exchange market, creating a significant exchange rate that culminated in the depreciation of the national currency. Additionally, the differential between the exchange rates of the formal and informal markets increased consecutively, with at the end of February 2016 set at around 66.7%. Several measures were taken throughout 2015, both in monetary and exchange rate scope. The devaluation of Kwanza, the new market regulations and the management of excess liquidity and the adoption of a mechanism for the sale of foreign exchange to priority segments were the main tools used the BNA for the adjustment of the economy in the current conjuncture. Despite the effort and measures taken by the BNA, there is still a need for vigorous market, which allows the value of the currency to be preserved, by not compromising external solvency and attenuate the current imbalance between the demand excessive in the face of a more limited supply. We intend to show the consequences of the fall in international oil prices on the angolan economy, in particular its impact on the balance of payments, on the country's net international reserves (ril), and on the way of managing by the National Bank of Angola. To this end, we have developed an information base on the current problem related to the currency market, where some components of the Balance of Payments that have pressed external accounts; we describe the current framework foreign exchange market and assess the main measures of the executive branch that generate savings and foreign exchange. When all it predicted that the price of oil would sustain itself at a long time at the level of 100 dollars, the barrel, went abruptly, in the third quarter of 2014, for the range of 50  40, and when we were preparing to start implementing the general budget for 2016, we were surprised by new price shock putting it on a plateau around 30. Thus, the value of our exports fell by 72% between June 2014 and January 2016 and to a decrease in the accumulation of reserves in currency 24.44% in the same period. It is this decrease in foreign currency reserves that has been the cause of the fall in our availability of foreign exchange for the settlement of transactions with the outside world, contributing significantly to the depreciation of Kwanza in the formal market by 59.48% in the period Above. In the informal market, where banknotes are traded, depreciation was 237.38%. The loss of international reserves and the pressure on the foreign exchange market forced the BNA to take restrictive measures on the sale of foreign exchange and adjustment of the exchange rate, in order to safeguard the country's external position. At an early stage, the devaluation of the national currency was the answer found to shield the implementation of the OGE and protect international reserves in the face of the shock in the Oil. The BNA proceeded to three most prominent devaluations (6.0% on 5 June 2015, 6.6% in September 2015 and 15% on 4 January 2016). On the other hand, exchange rate policy has also led to the establishment of the obligation of constitute with the BNA a specific reserve in terms of national currency, of an amount corresponding to the countervalue of foreign currency needs Intended. Consequently, the needs presented banks began to vary at a lower level. In parallel, the BNA in 2015, in addition to the sale of foreign exchange by auction, has now acted the foreign exchange market through sales directed to sectors considered as priorities by the Executive. The difference between the exchange rate in the primary market and the exchange rate in the informal market controllable and of little concern over the years. years, not exceeding 10% by mid-2014. However, as of June 2015 this differential has experienced a growing trend, assuming in the at the end of February 2016 66.7%. Currency devaluation and rising inflation have been the natural result of the substantial fall in our main source of income. The harsh reality is that we get poorer and so we have to adjust. The adjustment is being made through measures adopted by the Executive, through adjustments to the general budget of the state, taking as a reference lower levels for the price of oil. In the foreign exchange market, the adjustment is being made by the BNA, through the rationing of the allocation sold at auction and the attentive conduct of the inevitable process of devaluation of the national currency, induced by excessive demand for foreign exchange. The devaluation of Kwanza reflects the degree of impoverishment of Angola and Angolans, motivated by by reducing the selling price of your main product export. This impoverishment materialises in the temporary rise in domestic prices, which should not be confused with a chronic inflationary process, generated by deficits, financed with currency issuance. It is necessary to make it clear to the whole society that the Executive has sought to isolate the inflationary of this inevitable realignment of relative prices, for example monetary and fiscal policies consistent with the new reality of the price of oil. With monetary policy, the BNA seeks to avoid the occurrence of liquidity excesses in the economic growth in general, and in the financial system, in particular, which generate inflationary pressures in addition to price increases caused by the adjustment of Foreign exchange. With the fiscal policy adjusted to the new levels of tax revenue, public spending reduce to levels more consistent with the new economic reality lived by the country. But some temporary acceleration of inflation becomes inevitable, in situations like the one we are to live in recent times and so even she does not cease to it is also a way of adapting to the fact that we have become poorer. With the same amount of kwanzas, we are buying a smaller amount of goods and services. When we look at our Balance of Payments the Items that most put pressure on the Account Balance Current Transactions are imports of goods and Services. Imports of Goods were on an increasing trend until 2014, when on the basis of estimates for 2015 and projections for 2016 we now experience a decrease in the level of Imports to values close to those in 2011/2012. Imported goods have been mostly of current consumption, and there is no change in the structural structure in the composition of imports over the in recent years. In 2014, imports of consumer goods weighed 58.55% of imports, while imports capital goods (equipment) and consumer goods (raw materials) accounted for 29.44% and 12.01% respectively. Analyzing the import of goods by category, the weight of fuels has registered a marked evolution, rising almost 16 p.p. in the last 8 years, increased fuel consumption at national level, largely due to the practice of fuel consumption heavily subsidised prices. However, imports of fuels in 2015 contracted by around 42%, compared to 2014, associated, on the one hand, with the reduction of domestic consumption as a effect of the elimination of subsidies at prices and, on the other hand, of the lower prices of energy products at international. This reduction has made the weight of fuels in total imports from 17% to 14%. For its part, although more modest, the weight of the import of food has also risen since 2007. It should be said, however, in 2015, food imports contracted 26.6% compared to the previous year. However, this reduction is proportionally lower than the fall in total imports, which led to a 0.7 p.p. increase in the weight of total imports compared to 2014. The services account (import of services) presented in 2014 a deficit of 39.5% of the total balance of payments. In 2015 it is estimated that deficit reduction by 33.6%, while in 2016 a deficit reduction is projected compared to 2015 6,48%. The sectors most important in service imports are: Technical Assistance, whose estimate for 2015 and projection for 2016 represents, respectively, 43.6% and 41.4% of total imports of services; Transport and Travel Services, which in 2015 is estimated to have reached 22.2% and in 2016 it is projected 23.45% of total imports of services; construction, the estimate for 2015 represents 20.7% of total imports of services and the projection for 2016 represents 20.8%; The amount of services imported from these three rubrics represents 86.4% of the total imports of services in 2015. All this has a significant impact on the behaviour of our International Reserves net, which is proposed to remain in 2016, with a level of coverage of 7 months of Imports of Goods and Services. We cannot exhaust our reserves and to put the country in the face of an economic and social crisis of large proportions. What we currently have on foreign exchange reserves does not give us great comfort, but it also does not leave us critical position, of imminent risk. This is a well-accepted level by the international financial and economic community as a way of preserve the country's external solvency, evidenced by the their ability to bear their external commitments. We cannot allow foreign exchange reserves to fall below that amount, no penalty of us being viewed with suspicion on the part of economic agents internal and external, particularly by the international financial community. If this happens, the process of deteriorating the country's foreign exchange situation could worsen may lead to an "acute currency crisis" and the a deep and disorderly recession. Social costs would be dramatic. As a result of this prudential action, in 2015 the National Banking System, in relation to the executed 49% less in goods payments, 44% in invisible currents and 72% less in capital payments. Executions relating to the operations of goods include food, goods of goods and equipment, raw materials and others, with food accounted for 25% of the executions or the use of foreign currency for the payment of goods during the 2015. For current invisible operations, among others, services are included in the provided by non-residents, travel, transfers and income resulting from salaries, capital and financial investments. During 2015, travel and health operations accounted for 20% of the amount transferred relative to operations of invisible currents, while 4% is 76% is attached to services and income. The capital item relates to investments made by residents abroad, the reimbursement of financing contracted abroad, as well as operations of credit, fundamentally, commercial credit. With regard to foreign exchange replacement, it refers to transactions already settled, using the banks, such as international payment cards, and remittances of amounts. It should also be noted that the operations carried out in 2015 related to the telecommunications, television services, airlines and insurance companies were USD 438.66 million, USD 252.37 million, USD 430.02 million and USD 687.91 million million, respectively, totaling the amount of USD 1,808.96 million, representing 10% of the total amount executed. In August of last year, the measures relating to the New Operational Framework foreign exchange market, which can be defined as a group of activities that seek to give greater effectiveness to exchange control. Such activities may be brought together in two main stages: (a) verification of the transactions submitted by the banks, through the Needs Map, at the Presale b) Monitoring the liquidation of operations validated in the after-sales phase. The results of the checks provide the safe settlement of the prioritized operations, which are in appropriate regulatory conditions. There has been, in general, a high percentage of transactions sent by banks that do not are able to be subject to the allocation of for the following most frequent reasons: (a) transactions already settled, in whole or in part; (b) transactions already sold by BNA in another auction; and c) Franchise Number (Authorization of MINCO for Goods) /BAPIC (BNA authorization for incompatible with the records. The monitoring of the liquidation of validated transactions only gained robustness from January/2016, considering the availability to the BNA of the copy of swift system messages. From the information provided it became possible to verify the reliability of the information provided by banks in the systems, Integrated System of Foreign Exchange Operations - SINOC and SSIF - Financial Institutions Supervision System, ensuring confirmation of the destination of the currencies acquired from the BNA. Although recent, there are gains in the quality of the information provided, considering the perception of the banks in a more accurate follow-up of the BNA, supported by swift messages linked to each operation. On a weekly basis, banks inform bna of the respective stock of transactions to be executed, through the Needs Map, where the characteristics of each transaction pending payment or remittance abroad. The sale of foreign currency by the National Bank of Angola to Commercial Banks takes place through targeted auction or sales sessions, with the the process of allocating the currencies has been improved from this year onwith the creation of the Subcommittee on Foreign Exchange Operations (SOC), which participates in the Board of Directors of Management of the BNA and Directors with attributions linked to the execution of the Exchange Rate Policy. It is up to the Subcommittee to define the frequency of auctions, their objectives, according to the sectors of the economy considered as priorities by the Executive and the amount of foreign exchange to be sold at each session. Once the amount to be sold has been defined by the SOC, a price auction is held in which the amount repaid by each bank. Defined the assignment of each bank, they inform the BNA of the transactions they intend to allocate to that amount of money, starting with the the process of verifying the records of these operations by the bna, which wishes to ensure the appropriate destination of the currencies allocated in accordance with the objectives defined for each sales session. Mr President, Gentlemen Ladies and gentlemen, In the medium and long term the solution is the diversification of the Angolan production structure. The devaluation of the national currency, if, on the one hand, generates some sacrifice, by the temporary increase domestic prices, on the other hand, contributes to making it feasible to be produced in Angola. Many products, previously imported, can now be produced internally, relieving external dependence on the Angolan economy. However, you can't change that situation overnight. This is a medium- and long-term objective that has been on the executive's agenda since the end of of war and that is being intensified in the current circumstances. In this sense, the period of currency scarcity, through which we are going, can be considered, also an opportunity for investments to be made to diversify the country's productive structure. In the framework of the Exit from Crisis Strategy drawn up by the Executive, we consider in particular relevant to the stability of the national financial sector, Measures to: Control the hiring of technical assistance abroad, also ensured by the real transmission of knowledge to national frameworks; In the medium-long term encourage national fuel production as this is the product with greater weight of imports; Harness the country's enormous agricultural, fishing, hydraulic and energy potential scans to reduce dependence on imported products and produce products Exportable; Create conditions for the development of tourism that provides the entry of foreign exchange; Penalise the import of non-essential (or luxury) goods and food products the production of which may be carried out domestically; Do not penalise the importation of goods and services necessary for domestic production, in particular raw materials; Create conditions that facilitate the hiring of expatriate skilled labour, which is essential to the economic development process; Develop attractive conditions for increasing foreign investment in the country that provides the entry of resources in foreign currency and simultaneously contribute to the development of the production system; Develop enabling conditions for business creation in the country, particularly by implementing the actions identified in the context of improving the Business Index Thank you so much for your attention. 10 mar. 2016

JOS PEDRO DE MORAIS JNIOR Luanda, 03 de Maro de 2016 Excelentssimo Senhor Presidente da Comisso de Economia e Finanas da Assembleia Nacional; Excelentssimos Senhores Deputados, minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores; O Banco Nacional de Angola e os Bancos Comerciais gostariam de agradecer a oportunidade de estar presente a esta audincia e aproveitam, para manifestar toda a disponibilidade e empenho para clarificar as matrias constantes da agenda desta sesso. Nos ltimos tempos o BNA e o sistema bancrio nacional, com razo ou sem ela tm sido fustigados com crticas questionando a bondade dos critrios da sua gesto cambial e o rigor dos procedimentos das operaes bancrias em geral. Gostaramos de declarar que sempre que as crticas nos parecem justas, o BNA e os Bancos Comerciais ajustam os seus procedimentos e adaptam as suas polticas. Estamos preparados para ir o mais longe possvel no esforo da satisfao das expectativas dos Clientes. Penitenciamo-nos em relao a todas as situaes em que ficaremos aqum destas expectativas. Mas o que o sistema bancrio no pode fazer,  prometer distribuir vantagens e ganhos para todos sem custos para ningum! Senhor Presidente, Senhores Deputados, Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores, A conjuntura econmica em 2015, potenciada pela reduo do preo do petrleo, principal produto de exportao (cerca de 95%) levou a uma diminuio da entrada de moeda estrangeira no pas e consequentemente, menor disponibilidade de divisas para liquidao das transaces com o exterior, quer a nvel do estado quer a nvel das empresas e particulares. Estes factos contriburam significativamente para a existncia de um desequilibro no mercado cambial, criando uma presso cambial significativa que culminou na depreciao da moeda nacional. Adicionalmente, o diferencial entre as taxas de cmbio dos mercados formal e informal aumentou consecutivamente, estando em final de Fevereiro de 2016 fixado em torno de 66,7%. Vrias foram as medidas tomadas ao longo de 2015 quer de mbito monetrio, quer de mbito cambial. A desvalorizao do Kwanza, as novas regulaes do mercado cambial e da gesto da liquidez excedentria e a adopo de um mecanismo da venda de divisas a segmentos prioritrios foram as principais ferramentas utilizadas pelo BNA para o ajustamento da economia na conjuntura actual. No obstante o esforo e as medidas tomadas pelo BNA, persiste a necessidade de uma interveno vigorosa no mercado, que permita preservar o valor da moeda, no comprometendo a solvabilidade externa e atenue o actual desequilbrio entre a procura que continua excessiva face a uma oferta mais limitada. Pretendemos mostrar as consequncias da queda dos preos internacionais do petrleo sobre a economia angolana, em especial o seu impacto sobre a balana de pagamentos, sobre as reservas internacionais lquidas (ril) do pas, e sobre o modo de gesto cambial pelo Banco Nacional de Angola. Para o efeito desenvolvemos uma base informativa sobre a problemtica actual relacionada com o mercado de divisas, onde se analisam algumas componentes da Balana de Pagamentos que tm pressionado as contas externas; descrevemos o actual quadro operacional do mercado cambial e avaliamos as principais medidas do Executivo que geram poupanas e divisas. Quando tudo fazia prever que o preo do petrleo iria sustentar-se, longamente, no patamar dos 100 dlares, o barril, passou abruptamente, no 3 trimestre de 2014, para o intervalo de 50  40 dlares, e quando nos preparvamos para comear a implementar o oramento geral do estado para 2016, fomos surpreendidos com novo choque no preo colocando-o num patamar ao redor do 30 dlares. Assim, o valor das nossas exportaes baixou 72% entre Junho de 2014 e Janeiro de 2016 tendo levado a uma diminuio da acumulao de reservas em moeda externa de menos 24,44% no mesmo perodo.  esta diminuio das reservas em moeda externa que tem sido a causa da queda das nossas disponibilidades de divisas para liquidao das transaces com o exterior, contribuindo significativamente para a depreciao do Kwanza no mercado formal em 59,48% no perodo acima referido. No mercado informal, onde so transaccionadas notas, a depreciao foi de 237,38%. A perda de reservas internacionais e a presso sobre o mercado cambial obrigou o BNA  tomada de medidas restritivas na venda de divisas e de ajustamento da taxa de cmbio, visando salvaguardar a posio externa do Pas. Num momento inicial, a desvalorizao da moeda nacional foi a resposta encontrada para blindar a execuo do OGE e proteger as Reservas Internacionais face ao choque ocorrido no sector petrolfero. O BNA procedeu a trs desvalorizaes de maior destaque (6,0% a 5 de Junho de 2015, 6,6% em Setembro de 2015 e 15% a 4 de Janeiro de 2016). Por outro lado, a poltica cambial levou tambm ao estabelecimento da obrigao dos bancos comerciais de constiturem junto do BNA uma reserva especfica em moeda nacional, de montante correspondente ao contravalor das necessidades de moeda estrangeira pretendida. Consequentemente, as necessidades apresentadas pelos bancos comearam a variar num patamar mais baixo. Em paralelo o BNA no ano de 2015, para alm da venda de divisas por leilo, passou a ter uma actuao no mercado cambial atravs de vendas dirigidas a sectores considerados como prioritrios pelo Executivo. O diferencial entre a taxa de cmbio no mercado primrio e a taxa de cmbio no mercado informal apresentou nveis controlveis e pouco preocupantes ao longo dos ltimos anos, no ultrapassando 10% at meados de 2014. Contudo, a partir de Junho de 2015 este diferencial conheceu uma tendncia crescente, assumindo no final de Fevereiro de 2016 66,7%. A desvalorizao cambial e o aumento da inflao tm sido o resultado natural da queda substancial na nossa principal fonte de rendimento. A dura realidade  que ficamos mais pobres e por isso temos de nos ajustar. O ajustamento est a ser feito por intermdio de medidas adoptadas pelo executivo, atravs de ajustes ao oramento geral do estado, tomando-se como referncia nveis mais baixos para o preo do petrleo. No mercado cambial, o ajustamento est a ser feito pelo BNA, mediante o racionamento da alocao das divisas vendidas em leilo e a conduo atenta do inevitvel processo de desvalorizao da moeda nacional, induzido pelo excesso de procura por divisas. A desvalorizao do Kwanza reflecte o grau de empobrecimento de Angola e dos angolanos, motivado pela reduo do preo de venda do seu principal produto exportao. Esse empobrecimento materializa-se na elevao temporria dos preos internos, que no deve ser confundida com um processo inflacionista crnico, gerado por dfices fiscais, financiados com emisso de moeda.  preciso deixar claro para toda a sociedade que o Executivo tem procurado isolar o processo inflacionista desse inevitvel realinhamento de preos relativos, por meio de polticas monetria e fiscal consistentes com a nova realidade do preo do petrleo. Com a poltica monetria, o BNA procura evitar a ocorrncia de excessos de liquidez no sistema econmico, em geral, e no sistema financeiro, em particular, que possam gerar presses inflacionistas adicionais aos aumentos de preos provocados pelo ajuste cambial. Com a poltica fiscal ajustada aos novos patamares da receita tributria, os gastos pblicos reduzem-se para nveis mais condizentes com a nova realidade econmica vivida pelo pas. Mas, alguma acelerao temporria da inflao torna-se inevitvel, em situaes como a que estamos a viver nos ltimos tempos e por isso mesmo ela no deixa de ser, tambm, uma forma de nos adaptarmos ao facto de termos ficado mais pobres. Com a mesma quantidade de kwanzas, estamos a comprar uma menor quantidade de mercadorias e servios. Quando olhamos para a nossa Balana de Pagamentos as Rubricas que mais pressionam o Saldo da Conta de Transaces Correntes so as Importaes de Bens e Servios. As importaes de Bens estavam a registar uma tendncia crescente at 2014, altura em que com base nas estimativas para 2015 e nas projeces para 2016 passamos a registar uma diminuio do nvel de Importaes para valores prximos aos ocorridos em 2011/2012. Os bens importados tm sido maioritariamente de consumo corrente, no se verificando uma alterao estrutural na composio das importaes ao longo dos ltimos anos. Em 2014, a importao de bens de consumo pesava 58,55% das importaes, enquanto os bens de capital (equipamento) e os bens de consumo intermdio (matrias primas) representavam 29,44% e 12,01% respectivamente. Analisando a importao de bens por categoria verifica-se que o peso dos combustveis registou uma evoluo acentuada, subindo quase 16 p.p. nos ltimos 8 anos, fruto do aumento do consumo de combustveis a nvel nacional, em grande parte devido a prtica de preos fortemente subvencionados. Contudo, as importaes de combustveis em 2015 contraram cerca de 42%, comparativamente a 2014, associado, por um lado,  reduo do consumo interno por efeito da eliminao das subvenes a preos e, por outro, da baixa dos preos dos produtos energticos a nvel internacional. Esta reduo fez com que o peso dos combustveis no total das importaes descesse de 17% para 14%. Por seu lado, apesar de mais modesta, o peso da importao de alimentos tambm tem subido desde 2007. Refira-se, entretanto, que em 2015, as importaes de alimentos contraram 26,6% em relao ao ano anterior. Contudo esta reduo  proporcionalmente inferior  queda das importaes totais, o que levou a uma subida de 0,7 p.p. no peso das importaes totais face a 2014. A conta de servios (importao de servios) apresentou em 2014 um dfice de 39,5% da totalidade de dbitos da Balana de Pagamentos. Em 2015 estima-se uma reduo do dfice em 33,6%, enquanto em 2016 se projecta uma reduo do dfice face a 2015 de 6,48%. Os sectores com mais importncia nas importaes de servios so: Assistncia Tcnica, cuja estimativa para 2015 e projeco para 2016 representa, respectivamente, 43,6% e 41,4% das importaes totais de servios; Servios de Transporte e Viagens, que em 2015 se estima tenha atingido 22,2% e em 2016 se projecta venha a atingir 23,45%, das importaes totais de servios; Construo, cuja estimativa para 2015 representa 20,7% das importaes totais de servios e a projeco para 2016 representa 20,8%; O montante de servios importados destas trs rbricas representa 86,4% das importaes totais de servios em 2015. Tudo isto tem um impacto significativo no comportamento das nossas Reservas Internacionais Lquidas, que est proposto manterem-se em 2016, com um nvel de cobertura de 7 meses de Importaes de Bens e Servios. No podemos esgotar as nossas reservas e colocar o pas diante de uma crise econmica e social de grandes propores. O que temos actualmente de reservas cambiais no nos d grande conforto, mas, tambm, no nos deixa em posio crtica, de risco iminente. Trata-se de um nvel bem aceite pela comunidade financeira e econmica internacional, como forma de preservar a solvabilidade externa do pas, evidenciada pela sua capacidade de arcar com os seus compromissos externos. No podemos deixar que as reservas cambiais caiam abaixo daquele valor, sob pena de passarmos a ser vistos com desconfiana, por parte dos agentes econmicos internos e externos, particularmente por parte da comunidade financeira internacional. Se isso vier a acontecer, o processo de deteriorao da situao cambial do pas poder agravar-se rapidamente, podendo levar-nos a uma "crise cambial aguda" e a uma recesso profunda e desordenada. Os custos sociais seriam dramticos. Como resultado desta actuao prudencial, em 2015 o Sistema Bancrio Nacional, em relao ao ano anterior, executou menos 49% em pagamentos de mercadorias, menos 44% em invisveis correntes e menos 72% em pagamentos de capitais. As execues relativas s operaes de mercadorias contemplam bens alimentares, bens de equipamento, matrias-primas e outras, sendo que os bens alimentares representaram 25% das execues ou da utilizao das divisas para pagamento de mercadorias durante o ano de 2015. Relativamente s operaes de invisveis correntes, esto includas entre outras, servios prestados por no residentes, viagens, transferncias e rendimentos decorrentes de salrios, capital e de aplicaes financeiras. Durante o ano de 2015, as operaes de viagens e sade representaram 20% do montante transferido relativo as operaes de invisveis correntes, enquanto 4% se refere a transferncias e 76% est adstrito a servios e rendimentos. A rubrica capital reporta-se a investimentos realizados por residentes no exterior, a reembolso de financiamentos contrados no exterior, bem como operaes de crdito, fundamentalmente, crdito comercial. No que concerne  reposio cambial, refere-se as operaes j liquidadas, com recurso dos prprios bancos, como cartes de pagamento internacional, operaes de crdito e remessas de valores. Importa ainda referir, que as operaes executadas no ano de 2015, relacionadas ao sector de telecomunicaes, servios de televiso, companhias areas e seguradoras, foram de USD 438,66 milhes, USD 252,37 milhes, USD 430,02 milhes e USD 687,91 milhes respectivamente, perfazendo o montante de USD 1.808,96 milhes, representando 10% do montante total executado. No ms de Agosto do ano transacto implementaram-se as medidas relativas ao Novo Quadro Operacional do Mercado Cambial, que podem ser definidas como um conjunto de actividades que buscam dar maior eficcia ao Controle Cambial. Tais actividades podem ser reunidas em duas etapas principais: a) Verificao das operaes apresentadas pelos bancos, atravs do Mapa de Necessidades, na fase pr-venda, b) Acompanhamento da liquidao das operaes validadas na fase ps-venda. Os resultados das verificaes proporcionam a liquidao segura das operaes priorizadas, que se encontram em condies regulamentares adequadas. Tem-se observado, de forma geral, um elevado percentual de operaes enviadas pelos Bancos que no apresentam condies de serem objecto de atribuio de divisas, pelas seguintes razes mais frequentes: a) Operaes j liquidadas, total ou parcialmente; b) Operaes j objecto de venda pelo BNA em outro leilo; e c) Nmero de Franquia (autorizao do MINCO para mercadorias) /BAPIC (autorizao do BNA para invisveis) incompatveis com os registos. O acompanhamento da liquidao das operaes validadas s ganhou robustez a partir de Janeiro/2016, considerando a disponibilidade para o BNA da cpia de mensagens do Sistema Swift. A partir das informaes disponibilizadas tornou-se possvel verificar a confiabilidade das informaes prestadas pelos bancos nos sistemas, Sistema Integrado de Operaes Cambiais - SINOC e SSIF- Sistema de Superviso das Instituies Financeiras, garantindo assim a confirmao do destino das divisas adquiridas ao BNA. Embora recente, observam-se ganhos na qualidade das informaes prestadas, considerando a percepo dos bancos num mais acurado acompanhamento do BNA, apoiado nas mensagens Swift vinculadas a cada operao. Semanalmente, os bancos informam ao BNA o respectivo stock de operaes a executar, atravs de Mapa de Necessidades, onde so apresentadas as caractersticas de cada operao pendente de pagamento ou de remessa ao exterior. A venda de moeda estrangeira pelo Banco Nacional de Angola aos Bancos Comerciais ocorre atravs de sesses de leiles ou vendas direccionadas, tendo o processo de atribuio das divisas sido melhorado a partir do corrente ano com a criao do Subcomit de Operaes Cambiais (SOC), onde participa o Conselho de Administrao do BNA e Directores com atribuies vinculadas  execuo da Poltica Cambial. Cabe ao Subcomit definir a frequncia dos leiles, seus objectivos, segundo as finalidades e sectores da economia considerados prioritrios pelo Executivo e o montante de divisas a ser vendido em cada sesso. Uma vez definido pelo SOC o montante a vender, processa-se um leilo de preos em que  apurado o montante arrematado por cada banco. Definida a atribuio de cada banco, estes informam ao BNA as operaes que pretendem afectar  referida verba, iniciando-se o processo de verificao dos registos destas operaes pelo BNA, que pretende assegurar o destino adequado das divisas atribudas de acordo com os objectivos definidos para cada sesso de venda. Senhor Presidente, Senhores Deputados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, No mdio e longo prazo a soluo  a diversificao da estrutura produtiva angolana. A desvalorizao da moeda nacional, se, de um lado, gera algum sacrifcio, pelo aumento temporrio nos preos internos, por outro, contribui para tornar vivel produzir-se em angola. Muitos produtos, antes importados, agora podero ser produzidos internamente, aliviando a dependncia externa da economia angolana. Entretanto, no se consegue mudar essa situao da noite para o dia. Trata-se de um objectivo de mdio e longo prazo que tem estado na agenda do executivo desde o fim da guerra e que est a ser intensificado nas actuais circunstncias. Neste sentido, o perodo de escassez de divisas, pelo qual estamos a passar, pode ser considerado, tambm, uma oportunidade para a realizao de investimentos destinados a diversificar a estrutura produtiva do pas. No quadro da Estratgia da Sada da Crise elaborada pelo Executivo consideramos particularmente relevantes para a estabilidade do sector financeiro nacional, as medidas tendentes a: Controlar a contratao de assistncia tcnica ao exterior, velando-se igualmente pela real transmisso de conhecimento aos quadros nacionais; A mdio-longo prazo incentivar a produo nacional de combustveis uma vez que este  o produto com maior peso das importaes; Aproveitar os enormes potenciais agrcola, piscatrio, hidrulico e energtico do pas para reduzir a dependncia de produtos importados e produzir produtos exportveis; Criar condies para o desenvolvimento do turismo que proporcione a entrada de divisas; Penalizar a importao de bens no essenciais (ou de luxo) e bens alimentares cuja produo pode ser efectuada domesticamente; No penalizar a importao de bens e servios necessrios para a produo nacional, nomeadamente matrias-primas; Criar condies que facilitem a contratao de mo-de-obra especializada expatriada, essencial ao processo de desenvolvimento econmico; Desenvolver condies atractivas para o aumento do investimento estrangeiro no pas que proporcione a entrada de recursos em moeda externa e em simultneo contribua para o desenvolvimento do sistema produtivo; Desenvolver condies facilitadoras da criao de negcios no pas, implementando particularmente as aces identificadas, no mbito da melhoria do Doing Business Index Muito obrigado pela Vossa ateno. Title: Speech at the opening of the Seminar on Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing
text: Speech by the Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Suzana Camacho Monteiro, at the opening of the Seminar on Money Laundering Prevention and Financing terrorism Speech by the Deputy Governor of Banco Naciona Angola, Suzana Camacho Monteiro, at opening of the Seminar on Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of the Terrorism Mr. Members of the Board of Directors llustres Directors, Managers and senior employees of Banca Comercial Ladies and gentlemen, First of all, on behalf of the National Bank of Angola I thank you for the presence of all participants in this Seminar on the Prevention of money laundering and the fight against terrorist financing, a meeting that marks the continuity of the cycle of workshops initiated by the BNA, with the aim of interaction with commercial banking. Considering the relevance of the subject to the Angolan Financial System and the need for more effective practice to ensure the recognition and confidence of markets at national and international level, the National Bank of Angola carries out once further, awareness-raising action on the prevention of Money laundering and the fight against terrorist financing in the Financial System. The level of satisfaction issued by commercial banks, as well as requests for continuity of meetings of this nature, indicate the common interest in the face of the challenges currently faced. It is based on the fact that in the last 5 years, the BNA has been playing a key role in the National Financial System in policy improvement matters internal proceedings on the prevention of money laundering and the fight against money laundering, financing of terrorism, in particular: The publication of the underlying regulation, with regulatory requirements aligned with the requirements fatf-fati, both for the international institutions Banking financial institutions, as well as for non-bank financial institutions; The publication of practical implementation guides that facilitate the interpretation of regulation in a clearer and more operational logic; The preparation of continuous work of off-site supervision with the IFs, through various initiatives: Self-assessment questionnaires and AML chapter of the reports annual GC/SCI, prudential follow-up meetings, on-site supervision initiatives, issuing letters of recommendation; The realization of dissemination workshops for Banking and non-bank financial institutions. Thus, on the basis of legislative efforts and actions, the BNA played a key role in order to January 2016, Angola is no longer on the Grey List of the fatf, and is now considered a cooperating country, and therefore no longer needing the quarterly monitoring by FATF. In this sense, the SFA must continue its path of deepening prevention practices bc/ft, and in this context it is part of this seminar. The aim is to be jointly perceived with the commercial banking so that the our Country's Financial Statements, experience effective implementation prevention processes of BC/FT, with the proper evidence of compliance and performance, in several of the BC/FT obligations, in the process of achieving an effective "Risk-Based Approach". I am accompanied by the Managers of the Departments of Prudential Supervision and Regulation and Organization and Norms of the BNA, which for 2 hours will speak on this subject, with an enhancement to the existing challenges, the progress achieved by the BNA in prevention of BC/FT, and the next steps. I wish you all the best use, so that the objectives advocated here are achieved in the Full. I declare this session open. Aug. 4. 2016

Membros do Conselho de Administrao llustres Directores, Gestores e altos funcionrios da Banca Comercial Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Antes de mais, em nome do Banco Nacional de Angola agradeo a presena de todos os participantes no presente Seminrio referente  Preveno do branqueamento de capitais e luta contra o financiamento do terrorismo, encontro que marca a continuidade do ciclo de workshops iniciados pelo BNA, com o intuito de uma maior interaco com a banca Comercial. Considerando a relevncia do assunto para o Sistema Financeiro Angolano e a necessidade de reforo a uma prtica mais efectiva para garantir o reconhecimento e a confiana dos mercados a nvel nacional e internacional, o Banco Nacional de Angola realiza uma vez mais, a aco de sensibilizao sobre a preveno do Branqueamento de capitais e luta contra o financiamento ao terrorismo no Sistema financeiro. O nvel de satisfao emitido pelos Bancos Comerciais, bem como as solicitaes para a continuidade de encontros dessa natureza, indicam o interesse comum face os desafios enfrentados actualmente.  facto assente que nos ltimos 5 anos, o BNA tem vindo a desempenhar um papel fundamental no Sistema Financeiro nacional em matrias de melhoria de polticas e de processos internos sobre a preveno do Branqueamento de capitais e a luta contra o financiamento ao terrorismo, nomeadamente: A Publicao de regulao subjacente, com os requisitos regulamentares alinhados com s exigncias internacionais do FATF-GAFI, quer para as Instituies Financeiras bancrias, como para Instituies Financeiras no bancrias; A Publicao de guias prticos de implementao que facilitassem a interpretao da regulao numa lgica mais clara e operacional; A elaborao de Trabalhos contnuos de superviso off-site com as IFs, atravs de vrias iniciativas: Questionrios de auto-avaliao e captulo de AML dos relatrios anuais de GC/SCI, reunies prudenciais de acompanhamento, iniciativas de superviso on-site, emisso de cartas de recomendao; A realizao de Workshops de divulgao para Instituies Financeiras Bancrias e no bancrias. Assim, com base nos esforo legislativo e de aces, o BNA exerceu um papel fulcral, para que em Janeiro de 2016, Angola deixasse de constar na Lista Cinzenta do GAFI, passando a ser considerado um Pas cooperante, e por conseguinte deixando de necessitar da monitorizao trimestral pelo GAFI. Neste sentido o SFA deve prosseguir com o seu percurso de aprofundamento de prticas de preveno de BC/FT, sendo neste contexto que se enquadra o presente seminrio. O objectivo  de percepo conjunta com a banca comercial para que as Intituies Financeiras do nosso Pais, experimentem uma implementao efectiva de processos de preveno de BC/FT, com as devidas evidncias de cumprimento e realizao, em vrias das obrigaes de BC/FT, para que se atinja uma eficaz Abordagem Baseada no Risco. Fao-me acompanhar pelos Gestores dos Departamentos de Superviso Prudencial e de Regulao e Organizao e Normas do BNA, que durante 2 horas falaro sobre essa matria, com realce para os desafios existentes, os progressos atingidos pelo BNA na preveno do BC/FT, e os prximos passos. Desejo a todos o melhor aproveitamento, para que os objectivos aqui preconizados sejam atingidos na ntegra. Declaro aberta a presente sesso. Title: Speech at the opening of the lecture on "The History of Kwanza"
text: Public Interventions Address by the Governor, Valter Filipe da Silva, at the opening of the lecture on "The History of Kwanza" Speech by the Governor, Valter Filipe da Silva, at the opening of the lecture on "The History of First Honourable Members of the Angolan Executive, Very honorable members of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola, Distinguished Heads of Financial Institutions, Dear guests, ladies and gentlemen. The present ceremony that marks the 40th anniversary of the National Currency is a moment solemn that allows us to symbolize the occasion and mark a moment of great reflection, on this great historical and cultural heritage that is our Currency, symbol of our nation's sovereignty. Let me convey to you the past that this day represents, quoting the words of the founder of the Angolan nation, Dr. Antonio Agostinho Neto, at the time of the launch of the national currency, the Kwanza: "... it is necessary to reach a complete independence, not only to have another flag, to have a another hymn, to have a President of the Republic, but to have all the elements that may constitute an independent country. And now from a monetary point of view, we are also independent..." As in several countries, Angola's currency has seen several forms of over time, but always associated with the different moments of the socio-economic and political context of the country. Thinking about the trajectory of our currency, the Kwanza, it is imperative to associate it with the economic path of nation, highlighting the following historical milestones that have led us to the transformations registered in 1990 (Novo Kwanza), 1995 (Kwanza Readjusted), 1999 (Kwanza) and more recently, in 2013, the withdrawal from circulation of the 1999 series and the launch of the New family of Banknotes and Coins and Kwanza. In addition, the trajectory of our Currency allows us to make an incursion into the challenges related to the use of payment instruments in order to make the Kwanza increasingly adjusted to the intrinsic functions of the currency as a means of exchange, of payment and value reserve. Forecasts for 2016 point to a slowdown in world trade, especially in advanced economies, with impacts on the level of imports from 4.3% to 3.4% and exports from 3.4% to 2.5%, denoting that some remain risks to the development of world trade. In the national landscape, the monetary policy implemented by the BNA combined with fiscal policy and remained cautious in response to the monitoring of the inflation observed. In 2016, the Monetary Policy Committee of the National Bank of Angola, in order to to halt the inflationary process, adjusted the rates in the Second half of 201, increasing the BNA Rate from 12.00% to 16.00% per year, the liquidity-of-14.00% for the Liquidity Withdrawal Facility for 20.00% and the 7-day Liquidity Absorption Facility Rate (FAL 7 days) from 2.25% to 7.25% and increased compulsory expenditure, this policy has contributed to the to dry up the liquidity of the market, significantly, which has allowed the course of slowdown in monthly inflation in recent months. Angola is currently experiencing a scenario of implementing the process of diversifying the economy as fundamental precondition for the development and prosperity. This process certainly involves the development of agriculture and the strengthening the productive sector throughout the country. For the effect it will be necessary to ensure the maintenance of the functions of the national currency as a means of exchange, unit of account, reserve of value and savings instrument, of investment and credit The National Development Plan accurately underlines the crucial role of the private sector as a driving factor for economic growth. They are described various objectives and policies to facilitate access to credit, supports the nascent industry, creates conditions for increasing the supply of financial services to population in a safe and efficient manner, as well as to create the primary conditions for the formalisation of informal economy. In the current economic scenario, the the exercise of macroeconomic policy in general and monetary policy in particular in the management of its instruments, guarantors of price stability is an important component among policies promoting economic growth, assessed by the impact on investment decisions, ensuring the employment as well as a more appropriate distribution of available resources. To the National Bank of Angola, as an issuer and responsible for preserving the value of the national government, it is the honorable responsibility for the guarantee of stability of the value of the national currency, OUR KWANZA, which will certainly be the instrument spiritual and material to provide the necessary credit, boost export, agricultural, industrial production to boost the economy and provide credit for housing, car credit, consumer credit and microcredit for more than 75% of Angolan households have a middle-class social and economic level. It is kwanza the guarantor of our prosperity Congratulations to Kwanza 24 Jan. 2017

Title: Speech at the Seminar on Foreign Exchange Operations
text: Public Interventions Speech by Mr. Administrator, Dr. Victor Costa e Silva, at the Seminar on Foreign Exchange Operations Speech by Mr. Administrator, Dr. Victor Costa and Silva, at the Seminar on Foreign Exchange Operations Ladies and gentlemen of the Boards of Directors and technicians of commercial banks Mr. Representative of ABANC Distinguished representatives of the Ministries of Economy and Trade and the National Alfandegas Ladies and gentlemen Arriving at the end of this seminar, we would like on behalf of Dr. Jose Massano Governor of the National Government of Angola, to thank once again for the presence of and to praise the interest raised and the lively participation in the topics addressed. The National Bank of Angola believes that we should use every opportunity to leave the institutional domain and transmit and share with society, that that society matters, informing it and listening to its opinions. The legislation appreciated here is quite recent and we understand that its internalisation has not yet been has reached all economic actors, including banking institutions that with this regulatory framework should exercise greater oversight of the your customers. It is time to ask for the greatest commitment of all, because what is ultimately intended is ensure greater transparency, so that the currencies that the country is effectively used for the payment of goods and services under the conditions transactions to bring effective benefits to the country. The improvement of the country's insertion in international trade depended in fact on some changes in the procedure in foreign exchange matters. The term external insertion of the economy has two dimensions: commercial flows of goods and services from the country with the rest of the world; and the financial one that refers to capital movements between the domestic and foreign economy. It is these two dimensions that the legislation assessed here comes better regular, so that establish an effectively biunivocal relationship. The pattern of external insertion of the Angolan economy (which as we know has always been an open economy, both trade and capital flows) is not has changed. What has changed is the depth and size, which we want or not, if intensified in recent years, as a result of the end of hostilities and the climate conducive to economic development, on the one hand, and the gradual increase in export volumes and the price of oil in the international markets, on the other. We hope that from this seminar we have all come out stronger, so that the planning, management and implementation of the procedures for exchange rates can be carried out in accordance with universally accepted rules, strengthening the integration of the country into the global economic and financial context and contributing to the consolidation of macroeconomic stability. Thank you very much 10 Jul. 2012

Entende o Banco Nacional de Angola que devemos utilizar todas as oportunidades para deixar o domnio institucional e transmitir e partilhar com a sociedade, aquilo que  sociedade interessa, informando-a e em contrapartida ouvindo as suas opinies. A legislao aqui apreciada,  bastante recente e compreendemos que a sua interiorizao ainda no tenha atingido todos os agentes econmicos, incluindo as instituies bancrias que com esse quadro normativo devem exercer uma maior fiscalizao junto dos seus clientes.  o momento de solicitarmos o maior empenho de todos, pois o que se pretende em ltima instncia  assegurar maior transparncia, de modo que as divisas que saem do Pas sirvam efectivamente para o pagamento das mercadorias e servios nas condies definidas e que as transaces tragam benefcios efectivos ao Pas. O aprimoramento da insero do pas no comrcio internacional dependia na verdade de algumas alteraes de procedimento em matria cambial. O termo insero externa da economia comporta duas dimenses: a comercial, que diz respeito aos fluxos de bens e servios do pas com o resto do mundo; e a financeira que se refere aos movimentos de capitais entre a economia domstica e o exterior. So essas duas dimenses que a legislao aqui apreciada vem melhor regular, de modo que se estabelea uma relao efectivamente biunvoca. O padro de insero externa da economia angolana (que como sabemos sempre foi uma economia aberta, tanto aos fluxos de comrcio quanto os de capital) no se tem alterado. O que se tem alterado  a profundidade e dimenso, que quer queiramos, quer no, se intensificou nos ltimos anos, em decorrncia do fim das hostilidades e do clima propcio ao desenvolvimento econmico, por um lado, e do aumento paulatino dos volumes de exportao e do preo do petrleo nos mercados internacionais, por outro. Fazemos votos, que deste seminrio tenhamos sado todos mais fortalecidos, de modo que o planeamento, a gesto e a execuo dos procedimentos das operaes cambiais possam ser realizados de acordo com regras universalmente aceites, reforando o processo de insero do Pas no contexto econmico-financeiro mundial e colaborando na consolidao da estabilidade macroeconmica. Title: Speech at the opening ceremony of the Bank of China branch in Angola
text: Public Interventions Address of the Governor at the ceremony opening of the Bank of China's branch in Angola Speech by the Governor at the opening of the Bank of China's branch in Angola His Excellency Minister of State and Head of the House of Security, General Helder Vieira Dias; - His Excellency Minister and Head of the Civil House, Dr. Cruz Neto; - His Excellency Minister of Finance, Dr. Archer Mangueira; - His Excellency Minister of Foreign Affairs, Dr. Jorge Chicoty; - His Excellency State Advisor of the People's Republic of China, Mr. Wang Yong; - His Excellency President of the Bank of China, Mr. Chen Siqing; Your Honours, Members of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola; Distinguished Guests; Ladies and gentlemen; On behalf of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola, I would like to congratulate the bank of China, by the brilliant initiative to open branch of this bank in Angola that joins the other banking institutions that already operate in the the provision of new banking services. It is with pleasure and honor that we accept the invitation to participate in the inauguration ceremony of the China's first commercial bank in Angola, which contributes to harmonious and further development of the relations of friendship and cooperation between the Republic of Angola and the People's Republic of China, founded on strategic economic partnership, with reciprocal benefits for the two countries. I believe that we all consider the importance of today, for example, represent a major contribution in increasing relations between the Republic of Angola and the People's Republic of China, which have its highest point when funding is needed reconstruction and development of Angola. Excellencies It is not too much to emphasize that the presence of the Bank of China in Angola is an added value for the whole angolan financial system, and in particular for the angolan financial system banking, since, with the other commercial banks on the market, it will also facilitate trade between Angola and China that have reached of around USD 19.7 billion in 2015, however, the shock that affected the our economy, with the economic crisis and international financial policy. The opening of this bank thus strengthens this relationship and contributes to the increase in credit, domestic production and export, necessary for the increase of exchange rate needs; The initiative now consummated is also the result of a set of financial diplomacy actions that been held by the National Bank of Angola with the international partners. In this context, it should be noted that the National Bank of Angola Continue to: Strengthen relations with homologous institutions of the world's major economies and with the main international financial centres; Ensure with the main international partners the commitments that contribute to ensure a positive image of the national banking system, in its mission to safeguard the supreme interests of the Angolan State; Make efforts to reduce the current degree of uncertainty in the Financial System national level, by creating the conditions for monitoring the national economic and financial activity; Continue to provide information to its international partners on the existence of monetary and financial stability in Angola, with a view to adapt the Angolan Banking System to International Standards and Good Practices. Gentlemen and ladies, Distinguished guests; We recognise that there is still a long way to go, but we are convinced that with the actions carried out so far, we have taken steps important way towards the adequacy of our Banking System to international best practices, such as a of our greatest objectives. In particular, we would like to thank all stakeholders in the process of opening this new bank, in particular, the Board of Directors Management of the Bank of China, and we are certain that this banking institution, with the new financial products and services that it will make available to the our banking system, will certainly contribute to the better functioning of the banking system and the development of the two countries. Well-there, Bank of China. Thank you very much. 6 Jun 2017

Neste mbito, convm realar que o Banco Nacional de Angola continuar a: Estreitar relaes com Instituies homlogas das principais economias mundiais e com os principais centros financeiros internacionais; Assegurar junto dos principais parceiros internacionais, os compromissos que contribuem para garantir uma imagem positiva do sistema bancrio nacional, na sua misso de salvaguardar os interesses supremos do Estado angolano; Desenvolver esforos no sentido de reduzir o grau de incerteza actual do Sistema Financeiro Nacional, atravs da criao das condies de monitorizao da actividade econmica e financeira nacional; Continuar a prestar informaes aos seus parceiros internacionais, sobre a existncia de condies de estabilidade monetria e financeira em Angola, com vista a adequar o Sistema Bancrio Angolano s Normas e Boas Prticas Internacionais. Meus senhores e minhas senhoras, Distintos convidados; Reconhecemos que h ainda um caminho longo a percorrer, porm, estamos convictos de que com as aces realizadas at ao momento, temos dado passos importantes rumo  adequao do nosso Sistema Bancrio s melhores prticas internacionais, como um dos nossos maiores objectivos. De forma particular, queremos agradecer os esforos de todos os intervenientes no processo de abertura deste novo banco, especialmente, o Conselho de Administrao do Banco da China, e estamos certos de que esta instituio bancria, com os novos produtos e servios financeiros que colocar  disposio do nosso sistema bancrio, ir seguramente contribuir para o melhor funcionamento do sistema bancrio e o desenvolvimento dos dois pases. Bem-haja, Banco da China. Muito obrigado. Title: Opening Speech on The Relevance of Data from Companies Providing Services to the Oil Industry in Balance of Payments Statistics
text: Opening Speech of the Deputy Governor of bna, Manuel Tiago Dias on The Relevance of Data from Companies Providing Services to the Oil Industry in The Company's Statistics Balance of Payments Opening Speech of the Deputy Governor of the BNA, Manuel Tiago Dias on The Relevance of Data companies that provide services to industry Oil In The Balance Of Payments Your Excellese Members of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola (BNA); Distinguished Mr. President of the Association of Contracted Companies of the Petroleum Industry (AECIPA); Distinguished representatives of the Ministries of Petroleum, Finance, Economics and the Institute National Statistics (INE); Distinguished Directors and Employees of BNA; Ladies and Gentlemen On behalf of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola, I would like to welcome all guests attending this seminar, subordinate to the theme " The Relevance of Data from Companies Providing Services to the Oil Industry in Balance of Payments statistics" Since 2008, statistics have gained great size and usefulness, both globally and national level, in the face of the constant economic crises. The statistical literacy of the Angolan population has greatly improved, and with this the consultation of official statistical information has increased considerably. Therefore, the Country's Official Statistics Producing Bodies (PES) are producing in major challenges that go through improving statistics by themselves produced, taking into account the crucial role they play as an efficient tool for coordination and decision-making support, both of the managers businesses and families. In accordance with the Law of the National Bank of Angola and the National Statistical System Law, the National Government of Angola is the Responsible Body in the production and disclosure of balance of payments statistics, a delicate exercise with multiplicity of sources of information, with a highlight of the surveys directed at the companies from various sectors of the Angolan economy. As the Producer Body for Official Statistics, the National Bank of Angola has been improving the quality of the statistics produced by them, following international good practice. To this end, increased statistical coverage is a fundamental assumptions and which has deserved a of the National Bank of Angola, as can be seen today with the realization of this event. Dear Guests, Among the different sectors of the economy that provide statistical data for the purpose of compilation of the Balance of Payments, the activity of providing services to the oil industry have still insufficient statistical coverage, concern in the context of the consolidation of the Statistical System National. The law provides for sanctions for any refusal or falsity of statistical information to the National Angola, which is why the BNA has carried out actions to which have a formative and informative character of the respective target groups. It is from this perspective that we welcome this seminar, a joint initiative of bna and aecipa, with the aim of presenting the strategic importance that companies providing services to the oil industry may have in the development of the National Statistician through further expansion of the statistical coverage of this sector in the Balance of Payments. As everyone is aware, the oil sector is and will continue to be for some time the engine of the Angolan economy, so we can consider that companies represented here by the distinguished guests are the engine of the oil industry, because without them the oil sector would not survive. In this view, the collection and insertion of statistical data from the Companies Providing Services to the Oil Industry becomes an imperative need in the official statistics companies may better reflect the economic reality of the Country. 6 Jul. 2017

Title: Speech at the Opening Ceremony of the Conference on Banking Supervision, Experience and Challenges, Equivalence of Central Bank Banking Supervision
text: Speech by the Governor at the Opening Ceremony of the Banking Supervision Conference, Experience and Challenges, Equivalence of Banking Supervision of Central Banks. Speech by the Governor at the Opening of the Banking Supervision Conference, Experience and Challenges, Equivalence of Banking Supervision of Central Banks. Honourable Members of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola Distinguished Guests, Ladies and gentlemen; On behalf of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola, I would like to welcome all our guests, representatives of the institutions financial institutions, public and private entities, as well as international bodies present in this conference, which is proposed to be an indelible milestone in the addressing the new challenges of regulation for the strengthening of banking supervision that is intended to our country. Under the Constitution of the Republic of Angola, the Law of the National Bank of Angola and the Basis of Financial Institutions, the National Bank of Angola, as a regulatory and supervisor of the Angolan financial system, has assumed its functions of system change dynamic agent and the implementation of international best practices, the objective of which the main need is to adapt the existing regulatory framework to basel principles, with an equivalent supervision, i.e. the proximity of the effectiveness, methodology and results achieved between two supervisory bodies in different jurisdictions. DISTINGUISHED GUESTS, LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, When the current Board of Directors took office in 2016 and in the face of the current difficulties angolan financial system, caused by the clash with the international prices of the main export product, Petroleum, also the main source of revenue in the Angolan state, attention was paid to in particular to the enormous challenge of reviewing and modernising the regulation and supervision of banking and non-banking institutions. Thus, one of the first measures taken by express guidance of the Executive Holder was launch the project to adapt the Angolan financial system international standards and good practices. This was a key milestone in the approach of the new paradigms of banking regulation and supervision in stability of the Angolan financial system. The implementation of this plan has led us, in the context of the standardisation of supervisory practices banking, working in collaboration with similar entities countries in several countries, including South Africa, Portugal, Italy, France, the United Kingdom, United States of America. In the meantime, we are required, before addressing some of the issues more directed to the theme of this conference, give a brief note on the developments in the banking financial system. However, the Angolan banking system currently has 30 banking financial institutions of which 29 are in business. The banking rate in December 2016 was 52.92%, and the banking system has a total of 6,719,407 customers. In December 2016 the same banking system had a turnover of more than 10,000 million USD, the total credit to the economy corresponded to 3 billion, the overdue credit on total credit represents about 25.37%. In terms of capital adequacy, the financial system had a solvency ratio regulatory rate by about 19.74%. Ladies and gentlemen, In recent years there have been significant changes in the Angolan economy, in particular in the banking sector. In this regard, it should be considered that after an assessment of the actual state of the Angolan financial sector, through the sector's evaluation programme (FSAP), held in 2010, the National Bank of Angola took initiatives such as the confirmation of the legal and regulatory framework, in the context of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, Adequate Capital, Governance corporate governance and internal control system, as well as the full adoption of international accounting and financial reporting standards (IAS/IFRS), as well as consumer protection of financial products and services. Excellencies. Ladies and gentlemen, One of the main objectives of the BNA, as a monetary and exchange rate authority, is to ensure the stability, control of the inflation target and confidence in the financial and banking system. Thus, in order to adapt the Angolan banking system to prudent standards and good practices international markets, were proven and published in 2016, 48 regulatory rules, which regulate the matter on Regulatory Own Funds, full adoption of international standards of Accounting and Financial Reporting, Risk Governance, Credit Conceptualization, Stress Testing and Standards of Conduct. With regard to standards of conduct, I would like to highlight here the new package of measures on which aims to strengthen the soundness and mechanisms protection of consumers' interests in financial products and services, aimed at mitigating the risk of conduct of financial institutions within the framework of the exercise of its activity. Ladies and gentlemen, The actions listed above have greatly contributed to the development of the supervisory process financial institutions, aligning it with best practices the Supervisory Manual, which formalised and systematized the procedures for risk-based banking supervision. For its implementation, a Risk Assessment Model has been developed and implemented for Financial Institutions, considering the categories of Risk of Market, Operational and Liquidity Credit. The model is also composed of the following components: Internal Control Corporate Governance Prevention and Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Solvency and Liquidity, which has strengthened the supervisory intervention process, contributing to improving the quality of information. Different Participants We recognise that there is still a long way to go, but we are convinced that the actions carried out so far allows us to ensure that challenges of regulation and supervision that still persist, remain at the heart of our concerns towards their overcoming. Therefore, the National Bank of Angola, in collaboration with the other organs of the Angolan State, will continue to work on improving actions aimed at the adequacy of the Angolan Financial System to International Prudence standards and good practices, in particular, the three major regulatory packages that known as BASEL I, II and III, and giving relevance: BANKING REGULATION AND SUPERVISION, AT THE LEVEL OF RISK CONTROL AND MANAGEMENT THE FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES FOR EFFECTIVE BANKING SUPERVISION STRENGTHENING AND MONITORING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE ACTIONS FOR THE PREVENTION OF MONEY LAUNDERING AND COMBATING FUNDING FOR TERRORISM To this end, training and awareness-raising activities are also provided for by the under their supervision. Finally, in order to achieve internal supervision in terms of the approximation of the regulation and maturation of bna supervisory processes, is being brought to a high stage a programme of training and continuous training of regulatory and supervisory teams, administered by its BNA Academy, and training specialized abroad, within the framework of the cooperation agreements initialled with international supervision of similar supervisors, with a view to sharing experiences and knowledge in related matters. Excellencies My Lady and Gentlemen, Convinced that this great event by bringing together experts from different parts of the world, in the matters already referred to and which are topical issues undoubtedly boil down to the opportunity to reflect together on what best practices can be adopted so that the challenges that arise from the angolan financial system can be overcome. In this way, I declare with great satisfaction that this Conference is open, reiterating the speakers who agreed to attend the event, with votes of feel good in Angola, a country that welcomes you. Thank you so much for your attention. 10 Jul. 2017
