text: Home Publications and Media Speech by The Deputy Governor, Dr. Andre Lopes, at the Presentation Ceremony of the BNA Financial Products and Services Consumer Speech by The Deputy Governor, Dr. Andre Lopes, at the Presentation Ceremony of the Portal of the Consumer of Financial Products and Services of the BNA Exmos. Presidents of the Boards of Directors and Executive Committees of the Banking Financial Institutions, Dear members of the Board of Directors and Directors of bna Exma Madam Director of INADEC, Dear Directors and Staff of Banking Financial Institutions, Dear Guests Ladies and gentlemen, The levels of growth and development of the national economy in general and the financial system in particular in recent years, are an unquestionable reality that brings with it responsibilities to all actors in the institutional, business and social fabric of our country. Between 2005 and 2010, the number of banking financial institutions increased from 11 to 23 and expansion of the branch network, has allowed there to be around 1,100 branches spread throughout the country. Similarly, we highlight the increase and emergence of other non-bank financial institutions, currency and credit, including 67 (sixty-seven) Exchange Offices, 2 (two) micro-credit companies and one (1) securities remittance company., the contribute to diversification and technological innovation in the financial products and services. These changes permanently pose challenges for financial system regulators angolan parliament, including the National Bank of Angola, to whom the necessary conditions for the process of sustained development of the economy, based, at the same time, on the effective control of stability of the financial system. In parallel with the effects of this growth, diversification and sophistication of the financial system angolan crisis, the international financial and economic crisis that began in 2008, brought with it other challenges and awakened the sector to the importance of literacy and the need for decisions taken by bank customers, based on sound foundations and be taken on a conscious, informed and responsible basis, under penalty of concerned, the efficiency and stability of the system financial. For this reason, central banks, somewhat everywhere, have been attributing increasing importance to initiatives to promote the levels of information financial policy, involving itself in the definition and implementation of strategies at national level, for the conscious insertion of the population into the financial system. Naturally, such concerns are also part of the agenda of the National Bank of Angola, for example understand that financial education contributes to enhancing the knowledge of regulatory instruments, transparency and reporting duties and, in last resort, to enable the most efficient functioning of the financial markets. Practical actions need to be developed that allow us to rapidly evolve to an internship, where the national citizen is in a position to assess the risk and return associated with their savings and investment decisions, as variables that generally evolve in direct reason, in so far as they are are usually associated with increased exposure to risk. Knowledge of all cost and risk components associated with products and services offered by banking financial institutions, should be a concern of all consumers of banking services and products and this, as a matter of it is obvious, it also involves a proactive attitude of the financial institutions. Financial institutions must exercise active pedagogy, playing the role of directors, conveniently informing customers and taking measures at its power, in a way in so far as to make transparent the relations it establishes with the same and avoid conflicts arising therefrom. On this path and aware that "... the better informed the population, the smaller the probability of entering cycles of on indebtedness", the bet improving the level of financial education of populations, with programmes aimed at a more responsible for all actors, should be on the agenda of our institutions, considering here the Central Bank as supervisor of the system and the financial institutions. For all this, after having created in its organic structure the Department of Supervision behavioral, a unit dedicated to ensure the rigor and transparency in relations between financial institutions and their clients, and which has complemented the functions relating to the supervision of bna decided to create the Consumer Portal for Financial Products and Services. Through this important instrument, we will have a platform that will provide a set of financial information, such as basic concepts associated with the most frequent financial decisions of bank customers, as well as constituting a privileged channel for the handling of complaints arising from consumer public of financial products and services. With the entry into operation of the Consumer Portal of Financial Products and Services, a channel through which the general population and customers banks, in particular, may have access to a set of information of a formative characteristic, as well as a way to submit their complaints resulting from the relationships they establish with financial institutions, and may also be follow the process of their treatment. Convinced that, with this instrument, the conditions for the establishment and disclosure of rules of conduct that ensure the transparency of the information and fairness in transactions in financial products and services, between financial institutions and supervised by BNA and its customers, we have declaring open, this seminar presentation of the Consumer Portal of products and services Financial. Thank you very much! 14 Sep. 2012
text_original: Home Publicaes e Media Intervenes Pblicas Discurso do Sr. Vice Governador, Dr. Andr Lopes, na Cerimnia de Apresentao do Portal do Consumidor de Produtos e Servios Financeiros do BNA Discurso do Sr. Vice Governador, Dr. Andr Lopes, na Cerimnia de Apresentao do Portal do Consumidor de Produtos e Servios Financeiros do BNA Exmos. Senhores Presidentes dos Conselhos de Administrao e das Comisses Executivas das Instituies Financeiras Bancrias, Caros membros do Conselho de Administrao e Directores do BNA Exma Senhora Directora do INADEC, Prezados Directores e Quadros das Instituies Financeiras Bancrias, Caros Convidados Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores, Os nveis de crescimento e desenvolvimento da economia nacional em geral e do sistema financeiro em particular nos ltimos anos, so uma realidade inquestionvel que traz consigo responsabilidades a todos os actores do tecido institucional, empresarial e social do nosso Pais. Entre 2005 e 2010, o nmero de instituies financeiras bancrias aumentou de 11 para 23 e a expanso da rede de agncias, permitiu que neste momento, existam cerca de 1.100 balces espalhados por todo o territrio nacional. De igual modo, salientamos o aumento e surgimento de outras instituies financeiras no bancrias, ligadas  moeda e crdito, nomeadamente 67 (sessenta e sete) Casas de Cmbio, 2 (duas) sociedades de Micro-crdito e 1 (uma) sociedade de remessa de valores., a contriburem para a diversificao e inovao tecnolgica na oferta de produtos e servios financeiros. Estas mutaes colocam, permanentemente, desafios para os reguladores do sistema financeiro angolano, nomeadamente ao Banco Nacional de Angola, a quem compete, assegurar as condies necessrias para que o processo de desenvolvimento sustentado da economia, assente, simultaneamente, no controlo efectivo dos preos e na estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Paralelamente aos efeitos deste crescimento, diversificao e sofisticao do sistema financeiro angolano, a crise financeira e econmica internacional iniciada em 2008, trouxe consigo outros desafios e despertou o sector para a importncia da literacia financeira e da necessidade das decises tomadas pelos clientes bancrios, assentar em bases slidas e ser assumida de modo consciente, informado e responsvel, sob pena de por em causa, a eficincia e a estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Por esta razo, os bancos centrais, um pouco por toda a parte, tm vindo a atribuir crescente importncia s iniciativas de promoo dos nveis de informao financeira, envolvendo-se na definio e implementao de estratgias a nvel nacional, para a insero consciente da populao no sistema financeiro. Naturalmente, tais preocupaes, fazem igualmente parte da agenda do Banco Nacional de Angola, por entender que a educao financeira contribui para potenciar o conhecimento dos instrumentos de regulao, da transparncia e dos deveres de informao e, em ltima instncia, para permitir o funcionamento mais eficiente dos mercados financeiros.  necessrio desenvolvermos aces prticas, que nos permitam evoluir rapidamente para um estgio, em que o cidado nacional esteja em condies de avaliar o risco e retorno associados s suas decises de poupana e de investimento, enquanto variveis que evoluem, regra geral, na razo directa, na medida em que rendimentos elevados, esto normalmente associados a uma maior exposio ao risco. O conhecimento de todas as componentes de custo e risco associados aos produtos e servios oferecidos pelas instituies financeiras bancarias, deve ser uma preocupao permanente de todos os consumidores de servios e produtos bancrios e tal facto, como  bvio, passa, igualmente, por uma atitude proactiva das instituies financeiras. Com efeito, as instituies financeiras devem exercer uma pedagogia activa, exercendo o papel de conselheiros, informando convenientemente os clientes e tomando todas as medidas ao seu alcance, para tornar transparente as relaes que estabelece com os mesmos e evitar conflitos da decorrentes. Nesta senda e conscientes de que  quanto melhor informado estiver a populao, menor  a probabilidade de entrar em ciclos de sobre endividamento, a aposta na melhoria do nvel de educao financeira das populaes, com programas visando uma atitude mais responsvel de todos os actores, deve estar na ordem do dia das nossas instituies, considerando aqui o Banco Central enquanto supervisor do sistema e as instituies financeiras bancarias. Por tudo isso, depois de ter criado na sua estrutura orgnica o Departamento de Superviso Comportamental, uma unidade vocacionada para velar pelo rigor e pela transparncia nas relaes entre as instituies financeiras bancarias e os seus clientes, e que veio dar complementaridade as funes relativas  superviso prudencial, o BNA decidiu criar o Portal do Consumidor de Produtos e Servios Financeiros. Por via deste importante instrumento, passaremos a ter uma plataforma que disponibilizar um conjunto de informao de caracter financeiro, como conceitos bsicos associados s decises financeiras mais frequentes dos clientes bancrios, alm de constituir um canal privilegiado para o atendimento de reclamaes provenientes do pblico consumidor de produtos e servios financeiros. Com a entrada em funcionamento do Portal do Consumidor de Produtos e Servios Financeiros, cria-se um canal atravs do qual, a populao em geral e os clientes bancrios, em particular, podero ter acesso a um conjunto de informaes de caracter formativo, bem como uma via para apresentarem as suas reclamaes decorrentes das relaes que estabelecem com as instituies financeiras, podendo ainda acompanhar o processo de tratamento das mesmas. Convictos de que, com este instrumento, sairo reforadas as condies para o estabelecimento e divulgao de regras de conduta que assegurem a transparncia da informao e a equidade nas transaces de produtos e servios financeiros, entre as instituies supervisionadas pelo BNA e os seus clientes, terminamos declarando aberto, este seminrio de apresentao do Portal do Consumidor de produtos e servios financeiros. Muito Obrigado! Title: Speech at the opening X Meeting of Statistics of the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking Countries
text: Home Publications and Media Speech by the Vice-Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Manuel Antonio Tiago Dias, at opening X Meeting of Statistics of the Central Banks of the Language Countries Portuguese Speech by the Vice -Governor of Banco Naciona Angola, Manuel Antonio Tiago Dias, in opening X Bank Statistics Meeting Central Portuguese-speaking Countries Honourable Members of the Board of Directors and Delegations of the Central Banks of the Portuguese Language; Dignitacio Director of the Office of Studies and Planning of the Government of the Province of Benguela; Distinguished Representatives of the National Institute of Statistics and the General Tax Administration; Dear Regional Delegates, Directors and Technicians of the National Bank of Angola; Ladies and gentlemen. On behalf of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola, I would first like to express our warm greetings and welcome to all participants to the 10th Meeting of Statistics of the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries, that we are pleased to organize and welcome here in the city of Benguela. We wish you all a good stay. Dear Colleagues, Angola is currently experiencing a challenging economic climate, due to the fall in the average price of crude oil on international markets since the mid-2010s 2014, the country's main source of tax and export revenues. However, we can say that the Angolan economy is now undergoing a phase of stabilization Macroeconomic. After a period of two consecutive years with negative real GDP growth rates of 2.6% and 2.5% in 2016 and 2017, for the this year, a negative growth rate of only 1.1% and finally, from 2019 the country will resume its growth path with positive rates. Several economic reforms are underway, the measures of which are contained in the Macroeconomic and National Development Plan 2017-2022, defined by the Angolan Executive, with a highlight of the following economic policy measures: Increasing the competitiveness of domestic production; Diversification of exports and substitution of imports (PRODESI); Fiscal consolidation: increased revenues and reduction of public expenditure; Creating the conditions for a better business environment and attraction of investment foreigner; and The easing of the official exchange rate. Dear Colleagues, After the National Bank of Angola welcomed and organized for the first time in the city of Luanda the III Meeting of Statistics of the Central Banks of the Countries of Portuguese Language in March 2005, it is with great satisfaction that we are once again organising this event, with the integration of three more Lusophone countries in recent years, namely Brazil, East Timor and Macau. Macroeconomic statistics have gained greater visibility and utility in recent years, to the constant economic and financial crises that have erupted in the world since 2008. For example, the statistical literacy of the Angolan population has improved and with that the consultation and discussions on the data published by the official bodies has increased considerably. Therefore, central banks, as producers of official statistics, are challenged to improve the quality of statistics themselves more and more produced, taking into account the crucial role they play as an efficient tool for coordination and decision-making support, both of the managers companies and families. The central theme chosen for this meeting "The Role of Statistics in Risk Prevention and Vulnerabilities of the Financial System" clearly shows the commitment of our institutions to anticipate new systemic crises, using to reliable statistical information, for the adoption of reliable information more assertive policy measures. The National Bank of Angola, in particular, has given priority to its statistical function, seeking to adopt your Bureau of Statistics with qualified and competent, without destiture from other areas, which also play a key role in the institution's activities. The National Bank of Angola's strategic plan for the period 2017-2022 provides for a set of strategic actions on improving statistics international best practices, with an enhancement to the following: The creation of a balance sheet centre; The compilation of statistics of other financial corporations; The compilation of the National Financial Account; The automation of statistical processes; The reduction of the deadlines for the dissemination of statistics, with a view to the publication of the Balance of Quarterly payments; Centralizing statistical information and creating a single channel for its dissemination. Most of the strategic actions mentioned above are aligned with the themes of the work of this event, above all, sessions III and V, which will address developments in the field of national financial accounts and the solutions technology in the process of collecting, processing and publishing statistics. In addition to these sessions, the meeting will also serve to take stock of the main transformations that have occurred in the statistical function of the central banks of the cplp, analyse the different coincident indicators for monitoring economic activity used by each of the banks, experiences in the capture and insertion of indirect transactions in the statistics produced, as well as the role of statistics in the prevention of risks of the financial system Dear Colleagues, In fact, all working sessions have as their main objective, the exchange of experiences between the different central banks present here in the field of their statistical activity. Therefore, expectations are high regarding the results that this meeting could produce and aim to make the most of the will be presented, as well as the discussions that result from them. Finally, before i finish, I would like to address a word of appreciation to the members of the organizer of this meeting and wish all present a good work, and to enjoy the city of The Acacia Rubras, its people, as well as its rich gastronomy. Therefore, I declare open the 10th Meeting of Statistics of the Central Banks of the Language Portuguese. 13 Sep. 2018

Em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco Nacional de Angola, gostaria em primeiro lugar de exprimir as nossas calorosas saudaes e boas vindas a todos os participantes ao X Encontro de Estatsticas dos Bancos Centrais dos Pases da Lngua Portuguesa, que temos o prazer de organizar e acolher aqui na cidade de Benguela. Desejamos a todos uma boa estadia. Estimados Colegas, Angola atravessa actualmente uma conjuntura econmica desafiante, devido  queda do preo mdio de petrleo bruto nos mercados internacionais desde meados de 2014, a principal fonte de receitas fiscais e de exportao do Pas. Contudo, podemos afirmar que a economia angolana passa agora por uma fase de estabilizao macroeconmica. Aps um perodo de dois anos consecutivos marcados com taxas de crescimento real do PIB negativas de 2,6% e 2,5% em 2016 e 2017, para o corrente ano, perspectiva-se uma taxa de crescimento negativo de apenas 1,1% e finalmente, a partir de 2019 o Pas retomar a sua trajectria de crescimento com taxas positivas. Vrias reformas econmicas esto em curso, cujas medidas constam do Plano de Estabilizao Macroeconmica e Plano de Desenvolvimento Nacional 2017-2022, definidos pelo Executivo angolano, com realce para as seguintes medidas de poltica econmica: O aumento da competitividade da produo interna; A diversificao das exportaes e substituio das importaes (PRODESI); A consolidao fiscal: aumento das receitas e reduo das despesas pblicas; A criao de condies para um melhor ambiente de negcios e de atraco do investimento estrangeiro; e A flexibilizao da taxa de cmbio oficial. Estimados Colegas, Depois do Banco Nacional de Angola ter acolhido e organizado pela primeira vez na cidade de Luanda o III Encontro de Estatsticas dos Bancos Centrais dos Pases da Lngua Portuguesa em Maro de 2005,  com muita satisfao que estamos a organizar mais uma vez este certame, com a integrao de mais trs pases lusfonos nos ltimos anos, nomeadamente, Brasil, Timor Leste e Macau. As estatsticas macroeconmicas ganharam nos ltimos anos, uma maior visibilidade e utilidade, face s constantes crises econmicas e financeiras que eclodiram no mundo desde o ano de 2008. Por exemplo, a literacia estatstica da populao angolana melhorou bastante, e com isso a consulta e os debates sobre os dados estatsticos publicados pelos rgos oficiais aumentou consideravelmente. Assim sendo, os Bancos Centrais, na sua qualidade de produtores de estatsticas oficiais so desafiados a melhorar cada vez mais a qualidade das estatsticas por si produzidas, tendo em conta o papel crucial que estas desempenham, como instrumento eficiente de coordenao e suporte  tomada de decises, quer dos gestores pblicos, de empresas e das famlias. O tema central escolhido para este encontro O Papel das Estatsticas na Preveno de Riscos e Vulnerabilidades do Sistema Financeiro mostra claramente o comprometimento das nossas instituies em antecipar novas crises sistmicas, recorrendo-se para tal s informaes estatsticas fiveis, para a adopo de medidas de poltica mais assertivas. O Banco Nacional de Angola, em particular, tem dado primazia  sua funo estatstica, procurando adoptar o seu Departamento de Estatstica com quadros qualificados e competentes, sem desprimor das outras reas, que de igual forma desempenham um papel fundamental na prossecuo das actividades da instituio. O plano estratgico do Banco Nacional de Angola para o perodo de 2017 a 2022, prev um conjunto de aces estratgicas atinentes  melhoria das estatsticas segundo as boas prticas internacionais, com realce para as seguintes: A criao de uma central de balanos; A compilao das estatsticas das Outras Sociedades Financeiras; A compilao da Conta Nacional Financeira; A automatizao dos processos estatsticos; A reduo dos prazos de divulgao das estatsticas, com realce para a publicao da Balana de Pagamentos trimestralmente; A centralizao das informaes estatsticas e a criao de um canal nico para sua difuso. Grande parte das aces estratgicas referidas acima est alinhada com os temas das sesses de trabalho deste certame, sobretudo, as sesses III e V, que se debruaro sobre os desenvolvimentos no domnio das contas nacionais financeiras e as solues tecnolgicas no processo de recolha, tratamento e publicao das estatsticas. Para alm dessas sesses, o encontro servir tambm para fazer um balano das principais transformaes ocorridas na funo estatstica dos bancos centrais da CPLP, analisar os diferentes indicadores coincidentes de acompanhamento da actividade econmica utilizados por cada um dos bancos, as experincias na captao e insero das transaces informais nas estatsticas produzidas, bem como o papel das estatsticas na preveno de riscos do sistema financeiro Estimados Colegas, Na verdade, todas as sesses de trabalho tm como principal objectivo, a troca de experincias entre os diferentes bancos centrais aqui presentes no domnio da sua actividade estatstica. Por isso, as expectativas so grandes relativamente aos resultados que este encontro poder produzir e almejamos que tirem o mximo proveito possvel dos trabalhos que sero apresentados, bem como os debates que deles resultarem. Finalmente, antes de terminar gostaria de dirigir uma palavra de apreo aos membros da comisso organizadora deste encontro e desejar a todos os presentes um bom trabalho, e que desfrutem da cidade das Accias Rubras, da sua gente, bem como da sua rica gastronomia. Portanto, declaro aberto o X Encontro de Estatsticas dos Bancos Centrais dos Pases da Lngua Portuguesa. text: Home Publications and Media Speech by the Administrator of the National Bank of Angola, Pedro Castro e Silva, at the end of the X Meeting of Statistics of the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking Countries Speech by the Administrator of the National Bank of Angola, Pedro Castro e Silva, at the end of the X Central Bank Statistics Meeting portuguese-speaking countries Honourable Members of the Board of Directors and Delegations of the Central Banks of the Portuguese Language; Dignitacio Director of the Office of Studies and Planning of the Government of the Province of Benguela; Distinguished Representatives of the National Institute of Statistics and the General Tax Administration; Dear Directors, Sub-Directors, Regional and Technical Delegates of the National Bank of Angola; Ladies and gentlemen. It is with special interest that I witness the great relevance of the meetings of Statistics of Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking countries. These two days of work have provided several moments of reflection and debate on the more pressing issues and the challenges facing the compilation and dissemination of statistics at the level of our Central Banks. For example, the 10th Meeting of Statistics of the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking Countries once again highlight the importance and usefulness of compiling National Financial Accounts, an instrument that allows the monitoring of flows of financial institutions and positions of the various institutional sectors of a economy, that is, how their capital is financed and applied. Therefore, the techniques and methodological aspects discussed here will certainly serve to to boost the process of producing and disseminating statistics to level of our countries. The balance sheet made by each of the Central Banks on the main changes that have occurred in the years in its statistical function clearly shows that we're all aligned, though some more advanced than others, but the important thing is we all we walk in the same direction. Some technological solutions have also been shared here for the collection, treatment and publication of statistics, all of which are of great merit, which there are many alternatives to be explored in this area. The evidence of the benefits of automating collection processes and processing of statistical data, thereby reducing manual labour and the likelihood of occurrence of human errors. The existence of an informal economy with a very significant weight is an economic reality of some countries present here. It has become a challenge for some of us reflect in the statistics the transactions that occur in this sector, with a view to the transactions in cross-border informal trade. Not wanting to stretch me too much, I leave a word of appreciation to the distinguished speakers and moderators who shared their experiences and knowledge, helping us to reflect on the methodological aspects of the compilation of statistics, as was the case, for example, of the so-called coincident indicators of the economic activity, given the need for central banks to look at the evolution of the real sector at the moment they are taking the policy measures monetary. Due to the specificnature of the matters discussed here, it is well-thought that these reflections do not in a space like this. Therefore, we invite participants to continue to interact throughout the period between this and the next meeting. As senior central bank managers and technicians, we must take advantage of and apply in our professional activities all the knowledge acquired in this great event, for the benefit of our institutions. As stated in the final communique of this meeting, we hope to be together again in Macao from here two years ago for the 11th Statistics Meeting Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries, to be organised by the Monetary Authority of this sister country. For the success of this event it would be unfair of us if we did not say words of thanks to all those who deigned to set aside their agendas to share with us their knowledge and experiences. Many thanks to all the members of the delegations and guests present here. We address, also, our thanks to the Provincial Government of Benguela who gave all the institutional support necessary for the success of this event. Special thanks to the Organizing Committee of the X Meeting for the engagement and the exemplary way how he organized the event. Thank you and wish all participants a good homecoming! With these brief words, I declare that the 10th Meeting on Statistics of the Central Banks of the Portuguese language countries. 13 Sep. 2018

text: Home Publications and Media Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose de Lima Massano, at the opening of the 13th edition of the Study Banking in Analysis Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose de Lima Massano, at the opening of the 13th edition of the Study Banca em Analise Excellencies Ladies and gentlemen: Very good morning With great satisfaction I welcomed the invitation of Dr. Duarte Galhardas, President of Deloitte Angola, to the opening of this already traditional event. As is common knowledge, the National Bank of Angola, among other responsibilities, is responsible for ensure that the process of financial intermediation is in an environment of continuous stability of the financial system itself, stimulating savings, investment and thereby economic growth and the inclusion of social. The existence of financial stability is also essential for a monetary policy effective. The Central Bank will hardly perform the function of preservation of the value of the currency if it often grants liquidity in the form of a rebate to structural problems in its balance sheet. The stability index of the banking system has been degrading since 2015, with march 2018 assessed at 31%, but to world bank forecasts, as well as those of the BNA point to improved stability rates of the banking system in the This semester. As is also predictable, the macroeconomic vulnerability that is still observed increases the bna's responsibilities in the prevention, management and resolution of challenges facing the financial system. We highlight with concern the quality of credit assets, resulting from the worsening of levels of default in the credit portfolio in institutions financial statements of medium and high systemic importance. It should be noted that in the last 3 years, the ratio of bad-toe credit has more than doubled from 11% december 2015 to around 26% in June of the current year. This increased difficulties in repayment of loans by households and businesses, is most felt in the trade, construction and real estate activity, reflecting the pace of growth of the economy in recent years. This is why the increase in the profitability of commercial banking is mainly due to the increase in exchange rate results and income from securities and securities diverging from the granting of credit to the economy. This is an increased concern and that we have been sharing with the Angolan Association of and other institutional actors in order to jointly find the best ways to increase the granting of credit, but under conditions of greater security. As regards capital adequacy, although the financial system is above the levels of established minimum standards, it is certain that the risk in the credit may entail increased unevenness, with a negative impact on the solvency of banking financial institutions. Preliminary stress tests to the banking financial system for the control of material credit, market, operational and liquidity risks, determined the need to adjust the minimum values of share capital and own funds regulations, which must be complied with by 31 December of the current year. These results have also led us to publish standards that regulate the implementation of regular testing programmes for effort by the institutions themselves, constantly assessing the most important risk factors Relevant. Also in the context of improving financial stability, I highlight the restructuring process organic and functional function of the National Bank of Angola itself, established new organic units, one of which focused on prudential supervision of institutions non-bank financial statements, in recognition of the specificity of the supervision of such institutions, both in terms of regulation and the very processes of supervision. We empower the functions of investigation and action sanctioning of supervisory tasks, giving greater objectivity and impartiality of analysis and greater specialisation of teams that ensure the compliance with the rules and guidelines given by the National Bank of Angola. From a regulatory point of view, another relevant note of the ongoing initiatives of the National Angola is related to the updating of the rules on corporate governance and internal control systems, where particular emphasis will be placed on criteria more stringent prudential measures with regard to the rules of prevention and management of conflicts of interest, segregation of executive and non-executive functions, identification, control and mitigation of risks, as well as requirements of suitability and professional experience of managers of financial institutions. text: Opening Speech of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose de Lima Massano, in the IV Audit Meeting, Risk Management and Compliance of central banks of the Portuguese-speaking Countries - BCPLP Opening Speech of the Governor of the Bank National of Angola, Jose de Lima Massano, no IV Audit Meeting, Risk Management and Compliance of the Central Banks of the Portuguese language - BCPLP Mr. Provincial Governor of Huila; Members of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola; Distinguished Delegates of the Central Banks of the Community of Portuguese-speaking Countries; Dear representatives of the Banks of the Angolan Financial System; Dear representatives of IIA Angola; Directors, Regional Delegates and workers of the National Bank of Angola; Ladies and gentlemen; Allow me, first of all, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola, to address our compliments and to welcome all the members of the delegations present here and, in particular, the speakers who accepted the challenge of sharing your experiences with us. I also express our deep satisfaction and honor in welcoming here, in the city of Lubango - Province of Huila, this IV Audit Meeting, Risk Management and Compliance of the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries. I hope you all have had a good trip and Wish you a great stay. Esteemed Colleagues; Dear Guests; Ten years ago the world experienced the biggest financial and economic crisis since 1929 that had enormous economic and social consequences, the effects of which are still make themselves felt. This crisis has clearly exposed the risks to which financial institutions and the consequences of inadequate management of these risks for the financial system and economic activity in general, highlighting the need for strengthening corporate governance and internal control models. Although the various CPLP countries have experienced the financial crisis differently and the realities and challenges of each country's financial systems are diverse, as well as the pace of regulatory change, the way forward to create a financial system more robust and resilient and avoid a repeat of the financial crisis of 2008 and its consequences, is, in general, better defined. In the context of Angola, the National Bank of Angola has in recent years been strengthening the regulatory with the aim of establishing the implementation of appropriate models of corporate governance and internal control in financial institutions under the supervisory, through the publication of regulations on the various topics under discussion at this IV Audit, Risk Management and Compliance Meeting of banks CPLP Headquarters. At the same time, it has also been changing its own governance and control model with the aim of better responding to the challenges posed by the by the sector. However, it is also necessary to recognise that, regardless of the different levels of development, the financial sector, in general, continues to many challenges, requiring regulators and supervisors to pay more attention to the permanent and concentrated in order to maintain the regulation on corporate governance and up-to-date and relevant internal control, and thus resilience of the sector and the expected support for the dynamics of development of economies and societies. In this context of constant changes and challenges and increasing demands, the meeting of institutions of realities and with diverse experiences makes the discussion of the themes inscribed in the programme of this IV Meeting an added value for all its Participants. Thus, it is with satisfaction that the National Bank of Angola hosts this Meeting, so without further delay, I wish all present a fruitful encounter. I also hope that you can enjoy the beauty and charms of the city of Lubango and that in the end have all a good return to your countries. With these words, I declare open the IV Audit Meeting, Risk Management and Compliance of Central Banks of the CPLP. 24 Oct. 2018

text: Opening Speech of the Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Rui Miguens, at the VIII Meeting of the Payment Systems of the Central Banks of the Language Countries Portuguese (BCPLP) Opening Speech of the Deputy Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Rui Miguens, no VIII Meeting of Banks' Payment Systems Central Portuguese-speaking Countries (BCPLP) Exma. Ms. Massari Lima Fernandes Pontes, Deputy Governor of the Central Bank of S. Tome and Prince; Exmos. Members of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola; Distinguished Delegates of the Central Banks of the Community of Portuguese-speaking Countries; Directors and workers of the National Bank of Angola; Ladies and gentlemen, Allow me, first of all, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola, to address our compliments and to welcome all the members of the delegations present here and, in particular, the speakers who accepted the challenge of sharing your experiences with us. I also express our deep satisfaction and honor in welcoming here, in the city of Luanda - capital Republic of Angola - this VIII Meeting of Payment of the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking Countries. I hope you all have had a good trip and Wish you a great stay. Dear colleagues, Dear guests, The event that begins today is held on a rotating basis by the Central Banks of the CPLP members, in a two-year temporal environment for analysis and treatment of issues related to the payment systems of each State, with an emphasis on the prospects for development, as well as in assessing trends in international financial industry with an impact on payment systems. It is important to note that the increase in transactions in the national financial markets and international markets, the sophistication of financial products, the globalisation of markets and financial deintermediation, provided by technological advances, require the development of effective and secure payment systems, in order to preserve the stable functioning of financial systems and to provide more productive, commercial and financial activities. Another function, not least of the payment systems, is to provide a platform that allow financial inclusion, a critical function in some of the given our level of economic and social development. Thus, in order to comply with the public interest obejctivos of payment systems, safety, efficacy and inclusion, it is important to management is in line with international good practice. We recognize that CPLP countries have different stages of development in their payments, judging by the realities and challenges that each country faces. However, it is also necessary to recognise that, regardless of the different levels of development, payment systems, in general, continue to present many challenges in common, requiring regulators and supervisors to more permanent and concentrated attention in order to ensure their full functioning on the basis of sound, safe, effective and effective principles Reliable. In the specific case of the Angolan Payment System, the National Bank of Angola has been adjust and strengthen its regulatory framework with the aim of establish appropriate management and supervisory models through the publication of regulatory on the various topics, which in essence will also be in approach at this VIII Meeting of Payment Systems of the Central Banks of the Portuguese. In this context of constant changes and challenges and increasing demands, the meeting of institutions derived from realities and with experiences the discussion of the themes inscribed in the programme of this 8th Meeting an added value for all its participants. This Meeting takes place at a time when the convergence between technology and financial resources is increasing. The emergence of fintech and the growing the trend of elimination of financial intermediaries leads us to reflect on what should be banking business model in the not-too-distant future. The CPLP has among its members who can share their experiences with regard to the implementation of DSP2 and also mobile payments. Finally, the emergence of so-called cryptocurrencies and the technology that supports them, blockchain, put in our Central Banks an additional effort to understanding and foresight of future developments in payment systems and means. It is therefore with satisfaction that the National Bank of Angola welcomes this Meeting, and I therefore wish all excellent working sessions. I also hope that you can enjoy the beauty and charms of the city of Luanda and that in the end they have all a good return to your countries. With these words, I declare open the VIII Meeting of Payment Systems of central banks Portuguese-speaking countries. 29 Nov. 2018

Title: Opening Speech at the VIII Meeting of the Payment Systems of the Central Banks of Portuguese-speaking Countries (BCPLP)
text: Public Interventions Closing Speech Administrator Peter Castro e Silva at the Economics & Market Magazine Conference Closing Speech Administrator Peter Castro e Silva at the Magazine Conference Economics & Market First of all, I would like to thank the Invitation made to the National Bank of Angola to participate in this event to participate in one of the panels and to make the closing speech. I congratulate the promoters of the event for the choice of the theme - the transformation digital banking - which is already a reality in most of the developed and developing economies. Digital transformation is a process that sooner or later would affect the services Financial. We first observed the digitisation of services such as the purchase of a ticket, books and music. The same thing happened at the bank. Despite the physical channels of banks - bank branches - are still the preferred channel of the banking customer, it is no less true that, from an early age, banking services began to be offered through the ATMs, Internet Banking e do Mobile Banking. However, the question for commercial bank managers is as follows: we are sure that 10 years from now we're still going to need financial services, But will we need banks? So far, the experience of digitising financial services has shown that the benefits of are in reducing costs, through the automation of migration of front-office services to electronic platforms. It is common to see in the international market the entire process of analysis and concession through digital channels. The artificial intelligence behind these digital platforms allows such processes of analysis and granting of occur quickly and without disdecorating what is the main function of a bank, the risk management. In Africa, the digitisation of the banking system has manifested itself through payment systems. This is the case in Kenya, Zimbabwe, Ghana and Mozambique, which to cite a few examples. The great challenge remains the penetration of these services into the economy. A study by the consulting firm McKinsey indicates that 90% of retail payments in Kenya - where we have MPESA - remains on the basis of cash. Or same study shows that in 11 countries in the region 80% of the adult population makes payments and remittances using cash. Despite the still low penetration of mobile payments, the potential is in sub-Saharan Africa. Two-thirds of the adult population has a cell phone. Therefore, what is the National Bank of Angola doing with regard to the digitisation of Banking? Ladies and gentlemen, Before answering this question, let me share that financial digitisation in Angola is a fact. The offer of electronic channels goes not only through the network interbank services but also for internet and mobile banking solutions. We also have in the our mobile payment solutions market at a later stage Embryonic I take this opportunity to share some information about what the National Bank of Angola is mobile and instant payments. With the the World Bank, the BNA has launched a project aimed at modernising and innovating the Angolan payments. The underlying objective is the implementation of mobile and instant payments for greater financial inclusion. This work contains two very pressing actions. First, the review of the entire legislation related to the Angolan payment system and the creation of a roadmap for the implementation of mobile and instant payments in Angola. The revision of the Payment System Act aims at the creation of a competitive environment and conducive to innovation. We intend to create the necessary conditions to that mobile payment solutions emerge that may, in contribute to financial inclusion. Secondly, as far as the development of mobile and instant payments are, this is our vision. We know that most of the solutions that are only serve the customers of the commercial banks that launched them. However, we are convinced that communication between these solutions and others that may be launched soon is the critical factor for them to avenge the market. For the National Bank of Angola, interoperability between solutions is a short-term objective. We will take all these steps without disdecorating the aspects related to the management of the inherent risks the activity of mobile payments, especially those related to money laundering and terrorist financing. We are also researching the merits of creating a sandbox, that is, an incubator of fintechs that allows the National Bank of Angola to be close to the private sector initiatives with a high probability of success and thus regulatory towards to provide a user-friendly environment for the development of banking system in particular and the economy in general. The BNA Payment Systems Department is fully available to receive contributions from society in general on how we can have a payment system at the service of the citizen and promoter of financial inclusion. To the magazine Economia e Mercado, I reiterate our thanks for the invitation that was made to us to be here today. Thank you so much for your attention. 30 Sep. 2018

Title: Speech at the 2nd Ordinary General Meeting of the Order of Accountants and Accountants of Angola
text: Intervention of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose de Lima Massano, in the 2nd Ordinary General Assembly of the Order of Accountants and Accountants of Angola Intervention of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose de Lima Massano, in the 2nd Ordinary General Meeting of the Order of Accountants and Accountants' Experts of Angola Mr. President of the Bureau of the General Assembly of the Order of Accountants and Accountants of Angola; Former Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Order of Accountants and Accountants of Angola; Very honorable members of the Order of Accountants and Accountants of Angola; Ladies and gentlemen; With satisfaction, I welcomed the invitation to participate in this 2nd Ordinary General Assembly of the Order of Accountants and Accountants of Angola, with the opportunity to address the impact and challenges of the Implementation of International Standards of Accounting in the Angolan Financial System. But before I get into the theme, I would like to express a word of personal appreciation to the fact that continue with the materialization of the old desire to constitution and affirmation of this Order, an instrument for the defense of interests of the class of accountants and accounting experts, but also of the potential ization of the sustainability of the national business fabric. The National Bank of Angola was always present and sought, in a positive way, to influence a faster formalization and operationalization of OCPCA, even allocating senior management to the constitutive tasks of this organization. Know that the path is still long but far go the years in which organise accounts, report management acts were mere exercises of goodwill and often misunderstood even by business managers. The irreversible process of globalization, in our day, leveraged by unique technological developments that we have seen, has enhanced the internationalization of trade, business and financial markets. Investors seek to opportunities for diversification and investment around the world, companies raise capital, conduct transactions or have operations and subsidiaries international organisations in several countries. In this context, the advantage of having a single set of standards of accounting and financial reporting, which are generally accepted, which aim to promote the standardization, comparability, reliability and transparency of the financial statements between entities with reference to a particular period. Modern economies depend on international transactions and the free flow of capital. More than one third of all financial transactions takes place beyond the the continued growth of this number is expected. International financial reporting standards are understood as an almost embodiment of globalization. Currently adopted, 87% of the 166 jurisdictions profiled by the IFRS Foundation require the use of IFRS (International Standards of Accounting and Financial Reporting), although with levels of scope Distinct. On the African continent, this figure amounts to 95% and, in sadc's profiled jurisdictions, a 92%. In this context and considering the plan of the National Bank of Angola to have in the country a system financial sector that acts in accordance with international standards and which can be considered equivalent to those of its international partners, the reform of the Angolan banking sector, which could not fail to include the adoption of the International Accounting and Financial Reporting Standards. Moreover, the integration of our financial system into the global payment network, allowing us to financial flows can be moved and traded regardless of the geographical location of the participants, obliges us to ensure compliance with the high standards of security and transparency of financial institutions. The path of introducing IFRS into banking is almost a decade old. In 2010, the BNA published CONTIF - Financial System Account Plan, where it introduced principles of IFRS, and remarkable advances have been made in terms of the quality of reported information. In October 2013, with the aim of fully adopting IFRS in the banking sector, we the first formal contacts with the International Committee Accounting Standard Board (IASB), and BNA has chosen to by the adoption model by reference, i.e. the standards should be adopted as they are issued by the IASB. Still, not being lost the possibility of adjusting or defering them whenever aspects associated with stability of the national financial system are at stake. Given the specificities of IFRS and the complexity of their implementation, the BNA allowed the adoption of phased mode, starting with commercial banks with a total assets exceeding 300 billion Kwanzas or being subsidiaries of entities based in abroad, or banks based in the national territory with subsidiaries abroad. This phase consisted of 16 banks, whose market share corresponded, at that time, at about 80%. The first phase banks began to prepare and report their ifrs financial statements to from the 2016 financial year and the remainder from the financial year of 2017. BNA maintains a specialized IFRS core to continuously meet the needs of banking institutions in matters relating to the principles of issued by the International Acconting Standard Board and has published Instructional or Practical Guides to assist the market in the proper interpretation and implementation of relevant standards, including: (i) disclosure of financial instruments - IFRS 7, (ii) impairment losses for the credit portfolio - IAS 39, (iii) Leases - IAS 17, (iv) effective interest rate - IAS 39, (v) recognition and disclosure of benefits of employees - IAS 19, and (vi) securities - IAS 39. The implementation of the International Standards served to highlight the complexity of the process and the aspects that were the greatest challenges for financial institutions and which should continue to be improved, in particular: Qualification of human resources - internal training actions are needed to enable a good understanding of the Standards and also in the future, the identification and implementation of changes resulting from the evolution of the regulation. Procedures and internal control - there are significant impacts on procedures and controls in a a wide range of processes and areas, which are not only in the accounting. Changes and adjustments to the corporate governance model are required in so that transparency of management acts. Information systems - should evolve in the definition and implementation of the necessary functionalities to comply with the implementation of the ensure the effectiveness of general computer controls. The implementation of IFRS in the financial sector turns out to be another reminder that the change and continuous process improvement are a constant in successful organizations. A constant evolution of standards implies a constant evolution of the procedures. Banks should strengthen not only the internal control that guarantees best practices, but the culture of accountability and permanent adequacy of work systems and processes. The National Bank of Angola is also not oblivious to the process of change. In fact, since 2013, our financial statements are published in accordance with international accounting and financial reporting standards. This implementation led to the bna to define, on the one hand, a methodology of convergence, (i) revision of accounting roadmaps; (ii) drawing up a new plan of accounts and definition of conversion matrices; iii) identification of requirements (iv) definition of internal and external reporting maps. On the other hand, it has developed an updated accounting policy manual in compliance with the new accounting framework, including (i) assumptions used in the calculation of estimates, (ii) information circuits and (iii) levels of service associated with the preparation and dissemination of information financial statements, as well as how the financial statements and their financial statements are annexed in accordance with international best practices. The process of adoption of international standards has also led the BNA to adjust the governance model towards the development of a capacity building plan human capital, the introduction of changes in management and internal control policies, as well as the changes in computer systems. In our country, the financial sector is still the only one subject to the requirement of international Accounting and Financial Reporting, however, we have the prospect that, in the not-so-distant future, this requirement is extended to other sectors of the considering the benefits associated with its implementation and the efforts to attract more foreign investment to Angola. In this context, it is very important to train accounting in order to become proficient in the application of the International. The Order of Accountants and Accountants of Angola (OCPCA) has a key role to play in play in raising awareness and training of its members implementation and implementation of IAS/IFRS. The National Bank of Angola, considering its experience and skills created in this area over the long term, of recent years, is available to assist the Order in this challenge. We have been following the efforts that OCPCA has made over its early years of activity with accountants and accountants, in the updating and training in various subjects and we wanted to stimulate the continuation of this process even more intensively, considering that the the existence of well-qualified and prepared accountants is an essential factor for the development of our business sector and consequently of our economy. I take the opportunity to wish the Order and its professionals the greatest successes. Happy Party Vows! Thank you so much for your attention. 15 of Dec. 2018

Assembleia-Geral Ordinria da Ordem dos Contabilistas e Peritos Contabilistas de Angola Interveno do Governador do Banco Nacional de Angola, Jos de Lima Massano, na 2. Assembleia-Geral Ordinria da Ordem dos Contabilistas e Peritos Contabilistas de Angola Exmo. Presidente da Mesa da Assembleia-Geral da Ordem dos Contabilistas e Peritos Contabilistas de Angola; Exmo. Presidente do Conselho Directivo da Ordem dos Contabilistas e Peritos Contabilistas de Angola; Dignssimos membros da Ordem dos Contabilistas e Peritos Contabilistas de Angola; Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores; Com satisfao, acolhi o convite para participar nesta 2. Assembleia-Geral Ordinria da Ordem dos Contabilistas e Peritos Contabilistas de Angola, tendo a oportunidade de abordar o impacto e desafios da Implementao das Normas Internacionais de Contabilidade no Sistema Financeiro Angolano. Mas antes de entrar no tema, gostaria de expressar uma palavra de apreo pessoal ao facto de se prosseguir com a materializao do desejo antigo de constituio e afirmao desta Ordem, um instrumento de defesa de interesses da classe de contabilistas e peritos de contabilidade, mas tambm, de potenciao da sustentabilidade do tecido empresarial nacional. O Banco Nacional de Angola esteve sempre presente e procurou, de modo positivo, influenciar uma mais rpida formalizao e operacionalizao da OCPCA, chegando mesmo a alocar quadros superiores seus s tarefas constitutivas desta organizao. Sabemos que o caminho ainda  longo, mas longe vo os anos em que organizar contas, reportar actos de gesto eram meros exerccios de boa vontade e muitas vezes incompreendidos at mesmo por gestores empresariais. O processo irreversvel da globalizao, nos nossos dias, alavancado pelos desenvolvimentos tecnolgicos mpares a que assistimos, tem potenciado a internacionalizao do comrcio, negcios e mercados financeiros. Os investidores procuram oportunidades de diversificao e investimento em todo o mundo, enquanto que as empresas captam capital, realizam transaes ou possuem operaes e subsidirias internacionais em vrios pases. Neste contexto, foi internacionalmente reconhecida a vantagem de ter um conjunto nico de normas de contabilidade e relato financeiro, globalmente aceites, que visam promover a padronizao, comparabilidade, fiabilidade e transparncia das demonstraes financeiras entre entidades com referncia a um determinado perodo. Economias modernas dependem de transaces internacionais e do livre fluxo de capital. Mais de um tero de todas as transaces financeiras ocorre alm das fronteiras, sendo previsvel o crescimento contnuo desse nmero. Os padres internacionais de relato financeiro so entendidos como uma quase personificao da globalizao. Adoptadas presentemente, 87% das 166 jurisdies perfiladas pela IFRS Foundation requerem a utilizao das IFRS (Normas Internacionais de Contabilidade e Relato Financeiro), embora com nveis de abrangncia distintos. No continente Africano, este nmero ascende a 95% e, nas jurisdies perfiladas da SADC, a 92%. Neste enquadramento e considerando o desgnio do Banco Nacional de Angola de ter no pas um sistema financeiro que actua de acordo com padres internacionais e que possa ser considerado equivalente aos dos seus parceiros internacionais, foi iniciada a reforma do sector bancrio angolano, que no podia deixar de incluir a plena adopo das Normas Internacionais de Contabilidade e Relato Financeiro. Mais ainda, a integrao do nosso sistema financeiro na rede global de pagamentos, permitindo que fluxos financeiros possam ser movimentados e transaccionados independentemente da localizao geogrfica dos participantes, obriga-nos a assegurar o cumprimento de elevados padres de segurana e de transparncia das instituies financeiras. O percurso de introduo das IFRS na banca tem quase uma dcada. Em 2010, o BNA publicou o CONTIF - Plano de Contas do Sistema Financeiro, onde introduziu diversos princpios das IFRS, tendo-se registado avanos notveis em termos da qualidade de informao reportada. Em Outubro 2013, com o objectivo de se adoptar plenamente as IFRS no sector bancrio, desencademos os primeiros contactos formais com o Comit Internacional de Normalizao Contabilstica (Internacional Accounting Standard Board - IASB), tendo o BNA optado pelo modelo de adopo por referncia, isto , as normas devem ser adoptadas tal como elas so emitidas pelo IASB. Ainda assim, no se perdendo a possibilidade de ajust-las ou deferi-las sempre que aspectos associados  estabilidade do sistema financeiro nacional estejam em causa. Dadas as especificidades das IFRS e complexidade da sua implementao, o BNA permitiu a adopo de modo faseado, iniciando com bancos comerciais com um total de activo superior a 300 mil milhes de Kwanzas ou sendo subsidirias de entidades sedeadas no estrangeiro, ou ainda bancos sedeados no territrio nacional com subsidirias no estrangeiro. Essa fase comportou 16 bancos, cuja quota de mercado correspondia, naquela altura, a cerca de 80%. Os bancos da 1. fase comearam a preparar e a reportar as suas demonstraes financeiras em IFRS a partir do exerccio de 2016 e os restantes a partir do exerccio de 2017. O BNA mantm um ncleo especializado em IFRS para atender continuamente as necessidades das instituies bancrias em matrias relacionadas com os princpios emitidos pelo International Acconting Standard Board e tem publicado Instrutivos ou Guias Prticos para auxiliar o mercado na adequada interpretao e execuo das normas mais relevantes, incluindo: (i) divulgao de instrumentos financeiros - IFRS 7, (ii) perdas por imparidade para a carteira de crdito - IAS 39, (iii) Locaes - IAS 17, (iv) taxa de juro efectiva - IAS 39, (v) reconhecimento e divulgao de benefcios dos empregados - IAS 19, e (vi) ttulos e valores mobilirios - IAS 39. A implementao das Normas Internacionais serviu para salientar a complexidade do processo e os aspectos que constituram os maiores desafios para as instituies financeiras e que devem continuar a ser melhorados, nomeadamente: Qualificao dos recursos humanos - so necessrias aces de capacitao interna que permitam um bom entendimento das Normas e tambm no futuro, a identificao e implementao das alteraes que decorrerem da evoluo do normativo. Procedimentos e controlo interno - h impactos significativos em procedimentos e controlos num conjunto alargado de processos e reas, que no apenas na da contabilidade. Impem-se alteraes e ajustamentos ao modelo de governao corporativa, para que se garanta maior transparncia dos actos de gesto. Sistemas de informao - devem evoluir na definio e implementao das funcionalidades necessrias para dar cumprimento  implementao das Normas Internacionais, bem como assegurar a efectividade dos controlos gerais informticos. A implementao das IFRS no sector financeiro acaba por ser mais um lembrete de que a mudana e a melhoria contnua de processos so uma constante em organizaes de sucesso. Uma constante evoluo das normas implica uma constante evoluo dos procedimentos. Os bancos devem fortalecer no apenas o controlo interno que garanta as melhores prticas, mas a cultura de responsabilizao e de adequao permanente de sistemas e processos de trabalho. O Banco Nacional de Angola tambm no  alheio ao processo de mudanas. De facto, desde 2013, as nossas demonstraes financeiras so publicadas de acordo com as normas internacionais de contabilidade e de relato financeiro. Esta implementao levou o BNA a definir, por um lado, uma metodologia de convergncia, designadamente i) reviso de roteiros contabilsticos; ii) elaborao de um novo plano de contas e definio de matrizes de converso; iii) identificao de requisitos de divulgao e iv) definio de mapas de reporte interno e externo. Por outro lado, procedeu  elaborao de um manual de polticas contabilsticas actualizado em conformidade com o novo referencial contabilstico, entre as quais se encontram: i) pressupostos utilizados no clculo de estimativas, ii) circuitos de informao e iii) nveis de servio associados  preparao e divulgao de informao financeira, bem como a forma de apresentao das demonstraes financeiras e respectivas notas anexas de acordo com as melhores prticas internacionais. O processo de adopo das normas internacionais levou ainda o BNA a ajustar o modelo de governao no sentido de desenvolvimento de um plano de capacitao do seu capital humano, introduo de alteraes de polticas de gesto e de controlo interno, bem como a alteraes nos sistemas informticos. No nosso pas, o sector financeiro ainda  o nico sujeito  exigncia das Normas Internacionais de Contabilidade e Relato Financeiro, todavia, perspectivamos que, num futuro no to distante, este requisito seja alargado a outros sectores da economia considerando os benefcios associados  sua implementao e aos esforos do Executivo para atrair mais investimento estrangeiro para Angola. Neste contexto, torna-se muito importante a capacitao dos profissionais de contabilidade de forma a se tornarem proficientes na aplicao das Normas Internacionais. A Ordem dos Contabilistas e Peritos Contabilistas de Angola (OCPCA) tem um papel fundamental a desempenhar na sensibilizao e formao dos seus membros quanto  implementao e aplicao das IAS/IFRS. O Banco Nacional de Angola, considerando a sua experincia e as competncias criadas nesta matria ao longo dos ltimos anos, est disponvel para assistir a Ordem neste desafio. Temos acompanhado os esforos que a OCPCA tem desenvolvido ao longo dos seus primeiros anos de actividade junto dos contabilistas e peritos contabilistas, na sua actualizao e capacitao em diversas matrias e queramos estimular a continuao desse processo de forma ainda mais intensa, considerando que a existncia de contabilistas bem qualificados e preparados  um factor essencial para o desenvolvimento do nosso sector empresarial e consequentemente da nossa economia. Aproveito a oportunidade para desejar os maiores sucessos  Ordem e aos seus profissionais. Votos de Festas Felizes! Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno. Title: Opening Speech of the Conference on Private Sector Financing of H.E. Minister of State for Economic and Social Development
text: Opening Speech of the Conference on Financing the Private Sector of S.E.A. Minister of State of Economic and Social Development, Dr. Manuel Nunes Junior Opening Speech of the Conference on Financing for the Private Sector of S.Exa Minister of State for Development Economic and Social, Dr. Manuel Nunes Junior Excellency, Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Excellency, Members of the National Assembly, Excellencies, members of the Executive, Exmos. Presidents and members of the Boards of Directors of the commercial banks present, Distinguished representatives of the Business Associations, Distinguished guests, Ladies and gentlemen, My thanks to the National Bank of Angola, and in particular to the President. institution, for inviting me to give the speech of opening of this important conference on Private Sector Financing in Angola. This BNA initiative is not only of enormous relevance to the life of the country, but also highly timely. It is already almost commonplace to say that our economy is too dependent on oil and that needs to be diverse. Unfortunately, we will have to continue to make such a statement because it corresponds to the truth. It is a objective fact. Therefore, we must get out of the simple rhetoric and face the increase in national production and the diversification of the economy as a national imperative. An economy whose fundamental dynamics depends on a single product, the price of which is not controlled by us, it is not a sustained economy. It's an economy fragile and unprepared to face external shocks derived from negative price variations of this single export product. We want to build an economy based on strong and sustained growth in Angola. To this end, we will have to end this great dependence on one product that guarantees about 95% of the country's external resources and about 70% of all revenue angola's tax authorities. In order to achieve this goal, we need to to establish a fundamental factor in our economy: trust. Trust in institutions and business is a key element for the functioning of modern economies and societies. It can even be said that where there is no trust there are no investments at appropriate levels. Where there is no trust, the banks do not give credit to satisfactory levels and there is no credit there are investments. If there is no investment, there is no growth and where there is no growth there is no prosperity. In 2018, very important steps were taken to restore the confidence of economic impacts in the Angolan market. The foreign exchange market is moving towards standardisation, with the difference between the official exchange rate and the prevailing one on the parallel market to decrease considerably. Late foreign exchange payments for 2015, 2016 and 2017 are being regularised and commitments in the country's foreign currency begin to be honored regularly. The inflation rate is falling and last year will have fallen below 19%, when the OGE for 2018 predicted a rate of 28%. Confidence is starting to resettle in the Angolan market and this is very positive for investment, whether national or international. The Stabilization Program macroeconomic policy that we have been implementing since January 2018, essentially aims to restore the confidence in the market and is being successfully driven. This Macroeconomic Stabilisation Programme is now, as we know, being supported technically and financially by the International Monetary Fund. On the other hand, measures are being taken to install a genuine state of right that no one is above the Law. It is difficult to invest in a country where it is not certain that the law, where necessary, is applied in a objectively and equally for all. Today in this field begins to live a different environment in Angola. Our perception and perception of the rest of the world about us begins to change. This is positive either for us Angolans, as well as for foreigners who want to invest in Angola. Ladies and gentlemen, as confidence in our economy is restored, the conditions for the promoting the competitiveness of our companies with a view to increase in national production. The increase in the market share of domestic production of goods and services is a critical factor for the sustainability of both public finances and accounts external relations in the country. About 7 years ago, the National Bank of Angola conducted a study in which the the main constraints of the granting of credit by banks private sector, both on the demand and supply side. The study found that demand side, borrowers, the main constraints were the high interest rates and guarantees demanded by the banks. On the supply side, i.e. on the side of commercial banks, the main constraints found were the lack of organized accounting in companies and the low level of financial literacy. We are certain that all these constraints can and will have to be removed in so that the credit can flow into our economy. In this context, the State has an important role. In the period from 2013 to 2017 there was a sharp drop in total Treasury revenues, a fall in which was not accompanied by a proportional reduction in expenditure. This has resulted in systematic tax deficits financed through the state debt, both internal and external. In 2016 there was a deficit of 3.7% of GDP and in 2017 a deficit of 6.3%. Systematic deficits have resulted in an increase in the country's debt levels, with the from less than 30% of GDP in 2013 to around 30% of GDP in 2013. 79% of GDP in 2017. It should be noted that the higher the state indebtedness, the higher the interest rates Internal. This reduces the potential for economic growth, mainly because it inhibits credit to the private sector, which now has to face interest rates very high. Thanks to the implementation of the tax measures contained in the Macroeconomic Stabilisation Programme, the fiscal deficit will have decreased in 2018, having gone from a deficit from 6.3% in 2017 to a surplus of around 0.4% of GDP. For this year 2019, a surplus is expected to be around 1%. This great effort that the government is making to get out of deficit budget balances to surplus balances is key to reversing the trend of indebtedness of the country and make more room for commercial banks to provide more credit to the economy. We're doing our part, now we expect commercial banks to do theirs. In this room, people are gathered with the knowledge and experience necessary to make that credit to the economy increases and that the country enter a fast economic growth route, increasing domestic production, increasing employment, increasing angolan incomes and contributing to the prosperity of the Angolan nation. We must enter the virtuous circle of prosperity. The role of commercial banks in this process is crucial. Help us with all your wisdom to get there. Thank you for your attention and I declare open the Conference on Private Sector Financing. Jan. 23. 2019

Title: Opening Speech at the Meeting of the Financial Markets Subcommittee of the CCBG
text: Opening Speech of the Vice President - Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Manuel Antonio Tiago Dias, at the CCBG Financial Markets Subcommittee Meeting Opening Speech of the Vice - Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Manuel Antonio Tiago Days, at the Meeting of the Subcommittee on Markets CCBG Financial Exmos. Representatives of the Financial Markets Subcommittee of the Bank's Steering Committee SADC Plants (CCBG); Exmos. Representatives of the SADC Value Scholarship Committee; Exmos. Representatives of the Secretariat of the Southern African Development Community (SADC); Ladies and gentlemen, On behalf of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola, in particular governor Jose Lima Massano, I wish you all a welcome to the meeting of the Subcommittee on Financial Markets of the SADC Central Bank Steering Committee. It is an honor to welcome you to our country, particularly in the welcoming city of Benguela. Hope that, in addition to participating in this event, have some time to know the charms of this beautiful Angolan city and that can benefit from the hospitality of our people. Since the establishment of the CCBG Financial Markets Subcommittee, every year we have met, in one of the member countries in order to give a our modest contribution to the development of our financial markets. In the end, this contribution should provide a platform for the economic growth in the region. A well-developed and efficient financial market plays an important role in growth of the economy, financing the accumulation of capital, capacity-resourced resources, adaptation and emergence of innovative technologies. And how region, we want to achieve a high level of growth and economic development, which is why we are here, to help financial markets to role as catalysts. Thus, in 2019, we must continue to observe, at regional level, a further financial system, with the adequacy of our financial systems to the international best practices, both with regard to regulation and their supervision. This will boost economic growth and integration establishing bases for the diversification of the productive sectors, as well as for commercial partnerships within our sub-region. Greater regional integration in financial terms will allow greater resilience to shocks international countries such as the one that affects most African countries exporters of raw materials since 2014. This meeting takes place in Angola at a time when the financial and banking system, under supervision of the National Bank of Angola, as Central Bank of the Republic of Angola, is in a process of consolidation in terms of strengthening minimum capital and equity requirements regulations, but also to comply with international standards and standards of prevention and combating money laundering and the financing of terrorism. This requires financial system operators to strengthen internal control of risks, i.e. a better knowledge of its customers and the nature of of its operations. The realization of these types of events is also an opportune time to learn from each other, since each of us is at different levels of development in many areas. These meetings in addition to focusing on the convergence of regional financial markets, also offer a opportunity for us to grow together. I am sure that each of the participants, and all the countries represented here, will benefit from the certainly positive debates that will take place in this magna meeting. To finish, ladies and gentlemen, I wish the Subcommittee active and Constructive. We all hope for a pleasant stay in Angola. Thank you so much for your attention. Feb. 8. 2019

Desde o estabelecimento do Subcomit de Mercados Financeiros do CCBG, todos os anos nos reunimos, rotativamente, num dos pases membros, a fim de dar continuidade  nossa modesta contribuio para o desenvolvimento dos nossos mercados financeiros.
