Um mercado financeiro bem desenvolvido e eficiente desempenha um papel importante no crescimento da economia, financiando a acumulao de capital, potencializao dos recursos humanos, adaptao e surgimento de tecnologias inovadoras. E como regio, desejamos alcanar um patamar alto de crescimento e de desenvolvimento econmicos, razo pela qual aqui estamos, para ajudarmos os mercados financeiros a desempenharem o seu papel de catalisadores. Assim, no ano de 2019, devemos continuar a observar, a nvel regional, um maior aprofundamento financeiro, com a adequao dos nossos sistemas financeiros s melhores prticas internacionais, tanto no que se refere  regulamentao como  sua superviso. Tal permitir alavancar o crescimento econmico e a integrao regional, estabelecendo bases para a diversificao dos sectores produtivos, assim como para parcerias comerciais dentro da nossa sub-regio. Uma maior integrao regional, em termos financeiros, permitir maior resilincia a choques internacionais como o que afecta grande parte dos pases africanos exportadores de matrias-primas desde 2014. A realizao desta reunio em Angola ocorre numa altura em que o sistema financeiro e bancrio, sob superviso do Banco Nacional de Angola, na qualidade de Banco Central da Repblica de Angola, se encontra num processo de consolidao em termos de reforo dos requisitos mnimos de capital e de fundos prprios regulamentares, mas, igualmente, de adequao s normas e padres internacionais de preveno e combate ao branqueamento de capitais e ao financiamento do terrorismo. Tal exige dos operadores do sistema financeiro o reforo do controlo interno de riscos, ou seja, um melhor conhecimento dos seus clientes e da natureza das suas operaes. A realizao deste tipo de eventos  tambm um momento oportuno para aprendermos uns com os outros, uma vez que cada um de ns est em diferentes nveis de desenvolvimento em muitas reas. Estas reunies alm de se concentrarem na convergncia dos mercados financeiros regionais, tambm oferecem uma oportunidade para podermos crescer juntos. Tenho a certeza de que cada um dos participantes, e todos os pases aqui representados, iro beneficiar dos debates, certamente positivos, que ocorrero nesta magna reunio. Para terminar, minhas senhoras e meus senhores, desejo ao Subcomit deliberaes activas e construtivas. A todos formulamos votos de uma agradvel estadia em Angola. Muito Obrigado pela vossa ateno. Title: Opening Speech at the Presentation Workshop of the Osf Module of the DES Portal
text: Opening Speech Administrator Pedro Rodrigo Goncalves Castro E Silva Presentation Workshop of the OSF Module of the DES Portal Opening Speech Administrator Pedro Rodrigo Goncalves Castro E Silva Workshop Presentation of the OSF Module of the DES Portal -Dear Directors and Directors of Financial Institutions here Represented; - Dear Directors, Sub-Directors and Technicians of BNA; - Distinguished Statistical Correspondents; - Ladies and gentlemen; On behalf of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola, I would like to welcome all the guests to this workshop that has as to present the new module of the "PORTAL DES", a computer solution developed by the National Bank of Angola with a view to collecting and treating statistical information from various public and private institutions. The DES Portal has been operational since March 2015. As a first stage, the application meets the automation needs of the sources statistical information for the compilation of Balance of Payments statistics, i.e. bop module. From today the module is officially debuted Other Financial Corporations (OSF) of the DES Portal, which will support the compilation of OSF statistics through the submission of FDD standardized forms. Pursuant to Law No. 16/10 of July 15 (Law of the National Bank of Angola) and Law No. 3/11, January 14 (Law of the National Statistical System), the BNA to ensure and ensure an information system for the compilation of monetary and Financial. Therefore, after completing the process of compilation of OSF statistics later this year, the conditions will be created for the the compilation and publication of monetary statistics and angolan financial system (SFA). This will be a huge step, since on the one hand, users of the statistics produced by the BNA will have access to quality and higher-quality information coverage of the financial system, always safeguarding the principle of confidentiality, and on the other hand, these statistics will enable the BNA to produce the country's National Financial Accounts. The high degree of sophistication of financial products in many advanced countries has been increase the weight of the activities carried out by the Other Financial Corporations, such as Insurance Companies, Microcredit Corporations, Financial Credit, Leasing and Factoring Companies, Pension Funds, Investment Funds, etc. in the Gross Domestic Product of the respective countries. Angola's future also points to this path, although at present, the total other financial corporations represents no more than 7% of the total assets of the Angolan Financial System (SFA). In the contemporary world, it is not possible to define policies without relying on statistical data reliable solutions that can support decision-making. Face to this premise, the need to improve the quality and scope of monetary statistics is urgently needed to improve and financial institutions of the country, as these constitute the main instrument to support the Central Bank's monetary policy measures. As the Producer Body for Official Statistics, the National Bank of Angola has been to permanently improve the quality of statistics macroeconomic measures produced by them, following international good practice. Therefore, the automation of information sources and increased coverage fundamental assumptions for achieving this purpose. Dear guests, In the current context, the use of new technologies has been a strong ally for institutions dealing with large volume of information, however, the National Bank of Angola in ways to optimise the time and responsiveness of the compilation, is honored to present to all participants a new tool that will be available to all institutions that are part of the Other Financial Corporations. The aim of this action is to reduce the previously recorded constraints, such as failure to send the e-mail and the excessive human intervention in the process of analysis and treatment of the data. The system will have several levels of data validation and an instruction manual to assist in use of the application. In order to make the process transparent and accessible to all, all technical support will be provided through unilateral sessions of to clarify the implementation of those features. The BNA is not indifferent to the difficulties faced by the institutions present here, with respect to concerns the issues of mastery of concepts and methodology decompilation of monetary and financial statistics. So we have a group of technicians indicated to provide the necessary support in order to ensure the quality and reliability of the data. Finally, we want to call for the greatest possible collaboration of the institutions represented here, in particular, with regard to compliance with the time limits for sending or submission of forms in the portal. We believe that the country will have an invaluable gain, with the production of statistics of other financial corporations, and consequently the National Financial Accounts. With these brief words, I declare this workshop open. 1 sea. 2019

Directores, Subdirectores e Tcnicos do BNA; - Ilustres Correspondentes Estatsticos; - Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores; Em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco Nacional de Angola, gostaria de dar as boas vindas a todos os convidados a este workshop que tem como finalidade apresentar o novo mdulo do Portal DES, uma soluo informtica desenvolvida pelo Banco Nacional de Angola com vista  recolha e tratamento das informaes estatsticas de vrias instituies pblicas e privadas. O Portal DES entrou em funcionamento desde o ms de Maro do ano 2015. Numa primeira fase, o aplicativo atendia as necessidades de automatizao das fontes de informao estatstica para a compilao das estatsticas da Balana de Pagamentos, isto , mdulo da BOP. A partir de hoje estreia-se de forma oficial o mdulo das Outras Sociedades Financeiras (OSF) do Portal DES, que servir de suporte para a compilao das estatsticas das OSF atravs da submisso dos formulrios padronizados FDD. Nos termos da Lei n 16/10, de 15 de Julho (Lei do Banco Nacional de Angola) e da Lei n 3/11, de 14 de Janeiro (Lei do Sistema Estatstico Nacional), compete ao BNA garantir e assegurar um sistema de informao para compilao das estatsticas monetrias e financeiras. Por isso, depois de concludo o processo de compilao das estatsticas das OSF ainda no decorrer deste ano, estaro criadas as condies para a compilao e publicao das estatsticas monetrias e financeiras de todo o Sistema Financeiro Angolano (SFA). Este ser um passo gigantesco, visto que por um lado, os usurios das estatsticas produzidas pelo BNA tero acesso s informaes de qualidade e com maior cobertura do sistema financeiro, salvaguardando sempre o princpio da confidencialidade, e por outro lado, as referidas estatsticas permitiro ao BNA produzir  mdio prazo as Contas Nacionais Financeiras do Pas. O elevado grau de sofisticao dos produtos financeiros em muitos pases avanados, tem vindo a aumentar o peso das actividades desenvolvidas pelas Outras Sociedades Financeiras, tais como, Seguradoras, Sociedades de Microcrdito, Cooperativas de Crdito, Sociedades de Leasing e Factoring, Fundos de Penses, Fundos de Investimentos, etc, no Produto Interno Bruto dos respectivos pases. O futuro de Angola aponta tambm para este caminho, apesar de que actualmente, o total de activos das Outras Sociedades Financeiras representa no mais do que 7% do total de activos do Sistema Financeiro Angolano (SFA). No mundo contemporneo, no  possvel definir polticas sem basear-se em dados estatsticos fiveis que possam servir de suporte  tomada de decises. Face a estapremissa, urge a necessidade de se aprimorar a qualidade e o mbito das estatsticas monetrias e financeiras do Pas, pois estas constituem o principal instrumento de suporte s medidas de poltica monetria do Banco Central. Enquanto rgo Produtor de Estatsticas Oficiais, o Banco Nacional de Angola tem vindo a melhorar permanentemente a qualidade das estatsticas macroeconmicas por si produzidas, seguindo as boas prticas internacionais. Assim sendo, a automatizao das fontes de informao e o aumento da cobertura estatstica so pressupostos fundamentais para atingir este propsito. Caros convidados, No contexto actual, o recurso s novas tecnologias tem sido um forte aliado para as instituies que lidam com grande volume de informao, contudo, o Banco Nacional de Angola de formas a optimizar o tempo e a capacidade de resposta do processo de compilao, tem a honra de apresentar a todos os participantes uma nova ferramenta que estar disponvel a todas as instituies que integram as Outras Sociedades Financeiras. Pretende-se com esta aco reduzir os constrangimentos anteriormente registados, tais como falha no envio do correio electrnico e a excessiva interveno humana no processo de anlise e tratamento dos dados. O sistema ter vrios nveis de validao dos dados e um manual de instrues para auxiliar na utilizao do aplicativo. De forma a tornar o processo transparente e acessvel a todos, ser prestado todo o apoio tcnico por intermdio de sesses unilaterais de forma a clarificar a execuo das referidas funcionalidades. O BNA no est indiferente s dificuldades enfrentadas pelas instituies aqui presentes, no que diz respeito as questes de domnio de conceitos e metodologia decompilao das estatsticas monetrias e financeiras. Pelo que, temos um grupo de tcnicos indicados a prestarem o apoio necessrio, a fim de se garantir a qualidade e fiabilidade dos dados. Finalmente, queremos apelar a maior colaborao possvel das instituies aqui representadas, sobretudo, no que diz respeito ao cumprimento dos prazos de envio ou submisso dos formulrios no portal. Acreditamos que o Pas ter um ganho inestimvel, com a produo das estatsticas das Outras Sociedades Financeiras, e consequentemente das Conta Nacionais Financeiras. Com estas breves palavras, declaro aberto este workshop. text: Address of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the closing ceremony of the 7th Edition of the Banking Study in Analysis Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the closing ceremony of the 7th Edition of the Banking Study in Analysis Mr President of the Capital Markets Commission Former President of the Angolan Banking Association Dear Members, Presidents of the Boards of Directors and Executive Committees of The Banks Commercial; Mr. Delegate in Angola of Deloitte Ladies and gentlemen, On behalf of the National Bank of Angola, I would like to thank the invitation addressed to us to participate in the closure of this Forum. Throughout the morning we were able to appreciate the main indicators of the Angolan banking system, which report the 2011 financial year, which highlights the maintenance of the growth path, evidenced both by the increase in deposits and credit to the economy. Although this is not the case in economies strongly linked to Angola through trade international cooperation, financial stability has been a constant in our system. As you know, the National Bank of Angola has recently established the Financial Stability - THE COMEF - whose main objective is to identify potential risks and their impact on the balance sheet of the financial system in general and of each bank, in a particular way. In the few months since we began to study more deeply the determinants of financial stability in Angola, we have made it in fact, there is a strong relationship between this and monetary policy, and this is one of the on which I would like to address this opportunity. With inflation control it will be possible to eliminate expectations that prices will remain always at a high level and therefore reduce the space for the formation of speculative bubbles, and at the same time stimulate the decisions of investment, i.e. inflation control leads us to reduce the cost of capital, which is important for market stability and for the creation of an environment of sustainable socio-economic development. We have started the gradual migration to the flexible inflation target system, with the introduction of a new operational framework for the implementation of monetary policy in october 2011 and the results, measured by the behaviour of inflation, have been positive. Annual inflation rose from 11.91% to 9.65%, achieving the much-desired single-digit rate. The corresponding reduction in the interest rate on the secondary market is taking place positively on the economic and financial viability of without, however, causing damage to the solvency of commercial banks. Data in June 2012 show that the solvency ratio of the angolan banking, was 13.4%, above the minimum limit of 10% established by the regulations in force. But the full adoption of the inflation target scheme is a demanding process from the point of view of the accuracy and transparency of monetary policy decisions, but which also needs the participation of all economic actors, particularly operators financial resources, given the role reserved for it as a channel of transmission of policies and financial deepening of the economy. In Angola, financial deepening, measured by the m2 monetary aggregate ratio (which includes either banknotes and coins in public power such as deposits in the gross domestic product is around 32%. Credit to the economy, due to the GDP is 22%, i.e. although assinable is still short of some of the economies of the SADC region. The growth of the banking system and its weight in the economy will also be made by increasing the credit. In recent years, the rate of transformation of deposits in credit has been around 60%, on average for all banks, but it is necessary to improve both the governance rules of the institutions financial instruments, such as risk control instruments, so that more credit does not assume less than stability of the financial system. Ladies and gentlemen, On the BNA side, we will continue to conduct an attentive but prudent monetary policy, in the expectation of that by this way we are contributing to the protection of stability and stimulate investment in the national economy. At the September monetary policy committee meeting, we opted for the maintenance of the basic rate of interest rate at 10.25%, which has remained unchanged since February 2010. current year. In addition to staying positive in real terms, i.e. above inflation, it has no conditioning credit growth to the economy, which in the first 8 months of the year was about 17%. On the other hand, the evolution of the means of payment is also in line with the inflation target, despite the fact that there is a greater growth in the national law under the regulatory limitations imposed on the granting of credit in Foreign. In the year, the supply of national currency in the growth of around 15%. The accumulation of net international reserves has also been achieved and guaranteed by the favorable behavior of the price of crude oil in the markets International. This framework contributes to the stability of the parity of the national currency against the dollar of the United States of America, moreover, one of the elements considered as part of determinants of inflation in Angola. Despite the expectations of some analysts, it is our understanding that, at the present juncture, a more aggressive and sharp reduction in the basic interest rate could not cause significant gains in the immediate increase in credit to the economy, nor to support the containment of prices, but, on the contrary, could exert a stability of the financial system taking into account the current composition of the financial assets of commercial banks. In any case, we have reduced the rate of permanent liquidity-making facility to 11.5%, reducing the cost of financing with the bank in the expectation of reducing the gap between active and passive rates, and increasing the encouraging financial operators to continuously support the Business. Already in the quarter of higher demand for goods and services in our economy, the BNA will remain monitoring of liquidity flows, not in any case, significant changes to the course of monetary policy by the end of the current year. We want to continue to communicate with the market with the aim of sharing elements that underpin our decisions and that we hope will serve to sustain the your options. To Deloitte, we thank you once again for the invitation and congratulate you on the initiative and the way consistent with which it has held these presentation forums and public analysis of banking performance in Angola. Thank you very much. Oct. 17. 2012

Presidentes dos Conselhos de Administrao e das Comisses Executivas dos Bancos Comerciais; Exmo Senhor Delegado em Angola da Deloitte Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Em nome do Banco Nacional de Angola, gostaria de agradecer o convite que nos foi endereado para participar no encerramento deste Forum. Ao longo da manh pudemos apreciar os principais indicadores do sistema bancrio angolano, que reportam o exerccio de 2011, onde se destaca a manuteno da trajectria de crescimento, evidenciada quer pelo aumento dos depsitos como do crdito  economia. Ainda que no se verifique em economias fortemente ligadas a Angola por via do comrcio internacional, a estabilidade financeira tem sido uma constante no nosso sistema. Como  do vosso conhecimento, o Banco Nacional de Angola, instituiu recentemente o Comit de Estabilidade Financeira  o COMEF  cujo principal objectivo  o de identificar potenciais riscos e seu impacto no balano do sistema financeiro de uma forma geral e de cada banco, de forma particular. Nos poucos meses decorridos desde que comeamos a estudar com maior profundidade as determinantes da estabilidade financeira em Angola, comprovmos que, de facto, existe uma forte relao entre esta e a poltica monetria, e este  um dos aspectos sobre o qual gostaria de me debruar nesta oportunidade. Com o controlo da inflao ser possvel eliminar expectativas de que os preos se iro manter sempre num nvel elevado e por isso reduzir-se o espao para a formao de bolhas especulativas, e, em simultneo, estimular-se favoravelmente as decises de investimento, o seja, o controlo da inflao leva-nos a reduo do custo de capital, importante para a estabilidade dos mercados e para a criao de um ambiente de desenvolvimento socioeconmico sustentvel. Iniciamos a migrao gradual para o sistema de metas de inflao flexvel, com a introduo de um novo quadro operacional de execuo da Poltica Monetria em Outubro de 2011 e os resultados, medidos pelo comportamento da inflao, tm-se mostrado positivos. A inflao homloga passou de 11,91% para 9,65%, atingindo-se a to almejada taxa de um dgito. A reduo correspondente da taxa de juro no mercado secundrio est a acontecer impactando positivamente sobre a viabilidade econmica e financeira das empresas, sem no entanto causar danos sobre a solvabilidade dos bancos comerciais. Dados a Junho de 2012 mostram que o rcio de solvabilidade do sistema bancrio angolano, situava-se em 13,4%, acima do limite mnimo de 10% estabelecido pela regulamentao em vigor. Mas a adopo plena do regime de metas de inflao  um processo exigente do ponto de vista do rigor e transparncia das decises de poltica monetria, mas que carece tambm da participao de todos agentes econmicos, particularmente dos operadores financeiros, dado o papel que lhe  reservado enquanto canal de transmisso de polticas e de aprofundamento financeiro da economia. Em Angola, o aprofundamento financeiro, medido pelo rcio do agregado monetrio M2 (que inclui quer as notas e moedas em poder do pblico como os depsitos na banca) sobre o Produto Interno Bruto situa-se em torno de 32%. O crdito  economia, em razo do PIB  de 22%, ou seja, apesar de assinvel est ainda aqum de algumas das economias da regio SADC. O crescimento do sistema bancrio e do seu peso na economia, far-se- tambm por via do aumento do crdito. Nos ltimos anos, a taxa de transformao dos depsitos em crdito tem rondado os 60%, na mdia do conjunto dos bancos, mas  necessrio que se aprimorem tanto as regras de governao das instituies financeiras, como os instrumentos controlo de risco, para que mais crdito no pressuponha menor estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, Do lado do BNA, continuaremos a conduzir uma poltica monetria atenta mas prudente, na expectativa de que por essa via estejamos a contribuir para a proteco da estabilidade dos mercados e a estimular o investimento na economia nacional. Na sesso do Comit de Poltica Monetria de Setembro, optamos pela manuteno da taxa bsica de juro em 10,25%, que se mantm inalterada desde Fevereiro do ano em curso. Alm de se manter positiva em termos reais, ou seja, acima da inflao, no tem condicionado o crescimento do crdito  economia, que nos primeiros 8 meses do ano se situava em cerca de 17%. Por outro lado, a evoluo dos meios de pagamento tambm est em linha com o objectivo de inflao, pese o facto de se registar um maior crescimento da moeda nacional por fora das limitaes regulamentares impostas sobre a concesso de crdito em moeda estrangeira. No ano, a oferta de moeda nacional na economia regista um crescimento de cerca de 15%. A acumulao de reservas internacionais lquidas tambm tem sido conseguida e garantida pelo comportamento favorvel do preo do petrleo bruto nos mercados internacionais. Este quadro concorre para a estabilidade da paridade da moeda nacional face ao dlar dos Estados Unidos da Amrica, de resto, um dos elementos tido como parte das determinantes da inflao em Angola. Apesar das expectativas de alguns analistas,  nosso entendimento que, na actual conjuntura, uma reduo mais agressiva e brusca da taxa bsica de juro poderia no provocar ganhos relevantes no aumento imediato do crdito  economia, nem apoiar a conteno de preos, mas, pelo contrrio, poderia exercer uma presso negativa na estabilidade do sistema financeiro tendo em conta a composio actual da carteira de activos dos bancos comerciais. De todo o modo, procedemos  reduo da taxa de facilidade permanente de cedncia de liquidez para 11,5%, reduzindo o custo de financiamento junto do banco central, na expectativa de reduzir o diferencial entre as taxas activas e passivas, e aumentar o estmulo aos operadores financeiros visando o contnuo suporte  actividade empresarial. Estando j no trimestre de maior procura por bens e servios na nossa economia, o BNA manter-se- vigilante no acompanhamento dos fluxos de liquidez, no antevendo, de qualquer modo, alteraes significativas ao curso da poltica monetria at final do ano em curso. Queremos continuar a comunicar com o mercado com o objectivo de partilhar elementos que sustentam as nossas decises e que esperamos sirvam para sustentar as vossas opes.  Deloitte, agradecemos mais uma vez pelo convite e parabenizamos pela iniciativa e a forma consistente com que tem realizado estes fruns de apresentao e anlise pblica do desempenho da banca em Angola. Muito obrigado. Title: Speech at the launch of the Deposit Guarantee Fund
text: Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose de Lima Massano, at the launch of the Deposit Guarantee Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose de Lima Massano, at the launch of the Deposit Guarantee Fund Your Excellency, Dr. Vera Daves de Sousa, Secretary of State for Finance and Treasury, Very honorable members of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola and the Deposit Guarantee Fund Directive, Distinguished guests, Ladies and gentlemen, Banking, where the transformation of deposits into credit is basic, contains a risk in its implementation, and it is essential to adequately regulation and monitoring of the financial sector, preserving both the confidence of depositors, such as the benefits of supporting the development of Economies. Despite the best efforts of regulators to ensure the stability of the financial crisis, the main determinants of the security and soundness of each bank are its governance models and the economic environment in which they are included. When managers or investors fail in their role as effective risk management, situations with negative implications for the depositors and even for taxpayers. Prior to the widespread implementation of deposit guarantee funds, in the case of bankruptcy of banks, the alternatives were (i) governments to compensate for depositors for their losses, on a case-by-case basis, which necessarily meant that the cost of bankruptcy was borne by taxpayers, even though indirectly, or (ii) depositors simply lose all their savings. The various disruptions in financial markets over the years, including the crisis 2007/08, revealed the reduced capacity or governments' willingness to bear the cost of bank bankruptcies, especially as these are more likely in economic crises, when financial are already under enormous pressure. Thus, it was recognized the need to have a to ensure pre-planned protection, orderly and efficient manner of depositors, which will avoid improvised demand for funds, random policies and disorderly compensation arrangements and not Transparent. A deposit guarantee fund, in the event of a bank's bankruptcy, protects its depositors more vulnerable and those who are less able to diversification or other more sophisticated risk management measures. It also limits the extent to which security concerns and the solidity of a bank spread to others, by contagion, because the security of the guarantee of deposits up to a certain amount, reduces the likelihood of a "banking race", avoiding adverse effects on financial stability. Furthermore, a deposit guarantee fund can help support the diversification of the because without such a guarantee depositors may consider that only the big banks have implicit deposit security as a result of their status as a "too big to fall," and thus decide to focus on these banks, with a possible negative impact on the competitiveness of banking and on the levels of financial inclusion. Therefore, the existence of a deposit guarantee fund provides security to depositors, the scope and coverage of its deposits, promotes the public confidence in the financial sector and provides countries with an orderly process to deal with bank bankruptcies, limiting decision-making unpredictable and discretionary. It was with this framework that in 2013 the National Bank of Angola formalized the need to establish a deposit guarantee fund in the country, legal process resumed and ended in 2018 with the publication of Presidential Decree No. 195/2018, that created the Deposit Guarantee Fund of Angola and defined its regulation. In the creation of the Deposit Guarantee Fund, the national authorities also took into account the recommendations and principles of the International Association of Deposit Guarantee. Thus, the Deposit Guarantee Fund of Angola has as its principal allocation the guarantee of the reimbursement of deposits, regardless of the modality, entitled by natural and legal persons, residents and non-residents residents, expressed in national or foreign currency, with commercial banks authorised to raise deposits in the country, up to the limit of kz 12,500,000 (twelve million and five hundred thousand Kwanzas), covering, thereby, about 85% of depositors in national banking. The Fund is a legal person of public law, endorsing with administrative, financial and assets and is essentially anchored by contributions from commercial banks. Participation is mandatory for all Banking Financial Institutions that capture deposits in the country. At this point, with all eligible banks already making their initial contributions, totaling a value of Kz 13,800,000,000.00 (thirteen billion eight hundred million Kwanzas), the conditions for the formal launch of the Guarantee Fund for Deposits. With the full entry into operation of the Deposit Guarantee Fund, Angola joins the 100 countries in the world that already have security with the same purpose, and will also have another important instrument for building public confidence in the financial sector. To the management and supervisory teams, we wish to succeed in their mission to manage the Deposit Guarantee, in order to preserve, among other objectives, the security of the financial resources entrusted to it and the implementation of procedures ensure the prompt return of deposits in the event of an unexpected unavailability in some commercial bank. We have deposit guarantee fund! Thank you so much for your attention. 25 Jun 2019

Vera Daves de Sousa, Secretria de Estado para as Finanas e Tesouro, Dignssimos membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco Nacional de Angola e da Comisso Directiva do Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos, Distintos convidados, Minhas senhoras e meus senhores, A actividade bancria, em que a transformao de depsitos em crdito  basilar, encerra um conjunto de riscos na sua execuo, pelo que  fundamental a adequada regulamentao e monitorizao do sector financeiro, preservando-se tanto a confiana dos depositantes, como os benefcios de apoio ao desenvolvimento das economias. Apesar dos melhores esforos dos reguladores, no sentido de garantir a estabilidade da indstria financeira, os principais determinantes da segurana e solidez de cada banco so os seus modelos de governao e o enquadramento econmico em que se inserem. Quando os gestores ou investidores falham na sua funo de impor uma gesto de risco efectiva, podem ocorrer situaes com implicaes negativas para os depositantes e at mesmo para os contribuintes. Antes da implementao generalizada dos fundos de garantia de depsitos, nos casos de falncia de bancos, as alternativas eram (i) os governos compensarem os depositantes pelas suas perdas, caso a caso, o que significava, necessariamente, que o custo de falncia era suportado pelos contribuintes, ainda que indirectamente, ou (ii) os depositantes simplesmente perderem todas as suas poupanas. As vrias perturbaes nos mercados financeiros ao longo dos anos, em que se inclui a crise financeira global de 2007/08, vieram revelar a reduzida capacidade ou vontade dos governos de suportar o custo das falncias dos bancos, especialmente porque essas so mais provveis nas crises econmicas, quando as finanas pblicas j esto sob enorme presso. Assim, reconheceu-se a necessidade de se ter um mecanismo independente para garantir uma proteo pr-planeada, ordenada e eficiente dos depositantes, que evitar a procura improvisada por fundos, decises polticas aleatrias e arranjos de compensao desordenados e no transparentes. Um fundo de garantia de depsitos, no caso da falncia de um banco, protege os seus depositantes mais vulnerveis e aqueles que so menos capazes de se proteger por meio da diversificao ou de outras medidas mais sofisticadas de gesto de risco. Tambm, limita a extenso em que as preocupaes sobre a segurana e a solidez de um banco se espalham para outros, por contgio, porque a segurana da garantia dos depsitos at um certo montante, reduz a probabilidade de uma "corrida bancria", evitando efeitos adversos sobre estabilidade financeira. Ainda, um fundo de garantia de depsitos pode ajudar a suportar a diversificao do sector financeiro, porque sem essa garantia os depositantes podem considerar que apenas os grandes bancos tm segurana implcita de depsito, resultado do seu estatuto de muito grande para cair, e assim, decidirem concentrar nestes bancos as suas poupanas, com possvel impacto negativo sobre competitividade da banca e sobre os nveis de incluso financeira. Portanto, a existncia de um fundo de garantia de depsitos oferece segurana aos depositantes, quanto ao escopo e cobertura dos seus depsitos, promove a confiana do pblico no sector financeiro e fornece aos pases um processo ordenado para lidar com falncias bancrias, limitando a tomada de decises imprevisveis e discricionrias. Foi com este enquadramento que em 2013 o Banco Nacional de Angola formalizou a necessidade de se estabelecer um fundo de garantia de depsitos no pas, processo legal retomado e terminado em 2018 com a publicao do Decreto Presidencial n. 195/2018, que criou o Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos de Angola e definiu o seu regulamento. Na criao do Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos, as autoridades nacionais tiveram tambm presente as recomendaes e princpios da Associao Internacional de Garantia de Depsitos. Assim, o Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos de Angola tem como atribuio principal a garantia do reembolso dos depsitos, independentemente da modalidade, titulados por pessoas singulares e colectivas, residentes e no residentes, expressos em moeda nacional ou estrangeira, constitudos junto dos bancos comerciais autorizados a captar depsitos no pas, at ao limite individual de Kz 12.500.000 (doze milhes e quinhentos mil Kwanzas), cobrindo, desse modo, cerca de 85% dos depositantes na banca nacional. O Fundo  uma pessoa colectiva de direito pblico, dotada de autonomia administrativa, financeira e patrimonial e  fundeado, essencialmente, por contribuies dos bancos comerciais. A participao  obrigatria a todas as Instituies Financeiras Bancrias que captam depsitos no pas. Nesta altura, tendo todos os bancos elegveis j realizado as suas contribuies iniciais, totalizando um valor de Kz 13.800.000.000,00 (treze mil milhes e oitocentos milhes de Kwanzas), esto criadas as condies para o lanamento formal do Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos. Com a plena entrada em funcionamento do Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos, Angola junta-se aos cerca de 100 pases no mundo que possuem j esquemas de segurana com o mesmo propsito, passando tambm a contar com mais um importante instrumento de construo de confiana pblica no sector financeiro. s equipas de gesto e de fiscalizao, desejamos sucesso na sua misso de gerir o Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos, de forma a preservar, entre outros objectivos, a segurana dos recursos financeiros que lhe so confiados e a implementao de procedimentos que garantam a pronta devoluo de depsitos em caso inesperado da sua indisponibilidade nalgum banco comercial. Temos Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos! Muito obrigado pela vossa ateno. Title: Opening Speech of the Conference on Cyber Security for the Angolan Financial System
text: Public Interventions Opening Speech of the Conference on CyberSecurity for the Angolan Financial System Opening Speech of the Conference on CyberSecurity for the Financial System Angolan Former Mr. Governor of the National Bank of Angola Dr. Jose Massano Ladies and gentlemen of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola Exmo Mr. Ministry of Higher Education Science and Technology Exmo Mr. Ministry of Telecommunications and Information Technologies Mr. Home Office Representatives of Higher Education Institutions Former Mr. President of ABANC Mr. Entities, Administrators and managers of banking institutions Distinguished guests Ladies and gentlemen, On behalf of the National Bank of Angola, we thank you for your presence at this Seventh Edition of the Annual Conferences of the National Bank of Angola that in this opportunity will be dedicated to discussing a topic as topical as it is critical: cybersecurity in the Angolan financial sector. Today, countries are increasingly relying on the reliable functioning of their critical technological infrastructures and our country is not a exception, with the financial sector in general and banking in particular an exponent of this reality. Our operating financial system generates and processes data, communicates on closed networks and internet with its customers and local service providers and exposed to cybersecurity threats and risks that may cause a significant use of the its functioning and credibility Like financial risks and reputational risks, cybersecurity risk affects the capacity of financial systems to provide services, open up fraud and expose us to the possibility of identity theft of their users. These risks can increase costs and affect to a large extent the stability of the financial system. On the other hand, cyber risks can undermine an organization's ability to innovate and to win over and/or retain its customers. For a better treatment of these risks, it is necessary to create risk mechanisms and guidelines cybersecurity, which should be used by owners and operators of critical technological infrastructure. This effort will only be successful if it is a national plan covering the set of all cybersecurity policymakers in our country the which calls us to the urgent need to develop a national strategy for cybersecurity. In this way, I declare open the conference on "Cyber Security for the Financial System Angolan". 26 Jul. 2019

Nos dias de hoje, os pases dependem cada vez mais de um funcionamento confivel das suas infraestruturas tecnolgicas crticas e o nosso pas no  uma excepo, sendo o sector financeiro em geral e bancrio em particular, um exponente desta realidade. O nosso sistema financeiro para funcionar gera e processa dados, comunica em redes fechadas e pela internet com os seus clientes e provedores de servios locais e internacionais, ficando exposto a ameaas e riscos de segurana ciberntica que podem por em causa o seu funcionamento e credibilidade  semelhana dos riscos financeiros e riscos de reputao, o risco de segurana ciberntica afectam a capacidade dos sistemas financeiros proverem servios, abrem brechas para fraudes e expem-nos  possibilidade de roubo de identidade dos seus utilizadores. Estes riscos podem elevar os custos e afectar em grande medida a estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Por outro lado, os riscos cibernticos podem prejudicar a capacidade de uma organizao de inovar e de conquistar e/ou manter seus clientes. Para um melhor tratamento destes riscos,  necessrio que se criem mecanismos e diretrizes de risco de segurana ciberntica, que devem ser usados pelos proprietrios e operadores de infraestrutura tecnolgica crtica. Deste modo, declaro aberta a conferncia sobre Segurana Ciberntica para o Sistema Financeiro Angolano. Title: Speech - Presentation of the Basic Law of the Angolan Payment System to Parliament
text: Intervention of the Governor, Jose de Lima Massano - Presentation of the Basic Law of the Payments from Angola to Parliament Intervention of the Governor, Jose de Lima Massano - Presentation of the Basic Law of the Angola's Payment System to Parliament Excellency, Mr. President of the National Assembly, Distinguished Members, Ladies and gentlemen, Payment systems are decisive for economic operators, in particular, to consumers, companies, banks, state entities, can activities with confidence in the services and payment instruments available. In the last 15 years since the publication of Law No. 5/05 of 29 July, the Payment system currently in place, it has been significant developments not only in the national financial system, in particular at the level of volume and typology of payments, but also at the level of international level in terms of progress in IT systems and payment instruments, among others. In fact, we have seen an unavoidable and continuous dynamics of innovation in payment systems that can bring many advantages, as well as minimize risks to society. In this context, considering that the current Law no longer corresponded to the existence of a system of adequate payment in terms of security, efficiency, transparency and operational reliability, the National Bank of Angola, responsible for organisation, operation, management and supervision of compensation and payment under the Law of the National Bank of Angola, has developed and this proposal for a revision of the Law regulating the angola's payments. Firstly, we would like to point out that this bill has taken into account the best practices of SADC Country Payment Systems, contributions from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund. Secondly, we have to highlight some of the main changes: 1. The introduction of detailed rules for payment service providers, in particular access and general conditions of activity as well as the requirements for the authorisation and registration of payment service providers and companies operating payment systems in order to ensure the the suitability and ability of these entities to carry out their activity properly. 2. The introduction of more comprehensive, comprehensive and up-to-date rules taking into account the developments in the national and international markets, on the functioning of payment systems and the provision and use of such services. 3. The establishment of a "Technical Committee for the Development of the Payment System" to be chaired by the National Bank of Angola and composed of representatives of the actors in the payment system and of entities representing relevant interests in this, and which has functions of a on regulatory and defining strategies leading to the development of the system, with a view to its continuous modernisation and efficiency. 4. The establishment of the conditions of access and for the exercise of the activity of issuers of electronic money, i.e. payment service providers authorized to issue electronic money. 5. The amendment of the sanctioning regime in order to include the updates made in the provisions of the Law and also the formula for calculating fines, which in this proposals are defined in terms of value ranges and not as percentages of capital, as provided for in the previous Law. In conclusion, with this revision of the Payment System Act, we intend to return to a law of modern payments in a segment of great propensity to innovation, which contributes to the resilience of the national financial system and accelerates the financial inclusion programs and options in our country. 19 Jun 2020
text_original: Home Publicaes e Media Intervenes Pblicas Interveno do Governador, Jos de Lima Massano - Apresentao da Lei de bases do Sistema de Pagamentos de Angola ao Parlamento Interveno do Governador, Jos de Lima Massano - Apresentao da Lei de bases do Sistema de Pagamentos de Angola ao Parlamento Excelncia Sr. Presidente da Assembleia Nacional, Distintos Srs Deputados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Os sistemas de pagamento so decisivos para que os agentes econmicos, nomeadamente, consumidores, empresas, bancos, entidades Estatais, possam desenvolver as suas actividades com confiana nos servios e instrumentos de pagamento disponveis. Nos ltimos 15 anos desde a publicao da Lei n. 5/05 de 29 de Julho, Lei do Sistema de Pagamentos actualmente em vigor, tem-se vindo a verificar desenvolvimentos significativos no apenas no sistema financeiro nacional, nomeadamente a nvel de volume e tipologia de pagamentos, mas tambm a nvel internacional em termos de progressos nos sistemas informticos e nos instrumentos de pagamento, entre outros. De facto, assistimos a uma incontornvel e contnua dinmica de inovao nos sistemas de pagamento que podem trazer muitas vantagens, bem como minimizar os riscos, para a sociedade. Neste contexto, considerando que a actual Lei j no correspondia  existncia de um sistema de pagamento adequado em termos de segurana, eficincia, transparncia e fiabilidade operacional, o Banco Nacional de Angola, responsvel pela organizao, funcionamento, gesto e superviso dos sistemas de compensao e de pagamento nos termos da Lei do Banco Nacional de Angola, desenvolveu e apresenta a presente proposta de reviso da Lei que regula o sistema de pagamentos de Angola. Em primeiro lugar, queremos salientar que a presente proposta de Lei teve em considerao as melhores prticas dos Sistemas de Pagamento dos Pases da SADC, contributos do Banco Mundial e do Fundo Monetrio Internacional. Em segundo lugar, temos a destacar algumas das principais alteraes: 1. A introduo de regras detalhadas aplicveis aos prestadores de servios de pagamento, nomeadamente o acesso e condies gerais de actividade bem como os requisitos de autorizao e registo das sociedades prestadoras de servios de pagamento e sociedades operadoras de sistemas de pagamento de forma a garantir a idoneidade e capacidade destas entidades para exercer adequadamente a sua actividade. 2. A introduo de regras mais abrangentes, completas e actualizadas considerando os desenvolvimentos entretanto ocorridos no mercado nacional e internacional, sobre o funcionamento dos sistemas de pagamento e da prestao e utilizao desses servios. 3. A criao de uma Comisso Tcnica para o Desenvolvimento do Sistema de Pagamentos a ser presidida pelo Banco Nacional de Angola e composta por representantes dos intervenientes do sistema de pagamentos e de entidades representativas de interesses relevantes neste, e que tem funes de carcter consultivo em matrias de regulao e definio de estratgias conducentes ao desenvolvimento do referido sistema, tendo em vista a sua contnua modernizao e eficincia. 4. O estabelecimento das condies de acesso e para o exerccio da actividade dos emitentes de moeda electrnica, ou seja, prestadores de servios de pagamento autorizados a emitir moeda electrnica. 5. A alterao do regime sancionatrio de forma a contemplar as actualizaes feitas nas disposies da Lei e tambm a frmula de clculo das multas, que nesta proposta so definidas em termos de intervalos de valores e no como percentagens do capital, conforme disposto na Lei anterior. Em concluso, com esta reviso da Lei do sistema de pagamentos, pretendemos voltar a ter uma lei de pagamentos moderna num segmento de grande propenso  inovao, que contribua para a resilincia do sistema financeiro nacional e permita acelerar os programas e opes de incluso financeira no nosso pas. Title: Opening speech of the act of presentation of the new notes of Kwanza-Series 2020 to the Press
text: Opening speech by the Governor, Jose de Lima Massano, of the act of presenting the new notes from Kwanza-Series 2020 to the Press Opening speech by the Governor, Jose de Lima Massano, the act of presenting the new Kwanza-Serie 2020 notes to the Press Dear fellow citizens, Ladies and gentlemen, As we mark the 45th anniversary of our country's independence in 2020, we launched a new Kwanza Series of Notes. This is a happy coincidence, because in addition to honoring the collective achievements of all angolans, it has already been 7 years since the entry into circulation of the 2012 series of Kwanza banknotes, recommended period for review of banknote characteristics monetary instruments, allowing us to give our currency, modernity and more security. Kwanza's new notes, inspired by the grandeur of independent Angola and landscapes of beauty contain elements of our cultural identity and have, in as a central image, the effigy of the first President of the Republic, Dr. Antonio Agostinho Neto, national independence on 11 November 1975. The notes of 200, 500, 1,000 and 2,000 Kwanzas were produced in polymer, a material that resembles to plastic. They incorporate high-security elements and are more resistant in time, and can have an average durability 4 times longer than the notes traditional cotton. In our case, durability is very relevant because the intensity of use and handling notes causes their useful life to be reduced, raising the sanitation costs of the circulating environment. Furthermore, the fact that not all areas of the country delegations of the National Bank of Angola or branches of commercial banks, makes it difficult to control quality and timely replacement of banknotes in poor condition conservation measures. That is, with the polymer, we have not only the novelty of notes in new material, but also the possibility of greater convenience in its use and savings management of monetary circulation. Not least, is the fact that the new be recyclable, making them more environmentally friendly. The new Kwanza banknotes will enter into circulation progressively from 30 July, with the name of 200 Kwanzas. In September, we will have the 500 kwanza banknotes, in October those of 1,000 and in November the banknotes 2,000 banknotes will enter into circulation Kwanzas. The new 5,000 Kwanzas note, which will still be in the cotton (also known as paper), will be available in January 2021. At this time, despite the legal provision, it is not anticipated that the 10,000 Kwanzas, unless it is shown to be absolutely necessary. The entry into circulation of the new banknotes will be progressive to enable the knowledge of their characteristics and ensure that they are available throughout the national territory The new notes will coexist with the existing ones of the Series from 2012 until December 31, 2021. The Bank National Government of Angola will publish and give visibility to the calendar withdrawal of the oldest banknotes. Because they maintain their security characteristics for a longer period of time, the coins current metal systems will remain in circulation without any change. We will now start a wide program of presentation of kwanza notes of the new Series 2020. We live in a period that requires increased care with the health security, but we will not fail to ensure, implementing the protective measures that are require that the characteristics of the new banknotes be well Known. The introduction of new banknotes into the economy is not a new process, so we should not be afraid. In 2013, when the banknotes currently circulating came in, there was no negative impact on price formation, nor have we had incidents with rejection or loss of value of banknotes that were already in circulation. With these new notes from Kwanza the route will not be different and whenever they arise questions, they must be submitted to the National Bank angola, any commercial bank or local law enforcement authorities. Kwanza's new Series of Notes symbolizes our journey as an independent and sovereign country, valuing our history and aiming for a better future, for example this, although produced in more resistant material, we should always handle them carefully to that the gains are lasting. Thank you very much. 7 Jul. 2020
text_original: Home Publicaes e Media Intervenes Pblicas Discurso de abertura do Governador, Jos de Lima Massano, do acto de apresentao das novas notas de Kwanza-Srie 2020  Imprensa Discurso de abertura do Governador, Jos de Lima Massano, do acto de apresentao das novas notas de Kwanza-Srie 2020  Imprensa Prezados concidados, Caros colegas, Ao assinalarmos, neste ano de 2020, o 45. aniversrio da independncia do nosso pas, lanamos uma nova Srie de notas de Kwanza. Trata-se de uma feliz coincidncia, pois alm de homenagearmos os feitos colectivos de todos angolanos, passaram-se j 7 anos desde a entrada em circulao da Srie 2012 de notas de Kwanza, perodo recomendado para reviso das caractersticas das cdulas monetrias, permitindo-nos conferir  nossa moeda, modernidade e mais segurana. As novas notas de Kwanza, inspiradas na grandeza de Angola independente e em paisagens de beleza nica, contm elementos da nossa identidade cultural e tm, como imagem central, a efgie do primeiro presidente da Repblica, Dr. Antnio Agostinho Neto, proclamador da independncia nacional a 11 de Novembro de 1975. As notas de 200, 500, 1.000 e 2.000 Kwanzas foram produzidas em polmero, material que se assemelha ao plstico. Incorporam elementos de alta segurana e so mais resistentes no tempo, podendo ter uma durabilidade mdia 4 vezes superior  das notas tradicionais de algodo. No nosso caso, a durabilidade  muito relevante porque a intensidade da utilizao e manuseamento das notas faz com que a sua vida til seja reduzida, elevando os custos de saneamento do meio circulante. Para alm disso, o facto de nem todas as zonas do pas terem delegaes do Banco Nacional de Angola ou balces de bancos comerciais, dificulta o controlo de qualidade e substituio atempada de notas em mau estado de conservao. Ou seja, com o polmero, temos no apenas a novidade de notas em novo material, mas tambm a possibilidade de maior comodidade no seu uso e poupana financeira na gesto da circulao monetria. No menos importante,  o facto do novo substracto ser reciclvel, tornando-as mais amigas do ambiente. As novas notas de Kwanza entraro em circulao de modo progressivo, a partir do dia 30 de Julho, com a denominao de 200 Kwanzas. Em Setembro, teremos as notas de 500 kwanzas, em Outubro as de 1.000 e em Novembro entraro em circulao as notas 2.000 Kwanzas. A nova nota de 5.000 Kwanzas, que ser ainda no material actual, em algodo (tambm conhecido como papel), estar disponvel em Janeiro de 2021. Neste momento, apesar da proviso legal, no se antev a entrada em circulao da denominao de 10.000 Kwanzas, a menos que se venha a mostrar absolutamente necessrio. A entrada em circulao das novas notas ser progressiva para permitir o conhecimento das suas caractersticas e assegurar que estejam disponveis em todo o territrio nacional As novas notas convivero com as existentes da Srie de 2012 at 31 de Dezembro de 2021. O Banco Nacional de Angola publicar e dar visibilidade ao calendrio de retirada das notas mais antigas. Por manterem as suas caractersticas de segurana durante um perodo de tempo mais longo, as moedas metlicas actuais permanecero em circulao sem qualquer alterao. Vamos agora iniciar um amplo programa de apresentao das notas de Kwanza da nova Srie 2020. Vivemos um perodo que requer cuidados redobrados com a segurana sanitria, mas no deixaremos de assegurar, implementando as medidas de proteco que se impem, que as caractersticas das novas notas sejam bem conhecidas. A introduo de novas notas na economia no  um processo novo, pelo que no devemos ter receios. Em 2013, quando entraram as notas que actualmente circulam, no se assistiu a qualquer impacto negativo sobre a formao de preos, nem tivemos incidentes com rejeio ou perda de valor das notas que j se encontravam em circulao. Com estas novas notas de Kwanza o percurso no ser diferente e sempre que surgirem dvidas, as mesmas devem ser apresentadas ao Banco Nacional de Angola, a qualquer banco comercial ou s autoridades policiais locais. A nova Srie de notas de Kwanza simboliza o nosso percurso como pas independente e soberano, valorizando a nossa histria e almejando um futuro melhor, por isso, apesar de produzidas em material mais resistente, devemos sempre manuse-las com cuidado para que os ganhos sejam duradouros. Muito obrigado. Title: Opening Speech at the Day of Commemoration of the 45th Anniversary of the Day of the Bank Worker
text: Opening Speech of the Governor, Jose de Lima Massano, at the 45th Anniversary Commemoration Day Bank worker's day anniversary Opening Speech of the Governor, Jose de Lima Massano, at the Commemoration Day of 45th Anniversary of Bank Worker's Day Mr. President of the National Union of Banking Employees of Angola, Distinguished members of the Boards of Directors of commercial banks, Distinguished representatives of the associated workers of the National Union of Bank Employees angola, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and gentlemen. On behalf of the National Bank of Angola I thank you for the invitation addressed to me to participate in this already traditional event annually promoted by SNEBA. This year's motto - "Banking, 45 years old: yesterday, today and tomorrow", leads us first to walk a little by the history of the banking sector since our independence and recall the main stages of its development, which bring us to the present and allow us to project the future. After the act of 14 August 1975, marked by the taking of the banking destinations by nationalists angolans still in the early days of our independence, there are to highlight the enactment of Laws No. 69 and 70, both of November 5, 1976, which established the National Bank of Angola and the People's Bank of Angola, the first to detain the assets and liabilities of the Bank of Angola and the second, those of the Angola, however, nationalized. In 1978, Law No. 4 of March 27, consecrated the exclusive exercise of banking activity in the country by these two state banks, which resulted in the closure of all private commercial banks. In the system then established, the National Bank of Angola, which was part of the organic Central Government, exercised central bank and issuing functions, treasury and commercial bank, while the Banco Popular de Angola was only reserved for function of capturing savings from individuals, without exercise financial intermediation activity. The year 1991 brought the change in the legal and economic framework of banking activity in the country, with the adoption of a two-level system, the first being occupied by the National Bank of Angola, which ceased commercial banking activities and began to function as a central bank and issuing authority, as a regulatory body, supervisor of the financial system and, the second, occupied by commercial banks, through the no. 4/91 (Organic Law of the BNA) and No. 5/91 (Law of financial) both of April 20. In this brief trip, I also unlike the constitutional dignity conferred on the National Bank of Angola and the financial system, by establishing itself in the Constitution of the Republic the BNA as central bank and issuing of the Republic of Angola. Today, the banking sector consists of 26 banks, 23 of which are private, and 108 non-bank financial institutions, employing about 25,000 employees Direct. To accompany this development, we have a bankisation rate of around 40% of the population, in a trajectory that has been increasing over the years. The banking sector has a necessarily very dynamic paradigm, requiring, in the realization of financial intermediation activity, the creation of solutions, products and financial services under safety and efficiency criteria, capable of ensure confidence in saving custody and ensuring support in the development and economic and social development initiatives. We mark the 45th anniversary of the uptake of banking destinations in a macroeconomic context difficult and complex, conditioned by the low price of the barrel of oil - our main source of export revenues - and by the side effects covid-19 pandemic. This context coincides with (i) greater rigour regulatory and supervisory framework of financial institutions, (ii) the new behavioural and consumer protection requirements (iii) the strengthening the corporate governance system and (iv) the transition to more digital banking. In the regulatory and supervision chapter, banks face a demanding framework, within the framework of a model, today, more active, transversal and prospective, with a focus on rigorous assessment of risk and the institutionalisation of new instruments and actions to adopting universally accepted criteria for good practice. Or banking sector because of its importance in the economy is, of all sectors, the most scrutinised, regulated and supervised. Technological innovation has brought about major changes in all aspects of our lives, including, of course, the financial and has also been translating into the use of mobile devices at the heart of the technological-financial revolution. To this innovation challenge, the adoption of the new Payment System Act last month of july, will lead us to the implementation of the regulatory package aimed at ensure the effective of security, efficiency, competition and data protection with a view to provide a secure digital banking environment. On the same path, BNA developed the Payment System Innovation Laboratory (LISPA) with a view to risk management, promoting innovation and enhancing the supply of diversified financial products and services to consumers, thereby boosting the inclusion of financial. We are also in a moment of transition from an economy that is overly dependent on exports oil, for an economy more based on diversified national production, a more sustainable and inclusive economy. The banking system plays a key role in this transformation. It is therefore necessary for banks to develop the capabilities in order to be able to support the diversification of the economy through the granting of credit should align their people, policies and processes to this purpose. To finish, I would like to acknowledge the courage, dedication, merit of generations of banking angolans who, since independence, have engaged in all this process of framing, maturing and evolution of the national financial system. To today's workers and our banking of the future, I would like to stress the importance of continuing to to work with professionalism and rigour, so that together can continue to build a healthy, modern and inclusive financial system at the service of citizens and the economy. Wishing all participants a good working session and fruitful moments of reflection, learning and exchanging experiences on the way here and the challenges of building the banking of the future, I declare to open, this journey alusive on August 14th. Aug. 13. 2020

Tal contexto coincide com (i) um maior rigor  nvel do quadro regulatrio e de superviso das instituies financeiras, (ii) as novas exigncias a nvel comportamental e de proteco dos consumidores (iii) o reforo do sistema de governao corporativa e (iv) a transio para uma banca mais digital. No captulo da regulao e superviso, os bancos enfrentam um quadro exigente, no mbito de um modelo, hoje, mais activo, transversal e prospectivo, com enfoque na apreciao rigorosa do risco e a institucionalizao de novos instrumentos e aces de superviso, adoptando critrios universalmente aceites de boas prticas. A inovao tecnolgica veio trazer grandes alteraes em todos os aspectos da nossa vida, incluindo, obviamente, o financeiro e vem-se traduzindo tambm no uso massivo de dispositivos mveis que figuram no centro da revoluo tecnolgico-financeira.  esse desafio de inovao, aprovao da nova Lei do Sistema de Pagamentos no passado ms de Julho, levar-nos- a implementao do pacote regulatrio que visa garantir a efectivao da segurana, eficincia, concorrncia e a proteco de dados tendente a proporcionar um ambiente da banca digital seguro. Na mesma senda, o BNA desenvolveu o Laboratrio de Inovao do Sistema de Pagamentos (LISPA), tendo em vista a gesto de riscos, promoo da inovao e potenciao da oferta de produtos e servios financeiros diversificados ao consumidor, impulsionando assim, a incluso financeira. Estamos tambm num momento de transio de uma economia excessivamente dependente das exportaes de petrleo, para uma economia mais assente em produo nacional diversificada, uma economia mais sustentvel e inclusiva. Torna-se assim necessrio que os bancos desenvolvam as capacidades para poder apoiar o esforo de diversificao da economia atravs da concesso de crdito responsvel, devendo alinhar as suas pessoas, polticas e processos a esse objectivo. Aos trabalhadores de hoje e da nossa banca do futuro, quero salientar a importncia de continuarem a trabalhar com profissionalismo e rigor, para que juntos possamos continuar a edificar um sistema financeiro saudvel, moderno, e inclusivo ao servio dos cidados e da economia. Title: Speech at the Banca Forum
text: Public Interventions Speech of Governor Jose de Lima Massano, in the Banking Forum Speech by Governor Jose de Lima Massano, in the Banking Forum Illustrious Joao Armando, Director of The Expansion Journal, Distinguished representatives of the bank, Expensive participants, The Journal Expansao maintained this year the commitment to hold the Banking Forum, having chosen to give emphasis on the 'role of banking in crediting the economy in time of crisis. It is a relevant theme and which is certainly at the heart of each other's agenda today commercial banks operating in Angola. The figures on 30 June attest that bank credit still has a modest weight in our economy. As far as the business sector is concerned, it is no more than 12.5% of non-oil GDP, while for the private sector it does not reach 3%. In terms, credit represents only 16% of the company's assets and the rate of deposit transformation into credit is around 35%. Still, in our economy, the concentration levels of credit per sector are high. Or trade sector dominates, with about 25% of the total granted and tends to be short-term. In other words, credit has essentially served as support the import of consumer goods, some with large potential of local production, as is the case of food goods that make up the basic basket. This is a fast-granting credit as it has a restrained risk. However, it is only shown that sustainable in the short term, as it depends on a constant availability of foreign currency which, as we know, comes from a single sector that has seen its financial flow to significantly reduce, currently without any premonition of recovery to the highest levels seen a few years ago, and very less in the short term. Still, the undue credit rate is high, at around 22%, despite the decline 34% in the first six months of the year, associated with restructuring of the main public capital bank. Many were already diagnoses made around access, and the results were consistent; On the supply side, the main finding relates to the reliability of the information submitted to the banks for analysis and decision, resulting from the lack of accounting in many cases, but is also often referred to in the viability of the projects submitted. The fragility of the registration of guarantees and the lengthy handling of trade disputes, is among the main Constraints. On the other hand, on the demand side, procedures have been pointed out as excessively bureaucratic, sometimes unprofessional and collection of information, analysis, and hiring, and complaints are made about the lack of knowledge and mastery by the banks in the sector of activity, where the entity requesting the credit is insoused. But the greater emphasis is placed on the cost of credit, or interest rates and commissions are considered excessive and unfeasible projects. However, the weaknesses of the ecosystem of granting internal and external credit to banking, obliges us to a structuring approach, so that the desire for more bank credit to the economy has become an element of instability in the financial system. It is in this context that a number of measures are underway to contribute to the comprehensive improvement of lending. We highlight the proposals for Law on the Corporate Recovery and Insolvency Regime, as well as the Furniture Guarantees and Registration of Guarantees that are already in the possession of the National Assembly. Also, the installation of trading rooms is in advance with the district courts and, very recently, was approved by Presidential Decree, the regulation on Credit Guarantee Companies and on Central Private Credit Risk Information. The revision of the the basis of financial institutions, is another important part in the organization of our clarifying the nature of financial corporations, the role of regulators and, above all, the protection and protection of consumers from financial services. We are also in mind that macroeconomic stability is key to ensuring the normal functioning of the financial market. Fiscal consolidation in important for reducing the public accounts deficit, is also the cornerstone of the and consequent reduction in the cost of indebtedness. With less need for banking resources for the financing of public expenditure, we will have as result, lower interest rates and more resources available to support the private sector of the economy. Monetary policy will continue to target inflation reduction and support for migration to the exchange rate regime determined by market factors. Monetary policy measures have resulted in a reduction in the interest rate on the monetary policy since the beginning of the year, but more markedly since the introduction of the applicable custody rate on the excess reserves of commercial banks maintained with the National Bank of Angola. This development should have a cross-cutting impact on credit and may reduce the probability of non-compliance and, where appropriate, encourage use of new financial instruments to support economic activity, such as leasing or leasing factoring, which although instituted normatively have not been, still an option in our credit market, but that can make it safer and more accessible. The exchange rate adjustment, in turn, in addition to the protection of International Reserves, is a an important catalyst for the deisation of national production and a impulses to increase credit to the productive sector. We see, therefore, in the national production the common denominator for reducing inflation and maintaining a comfortable level of International Reserves To this end, we have set up mechanisms to stimulate the granting of credit to the real sector of economy, establishing the transformation of the minimum equivalent of 2.5% of the banking assets in credit to the productive sector, with a limit cost of 7.5% per year in interest commissions. On the other hand, we allow the amount of credit granted was deductible from mandatory reserves. That is, previously resources idle and without any return to the banks became paid and put at the service of the economy. After reaching around 83% of the amount foreseen by 2019, projects already corresponded to 71.5% of the minimum financial value established for the present financial year. We welcome this development, as sectors traditionally without access to credit have been gaining space to make their business initiatives. In the meantime, as an entity responsible for preserving the stability of the the BNA has been urging banks to ensure the granting of responsible for credit, and should, among others, invest in the continuous development of internal competences for the proper analysis and decision of the requests, develop risk management models compatible with the risk level of the credit in their balance sheets, as well as appropriate models of assessment of their exposure at risk to ensure the recording of the odd ities that correctly reflect credit risk. By stimulating the granting of credit, we are present that almost 80% of the resources held in the belong to private sector depositors and, for this reason, the granting of credit, as well as the responsible use of resources by borrowers, are conditions indispensable to ensure the stability of the system companies and households. Access to credit is key to speeding up the ongoing reform that is required to economy, particularly in a crisis context and despite challenges and work fronts, we have a bankroll that has shown to be sufficiently resilient and with which we count on to build an economy more sustainable and socially inclusive. Thank you very much. 11 Sep. 2020
