Title: Speech at the Banca Forum
text: Home Publications and Media Public Interventions Speech of Governor Jose de Lima Massano, in the Banking Forum Speech by Governor Jose de Lima Massano, in the Banking Forum Illustrious Joao Armando, Director of The Expansion Journal, Distinguished Presidents and members of the governing bodies of commercial banks, Expensive participants, Ladies and gentlemen First of all, I would like to thank the invitation that was formulated to me to be here and to make the closing of this conference that goes already in the 11th edition. As usual, the theme was well chosen for the times of change we live in and this morning we heard interesting contributions from the participants, in particular a presentation on the impacts of the new legislation governing the activities of financial institutions, a presentation and debate on the expectations of what the banking business will be like in the future in Angola. So, to complement, I will focus on the future of prudential supervision of the financial system angola, in particular, banking financial institutions. As we all know, the financial sector is fundamental to the proper functioning of the economies - promotes trust among economic actors, stimulates aggregate mobilization of savings to enable investment, facilitates integration and the relationship between with the foreign market. Countries with more developed financial systems tend to grow more consistently and sustained and there is ample evidence to suggest that this effect is causal: financial development is not simply a result of economic growth economic; contributes to this growth. The development of the financial sector goes far beyond the existence of infrastructure and financial intermediaries. It is essential to have robust policies and regulation and supervision. The global financial crisis of 2008-2009 served well to make us realize the political, economic and social consequences regulatory and supervisory options in the financial sector. This same financial crisis triggered financial reforms in all major economies, but in no jurisdiction the change will have been so comprehensive and radical as well as in the European Union, which decided to create a Banking Union, in which the first pillar was the establishment of a single supervisory body, in so as to consistency and consistency and thereby increase integration and financial stability in the Euro. The European Union has implemented legislation to restrict the exposure of its financial system to jurisdictions that did not, in principle, have regulations and supervision comparable to its own and in December 2014, in the first evaluation, recognised only 17 countries in the world as having equivalent systems, being that of these only one, South Africa, belonged to our continent and 2, Brazil and Mexico, to the Latin America. This scheme entered into force on 1 January 2015. Equivalence status brings benefits to economies that relate to the market financial policy of the European Union. It allows, among others, that its banks benefit from more favourable capital requirements with regard to exposures to third countries that have the recognition of equivalence of supervision. Taking into account the intensity of our commercial and financial relationship with the countries that make up the European Union, the National Bank of Angola formally initiated in 2020 to the application process for obtaining equivalence status, making the implementation of legislation and regulation for this purpose, but with appropriate adaptations, taking into account the specific characteristics of the financial sector national. But the gains are bigger. In the immediate future, the main advantage of this route is the strengthening of the of our regulatory framework and the increase in our supervisory capacity. Obtaining supervisory equivalence is therefore not an end in itself to the same, but rather a process of cross-cutting development of the our financial system so that it can safely attract capital and skills to support diversification and economic development efforts and social. We are also at an ideal time to start this process, considering that our is still of reduced complexity and depth compared to mature markets, thus enabling gradual implementation as the our market is developing. In terms of legislation and regulation, as mentioned in the initial submission of this conference, the Law of the General Regime of the financial sector, and we have also commend its regulation with the publication of various Notices and Instructional, and this process will naturally continue to complete the framework, and then to meet future developments. As I mentioned at the beginning, I will not go into this theme, because we have already seen a presentation about the same at this conference. At the level of the prudential supervision process, we are implementing the Methodology of Analysis and Avaliacao pelo Supervisor (Supervisory Review and Evaluation process in English, with the acronym "SREP"), a process developed and implemented by the supervision of the European Union. This is a methodology comprehensive, comprehensive, comprehensive, continuous and interventional evaluation of each institution financial. In very general terms, the SREP is a set of procedures applied by the supervisor aimed at ensure that each financial institution has strategies, capital and liquidity appropriate to the risks to which it is or may be exposed, as well as the how to determine the risk that each institution poses to the financial system. The SREP recognises the principle of proportionality through the categorisation of financial institutions in different classes according to their risk profile and the systemic importance. This categorization also informs the prudential supervision model to be be applied, including the frequency, scope and intensity of Evaluations. The results of this analysis allow the supervisor to establish particular requirements for each institution, by defining capital and liquidity requirements requirements of other nature, in order to ensure their viability and long-term sustainability. The implementation of this methodology significantly alters the supervisory approach prudential policy of national financial institutions and make the process more structured, consistent, robust, risk-based and forward-looking. On the other hand, the paths of financial inclusion in Angola, which today have about 50% of the adult population already with access to the provision of basic services banking, putting us, according to the World Bank, in line with the African continental average, leads us to developments in the systems of where instant transfers are pontificated. Here, regulation and supervision will also have to ensure that the digital transformation process of the financial system occurs under the criteria of safety, efficacy and competitiveness. Thus, in addition to aligning regulation and supervision with best practices international companies, we are considering another initiative that will have a significant impact on the way the National Bank of Angola works in the field of supervision. I am referring to the adoption of technology for supervision, also known as Suptech (short for Supervisory Technology). Distributed databases, robotics, artificial intelligence and capacity, increasingly quantum computing are at the basis of the transformation of many processes that foster innovation in the financial system, including in the field of supervision. The application of big data and artificial intelligence to the tools used by supervisors, significantly increase volume, variety, speed and validity data under management. Artificial intelligence allows you to perform complex data analyses and in volumes that exceed human capacity and thus replace current approaches based on the submission of time-consuming on-site reports and inspections and often reactive. The National Bank of Angola has a specific project underway for the gradual adoption of Suptech, aiming to achieve efficiency gains in the processes of prudential supervision through real-time monitoring of micro and social risks. macroprudential measures inherent to financial institutions. Gains that are expand behavioural supervision, the Credit Risk Center and even the Deposit Guarantee. Finally, and also with the sense of strengthening the scrutiny and transparency of financial statements, taking into account the reporting obligations to the timely market in compliance with the timetable requirements set by the exchanges, we want to encourage financial institutions to consider the quotation shares on the Angolan Stock Exchange. Entry into the regulated capital market can also facilitate the strengthening of the capital structure by access to finance through the issuance of shares to new investors or even to existing shareholders, or of bonds to be institutional or private investors, reaching a wide range of of investors; liquidity to shareholders by facilitating the sale of shares and providing the expansion of the investor base; give greater visibility and institutions and increase their credibility with suppliers, customers and banks international. It attracts foreign investment, values savings and guidance for financial assets in national currency. We live in challenging and changing times, and we have to mobilize to keep up and be a part of the process of transforming our economy through the development of the financial system, which is either credible, resilient, sustainable and inducing economic growth and social well-being. Congratulations to the Expansion for this Forum that has become an important platform for dialogue between actors in the financial system and society. Thank you very much. 30 Jul. 2021
text_original: Home Publicaes e Media Intervenes Pblicas Discurso do Governador Jos de Lima Massano, no Frum Banca Discurso do Governador Jos de Lima Massano, no Frum Banca Ilustre Joo Armando, Director do Jornal Expanso, Distintos Presidentes e membros dos rgos sociais dos bancos comerciais, Caros participantes, Minhas senhoras e meus senhores Antes de mais, gostaria de agradecer o convite que me foi formulado para c estar e fazer o encerramento desta conferncia que vai j na XI edio. Como de costume, o tema foi bem escolhido para os tempos de mudana que vivemos e esta manh ouvimos contribuies interessantes dos participantes, nomeadamente uma apresentao sobre os impactos da nova legislao que rege a actividade das instituies financeiras, uma apresentao e um debate sobre as expectativas de como ser o negcio bancrio no futuro em Angola. Assim, para complementar, vou-me centrar no futuro da superviso prudencial do sistema financeiro em Angola, em particular, das instituies financeiras bancrias. Como todos sabemos, o sector financeiro  fundamental para o bom funcionamento das economias - promove a confiana entre os agentes econmicos, estimula a mobilizao agregada da poupana para permitir o investimento, facilita a integrao e a relao com o mercado externo. Os pases com sistemas financeiros mais desenvolvidos tendem a crescer de modo mais consistente e sustentado e existe ampla evidncia para sugerir que esse efeito  causal: o desenvolvimento financeiro no  simplesmente um resultado do crescimento econmico; contribui para esse crescimento. O desenvolvimento do sector financeiro vai muito alm da existncia de infraestruturas e intermedirios financeiros.  imprescindvel ter polticas robustas e adequadas de regulao e de superviso. A crise financeira global de 2008-2009, serviu bem para fazer-nos perceber as consequncias polticas, econmicas e sociais de opes de regulao e de superviso pouco rigorosas no sector financeiro. Essa mesma crise financeira desencadeou reformas financeiras em todas as principais economias, mas em nenhuma jurisdio a alterao ter sido to abrangente e radical como na Unio Europeia, que decidiu criar uma Unio Bancria, em que o primeiro pilar foi o estabelecimento de uma entidade nica de superviso, para garantir coerncia e consistncia e assim aumentar a integrao e estabilidade financeira na Zona Euro. A Unio Europeia implementou legislao para restringir a exposio do seu sistema financeiro a jurisdies que no tinham, em princpio, regulamentao e superviso equiparadas s suas e em Dezembro de 2014, na primeira avaliao, reconheceu apenas 17 pases no mundo como tendo sistemas equivalentes, sendo que destes apenas um, a frica do Sul, pertencia ao nosso continente e 2, Brasil e Mxico,  Amrica Latina. Este regime entrou em vigor a 1 de Janeiro de 2015. O estatuto de equivalncia traz benefcios para as economias que se relacionam com o mercado financeiro da Unio Europeia. Permite, entre outros, que os seus bancos beneficiem de requisitos de capital mais favorveis no que diz respeito a exposies a pases terceiros que tenham o reconhecimento de equivalncia de superviso. Tendo em conta a intensidade da nossa relao comercial e financeira com os pases que compem a Unio Europeia, o Banco Nacional de Angola deu incio formal em 2020 ao processo de candidatura para obteno do estatuto de equivalncia, procedendo  implementao de legislao e regulamentao com esse propsito, mas com as devidas adaptaes, tendo em conta as caractersticas especficas do sector financeiro nacional. Mas os ganhos so maiores. No imediato, a principal vantagem deste percurso  o reforo da solidez do nosso quadro regulamentar e o aumento da nossa capacidade de superviso. A obteno da equivalncia de superviso, no , por isso, um fim em si mesmo, mas sim um processo de desenvolvimento transversal do nosso sistema financeiro para que possa, com segurana, atrair capitais e competncias, para apoiar os esforos de diversificao e desenvolvimento econmico e social. Tambm estamos num momento ideal para iniciar esse processo, considerando que o nosso sector financeiro  ainda de complexidade e profundidade reduzidas quando comparado com os mercados maduros, permitindo assim uma implementao gradual  medida que o nosso mercado se vai desenvolvendo. Em termos de legislao e regulamentao, conforme mencionado na apresentao inicial desta conferncia, foi publicada a Lei do Regime Geral do Sector Financeiro, e iniciamos tambm a sua regulamentao com a publicao de diversos Avisos e Instrutivos, sendo que este processo ir continuar, naturalmente, para completar o quadro, e depois para atender a futuros desenvolvimentos. Como j referi no incio, no me vou alongar nesse tema, pois j assistimos a uma apresentao sobre o mesmo nesta conferncia. Ao nvel do processo de superviso prudencial, estamos a implementar a metodologia de Anlise e Avaliao pelo Supervisor (Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process em ingls, com a sigla SREP), um processo desenvolvido e implementado pela autoridade de superviso da Unio Europeia. Trata-se de uma metodologia de avaliao extensa, abrangente, detalhada, contnua e interventiva, de cada instituio financeira. Em termos muito gerais, o SREP  um conjunto de procedimentos aplicados pelo supervisor que visa assegurar que cada instituio financeira dispe de estratgias, processos, capital e liquidez adequados aos riscos a que est ou poder vir a estar exposta, bem como determinar o risco que cada instituio constitui para o sistema financeiro. O SREP reconhece o princpio da proporcionalidade atravs da categorizao das instituies financeiras em classes distintas de acordo com o seu perfil de risco e a sua importncia sistmica. Esta categorizao informa tambm o modelo de superviso prudencial a ser aplicado, incluindo a frequncia, mbito e intensidade das avaliaes. Os resultados desta anlise permitem ao supervisor estabelecer requisitos particulares para cada instituio, atravs da definio de requisitos de capital e liquidez especficos, para alm de requisitos de outras naturezas, de forma a assegurar a sua viabilidade e sustentabilidade a longo prazo. A implementao desta metodologia vem alterar significativamente a abordagem de superviso prudencial das instituies financeiras nacionais e tornar o processo mais estruturado, consistente, robusto, baseado no risco e virado para o futuro. Por outro lado, os caminhos da incluso financeira em Angola, que hoje contam com cerca de 50% da populao adulta j com acesso  oferta de servios bsicos bancrios, colocando-nos, de acordo com o Banco Mundial, em linha com a mdia continental africana, leva-nos aos desenvolvimentos  nvel dos sistemas de pagamento, onde pontificam as transferncias instantneas. Aqui, a regulao e superviso ter tambm que assegurar que o processo de transformao digital do sistema financeiro ocorra sob critrios de segurana, eficcia e competitividade. Assim, em complemento ao alinhamento da regulamentao e superviso s melhores praticas internacionais, estamos a considerar uma outra iniciativa que ter um impacto significativo na forma de trabalhar do Banco Nacional de Angola no domnio da superviso. Refiro-me a adopo da tecnologia para superviso, tambm conhecida como Suptech (abreviao em ingls para Supervisory Technology). As bases de dados distribudas, a robtica, a inteligncia artificial e a capacidade, cada vez maior, de computao quntica esto na base da transformao de muitos processos que propiciam a inovao no sistema financeiro, incluindo no domnio da superviso. A aplicao de big data e inteligncia artificial s ferramentas utilizadas pelos supervisores, aumentam significativamente o volume, variedade, velocidade e validade dos dados sob gesto. A inteligncia artificial permite fazer anlises de dados complexos e em grandes volumes que ultrapassam a capacidade humana e assim substituir as abordagens actuais com base no envio de relatrios e inspees on-site morosas e frequentemente reactivas. O Banco Nacional de Angola tem em curso um projecto especfico para adopo gradual de Suptech, almejando obter ganhos de eficincia nos processos de superviso prudencial atravs de uma monitorizao em tempo real dos riscos micro e macroprudenciais inerentes as instituies financeiras. Ganhos que se alargaro a superviso comportamental, a Central de Risco de Crdito e at mesmo para o Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos. Por fim, e ainda com o sentido de reforar o escrutnio e a transparncia das instituies financeiras, considerando as obrigaes de prestao de informao ao mercado em tempo til em observncia das exigncias de calendrio estabelecido pelas bolsas, queremos encorajar as instituies financeiras a considerar a cotao das suas aces na Bolsa de Valores de Angola. A entrada para o mercado regulamentado de capitais, pode tambm facilitar o reforo da prpria estrutura de capitais por acesso ao financiamento atravs da emisso de aces a novos investidores ou mesmo a accionistas existentes, ou de obrigaes a investidores institucionais ou particulares, alcanando um leque mais alargado de investidores; dar liquidez aos accionistas facilitando a venda de aces e proporcionar o alargamento da base de investidores; dar maior visibilidade e prestigio s instituies e aumentar a sua credibilidade junto de fornecedores, clientes e banca internacional. Atrai o investimento externo, valoriza a poupana e a orientao para activos financeiros em moeda nacional. Vivemos tempos desafiantes e de mudana, e temos que nos mobilizar para acompanhar e ser parte activa do processo de transformao da nossa economia, atravs do desenvolvimento do sistema financeiro, que se quer credvel, resiliente, sustentvel e indutor de crescimento econmico e bem-estar social. Parabns ao Expanso por este Frum que se tem transformado numa plataforma importante de dilogo entre actores do sistema financeiro e a sociedade. Muito obrigado. Title: Speech at the workshop on companies in the securities market
text: Home Publications and Media Public Interventions Speech of Governor Jose de Lima Massano, workshop on companies in the securities market Speech by Governor Jose de Lima Massano, workshop on companies in the market for Securities Distinguished Dr. Maria Uni Baptista, President of the Capital Markets Commission, Distinguished guests and participants, Ladies and gentlemen. I begin by thanking the Capital Markets Commission for the invitation i have been asked to the opening of this Workshop on "Companies and securities market" that we are pleased to welcome in our Currency Museum, a space for that has been the regular stage of meetings on topics related to the development of the national financial sector, which we are very pleased with The challenges of mobilising capital to enhance the business fabric and stimulate the economic growth is on the agenda of all EU regulators our continental sub-region, taking into account the stage of development of our economies and the intervention that has been demanded of the financial system, particularly in the context of a crisis of enlarged proportions and which from the outside did not leave any company, sector of activity, or country. In our case, in addition, the fact that economic reforms focus on the diversification of economy and a more dominant participation of the private sector, it is essential to develop the financial system in all its aspects, including the capital market, so that it can be actively and effectively contributed to the sustainable growth, job creation and social well-being. Thus, in addition to the recent Basic Law for the financial system, it is important to highlight the publication of the Insolvency And The Register of Mortgage Susours, as well as the entry into operation of the Commercial, Property and Industrial and Intellectual Room of the luanda district, which were included in the obstacles to the concession of and the attraction of investments to the private sector. The granting of credit has been resuming, with an increase of 8.4% in the last 12 years approximately 14.12% of non-oil GDP and a weight of 17% of the banking assets commercial. Securities, on the other hand, have a weight of 33.63%, being the most important item in the assets of the bank, but represented exclusively by issues from the National Treasury. But as it should be noted, we still have a long way to go and other sources of private sector financing, with a highlight of the instruments typical of the securities market, facilitating the collection and channeling of savings to productive investment. The extension of sources of financing, diversification of risk and reduction of intermediation costs enhanced by direct funding are factors of competitiveness contribute to economic growth. The existence of an active primary securities market, which can serve as a source of financing of companies in order to enable them to achieve a efficient capital structure combining own resources (obtained by placing shares in market) with other people's resources (coming, inter alia, from bond issuance), facilitates their development and growth. However, the securities market will only be efficient and able to meet the needs of financing of companies if investors can afford a liquid, transparent and efficient secondary market. There is a regulatory, supervisory and supervisory framework as well as infrastructure physical and technological factors for the negotiation and liquidation of transactions, it is now necessary to attract securities issuing companies to capitalize on the market and investors to boost it. As for market capitalisation, it is expected that the ongoing privatisation process will forward to the stock exchange some companies that are expected to attract domestic investors and possibly also some foreign investors. The National Bank of Angola has also been encouraging commercial banks to consider the listing of its shares on the stock exchange. In the meantime, as already mentioned, it is important to recognize that we are at the beginning of this journey and that we have a lot of work to do in transmitting information about the securities market to all potential players so that that market can be play the role of promoting the growth of our economy we have, so the holding of this Workshop is an important and timely initiative. Finally, I would also like to point out that the National Bank of Angola is in consultation with the Capital Markets Commission to, in accordance with the General Scheme of Financial Institutions, set a deadline for banks to transfer the provision of services and investment activities in securities securities and derivatives for non-bank financial institutions linked to the market capital and investment. It is our expectation that the transfer process is completed in the first half of 2022, and it is another step towards for the dynamic of such an important market. Welcome to this timely journey of reflection that will surely result in relevant contributions to the continued deepening of our financial market. I hereby declare open the 1st Edition of the Workshop "Companies in the Securities." Thank you very much. 7 Sep. 2021

Maria Uni Baptista, Presidente da Comisso do Mercado de Capitais, Distintos convidados e participantes, Minhas senhoras e meus senhores. Comeo por agradecer a Comisso do Mercado de Capitais pelo convite que me foi formulado para proceder  abertura deste Workshop sobre As empresas e o mercado de valores mobilirios que temos o prazer de acolher no nosso Museu da Moeda, um espao que tem sido palco regular de encontros sobre temas relacionados com o desenvolvimento do sector financeiro nacional, o que muito nos apraz Os desafios de mobilizao de capitais para potenciar o tecido empresarial e estimular o crescimento econmico faz parte da agenda de todos os reguladores da nossa sub-regio continental, tendo em conta o estgio de desenvolvimento das nossas economias e a interveno que se vem demandando ao sistema financeiro, particularmente em contexto de crise pandmica de propores alargadas e que de fora no deixou nenhuma empresa, sector de actividade, nem pas. No nosso caso, em que acresce o facto de as reformas econmicas incidirem sobre a diversificao da economia e uma participao mais dominante do sector privado,  fundamental desenvolver o sistema financeiro em todas as suas vertentes, incluindo o mercado de capitais, para que se possa contribuir de modo activo e sustentvel para o crescimento econmico, a gerao de empregos e o bem-estar social. Assim, alm da recente Lei de bases para o sistema financeiro, h que destacar a publicao da Lei da Insolvncia e do Registo das Garantias Mobilirias, bem como a entrada em funcionamento do Sala de Comrcio, Propriedade e Industrial e Intelectual do Tribunal da Comarca de Luanda, que constavam dos entraves  concesso de crdito e  atraco de investimentos para o sector privado. A concesso de crdito tem sido retomada, registando-se um crescimento de 8,4% nos ltimos 12 meses, correspondendo a cerca de 14,12% do PIB no petrolfero e um peso de 17% do activo da banca comercial. Mas como se denota, temos ainda um longo caminho a percorrer e h que potenciar outras fontes de financiamento ao sector privado, com realce para os instrumentos tpicos do mercado de valores mobilirios, facilitando-se a recolha e canalizao directa da poupana para o investimento produtivo. O alargamento das fontes de financiamento, a diversificao do risco e a reduo dos custos de intermediao potenciados pelo financiamento directo so factores de competitividade que contribuem para o crescimento econmico. A existncia de um mercado primrio de valores mobilirios activo, que possa servir de fonte de financiamento das empresas de forma a permitir-lhes alcanar uma estrutura de capitais eficiente que combine recursos prprios (obtidos pela colocao de aces em mercado) com recursos alheios (provenientes, designadamente, da emisso de obrigaes), facilita o seu desenvolvimento e crescimento. Todavia, o mercado de valores mobilirios s ser eficiente e capaz de responder s necessidades de financiamento das empresas se os investidores puderem dispor de um mercado secundrio lquido, transparente e eficiente. Existindo o enquadramento regulamentar, de superviso e fiscalizao bem como as infraestruturas fsicas e tecnolgicas para a negociao e liquidao das transaces, torna-se agora necessrio atrair empresas emissoras de valores mobilirios para capitalizar o mercado e os investidores para o dinamizar. Quanto  capitalizao do mercado, espera-se que o processo de privatizaes em curso ir encaminhar para a bolsa algumas empresas que devero atrair investidores nacionais e possivelmente tambm alguns investidores estrangeiros. O Banco Nacional de Angola tem vindo, tambm, a encorajar os bancos comerciais a considerar a cotao das suas aces na bolsa. Entretanto, e como j referido,  importante reconhecer que estamos no incio deste percurso e que temos muito trabalho a fazer de transmisso de informao sobre o mercado de valores mobilirios a todos os potenciais intervenientes para que esse mercado possa exercer o papel de promoo do crescimento da nossa economia que perspectivamos, pelo que a realizao deste Workshop  uma iniciativa importante e oportuna. Por ltimo, aproveito tambm para referir que o Banco Nacional de Angola, est em concertao com a Comisso de Mercado de Capitais para, nos termos da Lei do Regime Geral das Instituies Financeiras, estabelecer um prazo limite para os bancos transferirem a prestao de servios e actividades de investimento em valores mobilirios e instrumentos derivados para instituies financeiras no bancrias ligadas ao mercado de capitais e ao investimento.  nossa expectativa que o processo de transferncia esteja concludo ainda no primeiro semestre de 2022, sendo mais um passo para a dinamizao de to importante mercado. Sejam todos muito bem-vindos a esta oportuna jornada de reflexo que seguramente resultar em contribuies relevantes para o contnuo aprofundamento do nosso mercado financeiro. Declaro assim aberta a 1. Edio do Workshop "As Empresas no Mercado de Valores Mobilirios". Muito obrigado. Title: Speech at the Economy and Finance Forum
text: Home Publications and Media Public Interventions Address of the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the Forum on Economics and Finance Speech by the Governor of the National Bank of Angola, at the Forum on Economics and Finance Former Mr. President of the Angolan Banking Association, Dr Mario Nascimento Exma. Madam President of the Capital Stake Committee, Dr. Maria Uini Baptista, Distinguished members of the governing bodies of commercial banks, Dear guests, Ladies and gentlemen I would like to begin by thanking ABANC for the invitation it has asked me to opening of its Economics and Finance, with the theme "The role of banks in economic recovery" The role of the financial system is indeed decisive not only for the recovery of economic, but also for the normal functioning and development of the economy. For this reason, the National Bank of Angola has as one of its main ensure the stability of the financial system. And it was in this sense that it was considered necessary to review 3 of the laws of the Angolan financial system, in particular, the Law of the National Bank of Angola, the Law of the General Financial Institutions and the Financial Systems Act Payment from Angola, all published in the last 12 months. The Law of Payment Systems of Angola published on December 16, 2020 replaced the law 5/05 of 29 July, and adapt legislation to the new context of digital transformation, paving the way for the development of an ecosystem of mobile and instant transfers that should contribute to the significant increase in financial inclusion, facilitating the participation of the low-income population and micro-enterprises in the national financial system. The Law of the General Regime of Financial Institutions, published in May 2021, harmonised the legal framework of the system angolan financial policy to the objective of building a robust regulatory and supervisory environment and modern, aligned with the best international practices. This law, in addition to a new model of prudential supervision, updates the requirements of the governance of the institutions which have become much more demanding, with the aim of ensuring adequate management of and prepared to face the increasingly complex challenges facing the financial sector, and thus ensure its stability. Finally, the new Law of the National Bank of Angola, approved by the National Assembly on 18 October, and which came to repeal Law No. 10/16 of 15 July also brought significant changes to the previous law, which aim to make converge the model of action and governance of the Bank to the recognised good practices that have been adopted by central banks. We therefore consider that a robust framework is created that equates the legislation and regulation of the our financial sector at international best practices and ensures not only their suitability in relation to the current context but also sustainability of the sector. Looking to the future, and beyond the consolidation of the implementation of these changes i've already mentioned, we have one more great challenge ahead of us. Climate change that is affecting climate change significant in the world, and which have implications for relevant to our sector. The theme is not new, but in recent years it has been gaining greater prominence, and today, the climate and environmental change, and promoting sustainable development as well as environmental protection are issues of undisputed importance on the agenda governments, companies, institutions, organizations, decision-makers, among others. Among the entities with attention focused on the theme of climate change and environmental policies are several central banks and supervisors of financial systems, for the preponderant role that financial institutions have on the economic development and the risks these changes bring to the resilience of these institutions and consequently the stability of the system financial. More specifically, for the financial system, climate risks have generally been identified and environmental impacts, two risk factors physical risk and transition risk. Physical risk refers to the financial impact resulting (i) from climate change, particularly the most frequent occurrence extreme weather events such as droughts, floods and storms or gradual climate change, such as rising sea temperatures or levels; as well as (ii) environmental degradation, e.g. pollution of air, water and Soil. The occurrence of these events may lead directly to, for example, property damage or, to a decreased productivity, which can be turned into losses for an institution that is the financier of the activity or on the impacted entity. The risk of transition refers to the financial losses of an institution, which may result, in directly or indirectly, of the adjustment for a more climate-sustainable and environmentally sustainable economy. This risk can be triggered, for example, e.g. by a relatively abrupt adoption of climate and environmental policies, by the progress of technology or by changes in market sentiment and preferences. In the financial sector, risks are covered by capital, and thus an inevitable consequence of the identification of these risks is the allocation by central banks and supervisors of capital requirements for the coverage of climate and environmental risks in financial institutions, as they do for all other risks. In this context, it is understood that financial institutions will necessarily have a very important role in the sustainable development, by the need to manage the financial risks arising from the climate change and environmental impacts and consequently their capital requirements, which will result in the directing funding to activities that promote sustainable development. What I have just said makes it obvious that international financial institutions currently finance the activities will be under increasing pressure. In fact, there are already several institutions financial institutions and very relevant investors, including investment funds, which do not finance or invest in the oil sector. Thus, this context also serves to strengthen the need for diversification of our economy, and in the shortest time possible. I refer to the oil sector because it is directly affecting us the most, but the high-risk activities in the context of climate change and environmental change are much more comprehensive. As I have already mentioned, globally, we see this theme of climate change and environmental and development to gain a mind-blowing and comprehensive speed. Very recently, on 3 November, the IFRS Foundation announced the creation of the "International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB)", to develop standards for disseminating information on climate issues sustainability to meet the needs of investorinformation needs. This Board will work in close cooperation with the IASB (International Accounting Standards Board), ensuring connectivity and compatibility between Accounting Standards IFRS and ISSB standards. In the face of these developments worldwide, the National Bank of Angola has on its agenda the analysis of the theme of the amendments climate and environmental impact and its impact on the national financial system in order to be able to define the way forward by the national financial institutions in this area, which will certainly be aligned with the good practices International. Returning to the undeferred need for the diversification of our economy, I refer to the 10/20, which served to boost credit to the real sector of the economy. By the end of October, they had been granted under that Notice, 345 credits, making up a total of 593.09 billion Kwanzas. The National Bank of Angola recognizes the effort banks did in the granting of financing to the real economy, but warns of the need to continue in this little change, because there is no other - we need to work to ensure that our financial sector and our economy are sustainable in the long term. We live in times of many constant challenges that require more and more knowledge, professionalism, rigour and dedication of professionals in the financial sector. It is up to each of you to be prepared to be able to respond fully these challenges and thus contribute to the sustainable development of our economy and the financial sector. I will end by declaring the X ABANC Economics and Finance Forum open. Thank you very much. Publliicado On:: Nov. 17 2021

Sr. Presidente da Associao Angolana de Bancos, Dr Mrio Nascimento Exma. Sra. Presidente da Comisso de Marcado de Capitais, Dra Maria Uini Baptista, Distintos membros dos rgos sociais dos bancos comerciais, Caros convidados, Minhas senhoras e meus senhores Queria comear por agradecer a ABANC pelo convite que me formulou para proceder a abertura do seu Frum de Economia e Finanas, com o tema O papel dos bancos na recuperao econmica O papel do sistema financeiro  de facto decisivo no apenas para a recuperao econmica, mas tambm para o normal funcionamento e desenvolvimento da economia. Por essa razo, o Banco Nacional de Angola tem como uma das suas principais funes assegurar a estabilidade do sistema financeiro. E foi com esse sentido que se considerou necessrio efectuar a reviso de 3 das leis basilares do sistema financeiro angolano, nomeadamente, a Lei do Banco Nacional de Angola, a Lei do Regime Geral das Instituies Financeiras e a Lei dos Sistemas de Pagamento de Angola, todas publicadas nos ltimos 12 meses. A Lei dos Sistemas de Pagamento de Angola publicada a 16 de Dezembro de 2020 veio substituir a lei n 5/05 de 29 de Julho, e adequar a legislao ao novo contexto de transformao digital, abrindo o caminho para o desenvolvimento de um ecossistema de transferncias mveis e instantneas que devero contribuir para o aumento significativo da incluso financeira, facilitando a participao da populao de baixa renda e das micro empresas no sistema financeiro nacional. A Lei do Regime Geral das Instituies Financeiras, publicada em Maio de 2021 veio harmonizar o enquadramento legal do sistema financeiro angolano ao objectivo de construo de um ambiente de regulao e superviso robusto e moderno, alinhado s melhores prticas internacionais. Esta lei, para alm de um novo modelo de superviso prudencial, actualiza os requisitos do modelo de governao das instituies financeiras, que se tornaram muito mais exigentes, com o objectivo de assegurar uma gesto adequada e preparada para enfrentar os desafios cada vez mais complexos que se colocam ao sector financeiro, e assim garantir a sua estabilidade. Por ltimo, a nova Lei do Banco Nacional de Angola, aprovada pela Assembleia Nacional a 18 de Outubro, e que veio revogar a Lei n. 10/16, de 15 de Julho, tambm trouxe alteraes significativas face  lei anterior, que visam fazer convergir o modelo de actuao e governao do Banco s reconhecidas boas praticas que vm sendo adoptadas pelos bancos centrais. Consideramos assim estar criado um framework robusto que equipara a legislao e regulamentao do nosso sector financeiro s melhores praticas internacionais e assegura no apenas a sua adequao face ao contexto actual mas tambm a sustentabilidade do sector. Olhando para o futuro, e para alm da consolidao da implementao destas alteraes que j referi, temos mais um grande desafio  nossa frente. As alteraes climticas que esto a afectar de forma significativa o mundo, e que tm implicaes relevantes para o nosso sector. O tema no  novo, mas nos ltimos anos tem vindo a ganhar maior protagonismo, e hoje, as alteraes climticas e ambientais, e a promoo do desenvolvimento sustentvel bem como a proteco do ambiente so questes de importncia incontestvel na agenda dos governos, empresas, instituies, organizaes, decisores, entre outros. Dentre as entidades com a ateno focada no tema das alteraes climticas e ambientais esto vrios bancos centrais e supervisores dos sistemas financeiros, pelo papel preponderante que as instituies financeiras tm no desenvolvimento econmico e pelos riscos que estas alteraes trazem para a resilincia dessas instituies e consequentemente a estabilidade do sistema financeiro. Mais concretamente, para o sistema financeiro, identificaram-se, no geral, nos riscos climticos e ambientais, dois factores de risco fundamentais, o risco fsico e o de transio. O risco fsico refere-se ao impacto financeiro que resulta (i) das alteraes climticas, nomeadamente a ocorrncia mais frequente de fenmenos meteorolgicos extremos como secas, inundaes e tempestades ou de alteraes climticas graduais, como o aumento das temperaturas ou dos nveis do mar; bem como (ii) da degradao ambiental, por exemplo, a poluio do ar, da gua e dos solos. A ocorrncia destes eventos pode conduzir directamente a, por exemplo, danos patrimoniais ou, a uma diminuio da produtividade, que se podem transformar em perdas para uma instituio financiadora da actividade ou sobre a entidade impactada. O risco de transio refere-se s perdas financeiras de uma instituio, que podem resultar, directa ou indirectamente, do processo de ajustamento para uma economia mais sustentvel em termos climticos e ambientais. Este risco pode ser desencadeado, por exemplo, por uma adopo relativamente abrupta de polticas climticas e ambientais, pelo progresso tecnolgico ou por mudanas do sentimento e das preferncias do mercado. No sector financeiro, os riscos so cobertos pelo capital, e assim, uma consequncia inevitvel da identificao destes riscos  a atribuio, pelos bancos centrais e supervisores, de requisitos de capital para cobertura dos riscos climticos e ambientais nas carteiras de crdito das instituies financeiras, como o fazem para todos os outros riscos. Neste contexto, compreende-se que as instituies financeiras vo necessariamente ter um papel muito importante no desenvolvimento sustentvel, pela necessidade que vo ter de gerir os riscos financeiros originados pelas alteraes climticas e ambientais e consequentemente os seus requisitos de capital, o que ir resultar no direccionamento do financiamento para as actividades que promovem um desenvolvimento sustentvel. O que acabei de referir torna bvio que as instituies financeiras internacionais que actualmente financiam as actividades petrolferas estaro submetidas a presso crescente. Alis, existem j vrias instituies financeiras e investidores muito relevantes, incluindo fundos de investimento, que no financiam nem investem no sector petrolfero. Voltando  necessidade inadivel da diversificao da nossa economia, fao referncia ao Aviso 10/20, que serviu para impulsionar o crdito ao sector real da economia. At ao final de Outubro, tinham sido concedidos ao abrigo desse Aviso, 345 crditos, perfazendo um total de 593,09 mil milhes de Kwanzas. O Banco Nacional de Angola reconhece o esforo que os bancos fizeram na concesso de financiamento  economia real, mas adverte para a necessidade de se continuar neste cambinho, porque no h outro  precisamos de trabalhar no sentido de assegurar que o nosso sector financeiro e a nossa economia so sustentveis a longo prazo. Vivemos tempos de muitos e constantes desafios que exigem cada vez mais conhecimentos, profissionalismo, rigor e dedicao de todos os profissionais do sector financeiro. Cabe a cada um a responsabilidade de estar preparado para poder responder cabalmente a estes desafios e assim contribuir para o desenvolvimento sustentvel da nossa economia e do sector financeiro. Title: Discurso de Abertura do VI Encontro Nacional de Tesouraria, Malanje 2 de Fevereiro de 2022
text: Opening Speech of the VI National Treasury Meeting, Malanje February 2, 2022 Hon. Mr. Norberto dos Santos, "Kwata Kanawa", Governor of Malanje Province, Dear Mr. Tavares Cristovao, Director of BNA, Dear Invited Central Bank Representatives, Dear Suppliers of Banknotes, Coins and Cash Handling Equipment, Dear Representatives of Commercial Banking, Ladies and Gentlemen Lecturers, Dear Directors, Colleagues of the National Bank of Angola and the Government of the Province of Malanje, Ladies and Gentlemen, It is with great pleasure that I take the floor at this opening session of the VI National Treasury Meeting, which has already become a tradition in our Institution every year and which this year we have the great pleasure of holding here, in the capital city of the province of Malanje. In the fulfilment of one of its functions, that of managing the circulating medium, the National Bank of Angola has improved its management instruments in the sc to adapt this activity to good international practices. To this end, the Policy and Regulation for the management of the circular environment were recently approved, fundamental tools for better coordination and accountability of the exercise of this activity. In order to improve the quality and enhance the security features of the Kwanza banknotes, in July 2020, the National Bank of Angola began to put the 2020 series banknotes into circulation, with 4 of the 5 denominations in circulation being produced on a polymer substrate whose main advantage is durability, contributing to the reduction of production costs since its life cycle is longer compared to cotton. In 2021, a survey was carried out to determine the levels of satisfaction of the population with the banknotes of the 2020 series and the results show that about the surveyed population expressed satisfaction with the banknotes currently in circulation, which for us, of course, is a reason for rejoicing. We take advantage of this Forum to reaffirm that the metal coins of the 2012 series have discharging power and, therefore, continue in circulation, so they should be put on everyone. A survey conducted last year showed that more than 93% of respondents said that they regularly use coins, mainly for the purchase of goods and services and for the facilitation of change. However, there are still challenges for economic agents and the population in general to have access to metal coins, so we urge the participants of the VI Treasury Meeting to reflect and propose strategies to contribute to a better circulation of metal coins. We held the VI Treasury Meeting in the year in which our country will mark 20 years since the achievement of peace and national reconciliation. On this date, the National Bank of Angola will put into circulation the commemorative metal coin of 200 Kwanzas, which will have discharging power and will circulate simultaneously with the non-denomination. We continue to emphasise the need to master the characteristics and security features of banknotes and coins in circulation, so that counterfeit banknotes can be placed on the market. It is a permanent concern of the Central Bank that the population has availability of banknotes and coins in adequate quantity and quality. And we recognize that there are still places where to find a banking financial institution, it is necessary to travel considerable distances, with losses of money. To bridge this gap, we urge commercial banks to make efforts to enter into correspondence banking agreements with companies located in locations where commercial banks are not established. In addition, in order to reduce the costs of transporting banknotes by commercial banks and improve access to cash by the population, the National Bank of An has opened 1 Regional Delegation and 3 Custodians of Securities in the last two years, thus making the Central Bank have a physical presence in 13 Provinces. As there is a need to strengthen the expansion of the services offered by Automatic Payment Terminals (POS), exclusively with regard to cash delivery at POS, in order to complement the network of Automated Teller Machines (ATMs), especially in the outskirts of large cities and in the interior of the country, Instruction No. 12/2021, September 14, rules on Cash Withdrawal Operations at Automatic Payment Terminals were established. Likewise, to facilitate access to cash by the population, through Instruction No. 24/21 of December 7, a new limit for ATM withdrawals was set in the amount of Kz 100,000.00, so that commercial banks should continue to make efforts, in partnership with equipment providers, so that ATMs are permanently supplied with resources. Taking into account the constant concern aimed at modernizing the management activity of the circulating medium, a Cash Center is under construction in Luanda, a logistics center for the storage and processing of banknotes and coins aimed at increasing the capacity of processing and storage of banknotes. Fully operational, the Cash Center, whose capacity is to simultaneously serve a total of 7 banking institutions, will revolutionize the exercise of this ac since it will improve the availability in quantity and quality of banknotes and coins to commercial banks. Excellencies The process of assessing the need to open other custody centers and Regional Delegations will continue. In this sense, the Custody of Values of Saurimo, in Lunda-Sul, is planned for this year. It should be noted that in addition to the availability of physical cash, the expansion of payment means and instruments in Angola is characterized by a change in the behavior associated with payments, a fact evidenced in the change in the pattern of use of these instruments in recent years, with a growing adoption of electronic instruments. It should be noted that the scenario of supply and demand for payment services continues to evolve rapidly, driven by the association of technologies with financial technologies, and making the payment environment increasingly dynamic, with the creation of new forms of payment service provision, changing the environment associated with more traditional structures and the demand for fast financial services, comfortable, low-cost and accessible to an increasingly large number of users than, not necessarily, the "banked". In this context of paradigm shift in payment services and the possibility of entry of new players, creation of alternative services and prospects for effective financial inclusion, the implementation of the Instant Transfer System (ITS) in the Angolan Payment System is underway, which aims at the financial inclusion of the unbanked population, through the use of more digital payment methods, such as mobile phones, tablets, computers and others. The themes scheduled for the working sessions during these two days will allow the exchange of experiences on best practices in the field of human management, so once again we thank the delegations from the various countries who will lend their knowledge and transmit their experiences, counting to enrich the debates and the adoption of best practices by the actors in this process in Angola. It is convenient to observe the biosecurity and physical distancing measures resulting from COVID 19, we held this meeting in a hybrid format, so presentations will be made remotely. We euphorically greet the national and foreign participants who will be with us in this way. I would not like to end my speech without, however, thanking the prompt welcome given to us by the government entities of pro\ Malanje, especially by His Excellency Mr. Governor, Norberto dos Santos "Kwata Kanawa", and his closest collaborators. With these words, I declare open the VI National Treasury Meeting. Good work to all and thank you very much.

Outrossim, visando reduzir os custos de transporte de notas pelos bancos comerciais e melhorar o acesso ao numerrio pela populao, o Banco Nacional de Angola ltimos dois anos procedeu a abertura de 1 Delegao Regional e de 3 Custdias de Valores estando assim o Banco Central com presena fsica em 13 Provncias. Havendo a necessidade de reforar a expanso dos servios oferecidos pelos Terminais de Pagamento Automtico (TPA), exclusivamente no que concerne ao levan de numerrio em TPA, de modo a complementar a rede de Caixas Automticos (ATMs), sobretudo nas periferias das grandes cidades e no interior do pas, atravs dc Instrutivo n. 12/2021, 14 de Setembro foram estabelecidas regras sobre Operaes de Levantamento de Numerrio nos Terminais de Pagamento Automtico. De igual modo, para facilitar o acesso ao numerrio pela populao, atravs do Instrutivo n 24/21 de 7 de Dezembro, foi fixado um novo limite de levantamento di Caixas Automticos no montante de Kz 100 000,00 pelo que os bancos comerciais devero continuar a envidar esforos, em parceria com os provedores de equipam para que os Caixas Automticos estejam permanentemente abastecidos de recursos. Tendo em conta a constante preocupao visando a modernizao da actvidade de gesto do meio circulante, est em construo, em Luanda, um Cash Center que  centro logstico de armazenamento e tratamento de notas e moedas metlicas destinado a elevar a capacidade de processamento e de armazenamento de notas. Quaiu totalmente em funcionamento, o Cash Center, cuja capacidade  de atender, em simultneo, um total de 7 instituies bancrias vai revolucionar o exerccio dessa ac uma vez que melhorar a disponibilidade em quantidade e qualidade de notas e moedas metlicas aos bancos comerciais. Excelncias, O processo de avaliao da necessidade de abertura de outros centros de Custdia e Delegaes Regionais vai continuar. Neste sentido, est prevista para este ano a; da Custdia de Valores de Saurimo, na Lunda-Sul. Salienta-se que para alm da disponibilizao de numerrio fsico, a expanso dos meios e instrumentos de pagamento em Angola caracteriza-se por uma alterao c no comportamento associado aos pagamentos, facto evidenciado na mudana do padro de utilizao destes instrumentos nos ltimos anos, com uma adeso cada ve crescente aos instrumentos eletrnicos. Ressalta-se que o cenrio da oferta e procura pelos servios de pagamento continua a evoluir de forma acelerada, impulsionado pela associao das tecnologias aos s financeiros, e tornando o ambiente de pagamentos cada vez mais dinmico, com a criao de novas formas de prestao de servios de pagamento, em alternativa ao ambiente associado s estruturas mais tradicionais e pela procura de servios financeiros rpidos, cmodos, de baixos custos e acessveis a um nmero cada vez mai< alargado de utilizadores que, no necessariamente, os bancarizados. Neste contexto de mudana de paradigma dos servios de pagamento e possibilidade de entrada de novos players, criao de servios alternativos e perspetivas de ui efectiva incluso financeira, est em curso a implementao do Sistema de Transferncias Instantneas (STI) no Sistema de Pagamentos de Angola que visa permitir incluso financeira da populao no bancarizada, atravs do uso de mtodos de pagamentos mais digitais, como telemveis, tablets, computadores e outros. As temticas agendadas para as sesses de trabalho durante estes dois dias permitiro a troca de experincias sobre as melhores prticas no domnio da gesto de tes( pelo que, mais uma vez, agradecemos as delegaes provenientes dos vrios pases que emprestaro o seu conhecimento e transmitiro as suas experincias, contribi para enriquecer os debates e a adopo das melhores prticas pelos intervenientes deste processo em Angola. Convindo observar as medidas de biossegurana e de distanciamento fsico decorrente da COVID 19, realizamos esse encontro em formato hbrido, pelo que algunu apresentaes sero feitas de maneira remota. Title: Notas de abertura do Vice Governador, Rui Miguns, na conferncia sobre o Financiamento ao Sector Real
text: Opening remarks by the Vice-Governor, Rui Miguens, at the conference on "Real Sector Financing" Honourable Members of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola; Distinguished Heads of Financial Institutions; Dear Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen; It is with great pleasure that we welcome all those present, and we are pleased to mark the opening of the First Conference, of the cycle of conferences of the National Bank of Angola, resuming its face-to-face format, which is under the theme "financing the Royal Sector", an activity that reaffirms the commitment and highlights the participation of the National Bank of Angola in the process of implementing an environment conducive to objective economic activity is to promote the discussion on the operationalization of credit to the Real Sector of the Economy, as a tool for the economic sustainability of the country In the current economic scenario, the rigor in the exercise of macroeconomic policy in general and monetary policy in particular, in the management of its instruments and price stability, is an important factor, Assessed by its impact on investment decisions, the guarantee of employment and the appropriate distribution of available resources. Angola has been implementing a set of macroeconomic reforms based on fiscal consolidation, the reduction of inflation, the balance of external accounts, resilience of the financial system and improvement of the business environment, so the focus of Banco 1 de Angola's activities, in accordance with its mandate, is aimed at promoting price stability and the soundness of the financial system and its alignment with good internationals. We recognize that the economic and financial framework of the world and in particular of Angola, devastated not only by the crisis in the oil sector, but by the slowdown in credit activity, demands the creation of responsible initiatives, compliance with legal and regulatory standards of the financial system and the construction of a conducive to the diversification of economic activity, through the promotion of credit as a support for the revitalization and socio-economic development of the country. As a result of this action, we are pleased to inform you that in general terms, within the scope of the regulations issued for this purpose, normally referred to in Notice 10/2020, until February 2022, the amount of credit disbursed by the banking sector to the real sector of the economy, was Kz 542,000,000,000.00 (five hundred and forty-million Kwanzas - about one billion US dollars) which represented 305.31% of the defined minimum limit and a total of 432 p corresponding to 98.18% of the established minimum. Evidently, the developments for the provision of a Central Registration of Movable Securities contribute to increase and enhance the granting of credit, so the adjustments made to give greater robustness to the Risk Information Center in qualitative and quantitative terms have become very timely and of high importance. Excellencies We recognize that there is still a long way to go, but efforts continue to be made to facilitate access to credit, support emerging economic ACLs, create conditions for increasing the supply of financial services to the population, in a safe and efficient way, as well as simplify business licensing and business start-up procedures. bringing beneficiaries closer to policies that stimulate investments. Our action is reinforced by the change in the status of the National Bank of Angola to an independent administrative entity in the exercise of its function as the exchange rate authority. Therefore, by embracing the responsibility of carrying out this activity, we reiterate the importance that the National Bank of Angola gives to the improvement of the business that is vital for the Angolan economy, including for the national entrepreneur, who must have the State institutions as allies in developing projects seen as drivers of economic growth. We hope that today's conference will have the necessary debate, in which we are all invited to share knowledge and experiences that reflect different social and economic realities and that affect the financing of the real economy so that we can, together, find ways to make the huge of our economy in sustainable economic growth, for the benefit of all Angolans. Finally, on behalf of the National Bank of Angola and its Board of Directors, we reiterate our thanks for your presence, which greatly dignifies this moment. I therefore declare open the Conference on the financing of the Real Sector. Thank you very much. Published in: Mar 18, 2022

Title: Governador Jos de Lima Massano Disserta na Conferncia de Alto Nvel sobre Poltica Monetria na frica Subsariana
text: Governor Jose de Lima Massano Speaks at the High-Level Conference on Monetary Policy in sub-Saharan Africa The Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Jose de Lima Massano, participated today in the high-level Conference: Modernizing monetary policy in South Africa promoted by the Training Institute for Africa (ATI), AFRITAC South (AFS) and AFRITAC Oriental (AFE) of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), held virtually, from February 28 to March 2 of this year. Invited to speak at the event, Governor Jose de Lima Massano spoke on the theme: Modernizing Monetary Policy in Sub-Saharan Africa - Bringing Exchange Parities to More Flexible Exchange Rate Regimes - the Case of Angola, having, on the occasion, emphasized that the pandemic has obviously caused some turbulence in the domestic foreign exchange market. However, the floating exchange rate for Angola played a significant role in absorbing shocks and ensured the functioning of the market, as it was possible to continue to ensure an efficient allocation of resources and foreign exchange. Thus, for the first time in economic history; of Angola, a drop in oil prices (mid-2020) did not result in a disruption of the foreign exchange market. Participating in the high-level conference are representatives of the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank, academics from Stanford University, the MIT School of D, Dartmouth University, the European Central Bank (ECB), the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) and the Central Banks of Namibia, Seichel Mauritius, Kenya, Zambia, Madagascar, Eswatini, Uganda, Ghana, Rwanda, Tanzania, Sweden and the Czech Republic. Published in: Mar 1, 2022

Para alm da j mencionada lei, foi ainda aprovado o decreto presidencial 35/11 de 15 de Fevereiro, que institucionaliza a Unidade de Informao Financeira (UIF). Esta instituio tm como objectivo a recolha e sempre que necessrio o pedido de informaes de operaes e/ou actividades suspeita de lavagem de dinheiro e financiamento do terrorismo; a anlise da mesma; e sua disseminao aos rgos policiais e judiciais, assim como  outras Unidades de Inteligncia no mundo. Esses avanos permitiram que Angola fosse considerada como uma jurisdio que est comprometida com a implementao do sistema de luta contra BC e FT e que est a desenvolver aces consistentes com as expectativas do Grupo de Aco Financeira Internacional- GAFI. Deste relatrio do Banco Mundial ser produzido o Plano de implementao para o Sistema de luta contra o BC e do FT para de Angola a ser apresentado em Maro de 2013. Temos j uma agenda muito preenchida de tarefas a desenvolver no Pas que envolvem no s a Unidade de Informao Financeira como todas as instituies Nacionais com responsabilidade reguladora e de superviso, assim como as entidades Judiciais e Policiais. O processo  longo, rduo mas certamente possvel e o vosso papel enquanto Magistrados ser determinante na cooperao que deve existir com a Unidade de Informao Financeira.  essencial a existncia de uma cooperao estreita e eficaz entre a UIF e as autoridades policiais e judiciais atravs da criao de canais de comunicao adequados, mediante a celebrao de protocolos de cooperao e troca de informao, permitindo um fluxo constante de informao que auxilie e suporte a analise realizada pela UIF e das investigaes levadas a cabo pelas autoridades Judiciais e policiais. As responsabilidades das autoridades Judiciais e Policiais esto detalhadas nas recomendaes do GAFI e transcritas na legislao Angolana relevante. Deixando o pdio para os nossos experts gostaria de desejar uma manh de muito proveito e assegurar que este  somente o primeiro dos nossos necessrios encontros Desta forma ajudaremos Angola a demonstrar ao mundo, que no s temos conscincia, mas como realmente estamos empenhados na implementao de um Sistema contra lavagem de dinheiro e contra o Financiamento ao Terrorismo efectivo e eficiente. Title: Interveno da Administradora, Beatriz Santos, na abertura da Semana Global do Dinheiro, em Malanje
text: Speech by the Administrator, Beatriz Santos, at the opening of the Global Money Week, in Malanje. His Excellency the Vice-Governor of the Province of Malanje, Domingos Manuel Eduardo; Distinguished representatives of the Provincial Directorates of the different Ministerial Departments; Dear Heads of Financial Institutions;, Dear Children and Young People, Ladies and Gentlemen, It is with great pleasure that we welcome you all, graced and honored by your presence at this Official Opening Act of the 10th.the Global Money Week Edition - 2022 - under the motto: "Build your future, be skillful with your money", which takes place in this beautiful and historic Province of Malanje, land of the Palanca Neg Gigante. Dear guests, The Global Money Week circumscribes the commitment to financial awareness, inspiring children and young people to learn about financial issues, livelihoods and entrepreneurship, as well as the participation of the National Bank of Angola and its national partners in an international event, whose primary organization is in charge of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD). The motto "Build your future, be skillful with your money", was chosen to highlight the importance of building financial resilience and staying healthy in the current context of the COVID-19 pandemic, which continues to affect people around the world, as well as to highlight the importance of financial education to maintain people's socioeconomic and financial being, in particular, and the soundness of the financial system in general. For a week, we will carry out an awareness campaign that aims to inspire children and young people to properly handle money and for its benefit through the transmission of financial management methods and entrepreneurship techniques, carrying out recreational activities and lectures. The realization of these activities also has the purpose of teaching children and young people to develop methods on how to create chains of financial sustainability. Excellencies This major event symbolizes the recognition of this activity as a fundamental means of transmitting good financial management practices to the current generation providing them with knowledge aimed at the development of coherent, assertive and disciplined attitudes and behaviors in the management of economic and financial resources. As the popular adage goes: "it is from a small age that the cucumber is twisted". That is, it is at an early age that the first steps should be taken towards building economic and financial awareness, in a responsible and healthy way. In this sense, we draw the attention of parents and guardians to the continuous reflection on the t "keeping money at home", as well as guidance on appropriate methods and strategies, so that, in the near future, they are in fact conscious adults, with habits of managing money wisely. Ladies and gentlemen, This activity also aims to promote financial inclusion by strengthening information sharing and training and thus raising the levels of Educ; Financial Inclusion of the general population, highlighting its contribution to the development of positive behaviors, such as:  Ability to examine and manage your savings and finances;  Ability to make assertive financial decisions and choices;  Ability to discuss financial matters;  Ability to plan for the future and invest in the short, medium and long term; and  To earn for himself and his family. It is worth noting that as the Central Bank, it is our responsibility to develop strategies aimed at promoting management and savings habits among citizens, putting them up to the constant transformations in the financial sector, such as banking, insurance and the capital market, in their daily lives. Excellencies In 2021, this activity was carried out in a semi-face-to-face manner, given the context imposed by the COVID-19 pandemic, with a total of 8,573 participants, including children, young people and adults from various public and private institutions in the country, with emphasis on educational institutions. The results indicate a long period to go, but efforts continue to be made in order to increase the levels of financial education of the population; Angolan government, associating this activity with the realization of awareness campaigns throughout the year with the participation of commercial banks. In this edition, it is important to highlight the need to comply with biosecurity measures in all activity spaces. To conclude, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the National Bank of Angola, I could not fail to express our sincere thanks to the Malanje Provincial Government, for the warm welcome of this great initiative to celebrate the 2022 Global Money Week. Our thanks are extended to the entire team that directly and indirectly dedicated itself to the preparation of this event, because without their distinguished work the realization of this ceremony would not be a fact. To all, our deep gratitude. Thus, I declare the 2022 Global Money Week open. Thank you very much. Published In: Mar 24, 2022

Title: Discurso do Administrador, Miguel Miguel, na abertura da terceira edio do Seminrio de Capacitao dos Jornalistas
text: Speech by the Administrator, Miguel Miguel, at the opening of the third edition of the Seminar on the Training of Journalists Dear Representative of the Association of Economic Journalists - AJECO, Dear Representative of the Union of Angolan Journalists, Distinguished Journalists, Ladies and gentlemen. First of all, I begin by expressing my deep gratitude for having accepted our invitation, in this Third Edition of the Cycle of Cap Seminars Aimed at Journalists, promoted in order to foster the sharing of knowledge about the mission of Banco Nacional Angola, enshrined in the Constitution of the Rej of Angola and in its Organic Law. As everyone knows, the National Bank of Angola positions itself as an institution of continuous learning, which within the scope of its mission and functions: seeks to share, but also to listen to social actors about the effectiveness of its action, with emphasis on the journalistic class, as the entity responsible for collecting, processing and disseminating credible information on matters of an economic and financial nature. This initiative is part of this vein, where we regularly address current and active issues, and in this edition we will deal with matters related to credit policy management mechanisms, banking consumer protection strategy, risk-based prudential supervision, the role of the banking agent in financial inclusion, accounting standardization and harmonization in the Angolan banking sector, policy and principles of cybersecurity in the banking sector and prospects for the development of the Angolan Payment System. The National Bank of Angola, in terms of its responsibilities regarding ensuring price stability in the economy and soundness of the financial system, has worked hard to build a solid, resilient and inclusive financial system, whose prudential standards and prudential supervision practices and behaviors are adjusted to internationally accepted standards. Dear Journalists, The programme of urgent reforms of the financial system is beginning to bear fruit, the impact of which is already being felt in the lives of families and economic operators In the field of credit enhancement to the real sector of the economy, the implementation of Notice No. 10/2020, now repealed by Notice No. 10/2022, more innovative, in February 2022, disbursing a total of 29 new loans to the real sector of the economy, making a total of 516 loans granted, of which 432 with actual disbursements. In terms of financial value, the credit granted corresponds to a total of 858.27 billion kwanzas (equivalent to USD 1,728.30 million The amount disbursed by commercial banks until February 2022 totalled 542.49 billion kwanzas (equivalent to USD 1,092.41 million), representing an increase of 26.21 billion kwanzas (5.08%) compared to January 2022. In the context of the flexibility of the foreign exchange market, today we point out a framework for the normalization of its operation, with greater security, predictability and access reducing bureaucracy for those who need foreign currency to honour legitimate commitments abroad, boost business or bear personal burdens. The Kwanza, our currency, which gained a new member on April 4, 2022, the commemorative metal coin of 200 Kwanzas, with discharging power, has been recovering from losses in previous years, having appreciated by about 33% at the stage against the United States Dollar, while international reserves are stable, covering close to 11 months of imports of goods and services. Dear Journalists, Given the imperative need to promote the construction of residential properties and to create the conditions for bank customers to contract housing compatible with the average level of income earned, the National Bank of Angola published Notice No. 09/22, of 6 April - which establishes special housing credit and construction credit regimes and defines the eligibility requirements, terms, conditions and costs applicable to these credits, as well as the treatment in the calculation of reserve requirements. The regulatory framework established by the aforementioned Notice is mandatory for systemically important Commercial Banks in the national market, and optionally applicable for other Banking Financial Institutions, respecting the duties of information within the scope of credit agreements, as well as the deadlines for analysis and communication of the final decision, formalisation and availability of credit. However, before granting credit, Commercial Banks are obliged to carry out a rigorous assessment of the financial capacity of customers and promote housing construction projects to meet their obligations under the housing credit agreement under the proposed terms, as well as to carry out regular monitoring of their customers, in order to detect financial difficulties or other circumstances that may increase the risk of default in a timely manner and take action. the appropriate measures to prevent or remedy the situation. Dear journalists, The new institutional framework of Banco Nacional Angola brings us enormous challenges, particularly with regard to ensuring price stability in the economy; promotion of financial inclusion and the strengthening of supervisory mechanisms for financial institutions. Therefore, we will continue to be determined to work with the media due to the relevance of their social role in guiding the expectations of economic agents. Finally, as has been the case, I reiterate my thanks for your presence and I take this opportunity to wish you success in your noble mission of training, and I wish you a very fruitful working session in the Macuta Auditorium of the National Bank of Angola.
