Title: Interveno do Governador Jos de Lima Massano na Abertura da Conferncia sobre Integridade, tica e Cibersegurana: Desafios e Oportunidades, organizada pela EY Angola.
text: Speech by Governor Jose de Lima Massan r at the Opening of the Conference on Integrity, FTE and Cybersecurity: Challenges and Opportunities, organized by EY Angola. Your Excellency Mr. Carlos Basto, Office Managing Partner of EY Angola, Excellencies, Distinguished guests, Ladies and gentlemen. First of all, I would like to thank EY for inviting me to open this conference on topics of enormous relevance in the current context I have experienced Integrity, ethics and cybersecurity are of special importance in the financial sector, considering the fundamental role that the institutions that operate there play in the economy and society. And for that reason, they are also permanent topics on the agenda of the National Bank of Angola. The global financial crisis of 2007/2008 and its aftermath have clearly demonstrated that without a commitment to competent management of financial resources, which promotes an organisational culture and conduct consistent with standards of ethics, integrity and professionalism, the sustainability of economies and the stability of the financial system itself cannot be guaranteed. Thus, the Basel principles began to assume special relevance in the regulation of the governance models of financial institutions, witnessing- dominance, an increasingly assertive regulatory framework. The National Bank of Angola is part of this process and in 2013 published Notices that brought to the national financial sector new requirements in corporate governance and internal control. In 2020, with the aim of bringing the functioning of the national financial system closer to the best international practices, the National Bank of Angola began to align the legislation and regulation of the financial sector and its own supervision model, with that in force in the European Union. As part of this process, in May 2021, the Law on the General Regime of Financial Institutions was published. Among the most relevant updates are related to the governance models of financial institutions, including requirements on the suitability of members of the management and supervisory bodies holding relevant functions. The BNA also published several regulations, of which I highlight Notices 9 and 11 in April 2020 on the process of authorisation for the constitution of bank financial institutions, their special registration and the authorisation for the exercise of functions by members of the governing bodies, and Notices 10/2021 and 1/2022 in July January 2022, respectively, which institute the Corporate Governance Code of Financial Institutions. The updating of the regulation is complemented by the new supervision model that incorporates a regular assessment by the National Bank of Angola of the governance and culture of each financial institution under its supervision, as well as its practical application on a daily basis, thus allowing for the anticipation of possible problems and preventive action. We thus have a regulatory and supervisory framework that aims to ensure the sound and prudent management of financial institutions, based on corporate governance and cultures that ensure conduct sustained by standards of ethics, integrity and professionalism. Cybersecurity is another extremely important topic. We live in an increasingly digitized world, and cybercrime is the most internationally related type of economic crime, with damage expected to cost the global economy 10.5 trillion annually by 2025, according to Interpol. Therefore, the topic has to be on the agenda of all entities and people active in cyberspace. The number of users and devices connected to the internet has been increasing significantly, mainly driven by the widespread use of 1 mobile phones worldwide. This growth was accelerated during the Covid 19 pandemic, due to the massive transfer of various services and activities to a digital one. More than 4.5 billion people in the world are "online" and therefore, more than half of the population is at risk of being a victim of cybercrime at any time. In Angola, the White Paper on Information and Communication Technologies 2019 - 2022, reflects the Government's Strategy for Digital Transformation, which aims to continue to massify internet access in the country, as well as embedding digital infrastructure in all aspects of society. According to INACOM's es, in the 3rd quarter of 2021, Angola had 14.8 million mobile phone subscribers, representing 46.5% of the population, and 7 million internet subscribers. Expanding connectivity brings a huge potential benefit to society and the economy, which makes it essential to implement a cybersecurity framework at all levels. In the financial sector, the Covid-19 pandemic has also accelerated the digitalization process, not only with products and services offered, but also with a change in the operating model, through the progressive automation of internal procedures and the widespread adoption of teleworking. Information technology is thus assuming a central role, both in the relationship between financial institutions and their customers, and in their operation. In Angola, we also have the intensification of initiatives to increase financial inclusion through the expansion of payment service providers. Initially, cyber risk was seen as a matter of internal information technology security of each financial institution. Technological developments have been changing the paradigm, as there has been an increase in the hiring of external suppliers of systems and networks, in addition to sources of cyber risk, which have come to cover operational risks linked to these suppliers, outside the control of financial institutions, and sometimes not diversifiable. The financial system uses common systems, such as central clearing platforms and transfer systems such as SWIFT, which while standardizing and secure global financial services, also increase risk due to the fact that their services cannot be easily replaced. The interconnectedness of financial institutions and services, not only nationally but also across borders, means that a cyberattack on a major IT service provider can quickly take on a national or even international systemic nature. A cyber attack on a single financial institution may imply the loss of confidence in that institution or have a negative impact on its liquidity, so that it may cause a systemic nature. A cyber attack may involve, among other consequences, the theft of customer data, financial losses and/or interruptions in the operation of the infrastructure and consequent unavailability of financial services, and it is generally accepted that the risk of successful financial institutions suffering attacks is high. being even more in the investment in the ability to recover after a successful attack. It is also imperative for financial institutions to create a strong culture of cyber risk awareness. It is common for workers to be the most important link in the infrastructure of information systems, often being "the door" through which cybercrime perpetrators gain access to the information systems of the target entity of the attack. Weaknesses in the field of training and the absence of regular monitoring mechanisms can result in uninformed workers, increasing the vulnerability of the financial institution. Thus, it is essential that in organizations everyone understands their cyberspace responsibility, from top to bottom, and the obligation to act with the greatest rigor in the use of access devices to information systems. In April 2020, recognizing the growing importance of operational risk associated with information and communication technologies, the National Bank of Angola issued Notice 8/2020 on the Cybersecurity Policy and Adoption of Cloud Computing, considering the need to establish rules on cybersecurity security, as well as the terms and conditions for contracting data processing and storage and cloud computing services to define the mechanisms of providing information regarding any situations with a significant impact on the stability of the Angolan Financial System. Before concluding, I would like to mention another aspect of the global financial system which, despite generating convenience and efficiency, also brings about the benefits of the financial system. I am referring specifically to decentralized finance that uses virtual assets, also known as cryptoassets, as an investment asset and, in some cases currency. Recognizing the irreversibility of this decentralized finance movement and the growing use of virtual assets, the International Financial Action Group - the FATF - has published recommendations on how to mitigate the risks associated with this type of financial service. It is on the basis of these recommendations that central banks and other regulatory bodies have initiated a regulatory process aimed at protecting financial systems, but also consumers of these services. As already publicly communicated, Angola, within the scope of the Council of Supervisors of the Financial System, is working on the pr of legal and regulatory instruments oriented towards virtual assets and virtual asset service providers. I conclude by congratulating EY for such a timely initiative. These exchanges of experience and ideas between people from different sectors of the economy are always enriched by the reflections and decisions that each one is responsible for. Thank you very much for your attention. Published In: Apr 21, 2022

Title: Discurso de Abertura do Administrador Pedro Castro e Silva, na Conferncia sobre a Dinamizao do Leasing e Factoring
text: Opening Speech by Administrator Pedro Castro e Silva, at the Conference on Dynamization; Leasing and Factoring Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen. Members of the BNA Executive Committee, Distinguished Presidents of Commercial Banks, Dear Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, It is with great satisfaction that I sincerely welcome another conference that is part of the annual cycle of conferences of the National Bank of Ang created to promote, share and disseminate scientific knowledge and experiences on current issues in the national and international financial universe. The Angolan Financial System has been making significant progress, namely the emergence of new financial products and services, which are increasingly complex for most of its consumers, such as leasing or leasing and factoring or financial assignment. In this edition, considering the objective of boosting credit to the economy through the introduction of stimuli and elimination of barriers to credit application, dynamism of credit supply and improvement of the legal and institutional framework that facilitates credit expansion, we decided to reflect on the dynamization of leasing factoring in Angola. The consensual doctrinal framework argues that financial leasing is the contract by which one of the parties undertakes, in return for consideration, to grant the temporary use of an object, movable or immovable, acquired or built by the latter's indication and that it can buy in whole or in part within a period of time agreed upon payment of a price determined or determinable under the terms of the contract itself. Factoring, on the other hand, consists of an improved system of collection of installment sales. It is an activity that ensures its current financing of the taking of credits on third parties, thus replacing cash credit. By means of the financial transfer, the financial intermediary (the factor) acquires the short-term credits which the suppliers (the members) grant to their customers (the debtors) and which arise from the sale of products or the provision of services. Factoring also includes complementary tasks, such as credit risk studies or legal, commercial and accounting support for the good management of transacted credits. Therefore, this meeting brings together specialists, banking sector operators and entrepreneurs from various parts of the country for an in-depth approach to the re; advantages of boosting leasing and factoring operations, as a source of financing essential to the diversification of the national economy. Thus, after the presentation of the result of the diagnosis on leasing and factoring, as well as some of the leasing products in Angola, we will have in the first pain an approach around the operability of leasing, advantages and disadvantages, main challenges, in the view of the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights and B Millennium Atlantico. In the second part of this webinar, we will take an in-depth look at the reality of leasing and factoring in African countries, the impact of these modalities on the social activities and economy of the countries, experience on leasing and factoring in the heavy vehicle and machinery sector, with the contributions of Cimertex and Standa de Angola. There is room for debate, thus making it possible to exchange best practice with a view to overcoming the obstacles to the low use of these means of financing in the national market. We believe that the conclusions resulting from the communications and discussions of this conference may contribute to the dynamization of leasing and factoring in A in order to provide the revision of the regulatory framework, the emergence of new leasing and financial assignment companies, as well as new products and services end. With these words I declare this conference open. Well done! Thank you very much for your attention. Published In: Jun 28, 2022

Title: Interveno do Vice-Governador, Rui Miguns de Oliveira, no XII Frum Banca sobre "O Impacto da Avaliao do GAFI no Sector Bancrio - Transformaes na estrutura e desafios futuros", promovido pelo Jornal Expanso.
text: Speech by the Vice-Governor, Rui Miguens de Oliveira, at the XII Banking Forum on "The Impact and Evaluation of the FATF in the Banking Sector - Transformations in the structure and future challenges", promoted by the Expansao newspaper. The Vice-Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Rui Miguens, participated, this Friday, July 22, inthe XII Edition of the Banking Forum, under the theme "The Assessment of the FATF in the Banking Sector: Transformations in the Structure and Future Challenges", promoted by the weekly newspaper Expansao. The National Bank of Angola, as the entity responsible for the country's financial system, said the Vice-Governor, has developed structuring programs to prevent and combat money laundering, terrorist financing and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, in accordance with the recommendations of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), with the strengthening of the legal framework established by Law No. 05/20, of 27 January, as well as complementary regulations on the matter, namely Notice 14/20. Within the scope of risk-based supervision, the National Bank of Angola is working to implement the supervisory technology project, Suptech, aimed at automating the collection, processing and use of information, based on the data produced by financial and non-financial institutions, "making it comprehensive, systemic, timely and preventive," said the Vice Governor. One of the main challenges is to expand the Risk matrix to non-banking financial institutions, as it is currently focused only on banking institutions, allowing to strengthen the scope of the financial system's supervisory mechanisms. Regarding banking institutions, despite the recognized advances in the matter under discussion, it is still expected that risk policies, their governance and modelling and, in particular, those related to the prevention and fight against MLFTR will be improved. Likewise, that the independence and qualification of collaborating compliance officers will be consolidated, as well as the processes and technologies that increase the reliability of data and improve its treatment and dissemination by the relevant entities. In this sense, he also highlighted the need for increasing financial inclusion not only to increase the prevention and fight against MLFTP, but to allow a fairer insertion of the population in the national economy. Regarding the growing regulatory costs and the limitation imposed on the free determination of fees by banks, the Vice-Governor explained that such limitations should be necessary to guide banks towards their main function, financial intermediation, while at the same time it is their role to be the guarantor of the protection of consumer rights, having informed that in order to strengthen the banks' ability to intervene in the national economy, the BNA is studying the possibility of increasing the share capital of banks to adapt it to the current economic situation. Finally, he closed the meeting, thanking the promoters and recognizing the public interest of the theme and its opportunity not only to engage the banks, but society in general. In addition to the central theme, the XII of the Banking Forum analysed "Changes in the internal structure of banks - digitalisation and compliance" and "The future challenges for national banking in view of the results of the FATF assessment". The event was also attended by the Secretary of State for Finance and Treasury, Ottoniel dos Santos, as well as personalities from the national and international financial sector, auditors, entrepreneurs, academics and managers. Closing Speech by Governor Jose de Lima Massano at i6.the Editing of Banca em Analise Exmo. Sr. Jose Barata, President of Deloitte Angola, Distinguished guests, Ladies and gentlemen. I would like to begin by thanking Deloitte for the invitation it made me to close this annual event to present the study Banca em Analise, which has a tradition of this, this being its 16th edition. When the project was launched, the banking sector was made up of 12 banks, with a total asset of 531 billion kwanzas. Today we have 24 banks in operation with consolidated assets of about 20 billion kwanzas, approximately 38 times that of 2005. By inviting us to this edition, the president of Deloitte Angola, Mr. Jose Barata, asks us for an assessment of the last 5 years of the central bank's action. The period was so inkful, it could be tedious for the participants to do such an exercise here. In any case, and respecting the requirement placed by our host, I would like to highlight, in summary, some of the most relevant milestones, both in the field of price stability and in the financial system. In 2017, the economic context was marked by marked imbalances, of which I highlight:  the rapid decline of International Reserves;  the prevalence of an inefficient foreign exchange market, with a differential of around 150% between the exchange rates in the formal and informal markets;  the accumulation of exchange rate arrears, estimated at around US5 billion;  the artificial overvaluation of the Kwanza, reflected in a negative gap in the real effective exchange rate of about 70%;  the general and sharp increase in the price level, with average inflation around 30%;  the poorly capitalized financial system;  a high level of non-performing loans without recognition of impairments and, also;  the loss of banking correspondents. In view of this situation, the National Bank of Angola, in line with the objectives set out in the Macroeconomic Stabilization Program adopted by the national authorities, has implemented a set of measures in the various areas of its action: In the monetary and foreign exchange sector, with the technical support of the International Monetary Fund, the operational framework of monetary policy was redefined, based on a regin monetary targets, no longer being anchored to foreign currency; We made the foreign exchange market more flexible, adopting an exchange rate regime determined by market forces and proceeded with the partial liberalization of the balance of payments account, ceasing the BNA to issue any licenses for entry or repatriation of capital within the scope of foreign direct investment in the ecc With regard to the stability of the financial system, the BNA carried out normative and procedural reforms with the aim of consolidating and ensuring the convergence of the prudential regime to international reference standards, which resulted in the establishment of the Deposit Guarantee Fund, a fundamental instrument for the consolidation of depositors, and the regulatory harmonization to the aforementioned international standards. These actions were also relevant for the recovery of the relationship of trust with international partners. It is important to mention here that in addition to having had to extensively review the regulations issued by the BNA, the revision of framing legal diplomas was decisive, of which I highlight the Law on the National Bank of Angola, clarifying the mission and conferring a status of independence of the central bank in the pursuit of its mandate, the Law on the General Regime of Financial Institutions, which grants the BNA the status of National Macroprudential Authority and establishes the Resolution Fund for the Prevention and Combating of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, incorporating the most recent recommendations of the Financial Action Groupi as well, the Angolan Payment System Law that frames the digital currency and creates space for innovation and safe availability of new payment instruments in the country. From an operational point of view, still in the field of stability of the financial system, we highlight the Asset Quality Assessment exercise of 13 banks that represented about 93% of the total banking assets. Based on these results, we started the restructuring process of two systemic public banks, as well as the requirement of a new minimum level of share capital and regulatory own funds for Financial Institutions, and defined the application of an additional capital reserve for systemically important banks, in order to increase the resilience of the sector. In the last 12 months, in particular, after the implementation of the legislative and regulatory framework, the National Bank of Angola has moved forward with the implementation of a new prudential supervision model based on the standard developed by the European banking authority, called the "Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process (SREP) which, as the name implies, It consists of the analysis and assessment of the risks inherent in a banking financial institution, focused on the business model, internal governance and risk management, capital adequacy and liquidity. The SREP has provided us with a uniform, structured, comprehensive and tested methodology that allows us to analyse and assess the risk profile of each bank, and whose implementation can be adapted to the characteristics of each institution, by adjusting its scope, depth and frequency. This exercise-penniti In this first SREP exercise, the National Bank of Angola, considering the principle of proportionality, selected 17 banking financial institutions, applied the analysis and evaluation process to its full extent, and applied a simplified process to the others. This action represented a profound change in the supervision model of the National Bank of Angola, which has a very high added value in meeting the needs of ensuring a resilient and sustainable financial sector. At this point, the National Bank of Angola carried out a diagnosis to assess the degree of compliance of its prudential and supervisory framework with those of the Euro and the Basel Fundamental Principles for Effective Banking Supervision. This exercise allowed us to conclude that our legislation, regulation and supervision, can be considered as broadly convergent with those of the Eurozone, and any divergences resulting from specificities of the national market, generally leading to a more conservative approach. As a result, large imbalances are being overcome and the stability, robustness and resilience of the financial system is being maintained. The deceleration of inflation, whose annual rate was 18.15% in September of this year, the normal functioning of the foreign exchange market and the solidity of the financial system with an average level of capital adequacy of around 20%, are part of this path. Meanwhile, in addition to the commitment to price stability and the financial system, the National Bank of Angola is also committed to promoting the development of a more competitive, inclusive banking sector capable of continuing with the investments required by the dynamics of the organization and functioning economy. In this sense, we continue to advocate the granting of credit in a responsible manner. We recognize that the quality of the information provided by customers, especially accounting and financial nature, is often not sufficient to allow a rigorous evaluation of credit applications, which is an insufficiency still present in small and even medium-sized companies, making it necessary for them to assume the commitment to improve this information. in order to enhance their access to credit. In the financing of large-scale business initiatives, it is important to consider solutions that include capital market instruments: in order to expand the internal financing capacity. The recent listing of the capital of BAI and Caixa banks on the Angolan debt and stock exchange shows a market interested, and perhaps avid, in new investment solutions and products. In the private segment, we sought with Notice 9/22 to boost housing credit up to medium and low income, supporting citizens in the purchase of their own home. This is just another contribution and not a definitive solution for home loans. Even so, we are aware of the difficulties that are occurring in granting this credit, both due to the general income levels of potential borrowers, and due to the constraints related to the legalization of real estate in the country. We are aware of the work of modernization and administrative simplification that is being carried out by the competent bodies of the State, so we will continue to support, as much as possible, so that such difficulties can be removed in the shortest possible time. Still in the private segment, we hope that in the immediate future we will be able to see the entry into operation of the Private Information Centers of Credii considering the importance they represent for improving credit risk management. In fact, more credit to the private segment, in a broad and safe way, is only possible with quality information on the real financial capacity of each private power station and will gather information on the behavior and responsibilities of each citizen in the national market, with, for example, suppliers of water, electricity, telephone, credit card, banking or even commercial establishments that offer staggered payments to their customers. With this additional information, which banks currently do not have, it will be safer and therefore less costly to grant and, consequently, obtain credit. It is with similar instruments that many countries have been able to stimulate consumer credit. In the provision of basic financial services, with emphasis on deposits and cash withdrawals and bank transfers, we consider it essential for citizens to be able to keep their money safe, access it when necessary, and transfer it at low cost and quickly, which led us to the implementation of v; measures in this regard, of which I highlight, i) a broad financial education program, ii) the simplification of account opening procedures, iii) the subsidization of TPAs, iv) the activation of cash withdrawals at POS, v) the flexibility of the opening hours of the banking network and, vi) the provision of services of AT1\ non-banking financial institutions. In addition, after consultation with the Angolan Association of Banks, we have very recently established rules for the expansion of basic banking services to all municipalities in the country by systemic banking entities. The rule brings novelties, by allowing the emergence of branches on a cost-sharing basis between banks on the one hand, and, on the other hand, by stimulating the expansion of the network of banking agents across the country. In the field of mobile and instant payment services, we have also followed an important path of development, and these payments will now operate under the 'kwik' brand, through a certified operational platform that guarantees the interoperability of the most varied operators of the payment system. For example, it will be possible for a Unitel Money user to transfer or receive money from those who use Banco Sol's e-Kumbu, e-Kwanza of BAI, or another licensed by the National Bank of Angola. In other words, the various mobile payment solutions will interact with each other, as is the case with the Multicaixa arrangement, a reference in payment services on our continent. Still on financial inclusion and modernization, last week, the Executive Committee of the National Bank of Angola approved the launch of the Opi Banking initiative, a service provided for in the Payment System Law. This initiative provides for banking financial institutions to share customer data, with their authorization, with other entities through their own digital platforms. We thus intend to create the conditions for entities to emerge in the market that use bank customers' data to offer new payment services, such as payment initiation and consultation of aggregated information about their accounts. We count on the Interbank Services Company and the Association of Banks to carry out this initiative of greater banking democratization. We have also acted to ensure that competition and transparency result in a better service to consumers of financial products and services. Practices that undermine customer trust, such as the failure to execute legitimate transfers, unjustified delays in the delivery of debit cards, or improper movement of accounts, all of them, at the top of the complaints received from citizens, by the National Bank of Angola, should deserve the particular attention of managers and those responsible for commercial banking. For all these reasons, and despite the fact that investments in technology and information systems are existential for the viability and sustainability of banks, no less important are investments in the training of human capital and in effective processes of management of the commercial relationship. The complexity of the financial sector is bound to grow, so basic limitations have to be decisively removed in order to have strong foundations on which to present products and services that respond to the needs of customers in a developing society and economy. In addition to prudential supervision and financial conduct, the banking sector is called upon to be perfectly aligned with best practices regarding the fight against money laundering, terrorist financing and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. An evaluation process of Angola by ESAAMLG is underway, focused on the country's technical compliance, in terms of laws and regulations, with the GAFE recommendations In the particular case of the Central Bank and banking and non-banking financial institutions, it is a critical success factor to continue to invest in the capacity to meet the threats coming from the national and international context, the internal vulnerabilities associated with the knowledge that the teams must have, as well as the co-operation of technological platforms, so that we can mitigate the risk of materialization of money laundering actions, Financing of the Terroris proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. Before I conclude my speech, I would like to make a brief reference to the current economic environment, because the financial sector does not act in a vacuum, within an economy and a society, with links, connections and dependencies to other economies. We are going through a positive phase in our economy internally, taking into account, among other factors, the recovery of economic growth and the reduction in inflation. But in the international context, we continue to have a framework of great challenges and concerns. The generalized levels of high inflation that have been determining the rise in interest rates, point to prospects of slowing growth at the global level, which, if it happens, should result in a reduction in demand for oil and a consequent drop in its price. Considering that oil continues to represent 90% of our exports and around 27% of GDP, it is not difficult to foresee an unfavorable impact on our economy, proportional to any decrease in its price, if this happens. In this scenario, it is clearly essential to continue the internal work of macroeconomic stabilization, in order to achieve sustained growth of the economy, it is essential to continue with the effort to diversify the economy, with emphasis on increasing the domestic production of food products for wide consumption, and our levels of food security. This is also a challenge that is renewed for national financial operators. As is understandable, there are advances and achievements, but the challenges are multiple and complex, so the commitment and contribution of all stakeholders in the ban sector are fundamental, so that, together, we can build a sector with full capacity to fulfill its role as a pillar of support for economic and social development. Finally, I express a word of gratitude to Deloitte, for maintaining regular this space of detailed incursion into the performance of banking activity in Angoh Berg. Thank you very much. Sr. Jos Barata, Presidente da Deloitte Angola, Distintos convidados, Minhas senhoras e meus senhores. Comeo por agradecer a Deloitte pelo convite que me formulou para fazer o encerramento deste evento anual de apresentao do estudo Banca em Anlise, que gani tradio, sendo esta a sua 16a edio. Quando o projecto foi lanado, o sector bancrio era composto por 12 bancos, com um total do activo de 531 mil milhes de Kwanzas. Hoje temos 24 bancos em act com um activo consolidado de cerca de 20 bilies de kwanzas, aproximadamente, 38 vezes o de 2005. Ao convidar-nos para esta edio, o presidente da Deloitte Angola, Sr. Jos Barata, solicita-nos um balano dos ltimos 5 anos da aco do banco central. De to ink foi o perodo, poderia ser fastidioso para os participantes fazer-se aqui tal exerccio. De qualquer modo, e respeitando o requisito colocado pelo nosso anfitrio, proci destacar, de forma sntese, alguns dos marcos mais relevantes, quer no mbito da estabilidade de preos, como no do sistema financeiro. Em 2017, o contexto econmico era marcado por acentuados desequilbrios, dos quais realo:  o rpido declnio das Reservas Internacionais;  a prevalncia de um mercado cambial ineficiente, com diferencial em torno de 150% entre as taxas de cmbio nos mercados, formal e informal;  a acumulao de atrasados cambiais, estimados em cerca 5 mil milhes de dlares norte-americanos;  a sobrevalorizao artificial do Kwanza, reflectida num hiato negativo da taxa de cmbio real efectiva de cerca de 70%;  o aumento generalizado e acentuado do nvel de preos, com uma inflao mdia rondando os 30%;  o sistema financeiro deficientemente capitalizado;  um elevado nvel de crdito vencido malparado sem reconhecimento de imparidades e, ainda;  a perda de correspondentes bancrios. Perante esse quadro, o Banco Nacional de Angola, em linha com os objectivos preconizados no Programa de Estabilizao Macroeconmica adoptado pelas autorida nacionais, implementou um conjunto de medidas nos diversos domnios da sua actuao: No sector monetrio e cambial, com o apoio tcnico do Fundo Monetrio Internacional, foi redefinido o quadro operacional da poltica monetria, assente num regin metas monetrias, deixando de estar ancorado  moeda estrangeira; Flexibilizamos o mercado cambial, adoptando um regime da taxa de cmbio determinada por foras de mercado e procedemos a liberalizao parcial da conta de caj balana de pagamentos, deixando o BNA de emitir quaisquer licenas para entrada ou repatriamento de capitais no mbito do investimento estrangeiro directo na ecc No que se refere  estabilidade do sistema financeiro, o BNA procedeu a reformas normativas e procedimentais com o objectivo de consolidar e garantir a convergn regime prudencial a padres de referncia internacional, de que resultaram, a instituio do Fundo de Garantia de Depsitos, um instrumento fundamental para a con dos depositantes, e a harmonizao regulamentar aos j citados padres internacionais. Essas aces foram, tambm, relevantes para a recuperao da relao de confiana com parceiros internacionais. Importa aqui referir que alm de ter sido necessrio rever de modo extensivo a regulamentao emitida pelo BNA, foi determinante a reviso de diplomas legais enquadradores, de que destaco a Lei do Banco Nacional de Angola, clarificando a misso e conferindo um estatuto de independncia do banco central na prossecu mandato, a Lei do Regime Geral das Instituies Financeiras, que atribui ao BNA o estatuto de Autoridade Macroprudencial Nacional e institui o Fundo de Resolu de Preveno e Combate ao Branqueamento de Capitais e Financiamento do Terrorismo, incorporando as recomendaes mais recentes do Grupo de Aco Financei tambm, a Lei do Sistema de Pagamentos de Angola que enquadra a moeda digital e cria espao para a inovao e disponibilizao segura de novos instrumentos de pagamento no pas. Do ponto de vista operacional, ainda no domnio da estabilidade do sistema financeiro, destacamos a realizao do exerccio de Avaliao da Qualidade dos Activos de 13 bancos que representavam cerca de 93% dos activos totais da banca. Na base desses resultados, demos incio ao processo de reestruturao de dois bancos pb sistmicos, bem como  exigncia de um novo patamar mnimo de capital social e fundos prprios regulamentares das Instituies Financeiras, e definimos a aplica uma reserva de capital adicional para os bancos de importncia sistmica, no sentido de aumentar a resilincia do sector. Nos ltimos 12 meses, em particular, terminada a implementao do framework legislativo e regulatrio, o Banco Nacional de Angola avanou com a implementa novo modelo de superviso prudencial baseado no standard desenvolvido pela autoridade bancria da Europa, denominado Processo de Anlise e Avaliao pelo Supervisor (em ingls, SREP - Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process) que, tal como o nome indica, consiste na anlise e avaliao dos riscos inerentes em ce instituio financeira bancria, focalizado no modelo de negcio, governo interno e gesto do risco, adequao do capital e liquidez. O SREP proporcionou-nos uma metodologia uniforme, estruturada, abrangente e testada que nos permite analisar e avaliar o perfil de risco de cada banco, e cuja implementao pode ser adaptada s caractersticas de cada instituio, atravs do ajustamento da sua abrangncia, profundidade e frequncia. Este exerccia-penniti pela primeira vez, definir requisitos de capital especficos a cada instituio, de acordo com o risco inerente em cada uma. Neste primeiro exerccio de SREP, o Banco Nacional de Angola, considerando o princpio da proporcionalidade, selecionou 17 instituies financeiras bancrias, s aplicou o processo de anlise e avaliao na sua total extenso, tendo aplicado s restantes um processo simplificado. Essa aco representou uma alterao profunda no modelo de superviso do Banco Nacional de Angola, de valor acrescentado muito elevado no cumprimento da su de assegurar um sector financeiro resiliente e sustentvel. Chegado a este ponto, o Banco Nacional de Angola realizou um diagnstico para aferir o grau de conformidade do seu quadro prudencial e de superviso face aos da Euro e dos Princpios Fundamentais de Basileia para uma Superviso Bancria Efectiva. Este exerccio permitiu-nos concluir, que a nossa legislao, regulamenta superviso, podem ser consideradas como largamente convergentes com as da Zona Euro, sendo as eventuais divergncias resultantes de especificidades do mercado nacional, geralmente conducentes a uma ptica mais conservadora. Como resultado, os grandes desequilbrios esto a ser superados e a estabilidade, robustez e resilincia do sistema financeiro vem sendo mantida. A desacelerao da inflao, cujo taxa anual foi de 18,15% em Setembro do corrente ano, o normal funcionamento do mercado cambial e a solidez do sistema financ com nvel mdio de adequao de capitais rondando de 20%, so parte desse percurso. Entretanto, para alm do compromisso com a estabilidade de preos e do sistema financeiro, o Banco Nacional de Angola est tambm empenhado em promover o desenvolvimento de um sector bancrio mais competitivo, inclusivo e capaz de prosseguir com os investimentos exigidos pela dinmica de organizao e funcionam economia. Nesse sentido, continuamos a advogar a concesso de crdito de forma responsvel. Reconhecemos que a qualidade da informao prestada pelos clientes, sobretudc natureza contabilstica e financeira, muitas vezes no  suficiente para permitir uma avaliao rigorosa das solicitaes de crdito, sendo essa uma insuficincia aind presente em empresas de pequena, e at mesmo, de mdia dimenso, tornando-se por isso, necessrio, que as mesmas assumam o compromisso de melhoria dessa informao, de forma a potenciar o seu acesso ao crdito. No financiamento de iniciativas empresariais de grande dimenso,  importante passar-se a considerar solues que contemplem instrumentos de mercado de capitai: modo a alargarmos a capacidade interna de financiamento. A recente listagem do capital dos bancos BAI e Caixa na bolsa de dvida e valores de Angola, mostram um mercado interessado, e talvez vido, em novas solues e produtos de investimento. No segmento de particulares, procurmos com o Aviso 9/22 impulsionar o crdito  habitao de at renda mdia, baixa, apoiando os cidados na compra de habita prpria. Trata-se apenas de mais um contributo e no de uma soluo definitiva para o crdito  habitao. Ainda assim, temos conscincia das dificuldades que vo ocorrend concesso desse crdito, quer pelos nveis gerais de rendimento dos potenciais muturios, quer pelos constrangimentos relacionados  legalizao de imveis no pas Sabemos do trabalho de modernizao e simplificao administrativa que est a ser realizado pelos rgos competentes do Estado, pelo que continuaremos a apoiar, que possvel, para que tais dificuldades possam ser removidas no mais curto espao de tempo. Ainda no segmento dos particulares, esperamos que no futuro imediato possamos assistir  entrada em funcionamento das Centrais Privadas de Informao de Crdii considerando a importncia que estas representam para melhoria da gesto do risco de crdito. De facto, mais crdito ao segmento de particulares, de modo alargado e seguro, s  possvel com informao de qualidade sobre a real capacidade financeira de cad As Centrais privadas tm essa vocao e vo congregar informao sobre o comportamento e responsabilidades de cada cidado no mercado nacional, junto de, por exemplo, fornecedores de gua, luz, servios de telefonia, cartes de crdito, banca ou at mesmo, junto de estabelecimentos comerciais que ofeream pagamentos escalonados aos seus clientes. Com esta informao adicional, que os bancos actualmente no tm, ser mais seguro e por isso menos oneroso conceder e, consequentemente, obter crdito. Foi coi instrumentos semelhantes que muitos pases conseguiram estimular o crdito ao consumo. Na disponibilizao de servios financeiros bsicos, com realce para depsitos e levantamento de numerrio e transferncias bancrias, consideramos imprescindvel os cidados poderem manter o seu dinheiro seguro, aced-lo quando necessrio, e transferi-lo a baixo custo e de modo clere, o que nos levou  implementao de v; medidas nesse sentido, das quais destaco, i) um amplo programa de educao financeira, ii) a simplificao de procedimentos de abertura de contas, iii) a subsidiai TPAs, iv) a ativao de levantamento de numerrio em TPA, v) a flexibilizao dos horrios de funcionamento da rede bancria e, vi) a prestao de servios de AT1\ instituies financeiras no bancrias. Para alm disso, aps consulta  Associao Angolana de Bancos, estabelecemos, muito recentemente, regras para a expanso de servios bancrios bsicos a todas  municipais do pas por entidades bancrias sistmicas. A norma traz novidades, ao permitir o surgimento de balces em regime de partilha de custos entre bancos coi por um lado, e, por outro, ao estimular o alargamento da rede de agentes bancrios pelo pas. No mbito dos servios de pagamentos mveis e instantneos temos trilhado, tambm, um caminho importante de desenvolvimento, e estes pagamentos passaro ag< funcionar sob a marca kwik, atravs de uma plataforma operacional certificada que garante a interoperabilidade dos mais variados operadores do sistema de pagam Por exemplo, passa a ser possvel um utilizador da Unitel Money transferir ou receber dinheiro de quem usa o e-Kumbu do Banco Sol, e-Kwanza do BAI, ou outra s licenciada pelo Banco Nacional de Angola. Ou seja, as vrias solues de pagamento mveis vo interagir entre si, tal como acontece com o arranjo Multicaixa, uma referncia de servios de pagamentos no nosso continente. Ainda sobre a incluso e modernizao financeira, na semana passada, o Comit Executivo do Banco Nacional de Angola aprovou o lanamento da iniciativa do Opi Banking, um servio previsto na Lei do Sistema de Pagamentos. Esta iniciativa prev que as instituies financeiras bancrias partilhem dados de clientes, mediante autorizao dos mesmos, com outras entidades atravs de platafc digitais prprias. Pretendemos assim criar as condies para que surjam no mercado entidades que utilizam os dados dos clientes bancrios para oferecer novos servi pagamento, tais como iniciao de pagamentos e consulta de informao agregada sobre as suas contas. Contamos com a Empresa Interbancria de Servios e com a Associao de Bancos para levarmos avante esta iniciativa de maior democratizao bancria. Temos actuado tambm para que a concorrncia e a transparncia resultem num melhor servio aos consumidores dos produtos e servios financeiros. Prticas que minam a confiana dos clientes, como a no execuo de transferncias legtimas, atrasos injustificados na entrega de cartes de dbito, ou movimenta indevida de contas, todas elas, no topo das reclamaes recebidas dos cidados, pelo Banco Nacional de Angola, devem merecer a ateno particular dos gestores e responsveis da banca comercial. Por tudo isto, e no obstante os investimentos na tecnologia e sistemas de informao serem existenciais para a viabilidade e sustentabilidade dos bancos, no menos importantes so os investimentos na capacitao do capital humano e em processos eficazes de gesto da relao comercial. A complexidade do sector financeiro ten crescer, pelo que limitaes bsicas tm que ser decididamente removidas para se ter bases fortes sobre as quais possam ser apresentados produtos e servios finance respondem s necessidades dos clientes, numa sociedade e economia em desenvolvimento. Para alm da superviso prudencial e de conduta financeira, o sector bancrio  chamado a estar perfeitamente alinhado s melhores prticas respeitantes ao combate branqueamento de capitais, financiamento do terrorismo e da proliferao de armas de destruio em massa. Decorre um processo de avaliao de Angola por parte do ESAAMLG, focado na conformidade tcnica do pas, em termos de leis e regulamentos, s recomendae GAFE No caso particular do Banco Central e das instituies financeiras bancrias e no bancrias,  factor crtico de sucesso, continuar a investir na capacidade qe se pnl as ameaas provenientes do contexto nacional e internacional, as vulnerabilidades internas associadas ao conhecimento que as equipas devem ter, assim coinrdo co funcionamento das plataformas tecnolgicas, para que possamos mitigar o risco de materializao de aces de branqueamento de capitais, financiamento do terroris proliferao das armas de destruio em massa. Antes de terminar a minha interveno, gostava de fazer uma breve referencia ao actual enquadramento econmico, porque o sector financeiro no actua num vazio, inserido numa economia e numa sociedade, com vnculos, conexes e dependncias a outras economias. Estamos a atravessar, internamente, uma fase positiva na nossa economia, tendo em conta, entre outros factores, a recuperao do crescimento econmico e a redu inflao. Mas no contexto internacional, continuamos com um enquadramento de grandes desafios e preocupaes. Os nveis generalizados de inflao elevada que tm vindo a determinar a subida das taxas de juro, apontam para perspectivas de abrandamento do crescimento econ nvel global, o que, ao acontecer, dever resultar na reduo da procura pelo petrleo e consequente descida no seu preo. Considerando que o petrleo continua a representar 90% das nossas exportaes e por volta de 27% do PIB, no  difcil antever um impacto desfavorvel na nossa economia, proporcional a qualquer descida do seu preo, se isso vier a acontecer. Neste cenrio,  claramente fundamental continuar-se o trabalho interno de estabilizao macroeconmica, para se conseguir o crescimento sustentado da economia, indispensvel continuar com o esforo de diversificao da economia, com destaque para o aumento da produo interna de bens alimentares de amplo consumo, e a dos nossos nveis de segurana alimentar. Esse  tambm um repto que se renova aos operadores financeiros nacionais. Com se compreende, h avanos e conquistas, mas os desafios so mltiplos e complexos, pelo que o empenho e contribuio de todos os stakeholders do sector ban so fundamentais, para, em conjunto, conseguirmos construir um sector com plena capacidade para cumprir o seu papel enquanto pilar de apoio ao desenvolvimento economia e da sociedade. Por fim, expresso uma palavra de reconhecimento  Deloitte, por manter regular este espao de incurso detalhada ao desempenho da actividade bancria em Angoh lanamento do debate para novas realizaes. Muito obrigado. Publicado Em: 25 de out. de 2022

Title: Interveno de Abertura do Vice-governador Manuel Tiago Dias, no Seminrio sobre Melhoria das Estatsticas do Investimento Directo Estrangeiro e das Actividades das Empresas Multinacionais
text: Opening Speech by Vice-Governor Manu Tiago Dias, at the Seminar on Improving Statistics on Foreign Direct Investment and Activities of Multinational Enterprises Mr. Astrit Sulstarova, Head of the Trends and Data Section of the Investment and Enterprise Division of UNCTAD (remotely), co-organizer of this seminar; Dr. Vitor Silveira, representative of the Bank of Portugal; Distinguished Representatives:  the Ministry of Finance;  the Ministry of Economy and Planning;  and the Ministry of Mineral Resources, Oil and Gas;  the Ministry of Industry and Commerce; Most Worthy Representatives,  the National Institute of Statistics;  the Angolan Private Investment and Export Promotion Agency;  the General Tax Administration;  and the Angolan National Company for Prospecting, Exploration, Cutting and Commercialization of Diamonds; Illustrious Representatives:  the Chambers of Commerce and Industry;  the National Agency of Petroleum, Gas and Biofuels;  Sonangol;  companies and associations in the Oil Sector;  commercial banking; Dear directors and colleagues of the National Bank of Angola; Ladies and Gentlemen, On behalf of the National Bank of Angola, I would first like to express our warm greetings and welcome to all participants in the seminar on the improvement of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) statistics and the activities of multinational enterprises. We are pleased to co-organize this active United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) and host it here in Luanda at the Currency Museum. We particularly wish the (UNCTAD) team our deep thanks for this valuable collaboration. It is with great satisfaction that I take the floor in this opening session, at a time of increasing challenges for countries with regard to the influence of RDI, economic growth and social responsibility of multinationals, requiring a reliable and systematized information structure for the analysis of macroeconomic programming trends. Macroeconomic statistics have gained greater visibility and usefulness in the face of the constant economic and financial crises that have erupted in the world since 2008. For example, the statistical literacy of the Angolan population has improved year after year, and with that the consultation and debates on statistical data published in official bodies has increased considerably. Therefore, the bodies that produce official statistics, and I am referring here particularly to the BNA and the INE, are challenged to increasingly improve the quality of the data produced by it, taking into account the crucial role that they play as an efficient instrument of coordination and support for the decision-making, both of companies and families, as well as of public managers, using statistical information, for the adoption of more serious policy measures The National Bank of Angola, in particular, has paid very special attention to its statistical function, seeking to provide its Department with qualified and competent staff who have played a fundamental role in the pursuit of the activities of our noble Institution. In this vein, in the strategic plan of the National Bank of Angola for the period 2018 to 2022, strategic actions have been developed to improve statistics in accordance with international best practices, including partnership and consultation with national and international bodies dedicated not only to the production of statistical information but also to the defence of the interests of consumers. Dear guests, The compilation of statistics is a noble task, but with many challenges, from the need to permanently increase its coverage, the adequacy of capital and automation of processes and procedures, as well as the harmonization of methodologies for collecting, processing and disseminating data, always bearing in mind internationally accepted practices. With the aim of materializing programs that aim to reduce and safeguard the challenges imposed on compilers, namely the lack of reports and resistance in the provision of information, the high turnover of staff, mechanization in their treatment, among others, UNCTAD and BNA coorg present a seminar on the improvement of statistical information regarding FDI and the activities of multinationals. Specifically, the activities of our partner, present here, are based on the experience acquired in maintaining one of the world's largest Foreign Direct Investment databases and the activities of multinationals, covering information on more than 200 economies over a 4C period, actively participating in the preparation and improvement of international references, such as the fourth edition of the Org's Direct Investment Statistics Manual for Cooperation and Cooperation. Economic Development (OECD) and the sixth edition of the Manual on the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position of the 1A, the latter manual is the basis used by the BNA for the compilation of external statistics and FDI in particular. UNCTAD's technical assistance, in the form of national seminars, brings together all relevant stakeholders (central banks, national institutes of enterprises, investment promotion agencies, etc.) dealing with Foreign Direct Investment statistics and the activities of multinationals. Seminar participants are encouraged to establish a unified, coherent and effective survey system to collect and disseminate data on FDI and CSAs of multinationals. The ultimate aim of the seminars is to enable developing economies to make appropriate decisions and formulate policies aimed at developing the development of the FDI. From the beginning of this programme, the seminars (a) raise awareness of internationally accepted standards and guidelines regarding the collection of data on the activities of foreign subsidiaries; (b) help to understand definitions and methodologies in the area of FDI statistics; and (c) provide advice on specific issues and challenges of particular interest to countries. This seminar on FDI statistics is based on the report on the Review of Angola's Investment Policy which recommends the revision of statistics in accordance with internationally accepted standards, as reliable statistics are needed to feed into a monitoring and evaluation system. Therefore, this seminar will be held under the Joint EU-UNCTAD Programme for Angola: Train for Trade II, with funding from the Eurc Union under the Investment Policy Review component. Ladies and gentlemen, We believe that the compilation of relevant and reliable statistics on FDI contributes to a better diagnosis of the economy and, therefore, the need to design and implement a prognosis that aims, among several actions, to create conditions for better business and to attract foreign investment. During the working sessions, participants will be able to share their experiences on the collection, classification and processing of information from the IDE, obtain a more comprehensive and sustainable information. perception of the structure of the balance of payments, particularly the financial account and the position of international investment, with an impact on the c; such as: direct investment - both in Angola and abroad; portfolio investment; financial derivatives and other investments; Obviously, of reserve assets. Therefore, an understanding of the collection, treatment and classification of FDI in external statistics. According to the latest global FDI report produced by UNCTAD with the motto "international tax reforms and sustainable investment" and global foreign direct investment in 2021 were US 1.6 trillion, representing an increase of 64% compared to the exceptionally low level of a recovery to pre-pandemic levels. The recovery has shown significant momentum, with M&A markets expanding and rapidly growing international project financing. However, the global environment for international business and investment has changed dramatically in 2022, as a result not only of the impacts of the 19 pandemic, but also by the implications of the armed conflicts that have erupted in the world, which in itself can increase the risk aversion of large investors. Currently, according to the statistics in our possession, the weight of FDI is remarkable in our balance of payments, with the oil sector having the largest weight with more FDI entering Angola, hence the importance of multinationals, a burning topic in this seminar. According to statistics from the Inten Investment Position, the stock of FDI represented, on average, in the last five years, about 8% of assets and 22% of liabilities. As mentioned above, an efficient diagnosis and assertive measures are only possible if the statistical information is timely and of quality. Therefore, expectations are high regarding the results that this seminar can produce and we hope that you will take the maximum possible advantage of the works that will be presented, as well as the debates that result from them. Finally, before concluding, I would like to address a word of appreciation to the members of the organizing committee, who have made this seminar possible. With these words, I declare open the seminar on the improvement of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) statistics and the Activities of Multinationals. Good work to all and thank you very much. Title: Interveno de Abertura do Vice-Governador Rui Miguns de Oliveira, no XI Frum Banca, sobre A Transformao Digital dos Servios Financeiros
text: Opening Speech by Vice-Governor Rui Miguens de Oliveira, at the XI Banking Forum, on / Digital Transformation of Financial Services Hon. Mr. Mario Nascimento - President of ABANC Hon. Ms. Andreia Vanessa Simoes - President of CMC Hon. Mr. Marcos Souto - IMF Representative in Angola Honorable Presidents of Banking Institutions Exmos Srs. Prelectors Dear Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, It was with great pleasure and satisfaction that the National Bank of Angola accepted the invitation to open this forum, promoted by ABANC, and which in this edition is dedicated to the theme of "Digital Transformation of Financial Services". In a relatively short historical time, we have moved from the introduction of punch card processing via the once innovative punch card readers, to the execution of banking operations with the simple press of a key on mobile devices, in the days. Technological disruption, which, not long ago, was seen only as an instrument to increase the productivity and efficiency of business processes in companies has now become unavoidable and critical for their survival and a factor of economic and social development. It is in the financial sector where, nowadays, the adoption of digital disruption as a differentiating factor in value propositions has been most observed. In it, financial, telecommunications and other technological institutions compete, based on innovative solutions that, most of the time, include mobile payments and other financial services. Digital disruption in the financial sector should not be seen only from the point of view of the end-to-end service offered by companies to other companies, individuals & governments. The disruptive cycle in the financial sector begins with the creation of databases, their maintenance and management and, consequently, the establishment of transactional platforms and associated services, until the creation of digital products per se, such as the very controversial digital assets, or even the "dii currencies". The National Bank of Angola is not oblivious to this process and beyond the regulatory space it has been offering for an ever-increasing supply of digital financial products and servq, has been studying and implementing technologies such as robotics and artificial intelligence, as a way to make business processes faster, safer and more transparent, as well as to improve its regulatory and supervisory role of financial activity and payment systems. The analysis of some indicators of our banking system leads us to believe that the traditional model of banking service is already being changed, through the disruption of the The evolution that we observe in the EMIS indicators shows that bank customers are beginning to privilege digital means to access banking services and carry out transactions. For example, the number of purchase transactions at automatic payment terminals (POS) was 12.3 million in December 2017. According to the EMIS report for the month of October 2022, they were 33.3 million, a growth of almost three times. The dematerialization of payments is a fact. We are all aware of the Multicaixa Express solution, an application launched by EMIS with the aim of dematerializing debit cards. The number of operations executed in this application in October 2022 was 34.2 million, it should be noted, higher than the movements in POS. The significant increase in the number of financial transactions using electronic means of payment is indicative of how rapid the penetration of ] and services other than those typically offered through the bank branch channel can be. Digital disruption in Angola has also shown that what is at stake is not just competition between channels of the same banking institution or between banking institutions. We have observed that, in addition to the operations of traditional non-banking institutions, gradually, start-ups oriented towards the commercialization of s started to have mobile wallets integrated into their applications. Through them, it is possible to make payments for services and products provided by these same platforms. Competition for the consumer of financial services is no longer just between banks. Currently, the National Bank of Angola has sixteen licensed payment service providers. Among them, we have companies promoted by telecommunications service providers and fintechs. In an increasingly online world, it is a crucial challenge for our society to ensure that more and more offline people - all of them, ideally - can access financial services easily, safely and cheaply. For the National Bank of Angola, the entry into the financial market of start-ups and telecommunications companies aims to increase the number of people with access to financial services, or simply, financial inclusion. Financial inclusion, through digital transformation, is a key tool for economic development and the reduction of social disparities. A World Bank concluded that the use of mobile payments, which allow users to store and transfer electronic money, save and access credit, has been shown to increase income and reduce poverty in several African countries, with Kenya being the one that is usually pointed out as the most successful In this reason we are focused on the implementation of Kwik, the interoperability platform of our Mobile and Instant Transfer System, managed by the Instant and Mobile Transfer System, which will allow customers of the various Payment Service Providers to make transactions with each other. In addition to the Mobile and Instant Transfer System, we have launched, in the past, the Innovation Laboratory of the Payment System of Angola, or LISPA. An initiative that includes an incubator for the development of fintechs and other start-ups not related to the financial system. Since 2019, the year LISPA was launched, we have received 602 applications for the various programs, most of which came from university students. In addition to LISPA, we approved our Regulatory Sandbox in September 2022. With the sandbox, we intend to provide the ideal environment for startups fu insurtechs and other entities in the country to test their financial products and services in the market, in an environment supervised by the BNA, for a certain period. Soon, we will start a communication campaign. In order to make the interaction of financial services digital transformation agents more flexible and inclusive, our challenge is to introduce solutions ( banking, which were officially initiated with the approval, last October, by the BNA Executive Committee, of the Open Banking initiative, whose next steps involve teamwork, including the Central Bank, EMIS, PSPs and Commercial Banks. With these words, I declare open the XI ABANC Forum on Economy and Finance, hoping that the reflections produced here will contribute to the acceleration of the digital transformation of the Angolan financial system and increase financial inclusion. Thank you very much! Published In: Nov. 21, 2022

text: Home Publications & Media Public Speeches Presentation of Year-End Greetings Presentation of End of Year Greetings The Governor of the National Bank of Angola, Dr. Jos8e de Lima Massano, proceeded today, December 21 2012, the presentation of year-end greetings to the Heads of the Institution and Chairmen of the Boards of Directors of Institutions Financial companies based in Angola. Members of the Governing Bodies of the BNA, Distinguished Members of the Boards of Directors of Commercial Banking, Directors and Heads of the BNA, Ladies and Gentlemen, We are heading towards the end of 2012, and as the tradition of our sector says, I will weave some Words about those who were the main milestones of our activity, as well as to put the next year into perspective. As far as the international economy is concerned, we are witnessing a slowdown in the economic pace, evidenced by the fall in real growth rates of advanced economies and emerging countries and by the decrease in the levels of international trade. Although monetary authorities have signaled a more relaxed course of monetary policy, by reducing key interest rates and injecting liquidity into the economy, the signs of a slow recovery in economic activity levels have not changed. The consolidation of public finances remains the main challenge of the most advanced economies and the underlying objective of the adjustment programmes under way in some Eurozone economies. In the SADC region, growth is expected in 2012 to be above the world average. The implementation of fiscal and monetary policy programmes have led to whereas in most economies in the region, the main macroeconomic indicators are remained stable. In the domestic domain, the Stand-By Agreement between the Angolan Executive and the International Monetary Fund, resulting in the availability of the last tranche of financing. Also noteworthy are the positive results of the visits made by the three rating agencies which, after analysing the evolution of the main macroeconomic indicators, reiterated their view of economic stability of for the Angolan economy. The inflation rate reached the single-digit level in August for the first time. At the end of the In November 2012, the accumulated inflation was 7.96%, while inflation in the last 12 months was 9.83%. It is expected that by the end of the year, the remains within the target set by the Government, which is 10%. The coordinated implementation of fiscal and monetary policies, and the stability of the exchange rate are determining factors for stability of prices in the Angolan economy. By the end of November, the average exchange rate of the primary market had depreciated by only 0.42%. Total foreign exchange placement by the BNA, USD 17 billion by 30 November this year, 33.5% higher than the amount placed in the same period of 2011. The strengthening of external accounts, necessary for the management of potential adverse shocks coming from the international economic environment, it was well Achieved. By the end of November, international reserves had accumulated net assets of USD 4.7 billion, with the stock standing at USD 30.8 billion. Within the scope of its responsibilities, the BNA consolidated the implementation of the New Operational Framework for Monetary Policy. The Monetary Policy Committee d0 CPM d0 assessed the evolution of global, regional and domestic economic indicators and, based on in the same countries, he made policy decisions, privileging the achievement of the main objective, that of reducing inflation. The LUIBOR Rate, in its six maturities, is now published daily on the BNA website, constituting an instrument of transparency and reference for the Expectation formation and decision-making by commercial banks, companies and companies. families. After approval by the National Assembly of the Law on the Foreign Exchange Regime of the Oil Sector, the BNA established a timetable for the entry into force of the various phases provided for in the said law. We meet regularly with the Association of Petroleum Exploration and Production Companies of Angola (ACEPA) and with commercial banks, in order to facilitate the operationalization of the new exchange rate regime, which has been occurring without any major disturbances. The Angolan banking system grew again in 2012. The banking network continued to expand and We already have around 1,155 branches and branches throughout the country. national territory. Total deposits grew by about 10% until November, having those denominated in national currency assumed greater weight, representing 52.43% of the total portfolio. Credit to the economy had grown, in the same period, in around 19%, highlighting the credit granted in currency which grew 32%. Having registered a growth in the business indicators of the banking sector, in the magnitude already However, it should be noted that the sector remained solid, while record a solvency ratio of 18.62%. The Financial Stability Committee was set up and held its first meeting in the month of April. It is an internal forum that enables analysis and discussion on the main business and risk indicators, their recent and long-term evolution, aiming at ensure the normal functioning of the intermediation process financial. In the regulatory domain, we highlight the rules on the rules and procedures to be observed in the marketing of financial services and products and on the prevention and repression of money laundering and terrorist financing. Adherence to best practices, international standards and recommendations of the Financial Action Task Force International earned an important recognition for Angola and its financial system. In fact, we have become full members of the regional anti-money laundering organisation and financing of terrorism and, not least, the first Annual Financing Report was published. Mutual Evaluation of Angola on this matter. In addition, the preparation of regulations related to consolidation is underway prudential, corporate governance, internal control system and adequacy of regulations on solvency, provisions for doubtful loans, large risks and also about concentration limits. Throughout this year, we continued to restructure the BNA in order to have a better organization prepared and adequate to market demands. Or Department of Prudential Supervision of Financial Institutions (DSI) adopts a new structure with emphasis on the combination of inspection activities direct (on site) and indirect (off site) and the creation of a new unit responsible for the analysis systemic risk and sensitivities (stress test). The National Bank of Angola understands that financial education is a determining factor for the deepening and stability of the financial system and its greater participation in the process of national economic development. The banking rate is 23%, when just over 18 months ago it stood at 11%. Or The growth of our populations' access to banking services was only possible with the commitment of the operators in the sector, for which we thank the sense of partnership demonstrated. These results should encourage us and serve as motivation to to continue this process with the same vigor, taking also an advantage of the already published regulation on correspondent banking. One of our most important achievements was the launch of the Product and Consumer Portal. Financial Services. It is a tool that addresses basic concepts associated with consumers' most frequent financial decisions and will serve as a a platform for the support and dissemination of financial information; as well as a privileged channel for handling complaints from the public consumer of financial products and services. At the level of the payment system, the BNA has continued to play its role as a catalyst for new solutions, while ensuring regulation necessary to promote the fulfilment of public interest objectives, in particular the security and transparency. In 2012, the credit transfer subsystem came into operation, and a new bank check model, and a model of reference for the development of the mobile payment system in Angola. It is also important to highlight the general growth of electronic payments, especially those that are carried out in the Multicaixa network (with an increase of about 58%). Despite the remarkable penetration of electronic means of payment, we recognize that the preference for the use of manual currency, requiring the BNA to careful monitoring of the quality of the paper money in circulation. This is how we will introduce the new banknote family in the course of 2013, which will result in an improvement in the physical and aesthetic characteristics of banknotes and coins, emphasizing our cultural values and enhancing our security features. Ladies and gentlemen; Monetary Policy in 2013 will prioritise the deceleration of the inflation rate, which aims to 9%, as established by the Angolan Executive in its proposal of the General State Budget submitted to the National Assembly. To this end, we want to increase the efficiency of the monetary policy transmission mechanisms. We will work so that, in the medium term, the interest rate is the The main instrument of monetary policy is the inflation rate, the nominal anchor for the purposes of formation of expectations on the part of economic agents. By That's right, we will continue the gradual implementation of the flexible inflation targeting system, consolidating the New Operational Framework for Policy Monetary. Studies carried out by the National Bank of Angola show that the exchange rate is one of the variables that most influence inflation. It is necessary, therefore, to continue the process of de-dollarization of the economy. From 1 July 2013, payments from the oil sector in the internal market only can be done in national currency, which will be another step important in that direction. To conclude, and to reiterate a point that I made in my speech at the end of 2011, I would like to emphasize the bet that the sector has to make on capital human. We have a responsibility to promote knowledge, professionalism and talent retention in our financial industry. Better Frames trained and motivated are the guarantee of the continuity and development of the sector and the strengthening of the its role in fostering the economic and social growth of the country. I take this opportunity to express my best wishes for the holidays and to wish you all a new year full of personal and collective achievements. Thank you very much.
